docs.text: The manager-issued sign-in secret is a credential like any other: identifier holds the displayable prefix (SFLT plus 8 characters), secret_hash the SHA-256 of the token (SFLT + 32 random bytes, base32), metadata records issued_by and single_use, and expires_at, active, revoked, revoked_at, revoked_reason, last_used_at and last_used_ip give it the standard lifecycle.

docs.title: Invariants enforced by managedprincipal.Service
docs.text:
# Invariant Enforcement 1 At least one active manager unless the principal has a verified email Create refuses len(Managers) == 0 (ErrNoManagers); RemoveManager refuses to deactivate the last active relationship of a principal whose email is missing or unverified (ErrLastManager). lockHuman takes a row lock on the principal for the transaction so concurrent removals serialize 2 A manager is an active human with an email validateManager requires type = human, active, email IS NOT NULL; a managed principal, having no email, cannot manage. A principal cannot manage itself 3 Both the deployment and the client allow managed principals Create and IssueLoginToken call Gate.ManagedPrincipalsAllowed(clientID) and return ErrNotAllowed otherwise 4 Email is independent of management, but decides whether management may end A managed principal may have an email from Create or AttachVerifiedEmail and keeps its managers and managed capabilities. Once the email is verified (VerifyEmail, or attached verified), RemoveManager may remove the last manager; with no active manager the principal is no longer managed and login tokens stop signing it in 5 A principal with no manager cannot be given one by a manager AddManager and RedeemClaim return ErrNotManaged for a principal with no active manager: entering management takes the principal's own consent (AcceptManagerInvite, below) 6 A managed principal is never a manager validateManager also requires the candidate to have no active manager of its own, whether or not it has an email; accepting an invitation is refused with ErrManagesOthers for a principal that manages others

Roles are checked against the registered set (ErrInvalidRole); the built-ins are managedprincipal.RoleGuardian and RoleEducator.

docs.title: Manager roles and permissions
docs.text:
The platform permissions a manager holds over a principal are defined in authz (authz/manager.go) and in the base SpiceDB schema (definition principal):

Permission guardian educator Covers manage_account yes no Consent, deletion, billing; attaching an email manage_credentials yes yes Issuing claims; listing and revoking login tokens and sessions view_profile yes yes Reading the profile manage_managers yes no Adding and removing other managers

authz.ManagerRolePermissions and ManagerRoleAllows mirror the schema; the parity test keeps them equal. The role-based provider evaluates a check on authz.NewPrincipalResource(managedID) through rbac.WithManagerRoleGetter, for which Service.ManagerRoles(managerID, managedID) is the getter; the service's default authorizer is exactly rbac.New(rbac.WithManagerRoleGetter(svc.ManagerRoles)), replaceable with WithAuthorizer. The relationship-based provider reads the guardian and educator relations that Syncer.AddPrincipalManager writes.

Which service operations consult the authorizer:

Operation Permission checked IssueClaim, ListLoginTokens, RevokeLoginToken, ListSessions, RevokeSession, RevokeAll manage_credentials AttachVerifiedEmail, Delete manage_account AddManager, RemoveManager, Release manage_managers ListManagersFor view_profile IssueLoginToken None through the authorizer: checkIssuer requires the issuer to be an active manager of the principal, in any role Create No principal exists to check a permission against, so the actor must be one of the managers being named (the manager creating the principal) or a platform administrator (authz.PlatformAuthorizer.IsPlatformAdmin); otherwise ErrForbidden. A missing actor is refused RedeemClaim The claim carries its issuer's authority: redemption is refused (ErrInvalidClaim) unless the issuer still holds manage_credentials on the principal, so removing a manager withdraws the claims they issued. The claimant must be a valid manager InviteManager The inviter must be a valid manager and the client must allow managed principals; consent is given by the invitee in AcceptManagerInvite, which checks the principal's own verified email, not a permission

The service accepts WithRoles for application-defined manager roles, but authz.ManagerRolePermissions grants nothing to them in the role-based provider; an application maps them in its own vocabulary.

docs.title: Creating and maintaining managers
docs.text:
Method Behavior Create(in CreateInput) Requires DisplayName, at least one ManagerInput{PrincipalID, Role}, a client that allows managed principals. In one transaction validates each manager, creates sf_principals (identifier human:<id>, managed capabilities), sf_humans, and the relationships. CreateInput.Email is optional: when set it is stored unverified, becomes the identifier, and ErrEmailInUse refuses a taken address. Emits managed_principal.created, then syncs RegisterPrincipal and AddPrincipalManager for each manager AddManager(managedID, m, actorID) Needs manage_managers, checked under the principal's row lock in the writing transaction. Idempotent: no-op when active, reactivates when inactive; emits managed_principal.manager_added; syncs RemoveManager(managedID, m, actorID) Needs manage_managers, checked under the principal's row lock in the writing transaction. Deactivates; refuses the last manager of a principal without a verified email (ErrLastManager); emits managed_principal.manager_removed; syncs ListManagers(managedID) Active relationships, oldest first; unchecked, for callers that already hold authority. ListManagersFor(actorID, managedID) checks view_profile Delete(actorID, managedID) Needs manage_account. Soft delete with erasure in one transaction: the principal is deactivated, its identifier becomes deleted:<id> and its display name "Deleted account"; email, verification, names and avatar are cleared (freeing the address); credentials, external identities, login sessions, OAuth consents and claims are deleted; OAuth and principal token families are revoked; memberships and manager relationships are deactivated; pending manager invitations to its address are withdrawn; an access change deactivated is recorded and announced (ADR-010); the authorization backend loses its relations and the principal. managed_principal.deleted. The row stays so identifiers elsewhere keep resolving; application data and any personal organization are the application's to remove Release(actorID, managedID) Ends management of a principal with a verified email: deactivates every remaining relationship, restores DefaultCapabilitiesForType(human) and records an access change (management_ended), in one transaction. Needs manage_managers, checked under the principal's row lock; ErrEmailNotVerified without a verified email; managed_principal.released; syncs each removal. RemoveManager of the last manager of a verified principal does the same InviteManager(in) A manager-to-be offers to manage the human with a verified Email. Needs a client that allows managed principals and a valid manager; returns the token once; managed_principal.manager_invited AcceptManagerInvite(token, principalID) The signed-in principal's consent. Spends the invitation conditionally, creates the relationship, sets ManagedHumanCapabilities, records an access change (management_granted), managed_principal.manager_invite_accepted, syncs. ErrInvalidInvite for any mismatch, ErrAlreadyManaged, ErrManagesOthers DeclineManagerInvite(token, principalID) The invitee's refusal, with the same identity match as acceptance (an active principal whose verified email is the invited address; ErrInvalidInvite for any mismatch, unknown, expired, revoked, accepted or already declined token). Single use: it marks the invitation declined (declined_at, declined_by) conditionally, so a concurrent acceptance or decline wins exactly once, and a declined invitation can be neither accepted nor revoked. Touches no relationship, capability or access change. managed_principal.manager_invite_declined, whose details carry the inviter and the invitation, is the inviter's notification: the service sends none itself, so the application delivers it RevokeManagerInvite(actorID, inviteID) The inviter withdraws a pending invitation; ErrNotFound otherwise, including after the invitee accepted or declined VerifyEmail(managedID, verifiedAt) Records that the principal controls the email it was created with; called by the verification flow, not by a manager. managed_principal.email_verified IssueClaim(actorID, managedID) Returns the plain code once; managed_principal.claim_issued RedeemClaim(code, claimantID) Normalizes the code (case, spaces, hyphens), compares the hash in constant time, spends the claim with a conditional update so two redemptions cannot both succeed, validates the claimant as a manager, and makes them guardian; managed_principal.claim_redeemed; syncs

Audit events go through contract/audit.Emitter when WithAuditEmitter is set; authorization sync follows authz.SyncMode (WithAuthzSyncer): a sync failure after the commit is returned in strict mode and logged in eventual mode.

docs.title: Sign-in: the login_token credential
docs.text:
Policy Default Source Reusable token lifetime 30 days (credential.DefaultLoginTokenTTL) managed_principals.login_token_ttl; a client's login_token_ttl (sf_oauth_apps.login_token_ttl) overrides it Ceiling 400 days (DefaultLoginTokenMaxTTL) managed_principals.login_token_max_ttl; longer requests are clamped and logged Single-use lifetime 20 minutes (DefaultSingleUseLoginTokenTTL) managed_principals.single_use_token_ttl

Service.IssueLoginToken(in) checks the client gate, requires the issuer to be an active manager with an email and the subject to be an active managed principal, resolves the expiry with credential.LoginTokenPolicy.ExpiresAt, and calls credential.Service.IssueLoginToken, which stores the hashed credential and returns the plain token once (credential.GeneratedLoginToken). The event managed_principal.login_token_issued records the prefix, expiry and whether the lifetime was clamped. Tokens use uppercase letters and digits so a QR code can encode them in alphanumeric mode; how an application renders them is its own choice.

credential.Service.VerifyLoginToken(plain, ip) looks the token up by prefix, compares the hash in constant time, requires it active, unrevoked and unexpired, records last_used_at and last_used_ip, and revokes a single-use token in the same conditional update (revoked_reason = "used"). Every failure is credential.ErrInvalidLoginToken.

docs.title: Exchange endpoint
docs.text:
SystemAuth mounts POST /login-token (systemauth.LoginTokenPath) when managed principals are enabled and a credential.Service is available (WithCredentialService, or the Ent storage's database). It takes form fields token, client_id and optional return_to, and:

  1. rate-limits per source address (DefaultLoginTokenAddressLimit, 60 per minute) and per registered client (DefaultLoginTokenClientLimit, 600 per minute; unregistered client IDs share one bucket), with WithLoginTokenRateLimit and WithLoginTokenClientIP for shared storage and proxy-aware addressing;
  2. resolves return_to against the redirect allowlist;
  3. requires the client to allow managed principals, verifies the token, and requires the principal to be active and managed (an email does not matter);
  4. establishes a browser login session (sf_login_sessions with provider = login_token) and redirects.

Every rejection is the same 401 invalid login token; the response never says which condition failed.

docs.title: Claims
docs.text: GetUserClaims adds "managed": true for a session whose principal has an active manager, whatever scopes were granted; email and email_verified appear only when the principal has an email and the email scope is granted. The claim appears in the ID token and at /oauth/userinfo (systemauth.ManagedClaim). The relying-party layer reads it into relyingparty.VerifiedIdentity.Managed from either source (IdentityFromClaims), and ResolvePrincipal creates a managed principal locally, with the email when the claims carry one but never linking by email; the BFF reports managed on the current user.

docs.title: Sessions and manager visibility
docs.text:
Service.ListSessions(actorID, managedID) returns every way the principal is signed in now, as managedprincipal.Session{ID, Kind, Provider, ClientID, CreatedAt, ExpiresAt, LastUsedAt, ClientIP}:

Kind Source Revocation login sf_login_sessions (browser sessions, provider such as login_token) Row deleted oauth sf_oauth_tokens, one entry per token family Family marked revoked (revoked_reason = "revoked by manager"), so its refresh token cannot renew it principal_token sf_principal_tokens, one entry per family Family marked revoked

ListLoginTokens returns live login tokens without their values; RevokeLoginToken revokes one; RevokeSession(kind, id) ends one session; RevokeAll revokes every login token and ends every session in one transaction. Each emits an audit event (login_token_revoked, session_revoked, all_revoked). managedprincipal.NewHandler(svc) exposes these and the managing operations as a chi router to mount behind requestprincipal.Middleware, which identifies the calling principal. The caller is always the actor; every route runs the service operation and so its authorizer check:

GET    /                                          ListManagedBy (?after=&limit=, at most 200)
POST   /                                          Create (JSON: client_id, display_name, email?, managers[] or role)
GET    /{principalID}/managers                    ListManagersFor
POST   /{principalID}/managers                    AddManager (JSON: principal_id, role)
DELETE /{principalID}/managers/{managerID}/{role} RemoveManager
POST   /{principalID}/release                     Release
DELETE /{principalID}                             Delete
POST   /{principalID}/claims                      IssueClaim
POST   /claims/redeem                             RedeemClaim (JSON: code)
POST   /manager-invites                           InviteManager (JSON: client_id, email, role)
POST   /manager-invites/accept                    AcceptManagerInvite (JSON: token)
POST   /manager-invites/decline                   DeclineManagerInvite (JSON: token); 204, 400 for any mismatch
DELETE /manager-invites/{inviteID}                RevokeManagerInvite
GET    /{principalID}/login-tokens
POST   /{principalID}/login-tokens                IssueLoginToken (JSON: client_id, name?, single_use?, expires_at?)
DELETE /{principalID}/login-tokens/{credentialID}
GET    /{principalID}/sessions
DELETE /{principalID}/sessions/{kind}/{sessionID}
POST   /{principalID}/revoke-all

Responses: 401 without a principal, 403 for a missing permission (or a client that does not allow managed principals), 404 for an unknown or unmanaged principal, 400 for malformed input or any unusable code, 409 for conflicts (ErrLastManager, ErrEmailInUse, ErrEmailNotVerified, ErrAlreadyManaged). Bodies are bounded and refuse unknown fields. client_id in a create, invite or login-token body is the caller's assertion; the deployment and that client's opt-in still gate it (ManagedPrincipalsAllowed).

In relying-party mode (WithRequestClient), which systemauthsvc uses to serve the API on SystemAuth, the client is the authenticated access token's and a different body client_id is a 400; create names only the caller as manager; POST /{principalID}/managers is refused (managers join through invitations and claims); and an unknown or unmanaged principal answers 403, like a principal the caller does not manage. WithCodeRateLimit adds a per-caller 429 on the routes that present a code.

docs.title: Attaching an email
docs.text: Service.AttachVerifiedEmail(actorID, managedID, email, verifiedAt) requires manage_account, and in one transaction sets sf_humans.email and email_verified_at on a managed principal that has no email, and makes the email the sf_principals.identifier. Management is unchanged (ADR-009): the relationships and the managed capabilities stay, and the verified email is what allows the last manager to be removed. A taken address is ErrEmailInUse; a principal that already has an email is ErrHasEmail. Proving control of the address is the caller's job (ADR-003 verification is not wired into this step). A principal created with an unverified email is verified with Service.VerifyEmail instead.

docs.title: Other surfaces today
docs.text: Surface Behavior Invites Accepting or listing invites requires a caller with an email; a managed principal gets 403 Signup and social login Look principals up by email; a managed identifier never matches Marketplace marketplace.PurchaserChecker (Service.IsManaged) refuses checkout for managed principals Deletion Service.Delete (above), restricted by manage_account to guardians, which ADR-005 requires

docs.title: Releasing a principal
docs.text: Management ends only for a principal that can be reached and has proven it controls its address (ADR-009). Release and the removal of the last manager of such a principal are the same event: the relationships are deactivated and the human capabilities that management withheld (CanManageProfile, CanDelegate) are restored in the transaction, and managed_principal.released is emitted. The platform records the release; whether the person must confirm first is the application's decision. Once released the principal is self-managed: managers lose their authority, the managed claim is no longer emitted, login tokens stop signing it in, and re-entering management takes a new invitation.

docs.title: Manager invitations
docs.text: A manager relationship with an existing principal gives up control of its own profile, so it is created only by that principal accepting an invitation while signed in (AcceptManagerInvite). The caller passes its own authenticated principal ID, and the invitation matches only when the principal's verified email is the invited address, so a leaked token alone does not enter anyone into management. The invitee may instead decline (DeclineManagerInvite), with the same identity match: the invitation is then spent, the inviter cannot withdraw it and nothing about the invitee changes. Creation by a manager (Create, RedeemClaim) remains the path for principals the manager creates or whose guardian claims them. How the token is delivered (email, link, QR) is the application's choice.

docs.title: Slugs
docs.text: A managed principal's personal organization (ADR-006) is never slugged from an email. signup.SlugForManaged produces the manager-entered value or a generated adjective-noun-NN; SystemAuth uses it, with the managers' display name and no provider avatar, when a managed principal signs in with an email of its own (personalOrgParamsFor). A handle therefore never reveals a child's address.

docs.title: What a managed principal may do for itself
docs.text: That is the application's decision, expressed in its authorization vocabulary (ADR-009 decision 7): the platform supplies the relationship, the roles and the managed claim. A managed principal may hold its own credentials (a password, a social login linked to its email, login tokens); manager authority (consent, deletion, credential and session revocation) is unchanged by the principal signing in itself.

docs.title: Organizations and Membership
docs.text:
This page describes how SystemForge models organizations, who belongs to them, how people get in, what an organization is entitled to, and how a relying party learns a principal's memberships. The first part describes the system as implemented in identity/organization, identity/invite, identity/signup, identity/systemauth, identity/relyingparty and marketplace; the last section records where the implementation differs from the wording of the decisions.

Decisions: ADR-006 (lifecycle, personal and team organizations, slugs, removal of plan), ADR-007 (memberships and entitlements as claims), ADR-008 (collaborators, resource grants, resource-targeted invites), ADR-010 (real-time invalidation of access), ADR-002 (account linking at login).

docs.title: Organization
docs.text: An organization is a tenant. Every principal-scoped record in a SystemForge application hangs off one, and a person's own namespace is itself an organization of type personal.

docs.title: Table sf_organizations (identity/ent/schema/organization.go)
docs.text:
Column Type Notes id UUID Primary key name string Display name; required (NotEmpty) slug string Unique URL-safe identifier; ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*[a-z0-9]$, 3–63 characters (organization.isValidSlug) org_type enum personal, team, enterprise Default team owner_principal_id UUID, nullable The owning principal; required for personal, set by the API for every organization it creates logo_url, description, website_url string, nullable Cosmetic settings JSON object Application-specific configuration active bool Delete sets it to false (soft delete)

Edges: principal_memberships, invites, oauth_apps, marketplace listings, licenses and subscriptions.

docs.title: Types
docs.text:
Kind Go constant Meaning today personal organization.OrgTypePersonal A person's own namespace, created by signup; Organization.IsPersonal() team organization.OrgTypeTeam A shared organization; the default enterprise organization.OrgTypeEnterprise A large organization; no behavioral difference from team in code

A personal organization requires an owner (Create refuses one without OwnerPrincipalID), and GetPersonalOrg(principalID) finds it by org_type = personal AND owner_principal_id = principalID.

A personal organization has exactly one member, its owner (ADR-006 decision 3). organization.RequireMembersAllowed is the check every path that creates or changes a membership applies: AddMember, UpdateMember (including deactivating the owner), invite.Create and invite.Accept, and SCIM group membership refuse a personal organization with ErrPersonalOrganization unless the role is organization.RoleCollaborator (ADR-008), and TransferOwnership refuses it outright. The members API answers 409 for ErrPersonalOrganization, and POST /organizations accepts only team and enterprise for org_type: personal organizations come from signup. The collaborator role is one of the organization roles and is in the members API's role enum.

docs.title: Slug is the identity
docs.text:
The slug is how an organization is addressed: every organization and membership endpoint is keyed by it (/organizations/{slug}, /organizations/{slug}/members/..., /organizations/{slug}/invites/...), and GetBySlug is the lookup the API uses. The display name is cosmetic and carries no identity. The slug is unique across every organization type, so personal and team organizations share one namespace.

The slug changes only through Rename (see Renaming and the cooling-off period): UpdateOrganizationInput has no slug field and PATCH /organizations/{slug} accepts only name, logo_url, description, website_url and settings. SlugAvailable(slug) checks sf_organizations.slug, the reserved list and live cooling-off reservations; GenerateSlug(name) slugifies the name (lowercase, spaces and underscores to hyphens, other characters dropped, -org appended below three characters) and appends -1 to -100, then an eight-character UUID fragment, until one is free.

Reserved slugs. organization.ReservedSlugs lists names no organization may take because they would collide with a route or a protocol path (admin, api, login, logout, oauth, scim, invites, organizations, well-known, www, support, help, about, settings, new, o). A deployment adds its own product names with WithReservedSlugs(...). SlugAvailable answers false with ErrSlugReserved for a reserved slug, Create and CreatePersonalOrg fail with it, GenerateSlug steps past a reserved base to its numeric suffix, and SCIM group creation refuses a reserved slug. Personal slugs derived at signup go through uniqueSlugInTx, which skips reserved names the same way (PersonalOrgParams.ReservedSlugs carries the deployment's additions). signup.SlugForLogin derives a login's base slug and signup.SlugForManaged returns a manager-entered slug or a generated one (two words and a number, never derived from an email address).

docs.title: Renaming and the cooling-off period
docs.text:
Rename(ctx, orgID, slug, actor) changes an organization's slug in one transaction. actor must be an active owner of the organization (ErrNotOwner); the new slug must be well formed (ErrInvalidSlug), not reserved (ErrSlugReserved), not used by an organization (ErrSlugTaken) and not held by someone else's reservation (ErrSlugCoolingOff). The old slug is written to sf_slug_reservations (slug unique, released_by_principal_id, released_from_organization_id, released_at, expires_at) and held for organization.SlugCoolingOff (7 days; WithSlugCoolingOff overrides it). The rule is the same for personal and team organizations in every direction.

  • Who may take a held slug. The principal who released it, or an owner of the organization that released it. Create passes its owner as the acting principal, so that owner may create an organization under the held slug, which spends the reservation; Rename does the same for its actor. SlugAvailable has no actor and answers false with ErrSlugCoolingOff.
  • Aliases. ResolveSlug(ctx, slug) returns the organization using the slug, else, while a reservation is live, the organization that released it with alias = true. The organization and invite handlers resolve {slug} through it, so old links keep working and responses carry the current slug. GetBySlug stays an exact match.
  • Expiry. An expired reservation is ignored everywhere and deleted when next read. Signup's uniqueSlugInTx skips a slug under a live reservation and takes the next numeric suffix.
  • There is no HTTP endpoint for renaming yet; Rename is a service method.

docs.title: Converting a personal organization to a team
docs.text: ConvertToTeam(ctx, orgID, teamSlug, actor) returns a ConvertResult{Team, Personal}. In one transaction it checks that the organization is personal (ErrNotPersonal) and that actor is its owner (ErrNotOwner), renames it to teamSlug with the rules above (which reserves the person's handle for actor), sets its type to team, and creates a new personal organization for actor under the handle, spending that reservation. The converted organization keeps its ID, data, settings and every membership, so its owner membership is the team's first owner and collaborators stay; it now accepts members like any team. The new personal organization is named after the owner's display name, has the owner as its only member, and is registered with the authorization syncer after commit. Any failure rolls everything back. There is no HTTP endpoint for the conversion yet.

docs.title: Service (identity/organization)
docs.text:
organization.Service is implemented by DefaultService over Ent, with an authz.RelationshipSyncer (default noop) and an authz.SyncMode (strict fails the call on a sync error after the database commit; eventual, the default, logs it).

Method Behavior Create(input) Validates and reserves the slug; creates the organization and, when an owner is given, an owner membership in one transaction; then syncer.RegisterOrganization(orgID, ownerID) CreatePersonalOrg(input) Create with org_type = personal, and the owner GetByID, GetBySlug, GetPersonalOrg Lookups Update(id, input) Name, logo, description, website, settings; never the slug or type Delete(id) Sets active = false; syncer.UnregisterOrganization List(input) Filters: OrgType, Active, MemberPrincipalID (active memberships only), limit and offset TransferOwnership(input) See Ownership transfer Rename(orgID, slug, actor), ResolveSlug(slug) See Renaming and the cooling-off period SlugAvailable, GenerateSlug See above

docs.title: HTTP API (identity/organization handlers, huma over chi)
docs.text:
The organization API requires an authz.Authorizer; until one is configured every endpoint except createOrganization and checkSlugAvailability answers 501. The caller is resolved by requestprincipal.PrincipalUUID (configurable through APIConfig.Caller). orgFor loads the organization by slug and checks the operation's permission; a caller who cannot even view the organization gets 404, so its existence is not confirmed to outsiders.

Operation Route Permission (authz) createOrganization POST /organizations Any authenticated principal; the caller becomes the owner. Default org_type = team getOrganization GET /organizations/{slug} view updateOrganization PATCH /organizations/{slug} settings deleteOrganization DELETE /organizations/{slug} delete (owner only) listOrganizations GET /organizations The caller's own memberships, or every organization for a platform admin checkSlugAvailability GET /organizations/check-slug/{slug} None

docs.title: Table sf_principal_memberships (identity/ent/schema/principal_membership.go)
docs.text:
Column Type Notes principal_id, organization_id UUID Unique together: one membership per principal per organization role string One of the organization roles owner, admin, member, collaborator (RoleOwner, RoleAdmin, RoleMember, RoleCollaborator); every service path that writes a membership refuses any other value with ErrInvalidRole, and the API's role enums are owner,admin,member,collaborator. editor and viewer were retired as organization roles; migration 0008_drop_editor_viewer_roles.sql maps stored editor to member and viewer to collaborator, recording an access change for each active membership it changes permissions JSON string array Optional per-membership permissions; stored and returned, not evaluated by the providers active bool Deactivated memberships are kept and excluded from listings unless organization.IncludeInactive() is passed

Any principal type can hold a membership. The owner's membership is created with the organization; there is no separate "owner" flag on the membership, only role = owner plus sf_organizations.owner_principal_id.

docs.title: Service methods
docs.text:
Method Behavior AddMember(input) Refuses when a membership (active or not) exists; creates it active; syncer.AddOrgMembership(principal, org, role) UpdateMember(membershipID, input) Role, permissions, active; a role change calls syncer.UpdateOrgMembership(old, new) RemoveMember(orgID, principalID) Deletes the row; syncer.RemoveOrgMembership GetMembership(orgID, principalID) Returns the row whatever its active value, or ErrMembershipNotFound ListMembers(orgID), ListMemberships(principalID) Active rows by default

organization.MembershipRoleGetter(svc) adapts GetMembership to rbac.WithRoleGetter: an inactive or missing membership has no role.

docs.title: Member endpoints
docs.text: Operation Route Rule listMembers, getMember GET /organizations/{slug}/members[/{principal_id}] view addMember POST /organizations/{slug}/members invite_member; granting owner additionally needs the owner-only permission (delete) updateMember PATCH /organizations/{slug}/members/{principal_id} change_role; touching an owner's role, or granting owner, needs the owner-only permission; deactivating needs remove_member removeMember DELETE /organizations/{slug}/members/{principal_id} A member may remove themself with view; removing someone else needs remove_member, and removing the owner needs the owner-only permission transferOwnership POST /organizations/{slug}/transfer-ownership delete, and the caller must be owner_principal_id

docs.title: Ownership transfer
docs.text: TransferOwnership requires the current owner's membership to have role = owner and the new owner to already be a member. In one transaction it sets the old owner's role to NewRoleForOld (admin by default; only admin or member are accepted), sets the new owner's role to owner, and updates owner_principal_id. Both role changes are then synced. A personal organization is refused with ErrPersonalOrganization.

docs.title: Table sf_invites (identity/ent/schema/invite.go)
docs.text: Column Notes organization_id, inviter_principal_id Who invited, to where email The invitee; the invite is bound to this address role Role granted on acceptance; default member; the API accepts owner, admin, member, collaborator token Hex SHA-256 of the URL token (32 random bytes, base64url); the token itself is never stored app_roles Optional JSON object, application identifier to role, granted on acceptance (ADR-007); migration migrations/0006_invite_app_roles.sql adds the column to an existing database resource_type, resource_id, resource_role Optional, all or none: the resource and the resource role to grant on acceptance (ADR-008); migration migrations/0009_invite_resource_target.sql adds the columns to an existing database status pending, accepted, declined, expired, revoked message, expires_at, accepted_at, accepted_by_principal_id, resend_count, last_sent_at Lifecycle

docs.title: Service (identity/invite)
docs.text: Method Behavior Create(input) Refuses when a pending, unexpired invite exists for the same organization and email; default expiry invite.DefaultInviteExpiry (7 days); returns the one-time InviteURL ({baseURL}/invites/{token}). With invite.WithAppRoles(approleService), AppRoles (none preselected) are validated against the registered vocabularies and the organization's entitlements, collaborators may carry none, and an admin or member invitation to an organization entitled to any application must choose at least one (ErrAppRoleRequired); owners hold every role implicitly. Without that option, AppRoles are refused and nothing is required. A resource target (ResourceType, ResourceID, ResourceRole, all three) requires Role to be collaborator and invite.WithResourceGrants(svc), and is validated with resourcegrant.Service.Validate (a registered application, a collaborator-able type, a valid identifier and role); a collaborator invitation with no target is refused for a personal organization, which accepts only resource-targeted invites. A person may hold several pending invites to one organization if each targets a different resource GetByToken, GetByID, List, ListPendingForEmail, HasPendingInvite Lookups; email matching is case-insensitive Accept(input) Requires pending and unexpired (an expired one is marked expired); in one transaction refuses an existing membership, creates the membership with the invite's role, grants the invite's application roles (approle.Service.AssignInTx, seat limits enforced under the same lock as Assign; an invitation that cannot grant a role, for example because no seat is left, is refused and stays pending), and marks the invite accepted. A resource-targeted invite instead calls resourcegrant.Service.GrantInTx in the same transaction, which creates the collaborator membership when the principal has none (an existing member keeps their role and gains the grant); a grant the store refuses leaves no membership and a pending invite. It writes the membership directly rather than through the organization service, so after commit it calls syncer.AddOrgMembership itself (options invite.WithAuthzSyncer, WithSyncMode, WithLogger; default noop and eventual, like the organization service) Decline(token), Revoke(id) Status changes Resend(id) New token, resend_count + 1, expiry reset to 7 days ExpireOld() Batch status update

docs.title: Invite endpoints
docs.text: Organization-side routes (POST/GET /organizations/{slug}/invites, DELETE .../{invite_id}, POST .../{invite_id}/resend) need invite_member; inviting an owner needs the owner-only permission, and inviter_principal_id must be the caller. The create body takes app_roles and invites in responses carry them. A member's roles are changed later, per application and without touching the membership, through the application role endpoints (PUT/DELETE /organizations/{slug}/members/{principal_id}/app-roles/{application}). Invitee-side routes (GET /invites/{token}, POST /invites/{token}/accept, POST /invites/{token}/decline, GET /invites) require the caller to have an email that matches the invite's address; a principal without an email (a managed principal) gets 403, and a mismatched invite answers 404. Signing up through an invite (signup.SignupWithInvite) applies the same match (signup.ErrInviteEmailMismatch).

docs.title: Signup (identity/signup)
docs.text:
signup.Service creates a person and their personal organization:

Method Behavior Signup(input) Requires a plain email, a display name and PersonalOrgSlug; refuses a taken email (ErrEmailTaken) or slug; creates the human principal with AllowedScopes openid profile email, then the personal organization (name defaults to the display name, logo to the avatar). With the default services the principal, organization and owner membership are written in one transaction (principal.HumanTxCreator.CreateHumanInTx and organization.PersonalOrgTxCreator.CreatePersonalOrgInTx), so a failure leaves nothing behind; the syncer registrations (RegisterPrincipal, then RegisterOrganization) run after the commit and, in strict sync mode, a failed one is returned with the rows kept. Services that do not implement those interfaces fall back to separate commits, and a failure after the principal exists deletes it again SignupWithInvite(input) Signup, then invite.Accept for the invite (email must match) SignupOrGetExisting(input) Returns the existing principal and personal organization for an email only when EmailVerified is set (ErrEmailNotVerified otherwise); creates them otherwise

docs.title: Signup on first social login
docs.text:
GitHub and Google login (systemauth.ResolveExternalLogin, ADR-002, ADR-006 decision 1) resolve a principal by (provider, subject) first, then link by a verified email to an existing principal whose own email is verified, and otherwise create one. An unverified email never links to or creates an account (ErrEmailNotVerified, nothing written).

The create step does not call signup.Service (neither Signup nor SignupOrGetExisting); it writes with the same in-transaction helpers rather than the services' syncer-aware *InTx variants, because it also creates the external identity row in that transaction. Instead EntPrincipalDirectory.CreateFromExternal opens one Ent transaction and writes the principal, its sf_humans row, the sf_external_identities link, and, through signup.CreatePersonalOrgInTx, a personal organization (type personal, owner set, name = display name, else provider username, else email local part, logo = avatar) with an active owner membership. A failure at any step rolls all of it back. After the commit, the directory registers the principal (syncer.RegisterPrincipal) and the organization with its owner (syncer.RegisterOrganization) with an authz.RelationshipSyncer, so both exist in rebac mode; the backfill path registers only the organization it creates. Configure it with systemauth.WithSocialAuthzSyncer(syncer, mode) on the server, or WithDirectoryAuthzSyncer, WithDirectorySyncMode and WithDirectoryLogger on NewEntPrincipalDirectory. The default is noop and eventual mode: a failed registration is logged. In strict mode it is returned, with the rows already committed.

  • Slug. signup.SlugForLogin(provider, username, email) returns the GitHub username for github, the email local part for google, and the username (else the local part) for any other provider, normalized to a valid slug. If that slug is taken or reserved (the built-in list, or the deployment's through PersonalOrgParams.ReservedSlugs), -1 to -100 and then an eight-character random suffix are tried inside the transaction. A managed principal's organization is never slugged from an email: signup.SlugForManaged returns a manager-entered value or a generated adjective-noun-NN (see Slugs).
  • Races. Two first logins of the same identity race on the unique (provider, subject) constraint; the loser's transaction rolls back and ResolveExternalLogin re-reads the winner. A lost race for the slug alone retries the transaction (up to three times).
  • Backfill. After every successful login ResolveExternalLogin calls EnsurePersonalOrg (the optional systemauth.PersonalOrgEnsurer, which EntPrincipalDirectory implements). A principal that has no personal organization, such as one created before this behavior or linked by verified email, gets one in its own transaction; a principal that has one is left untouched, so repeat logins create nothing. MemoryPrincipalDirectory keeps no organizations.
  • signup.SignupOrGetExisting is unchanged and still resolves by email only; social login does not use it. Note on ADR-006 decision 1: that ADR says social login calls SignupOrGetExisting; in practice it uses the in-transaction helpers described above, which is the behavior of record.

docs.title: No plan on the organization
docs.text:
An organization has no plan. The column was a placeholder from before the marketplace: set at creation and never consulted, and one value cannot describe an organization holding several subscriptions or licenses (ADR-006). It is gone from sf_organizations, from organization service inputs and the list filter, from the API, and from SCIM group provisioning; the organization.Plan* constants are removed. Existing PostgreSQL databases run migrations/0004_drop_organization_plan.sql; fresh databases need nothing.

What an organization may use is its entitlements, a list returned in every OrgResponse and derived from the marketplace (next section). APIConfig.Entitlements supplies the source; marketplace.EntitlementSource(subscriptions, licenses, listings, opts...) builds one from each active subscription (source subscription, tier = plan_tier, valid until the period end), each valid license (source license, the listing ID, tier = license type, valid until, and seats for a seat-based license) and the deployment's default entitlements (source default). An entitlement that comes from a listing naming an application carries that application. Without a source the list is empty.

docs.title: Entitlements via the marketplace
docs.text:
What an organization may use is recorded by marketplace, not by the organization:

Table Purpose Key columns sf_listings A product offered by a creator organization creator_org_id, owner_id, product_type, product_id, application (optional), pricing_model (free, one_time, subscription, per_seat), price_cents, currency, status (draft, pending_review, published, archived) sf_licenses An organization's right to a listing listing_id, organization_id, license_type (seat_based, team, unlimited), seats, used_seats, valid_from, valid_until, stripe_subscription_id, purchased_by sf_seat_assignments A seat of a license given to a principal license_id, principal_id, assigned_by, assigned_at sf_subscriptions A subscription of an organization: at most one platform-wide (no listing_id) plus one per listing organization_id, listing_id (optional), plan_tier (free, starter, pro, enterprise), status (active, trialing, past_due, canceled, unpaid), current_period_start/end, cancel_at_period_end, Stripe IDs

Services: marketplace.ListingService (create, publish, archive, list), LicenseService (Grant, Revoke, Check(listingID, orgID) for a valid license, CheckPrincipal(listingID, principalID) which passes any valid unlimited license outright and otherwise requires a seat assignment, AssignSeat/UnassignSeat), SubscriptionService (GetByOrg, which returns the platform subscription, IsActive, GetPlanTier, ChangePlan, Cancel, CancelImmediately, Reactivate) and CheckoutService (Stripe). A SubscriptionService that also implements the optional SubscriptionLister (ListByOrg) contributes every subscription of an organization to entitlements. Tiers are a property of a subscription, not of a listing. The marketplace.PurchaserChecker (implemented by managedprincipal.Service.IsManaged) refuses checkout for managed principals. marketplace.SpiceDBSyncer writes listing, license, seat and subscription relationships for the relationship-based provider (creator_org, owner, licensed_org, listing, purchased_by, seat_holder, subscriber).

A listing's optional application is the registered application identifier (an authz.AppVocabulary application) that an active subscription or a valid license on it entitles the organization to. It is not settable through the listing HTTP API, only through the service, so that a listing creator cannot entitle buyers to an application they do not control. An organization's entitled applications are therefore:

  • the application of each listing it holds an active (active or trialing) subscription or a currently valid license for, and
  • the deployment's default entitlements, marketplace.WithDefaultEntitlements(apps...) (configuration marketplace.default_entitlements), for applications free to everyone.

Seat accounting: the seat limit of an application is the sum of the seats of its valid seat_based licenses, and there is none when any entitlement for the application is not seat-limited (a subscription, an unlimited license, a default). approle counts sf_app_roles rows for (organization, application) against it and refuses with ErrNoSeats; the count and the insert run in one transaction under a PostgreSQL advisory lock keyed by (organization, application), so concurrent assignments cannot exceed the limit (SQLite is serialized in process); owners' implicit roles hold no seat. marketplace.WarnIfNoEntitlements logs a warning at startup when applications are registered but there is no default entitlement and no listing names an application, in which case every organization is refused every application role. authz.FeatureAuthorizer remains an interface with no implementation in the repository.

Existing PostgreSQL databases run migrations/0005_subscriptions_per_listing.sql, which adds the two nullable columns and relaxes the one-subscription-per-organization constraint; existing subscriptions become platform subscriptions.

docs.title: Application roles (identity/approle)
docs.text:
A principal's access inside an application is an application role, stored per (principal, organization, application) in sf_app_roles (Ent schema AppRole):

Column Notes principal_id, organization_id Foreign keys, cascade on delete application Identifier registered in authz.VocabularyRegistry role One of the application's AppVocabulary.Roles(); free text in the column, validated by the service assigned_by Principal who made the change; null if that principal is deleted id, created_at, updated_at BaseMixin

Unique on (principal_id, organization_id, application), indexed on (organization_id, application). Fresh databases get the table from the Ent migration; no SQL migration is needed.

approle.Service (built with NewService(client, registry, opts...)):

Method Behavior Assign(in) Creates the role; ErrAlreadyAssigned if the principal already has one in that application Change(in) Sets a different role; ErrNotAssigned if there is none Remove(org, principal, app, by) Deletes the role; ErrNotAssigned if there is none RemoveForMember(org, principal) Deletes every role of a member in the organization ListForPrincipal, ListForOrganization Stored roles only EffectiveRoles(principal, org) Map of application to role: stored roles plus the implicit owner role, only while the membership is active Roles(app) The application's roles, lowest first, for pickers

Rules enforced by Assign and Change: the application is registered, the role is one the application declares, the organization is entitled to the application and has a free seat if the application is seat-limited (WithEntitlementGrants, built from the marketplace by marketplace.ApproleOptions(marketplace.EntitlementSource(...)); without an entitlement option no organization is entitled to anything, and approle.EntitleAll is for development and tests), and the principal has an active owner, admin or member membership. Collaborators, non-members and deactivated members cannot hold roles. Each assignment is logged with who made it and whether it was to themself.

EffectiveRoles gives owners the top role of every entitled registered application, admin where the vocabulary declares it, else the highest role in its hierarchy; when an owner also has a stored role the higher wins. Admins and members hold only stored roles, and nobody holds any by default. Deactivating a membership leaves the rows but they are not effective; removing the member deletes them, in the same transaction (organization.Service.RemoveMember, and SCIM's group member removal).

HTTP endpoints, on the organization API when APIConfig.AppRoles is set (501 otherwise):

Route Permission GET /organizations/{slug}/app-roles[?application=] change_role GET /organizations/{slug}/members/{principal_id}/app-roles change_role, or view for one's own roles; returns stored and effective roles PUT /organizations/{slug}/members/{principal_id}/app-roles/{application} change_role; body {"role": "..."}; assigns or changes DELETE /organizations/{slug}/members/{principal_id}/app-roles/{application} change_role

With approle.WithAuthzSyncer, assign, change and remove also write to the authorization graph through the optional authz.AppRoleSyncer (see Keeping providers in step with identity).

Invites carry application roles (see Invites).

docs.title: Resource grants (identity/resourcegrant)
docs.text:
A collaborator reaches individual resources, not the organization (ADR-008). A grant is a principal's role (viewer, contributor or maintainer) on one resource of an organization, stored in sf_resource_grants (Ent schema ResourceGrant):

Column Notes principal_id, organization_id The grantee and the resource's organization; deleting either deletes the grant resource_type {app}_{type}, as declared in the application's vocabulary resource_id The application's identifier, 1 to 1024 characters of a-zA-Z0-9/_\|-=+ (the characters SpiceDB object identifiers allow, so both modes accept the same resources) role A resource role; free text in the column, validated by the service granted_by The granting principal, when known; cleared if that principal is deleted

Unique on (principal_id, resource_type, resource_id); indexed on (organization_id, principal_id), (resource_type, principal_id) and (resource_type, resource_id). The table is created by the schema migration; no SQL script is needed.

resourcegrant.Service (built with NewService(client, opts...)) implements authz.ResourceGranter and authz.ResourceGrantReader:

Method Behavior GrantResourceRole(principal, ref, role, by) Validates the role, the reference and, with WithVocabularies, that the type belongs to a registered application. In one transaction: gives the principal a collaborator membership when it has none in the organization (reactivating a deactivated collaborator; a deactivated member of another role is refused with ErrInactiveMembership), and creates the grant or replaces its role. Lowering a role records grant_reduced. A resource belongs to one organization: a grant naming another one for a resource that already has grants is refused with ErrResourceOrganizationMismatch GrantInTx(tx, ...) The same inside the caller's transaction, returning the function to call after commit (publishes the access changes and syncs); for flows that create membership and grant together, such as accepting an invitation RevokeResourceRole(principal, ref) Deletes the grant and records grant_reduced; when it was the principal's last grant in the organization and the membership is a collaborator's, deletes the membership and records membership_removed. ErrGrantNotFound when there is none ListResourceGrants(ref) The grants on a resource, highest role first ListResources(principal, type, permission) Resource identifiers on which a grant gives the principal view, edit or manage, in organizations where its membership is active ResourceRole(principal, ref) The principal's role through a grant, or empty when it has none or its membership is inactive

Grants and revocations of one principal in one organization are serialized by a PostgreSQL advisory lock, so concurrent first grants create one membership and concurrent revokes cannot both miss the last grant. organization.Service.RemoveMember deletes the member's grants with the membership and, with a syncer that implements authz.ResourceGrantSyncer, removes them from the graph. With WithAuthzSyncer the service writes the collaborator membership through AddOrgMembership and the grant through ResourceGrantSyncer; noop implements it, so any existing syncer keeps working.

The role-based provider consults the table: rbac.WithResourceGrants(svc) makes Can and Decide allow view, edit and manage on a resource the principal holds a role on when the organization role has not (see Authorization).

docs.title: How relying parties get memberships
docs.text:
A relying party (identity/relyingparty) authenticates a SystemAuth session, access token or API key and attaches memberships to the request through a MembershipSource:

type MembershipSource interface {
    Memberships(ctx context.Context, q MembershipQuery) ([]Membership, error)
}

MembershipQuery carries the app-local Principal, the SystemAuth Subject and, for sessions and JWT access tokens, the verified Claims. The default is ClaimsMemberships, which decodes the orgs claim (see The orgs claim); RemoteMemberships reads GET /oauth/userinfo/memberships, ClaimsOrRemoteMemberships combines them (endpoint used when orgs_truncated is set or the claim is absent, claims served if it fails), ProvisioningMemberships runs an idempotent per-organization hook on first use by a principal holding a role in the application, and LocalMemberships over a MembershipLister remains for development and tests only. relyingparty.Membership is {ID, OrganizationID, OrganizationName, OrganizationSlug, OrganizationType, Role, JoinedAt, Applications}; MembershipQuery.AccessToken lazily supplies the request's access token (the presented JWT, or a session's, refreshed when needed) for remote sources. BearerMiddleware, RequestAuthenticator and the BFF's CurrentSession all go through the source, and the BFF's GET /bff/api/v1/users/me returns the result as memberships. Requests without claims (API keys) get no memberships from the default source. A BFF session's claims are those of the sign-in; a source that must be fresher uses RemoteMemberships.

docs.title: The claims model
docs.text:
SystemAuth's claims come from SessionProvider.GetUserClaims, which feeds both the ID token (OIDCSession puts them in Extra) and /oauth/userinfo (filtered by UserInfoClaims to the granted scopes). For a principal signed in through social login or a login token they are:

Claim When sub Always; the SystemAuth principal ID, which relying parties store as sf_principal_id managed: true The human has an active manager relationship (a managed principal), with or without an email; emitted whatever the scopes email, email_verified email scope, and only when the principal has an email (a managed principal may have one) name, picture profile scope orgs, orgs_truncated When the server has an OrgsSource (systemauth.WithOrgsSource(systemauth.NewEntOrgsSource(client, approleService))); emitted whatever the scopes, like managed

Without an OrgsSource no organization claim is emitted. Access tokens are JWTs (relyingparty.AccessTokenVerifier yields Subject, ClientID, Scopes and the raw claims).

docs.title: The orgs claim
docs.text:
orgs lists the organizations the principal belongs to through an active membership in an active organization, personal organization first and then newest membership first, at most MaxOrgsInToken (50); orgs_truncated is true when any were left out. Each entry has the organization id, the principal's organization role (owner, admin, member or collaborator) and apps, a map from application identifier to the principal's role there, from approle.EffectiveRoles: owners hold admin in every entitled application, everyone else holds what was assigned, and a collaborator's apps is empty. An application absent from apps is one the principal may not open.

Where Form Entry fields ID token, /oauth/userinfo Full id, slug, name, type (personal, team, enterprise), role, apps JWT access token Compact id, role, apps GET /oauth/userinfo/memberships?limit=&cursor= Full, every organization as above, in {"orgs": [...], "next_cursor": "..."}; limit defaults to 50 and is at most 100; cursor is the last organization ID of the previous page; needs a token granted openid

systemauth.OrgsClaim (Server.OrgsClaim(ctx, principalID, compact)) builds the claim. The token endpoint recomputes it on every grant, so a refresh carries current roles in the access token and in the refreshed ID token; a refresh token is not revoked by a role or membership change (ADR-010 decision 5). Subjects that are not principals (a client under client_credentials) get no claim. If the claim cannot be read, issuance fails with server_error rather than issuing a token without it.

docs.title: Token freshness and revocation
docs.text:
Setting Default Where Access token lifetime 10 minutes, at most 15 (accesschange.DefaultAccessTokenLifetime, MaxAccessTokenLifetime) systemauth config tokens.access_token_lifetime (a larger value is refused at load); per client access_token_lifetime and sf_oauth_apps.access_token_ttl (600 s), both lowered to the maximum Refresh token lifetime 7 days (absolute lifetime 30 days) tokens.refresh_token_lifetime, refresh_token_absolute_lifetime ID token lifetime 1 hour tokens.id_token_lifetime

Revocation by principal status: every introspection, userinfo call and refresh runs Server.requireActiveSubject, which asks PrincipalStatus.PrincipalActive(subject) (implemented by the Ent and memory stores); a deactivated principal's token family is revoked and the token reported inactive. A role or membership change does not revoke refresh tokens: the next refresh re-evaluates the orgs claim (ADR-010 decision 5). The relying-party SessionStore can delete BFF sessions by SystemAuth session ID or subject, which is the hook back-channel logout would use.

docs.title: Access-change records (identity/accesschange)
docs.text:
Access tokens are self-contained, so a change that reduces what an existing token may claim is recorded and announced (ADR-010). accesschange.Record writes a row of sf_access_changes (principal_id, organization_id or null for every organization, changed_at on the server clock, reason) in the transaction that makes the change, and accesschange.Publish hands it to the service's accesschange.Sink after commit. The principal and organization are plain identifiers rather than foreign keys, so a row outlives the deletion it describes. Each recording service takes a sink option (WithAccessChangeSink; systemauth.WithEntAccessChangeSink for EntStorage); the rows are written with or without one.

The reasons form an open registry, documented with what records each in the access-change reasons table of the authorization page. The column is a plain string, so a new reason needs no migration; accesschange.Record rejects any reason that is not registered.

accesschange.Since reads the rows after a timestamp for pollers and the replay endpoint, and accesschange.PruneExpired deletes rows older than accesschange.Retention (the maximum token lifetime, a minute of clock-skew margin and an hour of slack); no scheduled job calls it yet, so a deployment runs it from its own maintenance loop. The embedded in-memory EmbeddedAuthProvider keeps no database and records nothing.

docs.title: Relying-party revocation cache (relyingparty.RevocationCache)
docs.text:
relyingparty.RevocationCache consumes the records. accesschange.ToSink adapts it to a Sink, so in a modular monolith one instance is passed to every service's WithAccessChangeSink and read by every relying party; it is written after the recording transaction commits. It keeps the latest change per principal and per principal and organization, and accepts a token only if iat >= changed_at + margin (default 30 s, floor 15 s); entries expire at changed_at + max lifetime + margin, swept on Record. BearerMiddleware (BearerConfig.Revocation, with an optional Organization function) answers a refused token 401 invalid_token, error_description="token expired", and NewBFF (BFFConfig.Revocation) refreshes a session's tokens and claims instead of ending it. See Access changes.

Replicas that share the database poll it: relyingparty.NewAccessChangePoller(pgstore.NewAccessChangeSource(db), cache) (or accesschange.NewSource over Ent) reads the rows newer than its last read every 1 to 2 seconds, re-reading one margin behind the newest so late-committing rows are not missed. After a restart, relyingparty.Replay rebuilds the cache from GET /access-changes?since= (systemauth.WithAccessChanges; a token with the access_changes:read scope; paged by next_since) or from the database. A cache created with WithSuspectStart refuses tokens issued before it started listening until the replay or the first poll succeeds.

Across separate deployments SystemAuth delivers each change as an OpenID Connect Back-Channel Logout token. A client registers backchannel_logout_uri (column sf_oauth_apps.backchannel_logout_uri, migration migrations/0007_oauth_app_backchannel_logout_uri.sql); systemauth.Server.NewBackchannel() is an accesschange.Sink that queues the change after commit, signs one logout+jwt per client carrying the urn:systemforge:event:access_change event (plus the standard logout event for deactivation and session revocation), POSTs it, retries with backoff up to one access-token lifetime and logs failures against the client ID. relyingparty.BackchannelHandler verifies it and feeds the cache and the session store; the BFF serves it at <BasePath>/auth/backchannel-logout. See Back-channel events.

docs.title: Where the implementation differs from the decisions
docs.text:
Every item of the accepted decisions this page covers is implemented. These are the places where the code is narrower than, or words things differently from, the ADR text; the ADRs are append-only and are not rewritten.

  • Listings have no tier. ADR-006 speaks of listings with tiers. Tiers (plan_tier) live on subscriptions, a listing maps to an application, and a subscription may be per listing (see Entitlements via the marketplace).
  • The display name is required. name is NotEmpty on sf_organizations; it does not default to the slug.
  • Social login does not call SignupOrGetExisting. See Signup on first social login.
  • Application roles do not replace seat assignments. ADR-007 decision 8 says the sf_app_roles table replaces seat assignments as the record of who may use what. The marketplace seat assignments (LicenseService.AssignSeat, CheckPrincipal) remain a separate record, and a seat-licensed application counts its sf_app_roles rows against the license (see Application roles).
  • addMember takes no application roles. Roles are granted by an invite or afterwards through the application role endpoints. The administration pages for choosing them are the application's to build; this repository ships no UI.
  • Rename and conversion are service methods. Rename and ConvertToTeam have no HTTP endpoint.
  • Refresh tokens survive a role change. ADR-010 decision 5 amends ADR-007 decision 9: only deactivation and explicit session revocation revoke refresh tokens.

    if len(c.RegisteredClaims.Audience) > 0 {
        return c.RegisteredClaims.Audience[0]
    }
    return ""
}

// HasAudience checks if the claims include a specific audience.
func (c *Claims) HasAudience(aud string) bool {
    for _, a := range c.RegisteredClaims.Audience {
        if a == aud {
            return true
        }
    }
    return false
}

func (c *Claims) WithAudience(audiences ...string) *Claims {
    c.RegisteredClaims.Audience = audiences
    return c
}

docs.title: PRD: JWT Audience Validation
docs.text: Status: Draft Target: SystemForge v0.5.0

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Add audience (aud) claim validation to SystemForge's JWT service to enable path-bound token separation. This prevents credential replay attacks where tokens obtained for web browser access (BFF) are used for direct API access, and vice versa.

docs.title: Problem Statement
docs.text:
Currently, SystemForge JWT tokens can be used interchangeably across all endpoints. This creates security risks:

  1. Token Replay: User extracts JWT from browser DevTools, replays against raw API
  2. Bypassed Restrictions: UI-enforced limits (rate limits, feature gates) can be bypassed
  3. Audit Gap: No distinction between WebUI and programmatic access in logs
  4. Compliance Risk: Some regulations require explicit API access grants

docs.title: Goals
docs.text:
1. Token Isolation: BFF tokens only work on BFF paths, API tokens only on API paths
  2. Explicit API Grants: Users must explicitly create API tokens with scoped permissions
  3. Backward Compatibility: Existing tokens continue to work during migration
  4. Zero Friction for Web Users: No UX changes for normal web app usage

docs.title: Non-Goals
docs.text:
• Token encryption (handled separately by DPoP)
  • Per-endpoint scopes (handled by existing scope middleware)
  • Token revocation (handled by session/apikey stores)

docs.title: WebUI Users
docs.text:
US-1: As a web user, my session token cannot be used outside the web application context.

US-2: As a web user, I don't need to do anything different - authentication works seamlessly.

docs.title: API Developers
docs.text:
US-3: As a developer, I can create API tokens that work only on /api/v1/* endpoints.

US-4: As a developer, my API tokens are rejected if used on BFF endpoints.

US-5: As a developer, I get clear error messages when using the wrong token type.

docs.title: Platform Operators
docs.text:
US-6: As an operator, I can configure which audiences are accepted on which paths.

US-7: As an operator, I can audit token usage by audience type.

docs.title: Target Applications
docs.text: Application BFF Path API Path Migration Status App3 /bff/v1/* /api/v1/* New implementation App1 /bff/* /api/* Future migration Dashforge /bff/* /api/* Future migration

docs.title: Success Metrics
docs.text:
1. Security: 0 successful BFF-to-API token replay attacks
  2. Adoption: All 3 apps using audience validation within 6 months
  3. Developer Experience: <5% increase in auth-related support tickets

docs.text:

  • SystemForge session/bff package

// ValidateAccessTokenWithAudience validates and checks expected audience.
func (s *Service) ValidateAccessTokenWithAudience(
    tokenString string,
    expectedAudience string,
) (*Claims, error) {
    claims, err := s.ValidateAccessToken(tokenString)
    if err != nil {
        return nil, err
    }

    // Check audience if expected audience is specified
    if expectedAudience != "" && !claims.HasAudience(expectedAudience) {
        return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: expected %s, got %s",
            ErrAudienceMismatch, expectedAudience, claims.Audience())
    }

    return claims, nil
}

// GenerateAPIToken creates a scoped token for API clients.
// Duration overrides the default access token expiry.
func (s *Service) GenerateAPIToken(
    principalID uuid.UUID,
    email, name string,
    scopes []string,
    duration time.Duration,
) (string, error) {
    if len(scopes) == 0 {
        return "", errors.New("at least one scope is required for API tokens")
    }

    claims := NewAccessClaims(s.config, principalID, email, name).
        WithAudience(AudienceAPI)
    claims.Scopes = scopes

    // Override expiry if duration provided
    if duration > 0 {
        claims.ExpiresAt = jwt.NewNumericDate(time.Now().Add(duration))
    }

    return s.signToken(claims)
}

// GenerateTokenPairWithAudience creates a token pair with explicit audience.
func (s *Service) GenerateTokenPairWithAudience(
    principalID uuid.UUID,
    email, name string,
    audience string,
    scopes []string,
) (*TokenPair, error) {
    accessToken, err := s.GenerateAccessTokenWithAudience(
        principalID, email, name, audience, scopes,
    )
    if err != nil {
        return nil, fmt.Errorf("generating access token: %w", err)
    }

    family := uuid.NewString()
    refreshToken, err := s.GenerateRefreshToken(principalID, family)
    if err != nil {
        return nil, fmt.Errorf("generating refresh token: %w", err)
    }

    return &TokenPair{
        AccessToken:  accessToken,
        RefreshToken: refreshToken,
        ExpiresIn:    int64(s.config.AccessTokenExpiry.Seconds()),
    }, nil
}

Acceptance Criteria: - [ ] Both tokens generated successfully - [ ] Access token has audience - [ ] Refresh token does not have audience (stateless)

// identity/ent/mixin/bff_session.go

package mixin

import (
    "time"
    "entgo.io/ent"
    "entgo.io/ent/schema/field"
    "entgo.io/ent/schema/index"
    "entgo.io/ent/schema/mixin"
)

// BFFSession provides common fields for BFF session entities.
type BFFSession struct {
    mixin.Schema
}

// Fields of the BFFSession mixin.
func (BFFSession) Fields() []ent.Field {
    return []ent.Field{
        field.String("id").
            NotEmpty().
            Unique().
            Immutable().
            Comment("Unique session identifier"),

        field.UUID("user_id", uuid.UUID{}).
            Comment("Owner of this session"),

        field.UUID("organization_id", uuid.UUID{}).
            Optional().
            Nillable().
            Comment("Organization context (optional)"),

        field.Bytes("access_token_encrypted").
            Sensitive().
            Comment("Encrypted access token"),

        field.Bytes("refresh_token_encrypted").
            Sensitive().
            Comment("Encrypted refresh token"),

        field.Time("access_token_expires_at").
            Comment("When the access token expires"),

        field.Time("refresh_token_expires_at").
            Comment("When the refresh token expires"),

        field.Bytes("dpop_key_pair_encrypted").
            Optional().
            Sensitive().
            Comment("Encrypted DPoP key pair (if DPoP enabled)"),

        field.String("dpop_thumbprint").
            Optional().
            MaxLen(64).
            Comment("DPoP JWK thumbprint"),

        field.String("ip_address").
            Optional().
            MaxLen(45).
            Comment("Client IP address"),

        field.String("user_agent").
            Optional().
            MaxLen(500).
            Comment("Client User-Agent"),

        field.JSON("metadata", map[string]string{}).
            Optional().
            Comment("Additional session metadata"),

        field.Time("last_accessed_at").
            Default(time.Now).
            Comment("When the session was last accessed"),

        field.Time("expires_at").
            Comment("When the session expires completely"),

        field.Time("created_at").
            Default(time.Now).
            Immutable(),

        field.Time("updated_at").
            Default(time.Now).
            UpdateDefault(time.Now),
    }
}

// Indexes of the BFFSession mixin.
func (BFFSession) Indexes() []ent.Index {
    return []ent.Index{
        index.Fields("user_id"),
        index.Fields("expires_at"),
        index.Fields("organization_id"),
    }
}

// identity/ent/mixin/api_key.go

package mixin

import (
    "time"
    "entgo.io/ent"
    "entgo.io/ent/schema/field"
    "entgo.io/ent/schema/index"
    "entgo.io/ent/schema/mixin"

// APIKey provides common fields for API key entities.
type APIKey struct {
    mixin.Schema
}

// Fields of the APIKey mixin.
func (APIKey) Fields() []ent.Field {
    return []ent.Field{
        field.UUID("id", uuid.UUID{}).
            Default(uuid.New).
            Immutable(),

        field.String("name").
            NotEmpty().
            MaxLen(100).
            Comment("User-provided name for identification"),

        field.String("prefix").
            NotEmpty().
            MaxLen(20).
            Comment("Visible prefix for identification (e.g., cf_live_xxxx)"),

        field.String("key_hash").
            NotEmpty().
            MaxLen(64).
            Sensitive().
            Comment("SHA-256 hash of the full key"),

        field.UUID("owner_id", uuid.UUID{}).
            Comment("User who owns this key"),

        field.UUID("organization_id", uuid.UUID{}).
            Optional().
            Nillable().
            Comment("Organization scope (optional)"),

        field.Strings("scopes").
            Default([]string{}).
            Comment("Granted permission scopes"),

        field.String("description").
            Optional().
            MaxLen(500).
            Comment("User-provided description"),

        field.Enum("environment").
            Values("live", "test").
            Default("live").
            Comment("Key environment"),

        field.Time("expires_at").
            Optional().
            Nillable().
            Comment("When the key expires (NULL = never)"),

        field.Time("last_used_at").
            Optional().
            Nillable().
            Comment("When the key was last used"),

        field.String("last_used_ip").
            Optional().
            MaxLen(45).
            Comment("IP that last used the key"),

        field.Bool("revoked").
            Default(false).
            Comment("Whether the key is revoked"),

        field.Time("revoked_at").
            Optional().
            Nillable().
            Comment("When the key was revoked"),

        field.String("revoked_reason").
            Optional().
            MaxLen(500).
            Comment("Why the key was revoked"),

        field.JSON("metadata", map[string]string{}).
            Optional().
            Comment("Additional key metadata"),

        field.Time("created_at").
            Default(time.Now).
            Immutable(),

        field.Time("updated_at").
            Default(time.Now).
            UpdateDefault(time.Now),
    }
}

// Indexes of the APIKey mixin.
func (APIKey) Indexes() []ent.Index {
    return []ent.Index{
        index.Fields("owner_id"),
        index.Fields("organization_id"),
        index.Fields("prefix"),
        index.Fields("key_hash").Unique(),
        index.Fields("environment"),
    }
}

docs.title: PRD: Ent Store Implementations
docs.text: Status: Draft Target: SystemForge v0.5.0

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Provide reference Ent (database) implementations for SystemForge's BFF session store and API key store interfaces. This enables apps to use PostgreSQL-backed storage with minimal boilerplate.

docs.title: Problem Statement
docs.text:
Currently, SystemForge provides: - session/bff.Store interface with only MemoryStore implementation - identity/apikey.Store interface with no implementations

Apps must write their own database implementations, leading to: 1. Duplicated Effort: Each app implements the same patterns 2. Inconsistent Quality: Varying levels of security and error handling 3. Slower Adoption: Barrier to entry for new apps 4. Maintenance Burden: Bugs fixed in one app aren't shared

docs.title: Goals
docs.text:
1. Reference Implementations: Production-ready Ent stores
  2. Ent Schema Mixins: Reusable schema definitions
  3. App Flexibility: Apps can customize or use as-is
  4. Security by Default: Proper encryption, indexing, cleanup

docs.title: Non-Goals
docs.text:
• Redis store implementations (future iteration)
  • Non-Ent ORMs (gorm, sqlx, etc.)
  • Automatic schema migration (apps manage their own)

docs.title: App Developers
docs.text:
US-1: As a developer, I can add BFF sessions to my app with 3 lines of code.

US-2: As a developer, I can add API keys to my app without writing storage code.

US-3: As a developer, I can customize the schema if my app needs additional fields.

US-4: As a developer, I can use SystemForge mixins and generate Ent code.

docs.title: Platform Operators
docs.text:
US-5: As an operator, sessions are automatically cleaned up when expired.

US-6: As an operator, API keys are stored with hashed values (not plaintext).

US-7: As an operator, I can query sessions/keys by user for account management.

docs.title: Task 2.1: Create Encryptor Struct
docs.text:
Priority: P0 Estimate: 2 hours Files: - session/bff/encryption.go - session/bff/encryption_test.go

Implementation: 

package bff

import (
    "crypto/aes"
    "crypto/cipher"
    "crypto/rand"
    "errors"
    "io"
)

var (
    ErrInvalidKeySize    = errors.New("encryption key must be 32 bytes for AES-256")
    ErrCiphertextTooShort = errors.New("ciphertext too short")
)

// Encryptor provides AES-256-GCM encryption for tokens at rest.
type Encryptor struct {
    gcm cipher.AEAD
}

// NewEncryptor creates a new encryptor with the given 32-byte key.
func NewEncryptor(key []byte) (*Encryptor, error) {
    if len(key) != 32 {
        return nil, ErrInvalidKeySize
    }

    block, err := aes.NewCipher(key)
    if err != nil {
        return nil, err
    }

    gcm, err := cipher.NewGCM(block)
    if err != nil {
        return nil, err
    }

    return &Encryptor{gcm: gcm}, nil
}

// Encrypt encrypts plaintext using AES-256-GCM.
func (e *Encryptor) Encrypt(plaintext []byte) ([]byte, error) {
    nonce := make([]byte, e.gcm.NonceSize())
    if _, err := io.ReadFull(rand.Reader, nonce); err != nil {
        return nil, err
    }

    return e.gcm.Seal(nonce, nonce, plaintext, nil), nil
}

// Decrypt decrypts ciphertext using AES-256-GCM.
func (e *Encryptor) Decrypt(ciphertext []byte) ([]byte, error) {
    if len(ciphertext) < e.gcm.NonceSize() {
        return nil, ErrCiphertextTooShort
    }

    nonce, ciphertext := ciphertext[:e.gcm.NonceSize()], ciphertext[e.gcm.NonceSize():]
    return e.gcm.Open(nil, nonce, ciphertext, nil)
}

Acceptance Criteria: - [ ] Encrypt/Decrypt round-trip succeeds - [ ] Invalid key size returns error - [ ] Corrupted ciphertext returns error - [ ] Different encryptions of same plaintext produce different ciphertext (nonce) - [ ] 100% test coverage

docs.title: Task 3.2: Implement EntStore
docs.text:
Priority: P0 Estimate: 4 hours Files: - session/bff/store_ent.go

Implementation: 

// EntStoreConfig configures the Ent-backed session store.
type EntStoreConfig struct {
    Client           EntClientInterface
    EncryptionKey    []byte
    CleanupInterval  time.Duration
    CleanupBatchSize int
}

// EntStore implements Store using Ent.
type EntStore struct {
    config    EntStoreConfig
    encryptor *Encryptor
    cleanup   *time.Ticker
    done      chan struct{}
}

// NewEntStore creates a new Ent-backed session store.
func NewEntStore(config EntStoreConfig) (*EntStore, error) {
    if config.Client == nil {
        return nil, errors.New("client is required")
    }
    if len(config.EncryptionKey) != 32 {
        return nil, ErrInvalidKeySize
    }

    encryptor, err := NewEncryptor(config.EncryptionKey)
    if err != nil {
        return nil, fmt.Errorf("creating encryptor: %w", err)
    }

    store := &EntStore{
        config:    config,
        encryptor: encryptor,
        done:      make(chan struct{}),
    }

    if config.CleanupInterval > 0 {
        store.startCleanup()
    }

    return store, nil
}

// Close stops the cleanup goroutine.
func (s *EntStore) Close() error {
    if s.cleanup != nil {
        s.cleanup.Stop()
        close(s.done)
    }
    return nil
}

Acceptance Criteria: - [ ] All Store interface methods implemented - [ ] Tokens encrypted before storage - [ ] Tokens decrypted after retrieval - [ ] Automatic cleanup goroutine starts if configured - [ ] Close() stops cleanup gracefully
