docs.title: ADR-1: Direct Client vs omniobserve Extension
docs.text:
Context: Should ProductGraph be a new omniobserve provider or a separate client?

Decision: Separate client (productgraph package).

Rationale:

  • ProductGraph is event-focused, not trace/metric focused
  • Different batching semantics (events vs spans)
  • Simpler to maintain independently
  • Can still integrate with observability provider via composition

docs.title: ADR-2: Sync vs Async Tracking
docs.text:
Context: Should Track() be synchronous or asynchronous?

Decision: Asynchronous with batching.

Rationale:

  • Minimal latency impact on request path
  • Better throughput with batching
  • Graceful degradation on network issues
  • Trade-off: Potential event loss on crash (acceptable)

docs.text: Author: PlexusOne Date: 2026-04-27 Status: Draft

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This document defines the product requirements for integrating systemforge's observability package with ProductGraph for backend telemetry correlation and analytics forwarding.

docs.title: Problem Statement
docs.text:
Backend services need to:

  1. Correlate with frontend events - Link backend spans to frontend sessions
  2. Forward events to analytics - Send backend events to Amplitude/Mixpanel
  3. Track business metrics - Auth, API usage, journeys from backend perspective
  4. Unified observability - Single destination for all telemetry

docs.title: Primary Goals
docs.text:
1. Frontend-backend correlation via session ID propagation
  2. Backend event forwarding to ProductGraph
  3. Analytics integration via omnidxi (Amplitude, Mixpanel)
  4. Journey tracking from backend (API-driven flows)

docs.title: Secondary Goals
docs.text:
1. Unified metrics dashboard in ProductGraph
  2. Error correlation between frontend and backend
  3. Performance analysis end-to-end

docs.title: US-1: Session Correlation
docs.text:
As a DevOps engineer, I want to correlate backend requests with frontend sessions so that I can debug user-reported issues end-to-end.

Acceptance Criteria:

  • Extract X-Session-ID from request headers
  • Attach session ID to OpenTelemetry spans
  • Events appear in ProductGraph linked to session

docs.title: US-2: Backend Analytics
docs.text:
As a product manager, I want backend events forwarded to Amplitude so that I can analyze API usage patterns.

Acceptance Criteria:

  • Backend events (auth, API calls) forward to ProductGraph
  • ProductGraph forwards to Amplitude/Mixpanel via omnidxi
  • Events include user ID when available

docs.title: US-3: Journey Completion
docs.text:
As a developer, I want to track journey completions from the backend so that I can measure server-confirmed conversions.

Acceptance Criteria:

  • Backend can emit journey.step events
  • Journey includes step ID and name
  • Correlates with frontend journey tracking

docs.title: US-4: Error Aggregation
docs.text:
As a SRE, I want frontend and backend errors unified in ProductGraph so that I can triage issues efficiently.

Acceptance Criteria:

  • Backend errors include session ID
  • Error events follow OTel semantic conventions
  • Errors appear alongside frontend errors in dashboard

docs.text: ID Requirement Priority FR-1 Extract session ID from X-Session-ID header P0 FR-2 Attach session ID to OpenTelemetry spans P0 FR-3 HTTP client for POST /v1/events P1 FR-4 Event batching (configurable size/interval) P1 FR-5 OTel semantic convention compliance P0 FR-6 Journey step emission from backend P2 FR-7 Error event emission with context P1 FR-8 Middleware for automatic request tracking P1

docs.text: ID Requirement Target NFR-1 Event dispatch latency < 10ms async NFR-2 Memory footprint < 10 MB NFR-3 Retry on failure 3 attempts NFR-4 No data loss on shutdown Graceful flush

docs.title: Option A: Direct ProductGraph Client
docs.text:
Send events directly to ProductGraph from Go backend.

systemforge → ProductGraph → omnidxi → Amplitude/Mixpanel

Pros: Simple, direct control Cons: Duplicate logic, another client to maintain

docs.title: Option B: Via omniobserve Extension
docs.text:
Extend omniobserve to forward to ProductGraph.

systemforge → omniobserve → ProductGraph → omnidxi → Amplitude/Mixpanel

Pros: Unified observability, existing patterns Cons: More complex, couples packages

docs.title: Option C: Via omnidxi Directly
docs.text:
Use omnidxi directly from systemforge, bypassing ProductGraph.

systemforge → omnidxi → Amplitude/Mixpanel

Pros: Simpler, fewer hops Cons: Loses ProductGraph aggregation and dashboard

docs.title: Recommendation
docs.text: Option A for Phase 1: Direct ProductGraph client with session correlation. This keeps the architecture simple and allows ProductGraph to be the single source of truth.

docs.text: Metric Target Measurement Session correlation rate > 95% Correlated events / total Event delivery rate > 99.9% Delivered / sent Latency impact < 5ms p99 Added overhead

  • Custom ProductGraph dashboard
  • Mobile backend correlation
  • Distributed tracing via ProductGraph (use OTel)

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This document describes the technical architecture for integrating systemforge's observability with ProductGraph for backend-frontend correlation and analytics forwarding.

docs.title: Correlation Middleware
docs.text:
Package: systemforge/observability/correlation

Purpose: Extract frontend correlation IDs and inject into context.

package correlation

import (
    "context"
    "net/http"
)

type ContextKey string

const (
    SessionIDKey  ContextKey = "session_id"
    RequestIDKey  ContextKey = "request_id"
    UserIDKey     ContextKey = "user_id"
)

// Middleware extracts correlation headers and injects into context.
func Middleware(next http.Handler) http.Handler {
    return http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
        ctx := r.Context()

        // Extract correlation headers
        if sessionID := r.Header.Get("X-Session-ID"); sessionID != "" {
            ctx = context.WithValue(ctx, SessionIDKey, sessionID)
        }
        if requestID := r.Header.Get("X-Request-ID"); requestID != "" {
            ctx = context.WithValue(ctx, RequestIDKey, requestID)
        }

        // Echo back for debugging
        if requestID := r.Header.Get("X-Request-ID"); requestID != "" {
            w.Header().Set("X-Request-ID", requestID)
        }

        next.ServeHTTP(w, r.WithContext(ctx))
    })
}

// SessionIDFromContext extracts session ID from context.
func SessionIDFromContext(ctx context.Context) string {
    if v, ok := ctx.Value(SessionIDKey).(string); ok {
        return v
    }
    return ""
}

// RequestIDFromContext extracts request ID from context.
func RequestIDFromContext(ctx context.Context) string {
    if v, ok := ctx.Value(RequestIDKey).(string); ok {
        return v
    }
    return ""
}

docs.title: ProductGraph Client
docs.text:
Package: systemforge/productgraph

Purpose: Send events to ProductGraph from Go backend.

package productgraph

import (
    "bytes"
    "context"
    "encoding/json"
    "fmt"
    "net/http"
    "sync"
    "time"

    "github.com/google/uuid"
)

// Config configures the ProductGraph client.
type Config struct {
    ProjectID     string        // Required: project identifier
    Endpoint      string        // Required: ProductGraph endpoint
    APIKey        string        // Optional: X-PG-API-Key header
    BatchSize     int           // Default: 50
    BatchInterval time.Duration // Default: 5s
    HTTPClient    *http.Client  // Default: http.DefaultClient
}

// Client sends events to ProductGraph.
type Client struct {
    config  Config
    buffer  []Event
    mu      sync.Mutex
    done    chan struct{}
    wg      sync.WaitGroup
}

// Event represents a ProductGraph event.
type Event struct {
    EventID     string                 `json:"event_id"`
    ProjectID   string                 `json:"project_id"`
    SessionID   string                 `json:"session.id"`
    UserID      string                 `json:"user.id,omitempty"`
    EventType   string                 `json:"event.type"`
    EventName   string                 `json:"event.name,omitempty"`
    Timestamp   string                 `json:"event.timestamp"`
    PagePath    string                 `json:"page.path,omitempty"`
    APIMethod   string                 `json:"api.method,omitempty"`
    APIPath     string                 `json:"api.path,omitempty"`
    APIStatus   int                    `json:"api.status_code,omitempty"`
    APIDuration int                    `json:"api.duration_ms,omitempty"`
    ErrorType   string                 `json:"error.type,omitempty"`
    ErrorMsg    string                 `json:"error.message,omitempty"`
    JourneyID   string                 `json:"gen_ai.journey.id,omitempty"`
    JourneyStep string                 `json:"gen_ai.journey.step.id,omitempty"`
    JourneyName string                 `json:"gen_ai.journey.step.name,omitempty"`
    Metadata    map[string]interface{} `json:"metadata,omitempty"`
}

// New creates a ProductGraph client.
func New(cfg Config) *Client {
    if cfg.BatchSize == 0 {
        cfg.BatchSize = 50
    }
    if cfg.BatchInterval == 0 {
        cfg.BatchInterval = 5 * time.Second
    }
    if cfg.HTTPClient == nil {
        cfg.HTTPClient = &http.Client{Timeout: 10 * time.Second}
    }

    c := &Client{
        config: cfg,
        buffer: make([]Event, 0, cfg.BatchSize),
        done:   make(chan struct{}),
    }

    c.wg.Add(1)
    go c.flusher()

    return c
}

// Track sends an event to ProductGraph.
func (c *Client) Track(ctx context.Context, event Event) {
    // Fill defaults
    if event.EventID == "" {
        event.EventID = uuid.New().String()
    }
    if event.ProjectID == "" {
        event.ProjectID = c.config.ProjectID
    }
    if event.Timestamp == "" {
        event.Timestamp = time.Now().UTC().Format(time.RFC3339)
    }

    // Extract session from context if not set
    if event.SessionID == "" {
        if sessionID, ok := ctx.Value("session_id").(string); ok {
            event.SessionID = sessionID
        }
    }

    c.mu.Lock()
    c.buffer = append(c.buffer, event)
    shouldFlush := len(c.buffer) >= c.config.BatchSize
    c.mu.Unlock()

    if shouldFlush {
        c.flush()
    }
}

// TrackAPICall tracks an API request/response.
func (c *Client) TrackAPICall(ctx context.Context, method, path string, status int, duration time.Duration) {
    c.Track(ctx, Event{
        EventType:   "api.response",
        APIMethod:   method,
        APIPath:     path,
        APIStatus:   status,
        APIDuration: int(duration.Milliseconds()),
    })
}

// TrackError tracks an error event.
func (c *Client) TrackError(ctx context.Context, errType, message string) {
    c.Track(ctx, Event{
        EventType: "error",
        ErrorType: errType,
        ErrorMsg:  message,
    })
}

// TrackJourneyStep tracks a journey step completion.
func (c *Client) TrackJourneyStep(ctx context.Context, journeyID, stepID, stepName string) {
    c.Track(ctx, Event{
        EventType:   "journey.step",
        JourneyID:   journeyID,
        JourneyStep: stepID,
        JourneyName: stepName,
    })
}

func (c *Client) flusher() {
    defer c.wg.Done()
    ticker := time.NewTicker(c.config.BatchInterval)
    defer ticker.Stop()

    for {
        select {
        case <-ticker.C:
            c.flush()
        case <-c.done:
            c.flush() // Final flush
            return
        }
    }
}

func (c *Client) flush() {
    c.mu.Lock()
    if len(c.buffer) == 0 {
        c.mu.Unlock()
        return
    }
    events := c.buffer
    c.buffer = make([]Event, 0, c.config.BatchSize)
    c.mu.Unlock()

    body, _ := json.Marshal(map[string]interface{}{
        "events": events,
    })

    req, _ := http.NewRequest("POST", c.config.Endpoint, bytes.NewReader(body))
    req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
    if c.config.APIKey != "" {
        req.Header.Set("X-PG-API-Key", c.config.APIKey)
    }

    resp, err := c.config.HTTPClient.Do(req)
    if err != nil {
        // Log error, consider retry
        return
    }
    defer resp.Body.Close()
}

// Close gracefully shuts down the client.
func (c *Client) Close() error {
    close(c.done)
    c.wg.Wait()
    return nil
}

docs.title: Request Tracking Middleware
docs.text:
Package: systemforge/observability

Automatically track API requests.

// RequestTracker middleware tracks requests to ProductGraph.
func (p *Provider) RequestTracker(next http.Handler) http.Handler {
    return http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
        start := time.Now()

        // Wrap response writer to capture status
        ww := &responseWriter{ResponseWriter: w, status: 200}

        next.ServeHTTP(ww, r)

        duration := time.Since(start)

        // Track to ProductGraph
        if p.productgraph != nil {
            p.productgraph.TrackAPICall(
                r.Context(),
                r.Method,
                r.URL.Path,
                ww.status,
                duration,
            )
        }
    })
}

type responseWriter struct {
    http.ResponseWriter
    status int
}

func (w *responseWriter) WriteHeader(status int) {
    w.status = status
    w.ResponseWriter.WriteHeader(status)
}

docs.title: Usage Example
docs.text:
package main

import (
    "net/http"

    "github.com/go-chi/chi/v5"
    "github.com/plexusone/systemforge/observability"
    "github.com/plexusone/systemforge/observability/correlation"
    "github.com/plexusone/systemforge/productgraph"
)

func main() {
    // Create ProductGraph client
    pgClient := productgraph.New(productgraph.Config{
        ProjectID: "proj_demo",
        Endpoint:  "https://api.productgraph.io/v1/events",
        APIKey:    os.Getenv("PRODUCTGRAPH_API_KEY"),
    })
    defer pgClient.Close()

    // Create observability provider with ProductGraph
    provider := observability.New(
        observability.ConfigFromEnv(),
        observability.WithProductGraph(pgClient),
    )
    defer provider.Shutdown()

    // Setup router
    r := chi.NewRouter()

    // Middleware chain
    r.Use(correlation.Middleware)        // Extract session/request IDs
    r.Use(provider.TracingMiddleware)    // OpenTelemetry tracing
    r.Use(provider.RequestTracker)       // ProductGraph tracking

    r.Post("/api/checkout", func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
        ctx := r.Context()

        // Business logic...

        // Track journey step from backend
        pgClient.TrackJourneyStep(ctx, "checkout_flow", "payment_confirmed", "Payment Confirmed")

        w.WriteHeader(http.StatusOK)
    })

    http.ListenAndServe(":8080", r)
}

func TestProductGraphClient(t *testing.T) {
    server := httptest.NewServer(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
        assert.Equal(t, "POST", r.Method)
        assert.Equal(t, "application/json", r.Header.Get("Content-Type"))

        var payload map[string]interface{}
        json.NewDecoder(r.Body).Decode(&payload)
        events := payload["events"].([]interface{})
        assert.Len(t, events, 1)

        w.WriteHeader(http.StatusAccepted)
    }))
    defer server.Close()

    client := productgraph.New(productgraph.Config{
        ProjectID:     "test",
        Endpoint:      server.URL,
        BatchSize:     1, // Immediate flush
    })
    defer client.Close()

    ctx := context.WithValue(context.Background(), correlation.SessionIDKey, "sess_test")
    client.Track(ctx, productgraph.Event{
        EventType: "test",
    })

    time.Sleep(100 * time.Millisecond) // Wait for flush
}

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text: This guide walks you through building a simple API with SystemForge authentication.

docs.title: Step 1: Create the Application
docs.text:
// main.go
package main

import (
    "context"
    "log"
    "net/http"

    "github.com/plexusone/systemforge/identity/ent"
    "github.com/plexusone/systemforge/identity/oauth"
    _ "github.com/lib/pq"
)

func main() {
    // Connect to PostgreSQL
    client, err := ent.Open("postgres",
        "host=localhost port=5432 user=myapp dbname=myapp password=secret sslmode=disable")
    if err != nil {
        log.Fatalf("failed to connect: %v", err)
    }
    defer client.Close()

    // Run migrations
    if err := client.Schema.Create(context.Background()); err != nil {
        log.Fatalf("failed to create schema: %v", err)
    }

    // Create OAuth provider
    cfg := oauth.DefaultConfig(
        "http://localhost:8080",           // Issuer URL
        []byte("your-32-byte-secret-key"), // HMAC secret
    )
    provider, err := oauth.NewProvider(client, cfg)
    if err != nil {
        log.Fatalf("failed to create provider: %v", err)
    }

    // Create OAuth API (endpoints auto-registered)
    oauthAPI, err := oauth.NewAPI(provider)
    if err != nil {
        log.Fatalf("failed to create oauth api: %v", err)
    }

    // Mount OAuth router (includes all OAuth and discovery endpoints)
    http.Handle("/", oauthAPI.Router())

    // Protected API endpoint
    http.Handle("GET /api/me", oauthAPI.Middleware(http.HandlerFunc(meHandler)))

    log.Println("Server starting on :8080")
    log.Fatal(http.ListenAndServe(":8080", nil))
}

func meHandler(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    userID := oauth.UserIDFromContext(r.Context())
    w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
    w.Write([]byte(`{"user_id":"` + userID + `"}`))
}

// Create a first-party OAuth app (your own frontend)
app, err := client.OAuthApp.Create().
    SetClientID("my-frontend-app").
    SetName("My Frontend App").
    SetAppType("spa").
    SetPublic(true).
    SetFirstParty(true).
    SetRedirectUris([]string{"http://localhost:3000/callback"}).
    SetAllowedScopes([]string{"openid", "profile", "email"}).
    SetAllowedGrants([]string{"authorization_code", "refresh_token"}).
    SetOwnerID(adminUserID).
    Save(context.Background())

docs.title: Step 4: Add User Registration
docs.text:
A person is a human principal; the password is a credential that belongs to it.

import (
    "github.com/plexusone/systemforge/identity/credential"
    "github.com/plexusone/systemforge/identity/principal"
)

person, err := principal.NewService(client).CreateHuman(ctx, principal.CreateHumanInput{
    Email:       "user@example.com",
    DisplayName: "John Doe",
})
if err != nil {
    return err
}

err = credential.NewService(client).CreatePassword(ctx, credential.CreatePasswordInput{
    PrincipalID: person.ID,
    Password:    "secure-password",
})
if err != nil {
    return err
}

CreatePassword hashes the password with Argon2id before storing it.

docs.title: Access-change invalidation
docs.text: Access tokens are self-contained JWTs, so removing a person from an organization or lowering a role does not reach a token already issued. SystemForge bounds that window two ways: short token lifetimes, and a record of every access-reducing change that relying parties consult. The design is in Organizations and Membership; the relying-party API is in Relying Parties.

docs.title: Token lifetime
docs.text:
Setting Default Limit tokens.access_token_lifetime 10 minutes 15 minutes; a larger value fails configuration loading with ErrInvalidConfig Per client access_token_lifetime (and sf_oauth_apps.access_token_ttl) The server value Capped at 15 minutes tokens.refresh_token_lifetime 7 days (absolute 30 days)

A membership or role change does not revoke refresh tokens: the next refresh re-evaluates the orgs claim and issues reduced claims. Only deactivation and explicit session revocation revoke refresh tokens.

docs.title: What is recorded
docs.text: sf_access_changes receives a row, in the transaction that makes the change, for: membership_removed, org_role_changed, app_role_changed, deactivated, sessions_revoked, management_granted, management_ended and grant_reduced. Adding access records nothing. Pass a sink to each service with WithAccessChangeSink; rows are written with or without one. accesschange.PruneExpired deletes rows past accesschange.Retention; call it from your own maintenance loop.

docs.title: Relying-party revocation cache
docs.text:
A token is accepted only if its iat is at or after the recorded change plus a clock-skew margin (30 seconds by default, never below 15).

cache := relyingparty.NewRevocationCache()
mw := relyingparty.BearerMiddleware(relyingparty.BearerConfig{
    Tokens: client, Principals: principals, Revocation: cache,
})
Deployment Feed the cache with Modular monolith, one process accesschange.ToSink(cache) passed to every service's WithAccessChangeSink Replicas sharing the database relyingparty.NewAccessChangePoller(source, cache).Run(ctx), polling every 1 to 2 seconds, with WithSuspectStart() on the cache Another process relyingparty.ReplayWithRetry against GET /access-changes?since=, plus back-channel delivery Separate deployments Back-channel events (below)

After a restart a cache created with WithSuspectStart refuses tokens issued before it started until the first replay or poll succeeds, so a restart never widens the window.

docs.title: Replay endpoint
docs.text:
Enable GET /access-changes?since=<RFC 3339>[&limit=] with systemauth.WithAccessChanges(accesschange.NewSource(db)). The caller needs a client-credentials token with the access_changes:read scope. The response is {"changes": [...], "next_since": ...}.

Status Cause 401 Missing or invalid token 403 The token lacks access_changes:read 400 since is not RFC 3339, or limit is not a positive integer 501 Access changes are not configured

docs.title: Back-channel delivery
docs.text:
Register the client's endpoint (an https URL, or http for a loopback host) as backchannel_logout_uri (ClientConfig.BackchannelLogoutURI, column sf_oauth_apps.backchannel_logout_uri, migration 0007_oauth_app_backchannel_logout_uri.sql) and run SystemAuth's sender:

bc := auth.NewBackchannel()
orgs := organization.NewService(db, organization.WithAccessChangeSink(bc))
go bc.Run(ctx)

SystemAuth POSTs an OpenID Connect Back-Channel Logout token carrying the urn:systemforge:event:access_change event to every registered client, retrying with backoff for up to one maximum token lifetime and never following redirects; a 4xx other than 408 and 429 is not retried. The receiver is relyingparty.BackchannelHandler(cache, client, ...); the BFF serves it at <BasePath>/auth/backchannel-logout.

docs.title: What a client sees
docs.text:
Situation Response Token issued before a recorded change 401 with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer error="invalid_token", error_description="token expired"; refresh and retry BFF session after a change The session refreshes its tokens and claims and stays signed in with reduced claims Refresh refused (deactivation, revoked sessions) The session ends Back-channel token invalid (signature, issuer, audience, typ, jti replay) The receiver refuses it; a failure to end sessions answers 500 so SystemAuth retries

Applications that bypass relyingparty must implement the same check.

docs.title: Application roles and entitlements
docs.text: An application role is a principal's role inside one application of an organization, stored in sf_app_roles per (principal, organization, application). An organization may hold roles only in the applications it is entitled to, which the marketplace decides. The design is in Organizations and Membership.

docs.title: Wiring
docs.text:
registry := authz.NewVocabularyRegistry()
_ = registry.Register(myAppVocabulary{}) // handle the error

src := marketplace.EntitlementSource(subscriptions, licenses, listings,
    marketplace.WithDefaultEntitlements("myapp")) // free to everyone, if any
roles := approle.NewService(db, registry,
    append(marketplace.ApproleOptions(src), approle.WithAuthzSyncer(res.Syncer, authz.SyncModeEventual))...)

cfg := organization.DefaultAPIConfig()
cfg.AppRoles = roles
cfg.Entitlements = src

Entitlement checks fail closed: with no entitlement option, no organization is entitled to anything and every assignment is refused. approle.EntitleAll exists for development and tests only. marketplace.WarnIfNoEntitlements logs a warning at startup when applications are registered but nothing entitles anyone.

docs.title: Where entitlements come from
docs.text:
An organization is entitled to an application through:

  • an active (active or trialing) subscription to a listing that names the application, or a currently valid license for such a listing;
  • the deployment's default entitlements.

A listing's application is settable only through the service, not the listing HTTP API, so a listing creator cannot entitle buyers to an application they do not control. Each OrgResponse carries the resulting entitlements list.

A seat-licensed application has a seat limit, the sum of the seats of its valid seat-based licenses; there is none when any entitlement is not seat-limited. Roles are counted against it under an advisory lock, and owners' implicit roles hold no seat.

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
• Roles come from the application's vocabulary (AppVocabulary.Roles()); there are no custom roles.
  • Only an active owner, admin or member may hold a role. Collaborators, non-members and deactivated members may not.
  • Owners hold the top role of every entitled application implicitly. Nobody else holds any by default, admins included.
  • Removing a member removes their roles and grants in the same transaction.

docs.title: Endpoints
docs.text:
Route Needs GET /organizations/{slug}/app-roles[?application=] change_role GET /organizations/{slug}/members/{principal_id}/app-roles change_role, or view for your own; returns stored and effective roles PUT /organizations/{slug}/members/{principal_id}/app-roles/{application} change_role; body {"role": "..."}; assigns or changes DELETE /organizations/{slug}/members/{principal_id}/app-roles/{application} change_role

Roles also travel on invites, and reach clients in the orgs claim (apps, a map of application to role).

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
Status Cause 400 approle: unknown application; approle: role not declared by the application; approle: organization is not entitled to the application; approle: principal is not an active owner, admin or member 403 The caller lacks change_role, or reads another member's roles without it 404 approle: role not assigned on DELETE; unknown organization or member 409 approle: role already assigned (service Assign); approle: no seats available for the application 501 APIConfig.AppRoles is not set

PUT assigns when there is no role and changes it otherwise, so it does not return already assigned.

Reducing or removing a role records an access change, so tokens issued before it are refused by relying parties that run a revocation cache; see Access-change invalidation.

docs.title: Configuring the authorization mode
docs.text: The authz key of the SystemAuth configuration selects how authorization is evaluated. Both modes implement the same contract (organization roles, application roles, resource grants, ListResources), so switching is a configuration change. The design is in Authorization.

docs.title: Modes
docs.text:
authz.mode Evaluates Needs rbac (default) Roles and direct grants in process, from the membership, role and grant tables Nothing else rebac Permissions derived through relationships by an engine A relationship engine; spicedb is the only one 
authz:
  mode: rebac
  engine: spicedb        # default; rebac only
  spicedb:
    mode: remote         # embedded (default) | remote
    endpoint: spicedb.internal:50051
    token: ${SPICEDB_TOKEN}
    write_schema: false  # remote only
Key Default Meaning mode rbac rbac or rebac engine spicedb Only with rebac spicedb.mode embedded embedded runs in process; remote connects over gRPC spicedb.datastore_engine memory Embedded only: memory or postgres spicedb.datastore_uri Embedded postgres only; required there spicedb.endpoint, spicedb.token Remote only; endpoint required spicedb.insecure false Remote without TLS; development only spicedb.write_schema false Remote only: write the composed schema at startup. Embedded instances always get it

docs.title: Building the provider
docs.text:
res, err := mode.New(ctx, cfg.Authz, mode.Deps{DB: db, Registry: registry})
if err != nil { return err }
defer res.Close()

orgs := organization.NewService(db, organization.WithAuthzSyncer(res.Syncer))
invites := invite.NewService(db, baseURL,
    invite.WithAuthzSyncer(res.Syncer), invite.WithResourceGrants(res.Grants))

mode.New applies defaults, validates, and for rebac starts or connects to the engine and writes the schema composed from the registered vocabularies. Result carries Provider, Syncer, Grants and Close(). The membership, role and grant tables remain the record in both modes; under rebac the services mirror each change into the graph.

Deps also takes SyncMode (strict returns a graph write failure, eventual, the default, logs it), AccessChangeSink, Logger, PlatformAdmin, ManagerRoles and RBACOptions.

docs.title: Switching from rbac to rebac
docs.text: A deployment that switches starts with an empty graph. Write the existing memberships, application roles and grants through the syncer before serving the first request; no bulk rebuild command ships yet.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
Configuration errors name the key and the accepted values and wrap systemauth.ErrInvalidConfig when loaded through SystemAuth:

Message Cause authz: unknown mode "..." (want rbac or rebac) Mode misspelled authz: engine "..." is set but mode is rbac Engine given with rbac authz: spicedb settings are given but mode is rbac SpiceDB block with rbac authz: unknown engine "..." for mode rebac Engine not supported authz: spicedb.mode remote requires spicedb.endpoint Remote without an endpoint authz: spicedb.endpoint and spicedb.token apply to spicedb.mode remote, not embedded Remote keys on an embedded instance authz: spicedb.datastore_engine postgres requires spicedb.datastore_uri Embedded postgres without a URI authz/mode: Deps.DB is required mode.New called without a database

At runtime, an organization API without an Authorizer answers 501, and a caller who lacks a permission answers 403 (or 404 when they cannot even view the organization).

docs.title: Package paths
docs.text: The role-based provider is authz/rbac and the relationship provider authz/rebac/spicedb. The former authz/simple and authz/spicedb paths are deprecated forwarders and will be removed in the next major release.

docs.title: Collaborators and resource grants
docs.text: A collaborator is a principal who belongs to an organization with role collaborator and reaches individual resources, not the organization. A resource grant gives a principal one of three roles on one resource. The design is in Organizations and Membership and Authorization.

docs.title: The model
docs.text:
Piece Rule Collaborator membership Role collaborator: no view, edit or manage on the organization, only list so an application can show the organization in a switcher. No application roles Resource roles viewer (view), contributor (view, edit), maintainer (view, edit, manage); each includes the ones below. The names are reserved for every application Resource {app}_{type} (a collaborator-able definition of a registered application) plus the application's own identifier, 1 to 1024 characters of letters, digits and /_\|-=+ Ownership A resource belongs to one organization; grants naming another organization for an already-granted resource are refused

An application declares which of its resource types accept collaborators by giving the definition the three relations viewer, contributor and maintainer in its vocabulary's schema fragment (authz.ResourceRoleFragment renders it); a vocabulary with no fragment accepts any type of its application.

docs.title: Granting and revoking
docs.text:
There is no HTTP API for grants: the application checks that its caller may manage the resource, then calls the service.

res, err := mode.New(ctx, cfg.Authz, mode.Deps{DB: db, Registry: registry})
ref := authz.ResourceRef{Type: "myapp_project", ID: projectID, OrganizationID: orgID}

err = res.Provider.GrantResourceRole(ctx, principalID, ref, authz.ResourceRoleContributor, callerID)
err = res.Provider.RevokeResourceRole(ctx, principalID, ref)
grants, err := res.Provider.ListResourceGrants(ctx, ref)
set, err := res.Provider.ListResources(ctx, principalID, "myapp_project", authz.PermResourceView)
// where org_id IN set.OrganizationIDs OR id IN set.IDs

Granting to a principal with no membership creates a collaborator membership in the same transaction; granting again replaces the role. Revoking the last grant of a collaborator removes the membership. An existing member keeps their role and gains the grant. The same grant can be made by accepting a resource-targeted invite.

Removing a member from the organization deletes their grants with the membership. Agents and managed principals are granted through the same operations, which confines them to the granted resources.

docs.title: Checking access
docs.text: Both modes answer Can(principal, view|edit|manage, resource) with the same result. The role-based provider needs rbac.WithResourceGrants(svc), which mode.New sets. Access that comes from an organization role (an admin's manage through the organization) is unaffected by grants.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text: The grant service does no authorization of its own. The application should require manage on the resource for resource grants, and invite_member for invites.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
Error Meaning authz.ErrInvalidResourceRole The role is not viewer, contributor or maintainer authz.ErrInvalidResource The reference is malformed, or the type is not a collaborator-able type of a registered application authz.ErrGrantNotFound Revoking a grant the principal does not hold authz.ErrResourceOrganizationMismatch The resource already has grants in another organization resourcegrant.ErrInactiveMembership The principal has a deactivated membership that is not a collaborator's; reactivate or remove it first organization.ErrPersonalOrganization Collaborator invites without a target are refused for a personal organization

Lowering or removing a grant records an access change (grant_reduced, plus membership_removed when it was the last), so relying parties with a revocation cache refuse earlier tokens; see Access-change invalidation.

docs.title: Connections to External Services
docs.text: Organizations connect accounts at services they already use, such as a CDN, product analytics or monitoring, and applications use those connections without ever holding the credential. SystemAuth stores the connections, seals their credentials, tests them, and hands applications authenticated HTTP clients. The design is ADR-017; the mechanism is connectforge.

docs.title: Enable connections
docs.text:
Add a connections section to the SystemAuth configuration. It needs a database and the role-based authorization mode (the default).

connections:
  keys_dir: /var/lib/systemauth/keys
  vault: env://
  root_key: SYSTEMAUTH_KEYS_ROOT
Key Meaning keys_dir Directory holding the key ring and its registry. Back it up with the database: without it, stored credentials cannot be read vault omnivault URI of the deployment's secret store: env://, file:///etc/systemauth/secrets, or a registered provider root_key Path in the vault of the key ring's root key: 32 random bytes as base64 or hex allow_private_egress Development only: lets provider requests reach loopback and private addresses over plain HTTP

Create the root key once and keep it in the secret store, not beside keys_dir:

export SYSTEMAUTH_KEYS_ROOT="$(openssl rand -base64 32)"

systemauth migrate (and --migrate at startup) creates the connection tables. On PostgreSQL it also enables row-level security on them, keyed on owner_id, the organization.

systemauth serve runs the key lifecycle jobs. A host that embeds SystemAuth calls Service.RunJobs itself.

docs.title: Register providers
docs.text:
Providers are registered by the application that embeds SystemAuth, through systemauthsvc.Options.Providers. A static-token service needs only a manifest and where its token goes:

reg := provider.NewRegistry()
p, err := apikey.New(apikey.Config{
    Manifest: provider.Manifest{
        Key: "cloudflare", DisplayName: "Cloudflare",
        BaseURLs: []string{"https://api.cloudflare.com"},
        AuthMethods: []provider.AuthMethod{{
            Key:    "api_token",
            Fields: []provider.Field{{Name: "token", Label: "API token", Secret: true, Required: true}},
        }},
    },
    Verify: apikey.Request{Path: "/client/v4/user/tokens/verify"},
})
if err != nil {
    return err
}
if err := reg.Register(p); err != nil {
    return err
}
svc, err := systemauthsvc.New(ctx, cfg, systemauthsvc.Options{Providers: reg})

Requests for a provider may reach only its manifest's BaseURLs, over HTTPS, never a private address, and never by a redirect to another host.

docs.title: Use a connection in process
docs.text:
An application in the same process gets an authenticated client from the broker and hands it to the provider's SDK:

ctx = rls.ContextWithTenant(ctx, orgID) // row-level security on PostgreSQL
hc, err := svc.Connections().Broker.HTTPClient(ctx,
    connections.OwnerFor(orgID),
    connectforge.Principal{Kind: connectforge.PrincipalUser, ID: userID.String()},
    connectionID,
    connectforge.Use{Consumer: connectforge.Consumer{Kind: "application", ID: "dashboards"}, Purpose: "traffic"},
)
if err != nil {
    return err
}
client := providersdk.New(providersdk.WithHTTPClient(hc)) // any SDK that accepts an *http.Client

The broker checks that the principal may use the connection and that it is connected. Make a client per unit of work: a disconnect applies to the next client.

docs.title: HTTP API
docs.text:
Every request carries a SystemAuth access token. Reads need the systemforge:connections:read scope; changes need systemforge:connections:write.

Method and path Action GET /api/v1/providers Provider manifests: methods, fields, scopes GET /api/v1/organizations/{org}/connections Connections the caller may view (?provider=, ?state=) POST /api/v1/organizations/{org}/connections Connect: {"provider", "authMethod", "displayName", "fields": {...}} GET /api/v1/organizations/{org}/connections/{id} One connection PATCH /api/v1/organizations/{org}/connections/{id} Rename: {"displayName"} POST /api/v1/organizations/{org}/connections/{id}/test Validate again; the result is in health POST /api/v1/organizations/{org}/connections/{id}/reconnect Replace the credential: {"fields": {...}} GET /api/v1/organizations/{org}/connections/{id}/bindings What depends on the connection PUT /api/v1/organizations/{org}/connections/{id}/bindings Record a dependency: {"consumerKind", "consumerId", "purpose"} DELETE /api/v1/organizations/{org}/connections/{id}/bindings?kind=&id=&purpose= Remove one GET /api/v1/organizations/{org}/connections/{id}/grants Who holds a role on the connection PUT /api/v1/organizations/{org}/connections/{id}/grants/{principal} Give a role: {"role": "viewer" \| "contributor" \| "maintainer"} DELETE /api/v1/organizations/{org}/connections/{id}/grants/{principal} Take it back DELETE /api/v1/organizations/{org}/connections/{id} Disconnect and destroy the credential

A connection is validated with its provider before it is stored, and a rejected credential stores nothing (422). No response contains a credential. A connection the caller may not view is reported as 404.

docs.title: Reconnecting
docs.text: When a token expires or is revoked, replace it in place with reconnect. The new credential is validated with the provider first and must belong to the same account; otherwise nothing changes (422). Everything bound to the connection keeps working.

docs.title: Who may do what
docs.text:
Role View Use Manage, share, disconnect Organization owner, admin Yes Yes Yes Member Yes With a grant With a grant Collaborator With a grant With a grant With a grant The connection's creator Yes Yes Yes

Creating a connection needs an owner or admin. Grants are resource roles (ADR-008) on type systemforge_connection:

Role Lets the principal viewer See the connection contributor Use it, and record what depends on it maintainer Manage it: rename, test, reconnect, share, disconnect

Giving someone a role on a connection who is not in the organization makes them a collaborator, with access to that connection only. Granting needs the share action, which is maintainer, an owner or an admin.

Roles are never visible to the connection's provider; they decide who in your organization may use the stored credential, not what the credential can do.

docs.title: Credentials and keys
docs.text: A connection's credential is sealed under keys that SystemAuth manages through keyforge, using the connections.keys_dir and connections.root_key settings above. Back up the keys directory with the database: without it, stored credentials cannot be read. See Key management.

docs.title: Current limits
docs.text:
• Static API tokens only; GitHub App and OAuth connections follow.
  • The role-based authorization mode only.
  • The API acts for the token's principal as a user; service principals and agents use the broker in process.
  • Connection events go to the server log until an audit store is configured.
  • A disconnect does not yet require acknowledging the bindings it would stop; list them first with GET .../bindings.

docs.title: Invites
docs.text: An invite brings a person with a known email address into an organization. It can also grant application roles on acceptance, or, for a collaborator, a role on one resource. The design is in Organizations and Membership; this guide is what a developer needs to wire and call it.

docs.title: Wiring
docs.text:
invites := invite.NewService(db, baseURL,
    invite.WithAuthzSyncer(res.Syncer),
    invite.WithAppRoles(appRoles),          // optional: application roles on invites
    invite.WithResourceGrants(res.Grants),  // optional: resource-targeted invites
)
cfg := invite.DefaultAPIConfig()
cfg.Authorizer = authorizer
api := invite.NewAPI(invites, orgService, cfg)

Without WithAppRoles, app_roles on an invite is refused and no application role is ever required. Without WithResourceGrants, a resource target is refused.

docs.title: Creating an invite
docs.text:
POST /organizations/{slug}/invites

Field Meaning email The invitee; the invite is bound to this address (case-insensitive) role Required: owner, admin, member or collaborator app_roles Optional map of application identifier to role, granted on acceptance resource_type, resource_id, resource_role Optional, all or none: a resource and the resource role (viewer, contributor, maintainer) to grant message, expires_in_hours Optional note; expiry defaults to 7 days, at most 720 hours inviter_principal_id Optional; if given it must be the authenticated caller

The response carries invite_url ({baseURL}/invites/{token}). The token is shown once: only its SHA-256 is stored, so deliver the URL yourself.

docs.title: Application roles on an invite
docs.text:
With WithAppRoles:

  • Each app_roles entry is validated: the application is registered, the role is one it declares, and the organization is entitled to it.
  • An admin or member invitation to an organization that is entitled to any application must choose at least one role (ErrAppRoleRequired). Owners hold every role implicitly, so an owner invite needs none.
  • A collaborator invite may carry none.
  • Roles are granted in the same transaction as the membership. If one cannot be granted at acceptance (no seat left, entitlement gone) the invite is refused and stays pending.

docs.title: Resource-targeted invites
docs.text:
A resource target requires role: collaborator and WithResourceGrants, and is validated against the application's vocabulary: the type must be {app}_{type} of a registered application and, when the vocabulary has a schema fragment, a collaborator-able definition. On acceptance the collaborator membership and the grant are created together; an existing member keeps their role and gains the grant.

A person may hold several pending invites to one organization if each targets a different resource. A personal organization accepts only resource-targeted collaborator invites. See Collaborators and resource grants.

docs.title: Accepting and declining
docs.text:
Route Rule GET /invites/{token} Landing-page lookup POST /invites/{token}/accept The caller's email must match the invite POST /invites/{token}/decline Same match GET /invites Lists the caller's own pending invites; another address is 403

Signing up through an invite (signup.SignupWithInvite) applies the same email match (signup.ErrInviteEmailMismatch).

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text: Operation Needs Create, list, resend, revoke invite_member on the organization (owner or admin) Invite with role: owner The owner-only permission (delete) Accept, decline, list own An authenticated principal whose email matches the invite

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
Status Cause 400 The service refused the request. The message names the cause: pending invite already exists for this email; invite: choose an application role for at least one entitled application; invite: collaborators hold no application roles; invite: application roles are not configured; invite: invalid resource target (incomplete target, role not collaborator, grants not configured, or a type or role the vocabulary rejects); a collaborator invite without a target to a personal organization; invite is no longer pending; invite has expired; principal is already a member of this organization; an application role that cannot be granted (approle: no seats available for the application, approle: organization is not entitled to the application) 403 inviter_principal_id is not the caller; an admin inviting an owner; a principal without an email (a managed principal) answering an invite; listing another address's invites; the caller can view the organization but may not invite 404 Unknown organization or invite; a caller who cannot even view the organization; an invite addressed to a different email (a mismatch looks like an unknown token) 501 No Authorizer, or no principal email lookup, is configured

Manager invitations, which put an existing person under the management of a guardian, are a separate flow; see Managed Principals.

docs.title: Key Management
docs.text:
SystemForge encrypts stored secrets under keys it manages through keyforge, so that keys rotate without re-encrypting data, a key's use is audited, and the root key is read from your secret store rather than kept beside the data. The design is ADR-013.

Pre-release

keyforge has not been externally audited and is not yet recommended for production use. Read its threat model before relying on it for data under legal hold.

docs.title: What uses it
docs.text: The keys package is the platform's one key library. Today SystemAuth uses it to seal the credentials of connections to external services. Applications can use it for their own data through the same interface.

docs.title: How it is laid out
docs.text:
Piece Where it lives Root key Your secret store, read through omnivault when the process starts. It is 32 random bytes, as base64 or hex Key ring A file in the keys directory, sealed under the root key Registry A SQLite database in the same directory: key versions, data keys and their states Data Your database, holding ciphertext that names the key version that sealed it

The key ring and the registry sit in one directory on purpose: they are backed up together, so a restore never pairs a registry with a key ring from another moment.

docs.title: Set it up
docs.text:
For a SystemAuth deployment, the connections section configures it (see Connections):

connections:
  keys_dir: /var/lib/systemauth/keys   # the key ring and registry
  vault: env://                        # omnivault URI: env://, file:///dir, ...
  root_key: SYSTEMAUTH_KEYS_ROOT       # the root key's path in that vault

Create the root key once, store it in the secret store, and keep a second copy offline. It is not recoverable:

export SYSTEMAUTH_KEYS_ROOT="$(openssl rand -base64 32)"

keyforge refuses a root key that is a file kept inside the keys directory, so the key never sits beside what it protects.

docs.title: Use it from Go
docs.text:
v, err := omnivault.VaultFromURI("env://")
if err != nil {
    return err
}
k, err := keys.Open(ctx, keys.Options{
    Dir:      "/var/lib/myapp/keys",
    Root:     keys.VaultSource(v, "MYAPP_KEYS_ROOT"),
    Purposes: []keyforge.Purpose{"myapp.sessions"},
    Audit:    auditStore, // optional: key events go to the platform audit trail
})
if err != nil {
    return err
}
defer k.Close()

sealed, err := k.Seal(ctx, "myapp.sessions", []byte("value"), []byte("user:42"))
plain, err := k.Open(ctx, "myapp.sessions", sealed, []byte("user:42"))
  • Purpose names what a key protects. Each purpose gets its own keys, so exposing or destroying one does not touch another.
  • The additional data ("user:42" above) is bound to the ciphertext. It must be the same to open it, so a value cannot be moved to another record.
  • Open fails closed. With no usable key it returns an error; it never falls back to something weaker.
  • Run the lifecycle jobs. k.Run(ctx) rotates keys on schedule and resumes unfinished work after a restart. systemauth serve does this for you.

docs.title: What it does for you
docs.text:
• Rotation without re-encrypting. Rotating a key-encryption key re-wraps data keys. Stored ciphertext is not rewritten, and old versions stay readable until nothing references them.
  • Audit. When you pass Audit, key creation, rotation, retirement and destruction are recorded in the platform audit trail with no key material. Ordinary seal and open are not logged one by one. SystemAuth does not pass an audit store to keys yet, so a SystemAuth deployment records no key events.
  • Backup checks. A key ring restored from a backup older than one this host has seen is refused unless keys.Options.AcceptRollback is set, so a stale copy is never used by mistake.

docs.title: Operate it
docs.text: Task How Back up Stop the process, copy the whole keys directory, and keep the root key separately. The key ring and the registry must come from the same moment Restore Stop the process, restore the directory, and open with keys.Options.AcceptRollback once to acknowledge a ring older than one this host has seen. SystemAuth's configuration does not expose it yet, so a restore there needs a one-off start of an embedding host Check status or rotate by hand Not served yet. SystemAuth runs the lifecycle jobs but does not mount keyforge's control plane or command line Move the registry to PostgreSQL Not yet: this release uses keyforge's single-host setup. ADR-013 records the follow-up

docs.title: Limits to know
docs.text:
• The local provider is as safe as the host and its root key source. It is not a hardware module. A managed key service is the recommended root of trust for data under legal hold.
  • A restore can undo an erasure. Shredding lives in the registry, and backups hold destroyed versions' material.
  • One process owns the directory. Run the jobs in one process, or share a workflow provider; do not point two processes at the same directory.

docs.title: Organization slugs
docs.text: The slug is an organization's identity in URLs and in the API: /organizations/{slug}, /organizations/{slug}/members, /invites/.... The display name is cosmetic. The slug is unique across personal and team organizations. The design is in Organizations and Membership.

docs.title: Format and generation
docs.text:
A slug matches ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*[a-z0-9]$ and is 3 to 63 characters (organization.IsValidSlug). GET /organizations/check-slug/{slug} answers {"slug", "available"}, and available is false for a taken, reserved or cooling-off slug. GenerateSlug(name) slugifies a name and appends -1 to -100, then a UUID fragment, until one is free.

Social login derives the personal slug from the provider: the GitHub username, the Google email local part, otherwise the username or local part; collisions take -1 to -100 and then a random suffix. A managed principal's slug is never taken from an email (signup.SlugForManaged).

docs.title: Reserved slugs
docs.text:
Names that would collide with a route or protocol path cannot be taken: about, admin, api, help, invites, login, logout, new, o, oauth, organizations, scim, settings, support, well-known, www (organization.ReservedSlugs). Add product names when you build the service:

orgs := organization.NewService(db, organization.WithReservedSlugs("billing", "console"))

For signup, pass the same names in PersonalOrgParams.ReservedSlugs; a reserved base slug gets a numeric suffix.

docs.title: Renaming
docs.text:
Rename(ctx, orgID, newSlug, actor) is a service method; there is no HTTP endpoint. The actor must be an active owner. In one transaction the old slug is written to sf_slug_reservations and held for the cooling-off period, 7 days by default (organization.WithSlugCoolingOff(d)).

While the old slug is held Rule Who may take it The principal who released it, or an owner of the organization that released it Everyone else ErrSlugCoolingOff; check-slug answers available: false Alias ResolveSlug returns the releasing organization with alias = true, and the organization and invite handlers resolve {slug} through it, so old links keep working and responses carry the current slug After expiry The reservation is ignored and deleted when next read

GetBySlug stays an exact match. Update your own URLs to the current slug from the response.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
Error HTTP Meaning organization.ErrInvalidSlug 400 on create Not lowercase alphanumeric with hyphens, or the wrong length organization.ErrSlugReserved 400 on create On the built-in or configured reserved list organization.ErrSlugTaken 400 on create Used by an organization organization.ErrSlugCoolingOff 400 on create Held by someone else's reservation organization.ErrNotOwner n/a (service) Rename by a principal who is not an active owner

PATCH /organizations/{slug} cannot change the slug; it accepts only name, logo_url, description, website_url and settings.

docs.title: Converting a personal organization to a team
docs.text:
Every person has a personal organization named after their handle. When they need to share it, ConvertToTeam turns it into a team without moving anything: the same organization (ID, data, settings, memberships) takes a team slug and becomes team, and the owner receives a new personal organization under their old handle. The design is in Organizations and Membership.

res, err := orgs.ConvertToTeam(ctx, personalOrgID, "acme", ownerID)
// res.Team is the converted organization; res.Personal is the new one.

There is no HTTP endpoint; call it from your own handler after checking the caller is the owner.

docs.title: What happens
docs.text:
In one transaction:

  1. The organization must be personal and ownerID its owner.
  2. It is renamed to the team slug with the normal rename rules: valid, not reserved, not taken, not held by someone else. The old handle is reserved for the owner.
  3. Its type becomes team. It now accepts members like any team, and its existing collaborators stay.
  4. A new personal organization is created for the owner under the handle, spending the reservation. It is named after the owner's display name and has the owner as its only member.

After commit, the new organization is registered with the authorization syncer. Any failure rolls everything back.

docs.title: Rules for personal organizations
docs.text: A personal organization has exactly one member, its owner. Adding a member, inviting a non-collaborator, SCIM group membership and ownership transfer are refused with organization.ErrPersonalOrganization; the members API answers 409. A collaborator, reached through a resource grant or a resource-targeted invite, is allowed. POST /organizations accepts only team and enterprise; personal organizations come from signup.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text: Error Meaning organization.ErrOrganizationNotFound No such organization organization.ErrNotPersonal The organization is already a team or enterprise organization.ErrNotOwner ownerID is not the owner ErrInvalidSlug, ErrSlugReserved, ErrSlugTaken, ErrSlugCoolingOff The team slug is refused; see Organization slugs

docs.title: AI Agents (AAuth)
docs.text:
A SystemForge resource server — a product API — can accept requests from AI agents alongside people. Agents authenticate with AAuth (draft -11): every request carries an HTTP message signature (RFC 9421) made with the agent's own key, plus a token in the Signature-Key header that binds the key to an identity. There are no shared secrets and no per-resource client registration.

Two packages make this work:

Package What it does identity/requestprincipal The protocol-neutral RequestPrincipal, the Authenticator interface, and a middleware that tries authenticators in order. No protocol dependencies. identity/requestprincipal/aauthrs The AAuth resource-side authenticator, built on github.com/aauth-dev/aauth-go. The only package that imports it.

Human credentials keep working through relyingparty.NewRequestAuthenticator, which wraps the same SystemAuth access tokens, API keys and BFF sessions as BearerMiddleware (see Relying Parties).

docs.title: The request principal
docs.text:
Every authenticator produces the same type, so handlers don't need to know which protocol was used:

p, ok := requestprincipal.FromContext(r.Context())
Field Human (relying party) Agent (AAuth auth token) PrincipalID app-local principal ID <ps>#<sub>: the person the agent acts for Type human, service, application agent Subject SystemAuth subject the person's directed sub at this resource Organization — tenant claim Actor — jkt:<agent key thumbprint> Delegator — same as PrincipalID Mission — mission_s256 Session — the auth token's jti Protocol session, oidc, apikey aauth Proof credential method, API key ID token type, issuer, audience, jti, key thumbprint, iat/exp, Signature-Input Scopes token or API key scopes granted scope Native *relyingparty.AuthenticatedPrincipal *aauth.AuthClaims

A Person Server's sub is directed: it is different at each resource and unique only within that Person Server. That's why PrincipalID qualifies it with the Person Server. Use Config.Resolve to map it to an application principal of your own.

docs.title: The challenge sequence
docs.text:
The AAuth authenticator only handles requests that carry a Signature-Key header. Requests without one go to the next authenticator. When no authenticator recognizes a request, the middleware returns a 401 that includes every authenticator's challenge:

HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
AAuth-Requirement: requirement=agent-token
Link: <https://api.example.com/.well-known/aauth-resource.json>; rel="aauth-resource"
WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="api"

With the default access mode (auth-token), an agent works through these steps:

Request signed with Response no Signature-Key 401 requirement=agent-token (plus the bearer challenge) agent token 401 requirement=person-token: which person is the agent acting for? person token from a trusted Person Server 401 requirement=auth-token; resource-token="..." auth token that grants the route's scopes served, RequestPrincipal{Type: agent} auth token missing a scope 401 requirement=auth-token with a new resource token (step-up) an invalid, expired, mis-addressed or wrongly bound token 401 with Signature-Error and a problem+json body

Draft -11 lets a resource issue a resource token only against a person token or an auth token that it has verified. So a request signed with only an agent token is challenged for a person token, not an auth token. The agent's aauth.Transport follows all of these challenges automatically: it gets a person token, exchanges the resource token at its Person Server, and retries.

docs.title: Wiring a resource server
docs.text:
import (
    aauth "github.com/aauth-dev/aauth-go"

    "github.com/plexusone/systemforge/identity/relyingparty"
    "github.com/plexusone/systemforge/identity/requestprincipal"
    "github.com/plexusone/systemforge/identity/requestprincipal/aauthrs"
)

agents, err := aauthrs.New(aauthrs.Config{
    Resource:       "https://api.example.com",            // this API's identifier
    TrustedIssuers: []string{"https://agents.example.com"}, // Person/Access Server(s)
    Key:            resourceKey,                           // Ed25519 or P-256 crypto.Signer
    Scopes: func(r *http.Request) []string {               // required per route
        if r.Method == http.MethodGet {
            return []string{"things:read"}
        }
        return []string{"things:write"}
    },
    ScopeDescriptions: map[string]string{
        "things:read":  "Read your things",
        "things:write": "Create and change your things",
    },
    HTTPClient: egressClient, // no private addresses, bounded timeouts
    Limiter:    ratelimit.Per(10, time.Minute), // optional, from aauth-go/ratelimit
})
if err != nil {
    return err
}

humans := relyingparty.NewRequestAuthenticator(relyingparty.BearerConfig{
    Tokens:     client,   // *relyingparty.Client
    APIKeys:    apiKeys,  // *apikey.Service
    Principals: principals,
    Sessions:   bff,      // optional: browser sessions too
})

mux := http.NewServeMux()
agents.Register(mux) // /.well-known/aauth-resource.json and the resource JWKS (public)

protect := requestprincipal.Middleware(requestprincipal.Options{}, agents, humans)
mux.Handle("/api/", protect(apiHandler))

Put the AAuth authenticator first. It only acts on requests that carry a Signature-Key header, so cookies and bearer tokens still reach the relying-party authenticator. Credentials that one authenticator recognizes and rejects are never passed to the next one.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: Field Purpose Resource The server identifier (https, host only). It is the aud of the tokens this API accepts and the iss of the resource tokens it issues. TrustedIssuers The Person Servers and Access Servers whose tokens are accepted. Tokens from other issuers are refused before key discovery, so an attacker can't make the API fetch keys from a URL of their choosing. AccessMode auth-token (default) serves only auth tokens. person-token also accepts person tokens, and agent-token also accepts bare agent tokens, in both cases only on routes that require no scopes. Scopes Returns the scopes a request requires. An auth token must grant all of them, and resource tokens request them. Key, KeyID Signs resource tokens. The key is published at JWKSPath (default /.well-known/aauth-resource-jwks.json). Audience For four-party access, the resource's Access Server. Resource tokens are addressed to it instead of to the Person Server. Resolver, AgentResolver, HTTPClient, JWKSCache Key discovery. The default is the library's JWKS resolver and cache: metadata → jwks_uri, cache headers honored, refreshed at most once a minute when an unknown kid appears. Signature Signature validity window, clock and extra required components. The library defaults apply when this is left zero. CheckSubject The resource's record check for (iss, sub). Resolve Maps or rejects the principal after verification. A returned *requestprincipal.Error is sent as the response. Limiter Rate-limits resource-token issuance per agent key. Refused requests get a 429 with Retry-After.

docs.title: What is verified
docs.text:
For an auth token, the authenticator calls the library's VerifyAndExtractAuth and enforces the issuer allowlist:

  • the token: typ aa-auth+jwt, an allowed algorithm, dwk, an issuer in TrustedIssuers with its key found through JWKS discovery, aud equal to Resource, iat present and not ahead of the clock by more than the signature window, a lifetime of one hour or less, exp in the future with no skew allowance, and sub, ps and cnf.jwk present;
  • the HTTP message signature: it covers @method, @authority, @path and signature-key, it was made with the key in cnf.jwk, and its created time is inside the validity window.

Resource tokens are issued only with IssueResourceToken, against the person or auth token just verified. This copies sub, mission_s256 and tenant and binds the agent's key with agent_jkt.

docs.title: Scopes and authorization
docs.text: Scope checks happen during authentication: an auth token that lacks a scope the route needs gets a step-up challenge, not a 403. Anything beyond scopes, such as organization membership, resource ownership or SpiceDB checks, runs in handlers or later middleware against the RequestPrincipal, the same way for people and agents.

docs.title: API Keys
docs.text: API keys provide server-to-server authentication for programmatic access.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
SystemForge provides a complete API key management system:

import (
    "github.com/plexusone/systemforge/identity/apikey"
)

// Create service with your store implementation
service := apikey.NewService(apikey.ServiceConfig{
    Store:         myStore,               // Your store implementation
    Prefix:        "myapp",               // Key prefix (default: "cf")
    AllowedScopes: []string{"read:*", "write:*"},
})

// Generate a new key
result, err := service.Create(ctx, apikey.CreateKeyRequest{
    Name:     "CI/CD Pipeline",
    OwnerID:  userID,
    Scopes:   []string{"read:deployments", "write:deployments"},
})
// result.Key = "myapp_live_abc123..._xyz789..." (show once)
// result.APIKey = metadata (store in UI)

// Validate incoming key
apiKey, err := service.Validate(ctx, rawKey)
if err != nil {
    // Invalid, expired, or revoked
}

// Check scope
if !apiKey.HasScope("write:deployments") {
    // Forbidden
}

docs.title: Storage
docs.text: The apikey.Service above works against a Store you provide. SystemForge does not ship an API key table of its own; choose one of two backing stores:

docs.title: Principal Credentials
docs.text:
Store keys as sf_credentials rows of type api_key, owned by a principal. The identity/credential service creates, validates, lists, and revokes them, storing only a hash and a display prefix:

import "github.com/plexusone/systemforge/identity/credential"

creds := credential.NewService(client)

key, err := creds.CreateAPIKey(ctx, credential.CreateAPIKeyInput{
    PrincipalID: principalID,
    Name:        "CI/CD Pipeline",
    Scopes:      []string{"read:deployments"},
})
// key.PlainKey is shown once; key.Credential is the stored record.

cred, err := creds.ValidateAPIKey(ctx, rawKey)

Use this when keys belong to a principal (a human or a service) and should share its lifecycle.

docs.title: Application Table
docs.text:
Keep keys in your own table by adding the API-key mixin to an Ent schema in your application, then implementing apikey.EntClientInterface over your generated client:

import "github.com/plexusone/systemforge/identity/ent/mixin"

func (APIKey) Mixin() []ent.Mixin {
    return []ent.Mixin{
        mixin.APIKey{},
    }
}

Use this when keys need application-specific fields or relationships.

docs.title: Key Format
docs.text: Keys generated by apikey.Service have the form <prefix>_<environment>_<random>_<random>, for example sf_live_4Fh2kQ9x_7K3mN9pQrS2tUvW4xYz6. The prefix defaults to sf and is set with ServiceConfig.Prefix; the environment is live or test. Only a SHA-256 hash of the full key is stored, along with the visible <prefix>_<environment>_<random> part for identification.

docs.title: Creating API Keys
docs.text:
result, err := service.Create(ctx, apikey.CreateKeyRequest{
    Name:    "CI/CD Pipeline",
    OwnerID: ownerID,
    Scopes:  []string{"read:deployments", "write:deployments"},
})
// result.Key is the full key: return it to the caller once, never store it.
// result.APIKey is the stored metadata.

CreateKeyRequest also accepts an organization, an expiration, and an environment.

docs.title: Validating API Keys
docs.text:
apiKey, err := service.Validate(ctx, rawKey)
if err != nil {
    // Malformed, unknown, expired, or revoked
}

// Or require a scope in the same call.
apiKey, err = service.ValidateWithScope(ctx, rawKey, "write:deployments")

docs.title: Scope Checking
docs.text:
APIKey matches scopes exactly and honors :* wildcards (read:* grants read:deployments):

if !apiKey.HasScope("write:deployments") {
    return ErrForbidden
}

apiKey.HasAnyScope("read:deployments", "read:builds")
apiKey.HasAllScopes("read:deployments", "write:deployments")

docs.title: Managing API Keys
docs.text:
keys, err := service.List(ctx, ownerID)               // by owner
keys, err = service.ListByOrganization(ctx, orgID)    // by organization

err = service.Revoke(ctx, keyID, "rotated")           // keeps the record
err = service.Delete(ctx, keyID)                      // removes it

docs.title: Security Best Practices
docs.text:
1. Never log API keys - Only log the prefix for debugging
  2. Set expirations - Use short-lived keys when possible
  3. Scope narrowly - Grant minimum required permissions
  4. Monitor usage - Track last_used_at for anomaly detection
  5. Allow revocation - Provide UI for users to revoke keys
  6. Rate limit - Protect against brute force attacks

docs.title: Usage Example
docs.text:
# Using an API key
curl https://api.example.com/v1/deployments \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sf_live_4Fh2kQ9x_7K3mN9pQrS2tUvW4xYz6"

docs.title: Ent Store Implementation
docs.text: SystemForge provides an Ent-backed store implementation for production use.

docs.title: Step 1: Add Schema Using Mixin
docs.text:
// internal/ent/schema/api_key.go

package schema

import (
    "entgo.io/ent"
    "entgo.io/ent/schema/edge"
    "github.com/plexusone/systemforge/identity/ent/mixin"
)

// APIKey holds the schema definition.
type APIKey struct {
    ent.Schema
}

// Mixin of the APIKey.
func (APIKey) Mixin() []ent.Mixin {
    return []ent.Mixin{
        mixin.APIKey{},
    }
}

// Edges of the APIKey.
func (APIKey) Edges() []ent.Edge {
    return []ent.Edge{
        edge.From("owner", User.Type).
            Ref("api_keys").
            Field("owner_id").
            Required().
            Unique(),
    }
}

docs.title: Step 2: Implement Client Interface
docs.text:
// internal/auth/apikey_store.go

package auth

import (
    "context"
    "time"

    "github.com/google/uuid"
    "github.com/plexusone/systemforge/identity/apikey"
    "myapp/internal/ent"
    entapikey "myapp/internal/ent/apikey"
)

// APIKeyClientWrapper implements apikey.EntClientInterface.
type APIKeyClientWrapper struct {
    client *ent.Client
}

func NewAPIKeyClientWrapper(client *ent.Client) *APIKeyClientWrapper {
    return &APIKeyClientWrapper{client: client}
}

func (w *APIKeyClientWrapper) CreateAPIKey(ctx context.Context, key *apikey.APIKey, keyHash string) error {
    create := w.client.APIKey.Create().
        SetID(key.ID).
        SetName(key.Name).
        SetPrefix(key.Prefix).
        SetKeyHash(keyHash).
        SetOwnerID(key.OwnerID).
        SetScopes(key.Scopes).
        SetEnvironment(entapikey.Environment(key.Environment)).
        SetCreatedAt(key.CreatedAt).
        SetUpdatedAt(key.UpdatedAt)

    if key.OrganizationID != nil {
        create = create.SetOrganizationID(*key.OrganizationID)
    }
    if key.Description != "" {
        create = create.SetDescription(key.Description)
    }
    if key.ExpiresAt != nil {
        create = create.SetExpiresAt(*key.ExpiresAt)
    }
    if key.Metadata != nil {
        create = create.SetMetadata(key.Metadata)
    }

    _, err := create.Save(ctx)
    return err
}

func (w *APIKeyClientWrapper) GetAPIKeyByPrefix(ctx context.Context, prefix string) (*apikey.APIKey, string, error) {
    k, err := w.client.APIKey.Query().
        Where(entapikey.PrefixEQ(prefix)).
        Only(ctx)
    if err != nil {
        if ent.IsNotFound(err) {
            return nil, "", apikey.ErrKeyNotFound
        }
        return nil, "", err
    }
    return toAPIKey(k), k.KeyHash, nil
}

func (w *APIKeyClientWrapper) GetAPIKeyByID(ctx context.Context, id uuid.UUID) (*apikey.APIKey, error) {
    k, err := w.client.APIKey.Get(ctx, id)
    if err != nil {
        if ent.IsNotFound(err) {
            return nil, apikey.ErrKeyNotFound
        }
        return nil, err
    }
    return toAPIKey(k), nil
}

func (w *APIKeyClientWrapper) ListAPIKeysByOwner(ctx context.Context, ownerID uuid.UUID) ([]*apikey.APIKey, error) {
    keys, err := w.client.APIKey.Query().
        Where(entapikey.OwnerIDEQ(ownerID)).
        Order(ent.Desc(entapikey.FieldCreatedAt)).
        All(ctx)
    if err != nil {
        return nil, err
    }

    result := make([]*apikey.APIKey, len(keys))
    for i, k := range keys {
        result[i] = toAPIKey(k)
    }
    return result, nil
}

func (w *APIKeyClientWrapper) ListAPIKeysByOrganization(ctx context.Context, orgID uuid.UUID) ([]*apikey.APIKey, error) {
    keys, err := w.client.APIKey.Query().
        Where(entapikey.OrganizationIDEQ(orgID)).
        Order(ent.Desc(entapikey.FieldCreatedAt)).
        All(ctx)
    if err != nil {
        return nil, err
    }

    result := make([]*apikey.APIKey, len(keys))
    for i, k := range keys {
        result[i] = toAPIKey(k)
    }
    return result, nil
}

func (w *APIKeyClientWrapper) UpdateAPIKey(ctx context.Context, key *apikey.APIKey) error {
    update := w.client.APIKey.UpdateOneID(key.ID).
        SetName(key.Name).
        SetScopes(key.Scopes).
        SetRevoked(key.Revoked).
        SetUpdatedAt(key.UpdatedAt)

    if key.Description != "" {
        update = update.SetDescription(key.Description)
    }
    if key.RevokedAt != nil {
        update = update.SetRevokedAt(*key.RevokedAt)
    }
    if key.RevokedReason != "" {
        update = update.SetRevokedReason(key.RevokedReason)
    }
    if key.Metadata != nil {
        update = update.SetMetadata(key.Metadata)
    }

    _, err := update.Save(ctx)
    return err
}

func (w *APIKeyClientWrapper) DeleteAPIKey(ctx context.Context, id uuid.UUID) error {
    return w.client.APIKey.DeleteOneID(id).Exec(ctx)
}

func (w *APIKeyClientWrapper) UpdateAPIKeyLastUsed(ctx context.Context, id uuid.UUID, ip string) error {
    now := time.Now()
    _, err := w.client.APIKey.UpdateOneID(id).
        SetLastUsedAt(now).
        SetLastUsedIP(ip).
        Save(ctx)
    return err
}

func toAPIKey(k *ent.APIKey) *apikey.APIKey {
    return &apikey.APIKey{
        ID:             k.ID,
        Name:           k.Name,
        Prefix:         k.Prefix,
        OwnerID:        k.OwnerID,
        OrganizationID: k.OrganizationID,
        Scopes:         k.Scopes,
        Description:    k.Description,
        Environment:    apikey.Environment(k.Environment),
        ExpiresAt:      k.ExpiresAt,
        LastUsedAt:     k.LastUsedAt,
        LastUsedIP:     k.LastUsedIP,
        Revoked:        k.Revoked,
        RevokedAt:      k.RevokedAt,
        RevokedReason:  k.RevokedReason,
        Metadata:       k.Metadata,
        CreatedAt:      k.CreatedAt,
        UpdatedAt:      k.UpdatedAt,
    }
}

docs.title: Step 3: Create the Store and Service
docs.text:
// main.go or wire.go

import (
    "github.com/plexusone/systemforge/identity/apikey"
    "myapp/internal/auth"
)

// Create the Ent store
store, err := apikey.NewEntStore(apikey.EntStoreConfig{
    Client: auth.NewAPIKeyClientWrapper(entClient),
})
if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}

// Create the service
service := apikey.NewService(apikey.ServiceConfig{
    Store:         store,
    Prefix:        "myapp",
    AllowedScopes: []string{
        "read:users",
        "write:users",
        "read:projects",
        "write:projects",
    },
    MaxKeysPerUser: 10,
})

docs.title: Mixin Fields
docs.text:
The mixin.APIKey provides these fields:

Field Type Description id UUID Primary key name string User-provided name prefix string Visible prefix (e.g., sf_live_xxxx) key_hash string SHA-256 hash (sensitive) owner_id UUID Owner user organization_id UUID Organization scope (optional) scopes []string Granted permissions description string User-provided note (optional) environment enum live or test expires_at time Expiration (optional) last_used_at time Last usage (optional) last_used_ip string Last IP (optional) revoked bool Revocation status revoked_at time Revocation time (optional) revoked_reason string Revocation reason (optional) metadata JSON Additional data (optional) created_at time Creation timestamp updated_at time Update timestamp

docs.title: Indexes
docs.text:
The mixin creates indexes for common queries:

index.Fields("owner_id")                // List by owner
index.Fields("organization_id")         // List by organization
index.Fields("prefix")                  // Lookup by prefix
index.Fields("key_hash").Unique()       // Validate by hash
index.Fields("environment")             // Filter by environment

docs.title: Service Methods
docs.text:
The apikey.Service provides these methods:

// Create a new API key (returns full key once)
result, err := service.Create(ctx, CreateKeyRequest{
    Name:           "My Key",
    OwnerID:        userID,
    OrganizationID: &orgID,
    Scopes:         []string{"read:*"},
    Description:    "For CI/CD",
    Environment:    apikey.EnvLive,
    ExpiresIn:      ptr(90 * 24 * time.Hour),
    Metadata:       map[string]string{"team": "platform"},
})

// Validate a key
apiKey, err := service.Validate(ctx, rawKey)

// Validate with scope check
apiKey, err := service.ValidateWithScope(ctx, rawKey, "write:projects")

// Get key by ID
apiKey, err := service.Get(ctx, keyID)

// List keys for a user
keys, err := service.List(ctx, ownerID)

// List keys for an organization
keys, err := service.ListByOrganization(ctx, orgID)

// Revoke a key
err := service.Revoke(ctx, keyID, "Compromised")

// Delete a key
err := service.Delete(ctx, keyID)

// Record usage (call after validation)
err := service.RecordUsage(ctx, keyID, clientIP)

docs.title: Middleware Integration
docs.text:
import (
    "github.com/plexusone/systemforge/session/middleware"
)

// Use the built-in middleware
apiAuth := middleware.APIKeyAuth(middleware.APIKeyConfig{
    Service:      service,
    RecordUsage:  true,
    ContextKey:   "api_key",
})

// Apply to routes
r.Route("/api/v1", func(r chi.Router) {
    r.Use(apiAuth)
    r.Get("/projects", listProjects)
})

// Access in handler
func listProjects(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    principal := middleware.GetPrincipal(r.Context())
    // principal.ID = owner_id
    // principal.Scopes = granted scopes
}

docs.title: Managed Principals
docs.text:
A managed principal is a human with at least one active manager: an account created and controlled by people who have a verified email. The managed principal may have an email of its own or none. SystemForge provides the primitive; applications supply the meaning. A learning application maps a child to a managed principal and a teacher or parent to a manager, but the same shape fits a caregiver and a dependent, a coach and an athlete, or an organization provisioning an account a person claims later.

Email stays required by default. Managed principals exist only where a deployment and an OAuth client both opt in, and the design of record is ADR-005.

docs.title: The Primitive
docs.text:
A managed principal is an ordinary Principal(type=human) with a Human row and an active manager relationship. Management comes from the relationship, not from the email (ADR-009):
