Field Value identifier human:<principal-id> without an email, a lookup key and never an address; the email when there is one capabilities can_access_ui only: no profile management, no delegation sf_humans.email Optional; unverified when given at creation

SystemForge enforces these invariants, transactionally:

  1. A managed principal has at least one active manager unless it has a verified email. Removing the last manager of a principal without one is refused with ErrLastManager; deactivate or delete the principal instead.
  2. A manager is an active human with an email who is not itself managed.
  3. Managed principals are created only when the deployment and the requesting client both allow them.
  4. A managed principal may have an email, from creation (CreateInput.Email, unverified until VerifyEmail) or attached later (AttachVerifiedEmail). It stays managed; the verified email is what allows its last manager to be removed.
  5. A principal with no manager cannot be given one by a manager (AddManager and claims return ErrNotManaged): entering management takes the principal's own consent.

docs.title: Enabling
docs.text:
Both switches default to off. In the SystemAuth configuration:

managed_principals:
  enabled: true
  login_token_ttl: 720h        # default lifetime of reusable login tokens
  login_token_max_ttl: 9600h   # ceiling on any login token
  single_use_token_ttl: 20m    # default lifetime of single-use tokens

clients:
  - id: learning-app
    managed_principals: true
    login_token_ttl: 7200h     # optional: this client's own default

Dynamically registered clients carry the same settings on OAuthApp (managed_principals_enabled, login_token_ttl). The single check every path uses is (*systemauth.Server).ManagedPrincipalsAllowed(ctx, clientID).

docs.title: Roles
docs.text:
Two manager roles are built in:

Role Authority guardian Full control: consent, deletion, billing, credentials, and adding or removing other managers educator Operational control: credentials, profile reads, and issuing a claim so a guardian can join. No deletion, billing, or consent

They are relations on principal in the base authorization schema, with these platform permissions:

Permission Granted to manage_account guardian manage_credentials guardian, educator view_profile guardian, educator manage_managers guardian

An educator cannot delete a managed principal, even one that never received a guardian; that is a guardian or platform-administrator action.

Applications may register further roles with managedprincipal.WithRoles. They grant no platform permissions; give them meaning in the application's authorization facets (see Authorization).

docs.title: Creating a Managed Principal
docs.text:
svc := managedprincipal.NewService(entClient, systemAuthServer,
    managedprincipal.WithAuditEmitter(auditEmitter),
    managedprincipal.WithAuthzSyncer(syncer, authz.SyncModeStrict),
)

learnerID, err := svc.Create(ctx, managedprincipal.CreateInput{
    ClientID:    "learning-app",
    DisplayName: "Robin",
    Managers: []managedprincipal.ManagerInput{
        {PrincipalID: teacherID, Role: managedprincipal.RoleEducator},
    },
    ActorID: teacherID,
})

The principal, its human row, and its manager relationships are written in one transaction. Nobody becomes a manager without agreeing: Create names only the acting manager, and other managers join by accepting an invitation or redeeming a claim. RemoveManager deactivates a relationship. Every action is audited through contract/audit.

Trusted administrator tooling, such as a migration, can build the service with managedprincipal.WithDirectManagerAdds(). Create may then name other managers, and AddManager attaches one directly; it is idempotent and reactivates a removed relationship. Without the option both return ErrConsentRequired.

docs.title: Sign-in with Login Tokens
docs.text:
A login token is a manager-issued sign-in secret for a managed principal. Applications render it as a QR code, a printed card, or a link; SystemForge does not care which.

tok, err := svc.IssueLoginToken(ctx, managedprincipal.IssueLoginTokenInput{
    ManagedID: learnerID,
    ClientID:  "learning-app",
    IssuedBy:  teacherID,
    Name:      "Robin's card",
})
// tok.PlainToken is shown once; only its hash is stored.

Tokens are SFLT followed by 52 uppercase letters and digits, so a QR code can encode them in alphanumeric mode, and typed entry tolerates lowercase, spaces, and hyphens. The issuer must be an active manager.

The lifetime resolves at issue time:

  1. An explicit ExpiresAt on the request.
  2. Else, for a reusable token, the client's login_token_ttl; else the deployment's login_token_ttl (30 days by default).
  3. Else, for a single-use token, single_use_token_ttl (20 minutes by default).
  4. Never beyond login_token_max_ttl (400 days by default); longer requests are clamped and the clamp is logged.

The 30-day default suits a general SaaS platform; a learning application typically sets a term or a school year on its client.

docs.title: Exchanging a Token
docs.text:
The application posts the token to SystemAuth:

POST /login-token
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

token=SFLT...&client_id=learning-app&return_to=/play

On success SystemAuth establishes its usual login session cookie and answers 303 See Other to return_to (checked against the redirect allowlist) or the default target. The authorization-code flow then proceeds as for any signed-in user.

Unknown, malformed, expired, revoked, and used tokens, a client that does not allow managed principals, and an inactive principal all receive the same 401. The endpoint is rate limited per source address (60 a minute by default, enough for a class signing in from one network) and per client (600 a minute); configure shared storage with systemauth.WithLoginTokenRateLimit when several instances serve it. A single-use token succeeds at most once, even when presented concurrently.

docs.title: Claims
docs.text: ID tokens and userinfo for a managed principal carry "managed": true, whatever scopes were granted, and omit email and email_verified when the principal has no email. Relying parties read it into relyingparty.VerifiedIdentity.Managed; the relying-party layer creates a managed principal locally on its first sign-in and never links one by email, so an application's PrincipalStore.CreatePrincipal must accept an identity with or without an email when Managed is set.

docs.title: Ending and Entering Management
docs.text:
Release ends management of a principal with a verified email: its managers are removed and its default human capabilities restored, as one audited event. Without a verified email it returns ErrEmailNotVerified; removing the last manager of a principal with one has the same effect.

err := svc.Release(ctx, guardianID, studentID) // needs manage_managers

A self-managed human enters management only by consent. A prospective manager invites its verified address, and the person accepts while signed in:

inv, err := svc.InviteManager(ctx, managedprincipal.InviteManagerInput{
    ClientID: "match-app", ManagerID: familyMemberID,
    Email: "adult@example.com", Role: managedprincipal.RoleGuardian,
})
// deliver inv.Token; then, as the signed-in invitee:
managerID, err := svc.AcceptManagerInvite(ctx, token, signedInPrincipalID)

An invitation is single use, expires after seven days, and matches only a principal whose verified email is the invited address.

docs.title: Authorization and the HTTP API
docs.text:
Every service operation consults the authorizer, so a Go caller and the HTTP handler are held to the same rules:

Operation Needs Create The actor is the only named manager, or a platform administrator; other managers need WithDirectManagerAdds AddManager WithDirectManagerAdds, and manage_managers (guardians) RemoveManager, Release manage_managers (guardians) Delete, AttachVerifiedEmail manage_account (guardians) IssueClaim, IssueLoginToken, tokens, sessions manage_credentials (guardians, educators); a role registered with WithRoles cannot issue a login token RedeemClaim A valid manager claimant, and an issuer that still holds manage_credentials

Delete deactivates the principal and erases what identifies or authenticates the person (email, names, credentials, sessions, consents), keeping the row so identifiers elsewhere keep resolving; data the application keeps is its own to remove.

managedprincipal.NewHandler(svc) serves the same operations as JSON; see the route list in the architecture page.

docs.title: Relying Parties: the API on SystemAuth
docs.text:
When a host builds SystemAuth with systemauthsvc and enables managed principals, SystemAuth serves the API to applications composed beside it, in the same process or another, at /managed-principals (systemauthsvc.ManagedPrincipalsPath). The principals stay in SystemAuth's database; an application keeps only their IDs.

Each call carries the signed-in manager's SystemAuth access token, granted the systemforge:managed_principals scope (managedprincipal.Scope). The manager is the actor, and the application is the client the token was issued to: that client must allow managed principals, and a body naming another client is refused. Give the client the scope and the opt-in:

managed_principals:
  enabled: true

clients:
  - id: learning-app
    managed_principals: true
    scopes: [openid, profile, email, systemforge:managed_principals]

The API differs from the in-process handler in a few ways:

  • Creation names only the caller as manager, by role. Further managers join with their consent, through an invitation or a claim; POST /{id}/managers is refused.
  • One answer for strangers. An unknown principal, one that is not managed, and one the caller does not manage all answer 403, so the API cannot be asked who is a managed principal.
  • Codes are rate limited per caller: 10 a minute by default across claim redemption and invitation answers (managedprincipal.DefaultCodeLimit). Pass shared storage in systemauthsvc.Options.ManagedPrincipalRates when several instances serve SystemAuth.
  • No email attachment. A relying party cannot prove an address belongs to the principal, so AttachVerifiedEmail stays an in-process operation.

systemauthsvc.Options.AuditEmitter records every write, and Options.ManagedPrincipalOptions passes roles, an authorizer or an authz syncer to the service. A host in the same process can call Service.ManagedPrincipals() directly.

Applications call the API with managedprincipal/mpclient, which depends on the standard library and uuid only:

mp := mpclient.New("https://auth.example.com/managed-principals", httpClient)

id, err := mp.Create(ctx, managerToken, mpclient.CreateInput{
    DisplayName: "Robin",
    Role:        mpclient.RoleEducator,
})
card, err := mp.IssueLoginToken(ctx, managerToken, id, mpclient.IssueLoginTokenInput{Name: "Robin's card"})
// card.Token is shown once; render it as a QR code or a printed card.

Errors match mpclient.ErrUnauthorized, ErrForbidden, ErrNotFound, ErrInvalidCode, ErrInvalidRequest, ErrConflict, and ErrRateLimited with errors.Is, and unwrap to *mpclient.APIError for the status, message and RetryAfter. The managed principal then signs in at POST /login-token as described in Exchanging a Token.

docs.title: Manager Visibility and Revocation
docs.text:
Managers holding manage_credentials can see and end every way a managed principal is signed in:

Method Covers ListLoginTokens, RevokeLoginToken Live login tokens, never their values ListSessions, RevokeSession Browser login sessions, OAuth token families, principal token families RevokeAll All of the above, in one transaction

Revoking a token family revokes all its tokens, so a refresh token cannot renew it. managedprincipal.NewHandler serves these as JSON for the manager identified by requestprincipal:

router.With(requestprincipal.Middleware(opts, authenticators...)).
    Mount("/managed-principals", managedprincipal.NewHandler(svc))

GET    /managed-principals/{id}/login-tokens
POST   /managed-principals/{id}/login-tokens
DELETE /managed-principals/{id}/login-tokens/{credentialID}
GET    /managed-principals/{id}/sessions
DELETE /managed-principals/{id}/sessions/{kind}/{sessionID}
POST   /managed-principals/{id}/revoke-all

Permissions are checked through an authz.Authorizer. The default is the simple provider backed by the service's ManagerRoles; pass managedprincipal.WithAuthorizer to use SpiceDB or to add a platform-administrator check.

docs.title: Claiming a Managed Principal
docs.text:
A teacher often creates the account before any parent is involved. A manager with manage_credentials issues a claim, a single-use code handed to the parent on paper or as a QR code:

claim, err := svc.IssueClaim(ctx, teacherID, learnerID)
// claim.Code is shown once; claim.ExpiresAt is seven days out by default.

learnerID, err = svc.RedeemClaim(ctx, code, parentID)
// The parent is now a guardian of the learner.

The claimant must be an active human with an email who is not managed. Claims are stored hashed in their own table, apart from credentials, so a claim code can never sign anyone in. WithClaimTTL changes the lifetime.

docs.title: Attaching an Email
docs.text:
When a managed principal is ready for its own account, a guardian attaches an email:

err := svc.AttachVerifiedEmail(ctx, parentID, learnerID, "robin@example.com", verifiedAt)

The email becomes the identifier and default human capabilities are restored, so the principal can set a password and manage its own profile. Manager relationships remain until removed, and now the last one may be. The caller must have verified that the principal controls the address.

docs.title: Authorization
docs.text:
The base SpiceDB schema defines:

definition principal {
    relation guardian: principal
    relation educator: principal

    permission manage_account     = guardian
    permission manage_credentials = guardian + educator
    permission view_profile       = guardian + educator
    permission manage_managers    = guardian
}

With WithAuthzSyncer, every committed relationship change is written to the authorization backend. The simple provider stores nothing; configure it with simple.WithManagerRoleGetter(svc.ManagerRoles) and it applies the same table, so both providers agree.

Applications add domain permissions in their own definitions, for example a learner's progress record, which the learner's managers and the organization's administrators may view:

definition learning_progress {
    relation learner: principal
    relation org: organization
    permission view = learner->view_profile + org->manage
}

docs.title: Other Surfaces
docs.text: Surface Behavior Password and social login A missing email never matches; managed principals have no password until an email is attached Invitations and signup Target an email; they never create managed principals SCIM Managed principals are not SCIM users: they are not listed, changed, or grouped through SCIM Marketplace stripe.WithPurchaserChecker(svc) refuses checkout with marketplace.ErrManagedPurchaser; billing is a guardian's action

docs.title: Application Responsibilities
docs.text: SystemForge supplies a manager with the authority to consent and delete. It does not record consent, ages, or regulatory evidence; the application records what its jurisdiction requires.

docs.title: Memberships
docs.text: A membership links a principal to an organization with a role. Any principal type can be a member, though most memberships belong to humans.

docs.title: Schema
docs.text:
The sf_principal_memberships table contains:

Field Type Description id UUID Primary key principal_id UUID The member principal organization_id UUID The organization role string Role within the organization permissions JSON Optional fine-grained permissions (string list) active bool Whether the membership is in effect created_at, updated_at time Timestamps

Unique constraint: one membership per principal per organization.

docs.title: The active Flag
docs.text: active lets a membership be suspended without deleting it. A membership that is inactive should be treated as absent for access decisions. The SCIM store returns only active memberships and reactivates an existing row when a member is re-added. organization.Service.ListMembers and ListMemberships return only active memberships unless organization.IncludeInactive() is passed; GetMembership returns the row whatever its active value.

docs.title: Roles
docs.text: Roles are strings, so each application defines its own vocabulary. The organization roles of the platform are owner, admin, member and collaborator (editor and viewer were retired; migration 0008 maps them to member and collaborator). A collaborator has no organization-wide access and holds roles on individual resources instead; see Authorization conventions for registering domain roles.

docs.title: Managing Memberships
docs.text:
Use the organization service, which also syncs membership changes to the authorization backend:

import "github.com/plexusone/systemforge/identity/organization"

orgs := organization.NewService(client)

m, err := orgs.AddMember(ctx, organization.AddMemberInput{
    OrganizationID: orgID,
    PrincipalID:    principalID,
    Role:           "member",
    Permissions:    []string{"projects:export"},
})

AddMember returns an error if the principal is already a member.

docs.title: Change Role or Suspend
docs.text:
role := "admin"
m, err := orgs.UpdateMember(ctx, membershipID, organization.UpdateMemberInput{Role: &role})

inactive := false
m, err = orgs.UpdateMember(ctx, membershipID, organization.UpdateMemberInput{Active: &inactive})

docs.title: Remove
docs.text: err := orgs.RemoveMember(ctx, orgID, principalID)

docs.title: Querying Memberships
docs.text:
// One principal's membership in one organization.
m, err := orgs.GetMembership(ctx, orgID, principalID)

// Everyone in an organization.
members, err := orgs.ListMembers(ctx, orgID)

// Every organization a principal belongs to.
memberships, err := orgs.ListMemberships(ctx, principalID)

docs.title: With Ent Directly
docs.text:
import "github.com/plexusone/systemforge/identity/ent/principalmembership"

admins, err := client.PrincipalMembership.Query().
    Where(
        principalmembership.OrganizationIDEQ(orgID),
        principalmembership.ActiveEQ(true),
        principalmembership.RoleIn("owner", "admin"),
    ).
    WithPrincipal().
    All(ctx)

for _, m := range admins {
    fmt.Printf("Admin: %s\n", m.Edges.Principal.DisplayName)
}

docs.title: Role Hierarchy
docs.text:
Implement a role hierarchy in your application:

var roleLevel = map[string]int{
    "owner":        100,
    "admin":        80,
    "member":       40,
    "collaborator": 20,
}

func HasMinRole(m *organization.Membership, required string) bool {
    return m.Active && roleLevel[m.Role] >= roleLevel[required]
}

docs.title: Permission Checks
docs.text:
func HasPermission(m *organization.Membership, permission string) bool {
    if !m.Active {
        return false
    }
    if m.Role == "owner" {
        return true
    }
    return slices.Contains(m.Permissions, permission)
}

docs.title: Ownership Transfer
docs.text:
Transfer organization ownership from one member to another:

err := orgs.TransferOwnership(ctx, organization.TransferOwnershipInput{
    OrganizationID: orgID,
    FromPrincipal:  currentOwnerID,
    ToPrincipal:    newOwnerID,
    NewRoleForOld:  "admin", // or "member"; defaults to "admin"
})

docs.title: Validation Rules
docs.text:
• The current owner must have the owner role
  • The new owner must be an existing member
  • The new role for the previous owner must be admin or member
  • Ownership cannot be transferred to yourself

docs.title: Transaction Safety
docs.text:
The transfer runs in one transaction:

  1. Demote the current owner to the specified role (default admin)
  2. Promote the new owner to owner
  3. Update the organization's owner_principal_id
  4. Sync the changes to the authorization backend

docs.title: API Endpoint
docs.text:
POST /organizations/{slug}/transfer-ownership

Request body:

{
  "new_owner_principal_id": "uuid",
  "new_role_for_old_owner": "admin"
}

Response:

{
  "message": "Ownership transferred successfully"
}

Only the current owner can transfer ownership.

docs.title: OAuth Client
docs.text: The identity/oauthclient package provides utilities for accepting OAuth logins from external providers (GitHub, Google, SystemAuth) in your application.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
This package handles the client-side of OAuth flows where your app is the relying party accepting logins from external identity providers. This is different from the oauth package which implements an OAuth server.

It is the single sanctioned place in SystemForge that talks to github.com and google.com. The former session/oauth package was folded into it and removed. SystemAuth's built-in GitHub/Google login (see SystemAuth Social Login) is built on this package; prefer federating to SystemAuth over wiring social login into each application.

docs.title: Supported Providers
docs.text:
• GitHub - OAuth 2.0 with user/email scopes
  • Google - OpenID Connect with profile scopes
  • SystemAuth - SystemForge's identity provider

docs.title: 1. Configure OAuth Provider
docs.text:
import cfoauth "github.com/plexusone/systemforge/identity/oauthclient"

// GitHub configuration
githubCfg := cfoauth.GitHubConfig(cfoauth.ProviderConfig{
    ClientID:     os.Getenv("GITHUB_CLIENT_ID"),
    ClientSecret: os.Getenv("GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET"),
    RedirectURL:  "http://localhost:8080/auth/oauth/github/callback",
    Scopes:       []string{"read:user", "user:email"},
})

// Google configuration
googleCfg := cfoauth.GoogleConfig(cfoauth.ProviderConfig{
    ClientID:     os.Getenv("GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID"),
    ClientSecret: os.Getenv("GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET"),
    RedirectURL:  "http://localhost:8080/auth/oauth/google/callback",
    Scopes:       []string{"openid", "email", "profile"},
})

docs.title: 2. Generate State for CSRF Protection
docs.text:
state, err := cfoauth.GenerateState()
if err != nil {
    return err
}
// Store state in session/cookie for validation in callback

docs.title: 3. Redirect to Provider
docs.text:
func handleGitHubRedirect(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    state, _ := cfoauth.GenerateState()
    // Store state in cookie or session

    cfg := cfoauth.GitHubConfig(providerConfig)
    redirectURL := cfg.AuthCodeURL(state)

    http.Redirect(w, r, redirectURL, http.StatusFound)
}

docs.title: 4. Handle Callback
docs.text:
func handleGitHubCallback(ctx context.Context, code string) (*cfoauth.User, error) {
    cfg := cfoauth.GitHubConfig(providerConfig)

    // Exchanges code for tokens and fetches user info in one call
    user, err := cfoauth.FetchGitHubUser(ctx, cfg, code)
    if err != nil {
        return nil, err
    }

    return user, nil
}

docs.title: Connector
docs.text:
Connector bundles the OAuth2 config, the profile API location, and an optional HTTP client. Endpoint fields are overridable (tests, GitHub Enterprise):

gh := cfoauth.NewGitHubConnector(cfoauth.ProviderConfig{
    ClientID:     os.Getenv("GITHUB_CLIENT_ID"),
    ClientSecret: os.Getenv("GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET"),
    RedirectURL:  "https://auth.example.com/login/github/callback",
})

verifier := oauth2.GenerateVerifier()
authURL := gh.AuthCodeURL(state, oauth2.S256ChallengeOption(verifier))

// in the callback
token, err := gh.Exchange(ctx, code, oauth2.VerifierOption(verifier))
user, err := gh.FetchUser(ctx, token)

docs.title: User Struct
docs.text:
All providers return a normalized User struct:

type User struct {
    ProviderID   string         // Unique ID from the provider
    Provider     string         // "github", "google", "systemauth"
    Email        string         // User's email address
    EmailVerified bool          // Provider asserts the user controls Email
    Name         string         // Display name
    AvatarURL    string         // Profile picture URL
    Username     string         // Username (GitHub) or empty
    AccessToken  string         // OAuth access token
    RefreshToken string         // OAuth refresh token (if provided)
    TokenExpiry  time.Time      // When access token expires
    Raw          map[string]any // Raw response data
}

docs.title: State Management
docs.text:
The package includes a StateManager for cookie-based CSRF protection:

// Create state manager (defaults to Secure: true, requires HTTPS)
stateManager := cfoauth.NewStateManager()

// For local development over HTTP only:
// stateManager := cfoauth.NewStateManagerInsecure()

// In redirect handler: set state cookie
func handleRedirect(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    state, _ := cfoauth.GenerateState()
    stateManager.SetStateCookie(w, state)

    redirectURL := oauthConfig.AuthCodeURL(state)
    http.Redirect(w, r, redirectURL, http.StatusFound)
}

// In callback handler: validate state
func handleCallback(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    state := r.URL.Query().Get("state")

    if !stateManager.ValidateState(w, r, state) {
        http.Error(w, "Invalid state", http.StatusBadRequest)
        return
    }

    // State is valid, continue with code exchange...
}

docs.title: Server-side state store
docs.text:
StateStore keeps per-flow data (provider, validated post-login redirect, PKCE verifier) server-side. Take is single-use. MemoryStateStore is concurrency-safe but single-instance only; supply a shared implementation when running multiple replicas.

store := cfoauth.NewMemoryStateStore()
_ = store.Put(ctx, state, cfoauth.StateData{Provider: cfoauth.ProviderGitHub, PKCEVerifier: verifier}, 10*time.Minute)
data, err := store.Take(ctx, state) // cfoauth.ErrInvalidState if unknown/expired/reused

docs.title: Complete Example
docs.text:
package main

import (
    "context"
    "net/http"

    cfoauth "github.com/plexusone/systemforge/identity/oauthclient"
)

type AuthHandler struct {
    githubConfig *oauth2.Config
    googleConfig *oauth2.Config
    stateManager *cfoauth.StateManager
    userService  *UserService
}

func NewAuthHandler(cfg *Config) *AuthHandler {
    return &AuthHandler{
        githubConfig: cfoauth.GitHubConfig(cfoauth.ProviderConfig{
            ClientID:     cfg.GitHubClientID,
            ClientSecret: cfg.GitHubClientSecret,
            RedirectURL:  cfg.GitHubCallbackURL,
            Scopes:       []string{"read:user", "user:email"},
        }),
        googleConfig: cfoauth.GoogleConfig(cfoauth.ProviderConfig{
            ClientID:     cfg.GoogleClientID,
            ClientSecret: cfg.GoogleClientSecret,
            RedirectURL:  cfg.GoogleCallbackURL,
            Scopes:       []string{"openid", "email", "profile"},
        }),
        stateManager: cfoauth.NewStateManager(), // Secure by default
    }
}

func (h *AuthHandler) GitHubRedirect(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    state, _ := cfoauth.GenerateState()
    h.stateManager.SetStateCookie(w, state)
    http.Redirect(w, r, h.githubConfig.AuthCodeURL(state), http.StatusFound)
}

func (h *AuthHandler) GitHubCallback(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    ctx := r.Context()

    // Validate state
    state := r.URL.Query().Get("state")
    if !h.stateManager.ValidateState(w, r, state) {
        http.Error(w, "Invalid state", http.StatusBadRequest)
        return
    }

    // Exchange code and fetch user
    code := r.URL.Query().Get("code")
    oauthUser, err := cfoauth.FetchGitHubUser(ctx, h.githubConfig, code)
    if err != nil {
        http.Error(w, "OAuth failed", http.StatusInternalServerError)
        return
    }

    // Find or create local user
    user, err := h.userService.FindOrCreateFromOAuth(ctx, oauthUser)
    if err != nil {
        http.Error(w, "User creation failed", http.StatusInternalServerError)
        return
    }

    // Generate session/JWT and redirect
    // ...
}

docs.title: GitHub
docs.text:
• Default scopes: user:email
  • Use read:user for profile access without write permissions
  • Email may be private; the package fetches from /user/emails if needed
  • EmailVerified is set from /user/emails; a public profile email whose verification cannot be confirmed (e.g. missing user:email scope) is reported as unverified

docs.title: Google
docs.text:
• Uses OpenID Connect
  • Default scopes: openid, email, profile
  • ProviderID is the Google sub claim
  • EmailVerified is the userinfo email_verified claim

docs.title: SystemAuth
docs.text:
SystemAuth is SystemForge's identity provider for SSO across SystemForge apps:

ccConfig := cfoauth.SystemAuthConfig{
    ProviderConfig: cfoauth.ProviderConfig{
        ClientID:     os.Getenv("SYSTEMAUTH_CLIENT_ID"),
        ClientSecret: os.Getenv("SYSTEMAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET"),
        RedirectURL:  "http://localhost:8080/auth/oauth/systemauth/callback",
        Scopes:       []string{"openid", "profile", "email"},
    },
    BaseURL: "https://auth.example.com",
}

oauth2Config := ccConfig.OAuth2Config()

docs.title: Integration with Session/JWT
docs.text:
After OAuth callback, generate your app's session tokens:

import cfjwt "github.com/plexusone/systemforge/session/jwt"

func (h *AuthHandler) GitHubCallback(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    // ... OAuth validation and user fetch ...

    // Generate JWT tokens for your app
    jwtService := cfjwt.NewService(jwtConfig)
    tokens, err := jwtService.GenerateTokenPair(user.ID, user.Email, user.Username)
    if err != nil {
        return err
    }

    // Return tokens to client
    json.NewEncoder(w).Encode(map[string]any{
        "access_token":  tokens.AccessToken,
        "refresh_token": tokens.RefreshToken,
        "expires_in":    tokens.ExpiresIn,
    })
}

docs.title: Linking Provider Logins to Principals
docs.text:
SystemForge keys every upstream login by its (provider, subject) pair and links it to a human principal as an external identity. systemauth.ResolveExternalLogin implements the account-linking rules over a systemauth.PrincipalDirectory:

  1. If the (provider, subject) pair is already linked, that principal signs in, regardless of the email the provider reports today.
  2. Otherwise a verified upstream email links to an existing principal whose own email is also verified.
  3. Otherwise a new human principal is created, which requires a verified email.

An unverified email never links to or creates an account.

import (
    "errors"
    "time"

    cfoauth "github.com/plexusone/systemforge/identity/oauthclient"
    "github.com/plexusone/systemforge/identity/systemauth"
)

// dir := systemauth.NewEntPrincipalDirectory(client)
func signIn(ctx context.Context, dir systemauth.PrincipalDirectory, u *cfoauth.User) (*systemauth.HumanPrincipal, error) {
    p, err := systemauth.ResolveExternalLogin(ctx, dir, systemauth.ExternalLogin{
        Provider:      u.Provider,
        Subject:       u.ProviderID,
        Email:         u.Email,
        EmailVerified: u.EmailVerified,
        Name:          u.Name,
        AvatarURL:     u.AvatarURL,
    }, time.Now())
    switch {
    case errors.Is(err, systemauth.ErrEmailNotVerified):
        // The provider did not assert a verified email; ask the user to verify it.
    case errors.Is(err, systemauth.ErrEmailConflict):
        // An account with this email exists but cannot be linked automatically.
    case errors.Is(err, systemauth.ErrPrincipalInactive):
        // The principal is deactivated.
    }
    return p, err
}

The returned HumanPrincipal.ID is the principal ID to issue tokens for. NewEntPrincipalDirectory stores principals in sf_principals and sf_humans and links in sf_external_identities; NewMemoryPrincipalDirectory is available for development and tests. SystemAuth's built-in social login uses this same resolver, so a person who signs in through your application and through SystemAuth resolves to one principal.

docs.title: Security Considerations
docs.text:
1. Always validate state - Use StateManager or your own CSRF protection
  2. Use HTTPS in production - NewStateManager() defaults to Secure: true; only use NewStateManagerInsecure() for local HTTP development
  3. Store tokens securely - Encrypt any provider tokens you keep at rest
  4. Validate email ownership - Key accounts by Provider + ProviderID; only use Email to link to an existing account when EmailVerified is true
  5. Check token expiry - Refresh tokens before they expire

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text:
• Organizations - Multi-tenant user management
  • API Keys - Server-to-server authentication
  • Authorization - SpiceDB integration

docs.title: Organizations
docs.text: Organizations represent tenants in a multi-tenant application.

docs.title: Schema
docs.text:
The sf_organizations table contains:

Field Type Description id UUID Primary key name string Display name slug string URL-safe identifier logo_url string Organization logo settings JSON Custom configuration org_type enum personal, team (default) or enterprise owner_principal_id UUID Owner of a personal organization active bool Organization status created_at time Creation timestamp updated_at time Last modification

docs.title: No plan column
docs.text: An organization has no plan. What it may use is its entitlements, derived from its marketplace subscriptions and licenses; see Entitlements via the marketplace. Existing databases drop the column with migrations/0004_drop_organization_plan.sql.

docs.title: Creating Organizations
docs.text:
org, err := client.Organization.Create().
    SetName("Acme Corporation").
    SetSlug("acme-corp").
    SetSettings(map[string]any{
        "timezone": "America/New_York",
        "features": []string{"advanced_analytics"},
    }).
    Save(ctx)

docs.title: Slugs
docs.text:
Slugs must be unique and URL-safe:

import "github.com/gosimple/slug"

orgSlug := slug.Make("Acme Corporation") // "acme-corporation"

org, err := client.Organization.Create().
    SetName("Acme Corporation").
    SetSlug(orgSlug).
    Save(ctx)

docs.title: By Slug
docs.text:
org, err := client.Organization.Query().
    Where(organization.SlugEQ("acme-corp")).
    Only(ctx)

docs.title: A Principal's Organizations
docs.text:
orgs, err := client.Organization.Query().
    Where(organization.HasPrincipalMembershipsWith(
        principalmembership.PrincipalIDEQ(principalID),
        principalmembership.ActiveEQ(true),
    )).
    All(ctx)

docs.title: With Members
docs.text:
org, err := client.Organization.Query().
    Where(organization.IDEQ(orgID)).
    WithPrincipalMemberships(func(q *ent.PrincipalMembershipQuery) {
        q.WithPrincipal()
    }).
    Only(ctx)

for _, m := range org.Edges.PrincipalMemberships {
    fmt.Printf("Member: %s, Role: %s\n", m.Edges.Principal.DisplayName, m.Role)
}

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
Organization settings store custom configuration:

// Update settings
org, err := client.Organization.UpdateOneID(orgID).
    SetSettings(map[string]any{
        "timezone": "Europe/London",
        "branding": map[string]any{
            "primary_color": "#3B82F6",
            "logo_url": "https://example.com/logo.png",
        },
    }).
    Save(ctx)

// Read settings
timezone := org.Settings["timezone"].(string)

docs.title: Feature Checks
docs.text: Gate a feature on the organization's entitlements, not on a plan value. Each OrgResponse carries an entitlements list, and application roles can be granted only for entitled applications; see Application roles and entitlements.

docs.title: Organization Edges
docs.text:
Organizations have relationships to:

Edge Target Description principal_memberships PrincipalMembership Organization members principals Principal Principals scoped to the organization oauth_apps OAuthApp OAuth apps owned by org owner Principal Owner of a personal organization

docs.title: Scope All Queries to Organization
docs.text:
func getHumansInOrg(ctx context.Context, client *ent.Client, orgID uuid.UUID) ([]*ent.Principal, error) {
    return client.Principal.Query().
        Where(
            principal.TypeEQ(principal.TypeHuman),
            principal.HasPrincipalMembershipsWith(
                principalmembership.OrganizationIDEQ(orgID),
                principalmembership.ActiveEQ(true),
            ),
        ).
        WithHuman().
        All(ctx)
}

docs.title: Organization Context
docs.text:
Store organization ID in context for automatic scoping:

type contextKey string

const orgKey contextKey = "organization_id"

func WithOrganization(ctx context.Context, orgID uuid.UUID) context.Context {
    return context.WithValue(ctx, orgKey, orgID)
}

func OrganizationFromContext(ctx context.Context) uuid.UUID {
    orgID, _ := ctx.Value(orgKey).(uuid.UUID)
    return orgID
}

docs.title: Identity Module Overview
docs.text: The Identity module provides principal and organization management for multi-tenant SaaS applications.

docs.title: Principals
docs.text:
A principal is any actor that can authenticate: a human, an OAuth application, an AI agent, or a backend service. Every principal is a row in sf_principals, with a one-to-one extension table for its type. A person is a human principal; there is no separate user table. See Humans.

import "github.com/plexusone/systemforge/identity/principal"

principals := principal.NewService(client)

p, err := principals.CreateHuman(ctx, principal.CreateHumanInput{
    Email:       "user@example.com",
    DisplayName: "Jane Doe",
})

docs.title: Organizations
docs.text:
Organizations (tenants) group principals with shared resources. Each organization has its own settings, members, and data.

org, err := client.Organization.Create().
    SetName("Acme Corp").
    SetSlug("acme-corp").
    SetPlan("pro").
    Save(ctx)

docs.title: Memberships
docs.text:
Memberships link principals to organizations with a role, and can be suspended with their active flag. See Memberships.

import "github.com/plexusone/systemforge/identity/organization"

orgs := organization.NewService(client)

m, err := orgs.AddMember(ctx, organization.AddMemberInput{
    OrganizationID: org.ID,
    PrincipalID:    p.ID,
    Role:           "admin",
})

docs.title: Credentials
docs.text: Passwords, API keys, client secrets, and public keys are rows in sf_credentials, typed and owned by a principal, and managed by identity/credential.

docs.title: Database Schema
docs.text:
All tables use the sf_ prefix:

Table Description sf_principals Every actor: humans, applications, agents, services sf_humans Human extension (email, names, avatar, platform admin) sf_applications OAuth application extension sf_agents AI agent extension sf_service_principals Backend service extension sf_organizations Organizations (tenants) sf_principal_memberships Principal-organization memberships sf_credentials Passwords, API keys, client secrets, keypairs sf_external_identities Linked upstream logins (GitHub, Google, federation) sf_principal_tokens Tokens issued to principals

docs.title: Multi-Tenancy
docs.text:
Every resource can be scoped to an organization. To find the human members of an organization:

import (
    entprincipal "github.com/plexusone/systemforge/identity/ent/principal"
    "github.com/plexusone/systemforge/identity/ent/principalmembership"
)

members, err := client.Principal.Query().
    Where(
        entprincipal.TypeEQ(entprincipal.TypeHuman),
        entprincipal.HasPrincipalMembershipsWith(
            principalmembership.OrganizationIDEQ(orgID),
            principalmembership.ActiveEQ(true),
        ),
    ).
    WithHuman().
    All(ctx)

docs.title: Platform Admins
docs.text:
Humans can be marked as platform admins for cross-organization access:

admin := true
_, err := principals.UpdateHuman(ctx, p.ID, principal.UpdateHumanInput{
    IsPlatformAdmin: &admin,
})

docs.title: Upstream Logins
docs.text:
Humans can authenticate through upstream OAuth providers (GitHub, Google, SystemAuth). The OAuth Client package handles the OAuth flow:

import cfoauth "github.com/plexusone/systemforge/identity/oauthclient"

// Exchange an OAuth code for the provider's user info.
info, err := cfoauth.FetchGitHubUser(ctx, githubConfig, code)

The upstream identity is recorded as an external identity on the human principal, keyed by provider and subject, so later logins from the same provider resolve to the same person. SystemAuth's social login does this automatically.

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text:
• Humans - Human principals, passwords, and SystemAuth storage
  • Managed Principals - People without an email, controlled by guardians and educators
  • Organizations - Organization setup
  • Memberships - Role-based membership
  • API Keys - Server-to-server authentication
  • OAuth Client - Accept OAuth logins from GitHub, Google, SystemAuth

docs.title: Account Security
docs.text: SystemForge provides security features for identity management including account lockout protection against brute-force attacks.

docs.title: Account Lockout
docs.text: The lockout package protects against brute-force password attacks by temporarily locking accounts after repeated failed login attempts.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Configurable max attempts and lockout duration
  • Sliding window for attempt tracking
  • Memory and Redis storage backends
  • Manual lock/unlock capabilities
  • Automatic expired lock cleanup

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
import (
    "github.com/plexusone/systemforge/identity/security"
)

// Create a memory store for development
store := security.NewMemoryLockoutStore()

// Create the lockout service
lockout := security.NewLockout(store,
    security.WithMaxAttempts(5),
    security.WithLockoutDuration(15*time.Minute),
)
defer lockout.Close()

// In your login handler
func handleLogin(ctx context.Context, email, password string) error {
    // Check and record in one call (recommended)
    success := validateCredentials(email, password)
    err := lockout.CheckAndRecord(ctx, email, success)
    if err != nil {
        if errors.Is(err, security.ErrAccountLocked) {
            return fmt.Errorf("account locked, try again later")
        }
        return err
    }

    if !success {
        return fmt.Errorf("invalid credentials")
    }

    // Login successful
    return nil
}

docs.title: Lockout Options
docs.text: Option Description Default WithMaxAttempts(n) Failed attempts before lockout 5 WithLockoutDuration(d) How long account stays locked 15 minutes WithLockoutConfig(cfg) Full configuration struct See below

docs.title: Config Struct
docs.text:
cfg := security.LockoutConfig{
    MaxAttempts:     5,                // Lock after 5 failures
    LockoutDuration: 15 * time.Minute, // Lock for 15 minutes
    AttemptWindow:   15 * time.Minute, // Only count recent attempts
    CleanupInterval: 5 * time.Minute,  // Clean up old data every 5 min
}

lockout := security.NewLockout(store, security.WithLockoutConfig(cfg))

docs.title: Memory Store
docs.text:
For development and single-instance deployments:

store := security.NewMemoryLockoutStore(
    security.WithLockoutCleanupInterval(5*time.Minute),
)

docs.title: Redis Store
docs.text:
For production and multi-instance deployments:

import "github.com/redis/go-redis/v9"

client := redis.NewClient(&redis.Options{
    Addr: "localhost:6379",
})

store := security.NewRedisLockoutStore(client,
    security.WithRedisKeyPrefix("myapp:lockout:"),
)

docs.title: Checking Lock Status
docs.text:
// Check if an account is currently locked
locked, err := lockout.IsLocked(ctx, identifier)

// Get detailed status
status, err := lockout.GetStatus(ctx, identifier)
fmt.Printf("Locked: %v\n", status.IsLocked)
fmt.Printf("Failed attempts: %d\n", status.FailedAttempts)
fmt.Printf("Remaining attempts: %d\n", status.RemainingAttempts)
fmt.Printf("Locked until: %v\n", status.LockedUntil)

docs.title: Recording Attempts
docs.text:
// Record a failed attempt (may trigger lockout)
err := lockout.RecordFailure(ctx, identifier)
if errors.Is(err, security.ErrAccountLocked) {
    // Account is now locked
}

// Record a successful login (resets attempt counter)
err := lockout.RecordSuccess(ctx, identifier)

// Combined check-and-record (recommended for login flows)
err := lockout.CheckAndRecord(ctx, identifier, success)

docs.title: Manual Lock Management
docs.text:
// Manually lock an account (e.g., admin action)
err := lockout.Lock(ctx, identifier, time.Now().Add(24*time.Hour))

// Manually unlock an account
err := lockout.Unlock(ctx, identifier)

// Reset all lockout state
err := lockout.Reset(ctx, identifier)

docs.title: Lockout Status
docs.text:
The LockoutStatus struct contains:

type LockoutStatus struct {
    IsLocked          bool      // Account currently locked
    FailedAttempts    int       // Failed attempts in window
    RemainingAttempts int       // Attempts before lockout
    LockedUntil       time.Time // When lock expires
    LastAttempt       time.Time // Last failed attempt time
}

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
1. Use email as identifier: Lock by email/username, not by IP (IPs can be shared)

  2. Show remaining attempts: Help legitimate users avoid lockout 

    status, _ := lockout.GetStatus(ctx, email)
if status.RemainingAttempts <= 2 {
    log.Printf("Warning: %d attempts remaining", status.RemainingAttempts)
}

  3. Combine with rate limiting: Add IP-based rate limiting for defense in depth

  4. Log lockout events: Monitor for attack patterns 

    err := lockout.RecordFailure(ctx, email)
if errors.Is(err, security.ErrAccountLocked) {
    log.Printf("Account locked: %s", email)
    // Alert security team for repeated lockouts
}

  5. Provide recovery path: Allow password reset to unlock accounts

docs.title: Errors
docs.text: Error Description ErrAccountLocked Account is currently locked ErrStorageFailure Storage backend error ErrInvalidThreshold Invalid configuration value

docs.title: Login Tokens
docs.text:
A managed principal signs in with a manager-issued login token, which is password-equivalent for that principal while it is valid. The mitigations are structural:

  • Tokens are 256-bit random values stored only as SHA-256 hashes and compared in constant time; their values appear once, at issue, and never in listings, audit events, or logs.
  • They expire: 30 days by default, never more than the 400-day ceiling, and 20 minutes for single-use tokens, which succeed at most once even under concurrent presentation.
  • The POST /login-token exchange gives every failure the same response and is rate limited per source address and per client.
  • Managed principals carry reduced capabilities: they cannot manage their own profile or delegate.
  • Managers see every live token and session and can revoke any of them, or all at once; every issue and revocation is audited.

Applications that need stronger assurance can issue single-use tokens or add device binding of their own.

docs.title: Humans
docs.text: A person is a human principal: a row in sf_principals with type = human, joined one-to-one with its sf_humans extension. There is no separate user table. Every sign-in method (password, social login, federation sync, SCIM) resolves to the same human principal, so one person has one identity.

docs.title: Schema
docs.text:
sf_principals holds what every principal type shares:

Field Type Description id UUID Primary key, used as the subject (sub) in tokens type enum human, application, agent, or service identifier string Unique lookup key: the email for humans, or human:<id> for a managed principal display_name string Human-readable name organization_id UUID Optional owning organization active bool Whether the principal can authenticate capabilities JSON Principal capabilities allowed_scopes JSON Scopes the principal may request metadata JSON Custom metadata created_at, updated_at time Timestamps

sf_humans holds the human-specific fields:

Field Type Description principal_id UUID The owning principal email string Primary email address; null only for a managed principal given_name, family_name string Name parts avatar_url string Profile picture URL locale, timezone string Preferences is_platform_admin bool Cross-organization admin access last_login_at time Last successful login email_verified_at time When the email was verified

Related records:

  • Passwords are rows in sf_credentials with type password (Argon2id hashes).
  • Upstream logins (GitHub, Google, a federation hub) are rows in sf_external_identities, keyed by provider and subject.
  • Organization memberships are rows in sf_principal_memberships; see Memberships.

docs.title: Creating Humans
docs.text:
Use the principal service, which creates the principal and its human extension in one transaction:

import "github.com/plexusone/systemforge/identity/principal"

principals := principal.NewService(client)

p, err := principals.CreateHuman(ctx, principal.CreateHumanInput{
    Email:       "user@example.com",
    DisplayName: "Jane Doe",
    GivenName:   "Jane",
    FamilyName:  "Doe",
})
if err != nil {
    return err
}
// p.ID is the principal ID; p.Human holds the extension fields.

docs.title: Setting a Password
docs.text:
import "github.com/plexusone/systemforge/identity/credential"

creds := credential.NewService(client)

err := creds.CreatePassword(ctx, credential.CreatePasswordInput{
    PrincipalID: p.ID,
    Password:    password,
})

VerifyPassword and UpdatePassword on the same service check and rotate it. A human without a password credential signs in only through an upstream provider.

docs.title: Email Requirement
docs.text:
Every human has an email unless it is a managed principal: a human whose account is created and controlled by managers with an email, enabled per deployment and per client. Every creation path documented here (the principal service, SystemAuth storage, signup, SCIM, social login, and federation sync) refuses a human without an email; managed principals are created only through identity/managedprincipal. See Managed Principals.

The identifier is a lookup key, not an address: never send mail to it.

docs.title: Email Uniqueness
docs.text: Emails are unique ignoring case. Lookups by email are case-insensitive, and SystemAuth's storage rejects a create or update whose email differs only in case from another human's, so Ada@Example.com and ada@example.com cannot both exist.

docs.title: By ID or Email
docs.text:
p, err := principals.GetByID(ctx, principalID)

// The identifier of a human principal is its email.
p, err = principals.GetByIdentifier(ctx, "user@example.com")

docs.title: With Ent Directly
docs.text:
import (
    "github.com/plexusone/systemforge/identity/ent/human"
    entprincipal "github.com/plexusone/systemforge/identity/ent/principal"
)

p, err := client.Principal.Query().
    Where(
        entprincipal.TypeEQ(entprincipal.TypeHuman),
        entprincipal.HasHumanWith(human.EmailEqualFold("user@example.com")),
    ).
    WithHuman().
    Only(ctx)

docs.title: Updating Humans
docs.text:
name := "Jane Smith"
family := "Smith"

p, err := principals.UpdateHuman(ctx, principalID, principal.UpdateHumanInput{
    UpdateInput: principal.UpdateInput{DisplayName: &name},
    FamilyName:  &family,
})

Deactivate and Reactivate toggle active; a deactivated principal cannot authenticate.

docs.title: SystemAuth Storage
docs.text:
The SystemAuth server works with humans through its Storage interface using one value type, systemauth.HumanPrincipal, which joins a human principal with its extension:

Method Purpose CreateHuman(ctx, h) Create a human; assigns h.ID when it is uuid.Nil GetHuman(ctx, id) Look up by principal ID GetHumanByEmail(ctx, email) Look up by email, ignoring case GetHumanByExternalIdentity(ctx, provider, subject) Look up through a linked upstream identity LinkExternalIdentity(ctx, principalID, provider, subject) Link an upstream identity; relinking the same pair is a no-op UpdateHuman(ctx, h) Replace the profile fields DeleteHuman(ctx, id) Delete the human with its extension, external identities, and credentials

Not-found lookups return systemauth.ErrPrincipalNotFound; a taken email returns systemauth.ErrPrincipalExists; an upstream identity already linked to another human returns systemauth.ErrExternalIdentityExists. Both systemauth.NewEntStorage and systemauth.NewMemoryStorage implement these methods.

docs.title: Password Login
docs.text:
Password login uses an injectable verifier. Because identity IDs are principal IDs, the credential service's VerifyPassword plugs in directly:

creds := credential.NewService(client)

providers := systemauth.NewProvidersFromStorage(
    systemauth.NewEntStorage(client),
    systemauth.WithProviderPasswordVerifier(creds.VerifyPassword),
)

session, err := providers.Authentication.Authenticate(ctx, &systemauth.AuthenticateRequest{
    Method:     systemauth.AuthMethodPassword,
    Identifier: "user@example.com",
    Password:   password,
})

A person who first signed in with a social provider and later sets a password authenticates as the same principal.

docs.title: Federation Sync
docs.text: Identities synced from a federation hub are linked as external identities with the provider systemauth.FederationProvider and the federation identity ID as the subject. Creating an identity whose email already exists links the existing human instead of creating a second one.

docs.title: Platform Admins
docs.text:
is_platform_admin on the human extension grants cross-organization access:

admin := true
_, err := principals.UpdateHuman(ctx, principalID, principal.UpdateHumanInput{
    IsPlatformAdmin: &admin,
})

docs.title: Edges
docs.text:
A human principal relates to:

Edge Target Description human Human Human extension credentials Credential Passwords, API keys, keypairs external_identities ExternalIdentity Linked upstream logins principal_memberships PrincipalMembership Organization memberships principal_tokens PrincipalToken Issued tokens owned_organizations Organization Personal organizations owned_oauth_apps OAuthApp OAuth apps it owns oauth_consents OAuthConsent Consent grants

docs.title: Integrating with Existing Apps
docs.text: This guide covers integrating SystemForge into an existing Go application that already has its own users, organizations, and memberships.

docs.title: How SystemForge Models People
docs.text:
Every actor in SystemForge is a principal. A person is a principal of type human plus a one-to-one Human row with their email and profile. Passwords are credentials, organizations are organizations, and membership links a principal to an organization with a role:

existing tables          SystemForge tables
─────────────────       ──────────────────────────────────────
users            ←──→   sf_principals (type = 'human') + sf_humans
                        sf_credentials (type = 'password')
organizations    ←──→   sf_organizations
user_orgs        ←──→   sf_principal_memberships

See the schema reference for every column.

docs.title: Pattern 1: Side-by-Side Tables
docs.text: Keep your existing tables and add the SystemForge tables alongside them, copying data across and switching reads over time. The migration guide covers the copy in detail.

docs.title: Pattern 2: Extension Tables
docs.text:
Keep app-specific data in your own tables and reference the SystemForge principal by ID:

type UserProfile struct {
    ent.Schema
}

func (UserProfile) Fields() []ent.Field {
    return []ent.Field{
        field.UUID("principal_id", uuid.UUID{}).Unique(),
        field.String("username").Unique(),
        field.String("bio").Optional(),
    }
}

The principal ID is stable across every sign-in method (password, social login, federation, SCIM), so it is the right key for application data.

docs.title: Step 1: Add the Dependency
docs.text: go get github.com/plexusone/systemforge

docs.title: Step 2: Create the SystemForge Tables
docs.text:
Run systemauth migrate, or create the schema from your own code:

import (
    "database/sql"

    "entgo.io/ent/dialect"
    entsql "entgo.io/ent/dialect/sql"
    _ "github.com/jackc/pgx/v5/stdlib"

    "github.com/plexusone/systemforge/identity/ent"
)

func migrate(ctx context.Context, dsn string) (*ent.Client, error) {
    db, err := sql.Open("pgx", dsn)
    if err != nil {
        return nil, err
    }
    client := ent.NewClient(ent.Driver(entsql.OpenDB(dialect.Postgres, db)))
    if err := client.Schema.Create(ctx); err != nil {
        return nil, errors.Join(err, client.Close())
    }
    return client, nil
}

docs.title: Step 3: Copy Existing Data
docs.text: Copy users into sf_principals and sf_humans, compatible password hashes into sf_credentials, and then organizations and memberships. The migration guide has the SQL, including which password hash formats can be imported.

docs.title: Step 4: Set Up Dual-Write
docs.text:
Create people through the principal service, which writes the principal and its human row together and uses the email as the principal's identifier. Then write your own row with the returned principal ID:

import (
    "github.com/plexusone/systemforge/identity/credential"
    "github.com/plexusone/systemforge/identity/principal"
)

type UserService struct {
    appClient  *appent.Client
    principals principal.Service
    creds      credential.Service
}

func NewUserService(appClient *appent.Client, sfClient *ent.Client) *UserService {
    return &UserService{
        appClient:  appClient,
        principals: principal.NewService(sfClient),
        creds:      credential.NewService(sfClient),
    }
}

func (s *UserService) CreateUser(ctx context.Context, email, name, password string) error {
    p, err := s.principals.CreateHuman(ctx, principal.CreateHumanInput{
        Email:       email,
        DisplayName: name,
    })
    if err != nil {
        return err
    }

    if password != "" {
        if err := s.creds.CreatePassword(ctx, credential.CreatePasswordInput{
            PrincipalID: p.ID,
            Password:    password,
        }); err != nil {
            return err
        }
    }

    // Write to app tables with the same ID.
    _, err = s.appClient.User.Create().
        SetID(p.ID).
        SetEmail(email).
        SetName(name).
        Save(ctx)
    return err
}

CreatePassword hashes with Argon2id, and credential.Service.VerifyPassword checks a password against it.

docs.title: Step 5: Switch Reads
docs.text:
Read people from SystemForge. GetByID returns the principal with its human extension populated in Human:

func (s *UserService) GetUser(ctx context.Context, id uuid.UUID) (*User, error) {
    p, err := s.principals.GetByID(ctx, id)
    if err != nil {
        return nil, err
    }

    profile, err := s.appClient.UserProfile.Query().
        Where(userprofile.PrincipalIDEQ(id)).
        Only(ctx)
    if err != nil && !appent.IsNotFound(err) {
        return nil, err
    }

    return &User{Principal: p, Profile: profile}, nil
}

To find someone by email, query the human row without regard to case, since SystemForge treats emails case-insensitively:

p, err := sfClient.Principal.Query().
    Where(
        principal.TypeEQ(principal.TypeHuman),
        principal.HasHumanWith(human.EmailEqualFold(email)),
    ).
    WithHuman().
    Only(ctx)

This query uses the Ent packages identity/ent/principal and identity/ent/human.

docs.title: Step 6: Remove Old Tables
docs.text:
After validation, archive and drop the old user tables:

CREATE TABLE users_archive AS SELECT * FROM users;
DROP TABLE users;

docs.title: OAuth Integration
docs.text:
SystemForge's OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect server is SystemAuth. An existing application has two supported ways to use it:

  • Run SystemAuth as an identity provider and federate to it. The application becomes an OpenID Connect client with the identity/relyingparty package, which handles the authorization flow, token verification, and finding or creating the application's local record for each principal. See Relying Parties.
  • Embed SystemAuth in the application's binary. The identity/systemauthsvc package runs the same server as the standalone systemauth binary inside your process, with the same configuration, production checks, and database setup. See Embedding SystemAuth.

Either way, the subject of every token is the SystemForge principal ID, so it can be used directly as the key into your extension tables.

docs.title: Map Existing Tenants
docs.text:
func copyOrganizations(ctx context.Context, appClient *appent.Client, sfClient *ent.Client) error {
    tenants, err := appClient.Tenant.Query().All(ctx)
    if err != nil {
        return err
    }
    for _, t := range tenants {
        if _, err := sfClient.Organization.Create().
            SetID(t.ID).
            SetName(t.Name).
            SetSlug(t.Slug).
            Save(ctx); err != nil {
            return err
        }
    }
    return nil
}

Organizations have no plan; carry a tenant's paid tier over as a marketplace subscription or license.

docs.title: Map Existing Memberships
docs.text:
func copyMemberships(ctx context.Context, appClient *appent.Client, sfClient *ent.Client) error {
    members, err := appClient.TenantMember.Query().All(ctx)
    if err != nil {
        return err
    }
    for _, m := range members {
        if _, err := sfClient.PrincipalMembership.Create().
            SetPrincipalID(m.UserID).
            SetOrganizationID(m.TenantID).
            SetRole(mapRole(m.Role)).
            Save(ctx); err != nil {
            return err
        }
    }
    return nil
}

role is an application-defined string; PrincipalMembership also has an active flag (default true) for deactivating a membership without deleting it.

docs.title: Validation Checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] SystemForge tables created (sf_*)
  • [ ] People copied to sf_principals and sf_humans
  • [ ] Compatible password hashes copied to sf_credentials; other users told to reset
  • [ ] Organizations and memberships copied
  • [ ] Dual-write enabled
  • [ ] Read paths switched
  • [ ] Sign-in through SystemAuth working, with token subjects mapped to principal IDs
  • [ ] Old tables archived
  • [ ] Dual-write disabled
  • [ ] Old tables dropped

docs.title: Migration Guide
docs.text: This guide covers moving an existing application's users, organizations, and memberships into SystemForge's identity tables.

docs.title: Target Model
docs.text:
SystemForge has a single identity root. Every person is a principal:

Concept Table Notes Person sf_principals (type = 'human') + sf_humans sf_principals.identifier is the email; sf_humans.principal_id links the two Password sf_credentials (type = 'password') Argon2id hash in secret_hash Social or SSO login sf_external_identities One row per (provider, subject) Organization sf_organizations Membership sf_principal_memberships One row per (principal_id, organization_id)

All tables use the sf_ prefix. See the schema reference for every column.

docs.title: Phase 1: Side-by-Side
docs.text:
• Create the SystemForge tables alongside your existing ones.
  • Copy existing users, organizations, and memberships.
  • Write new data to both until reads move over.

docs.title: Phase 2: Cutover
docs.text:
• Switch reads to SystemForge.
  • Validate counts and spot-check records.
  • Stop writing to the old tables.

docs.title: Phase 3: Cleanup
docs.text:
• Archive the old tables.
  • Drop them once nothing reads them.
  • Remove the dual-write code.

docs.title: Using the SystemAuth CLI
docs.text:
systemauth migrate

This creates or updates every table from the current schema and is safe to run repeatedly.

docs.title: Using Ent Directly
docs.text:
package main

import (
    "context"
    "database/sql"
    "log"

    "entgo.io/ent/dialect"
    entsql "entgo.io/ent/dialect/sql"
    _ "github.com/jackc/pgx/v5/stdlib"

    "github.com/plexusone/systemforge/identity/ent"
)

func main() {
    db, err := sql.Open("pgx", "postgres://user:pass@localhost/myapp?sslmode=disable")
    if err != nil {
        log.Fatal(err)
    }
    client := ent.NewClient(ent.Driver(entsql.OpenDB(dialect.Postgres, db)))
    defer client.Close()

    if err := client.Schema.Create(context.Background()); err != nil {
        log.Fatal(err)
    }
    log.Println("SystemForge tables created")
}

Ent's migration creates and alters tables and columns but never drops them.

docs.title: Copying Data
docs.text:
The examples below use PostgreSQL and copy from users, tenants, and tenant_members tables; adapt the source queries to your schema. Several columns have no database default because Ent fills them in Go, so the inserts set them explicitly:

  • id on sf_humans, sf_credentials, and sf_principal_memberships
  • created_at and updated_at
  • capabilities (JSON object) and allowed_scopes (JSON array) on sf_principals
  • scopes (JSON array) on sf_credentials

docs.title: Users
docs.text:
Each user becomes a principal plus a human row. Reusing the existing user ID as the principal ID keeps foreign keys in your application valid.

func copyUsers(ctx context.Context, src, dst *sql.DB) error {
    rows, err := src.QueryContext(ctx, `
        SELECT id, email, name, COALESCE(avatar_url, ''), created_at
        FROM users
        WHERE deleted_at IS NULL
    `)
    if err != nil {
        return err
    }
    defer rows.Close()

    tx, err := dst.BeginTx(ctx, nil)
    if err != nil {
        return err
    }
    defer tx.Rollback()

    count := 0
    for rows.Next() {
        var id uuid.UUID
        var email, name, avatar string
        var createdAt time.Time
        if err := rows.Scan(&id, &email, &name, &avatar, &createdAt); err != nil {
            return err
        }

        if _, err := tx.ExecContext(ctx, `
            INSERT INTO sf_principals
                (id, created_at, updated_at, type, identifier, display_name, active, capabilities, allowed_scopes)
            VALUES ($1, $2, $2, 'human', $3, $4, true, '{}', '[]')
            ON CONFLICT (id) DO UPDATE SET
                identifier = EXCLUDED.identifier,
                display_name = EXCLUDED.display_name,
                updated_at = now()
        `, id, createdAt, email, name); err != nil {
            return fmt.Errorf("copy principal %s: %w", id, err)
        }

        if _, err := tx.ExecContext(ctx, `
            INSERT INTO sf_humans (id, created_at, updated_at, principal_id, email, avatar_url)
            VALUES (gen_random_uuid(), $2, $2, $1, $3, NULLIF($4, ''))
            ON CONFLICT (principal_id) DO UPDATE SET
                email = EXCLUDED.email,
                avatar_url = EXCLUDED.avatar_url,
                updated_at = now()
        `, id, createdAt, email, avatar); err != nil {
            return fmt.Errorf("copy human %s: %w", id, err)
        }
        count++
    }
    if err := rows.Err(); err != nil {
        return err
    }
    if err := tx.Commit(); err != nil {
        return err
    }
    log.Printf("copied %d users", count)
    return nil
}

Before copying, check your source for emails that differ only in case. SystemForge looks people up by email without regard to case, so two rows such as Ada@example.com and ada@example.com make that lookup ambiguous. Merge or rename them first:

SELECT lower(email), count(*)
FROM users
WHERE deleted_at IS NULL
GROUP BY lower(email)
HAVING count(*) > 1;

docs.title: Passwords
docs.text:
Passwords are sf_credentials rows of type password. SystemForge verifies only Argon2id hashes in the standard encoded form:

$argon2id$v=19$m=<memory>,t=<iterations>,p=<parallelism>$<salt>$<hash>

where the salt and hash are unpadded standard base64. Any parameters are accepted; they are read from the hash. A hash in any other format (bcrypt, scrypt, PBKDF2, Argon2i) is rejected at login with an error, so do not import it. Leave those users without a password credential and have them reset their password, which stores a new Argon2id hash.

INSERT INTO sf_credentials
    (id, created_at, updated_at, principal_id, type, secret_hash, scopes, active, revoked)
SELECT gen_random_uuid(), now(), now(), u.id, 'password', u.password_hash, '[]', true, false
FROM users u
WHERE u.deleted_at IS NULL
  AND u.password_hash LIKE '$argon2id$v=19$%'
  AND NOT EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM sf_credentials c
      WHERE c.principal_id = u.id AND c.type = 'password'
  );

To set passwords from application code instead, use the credential service, which hashes with Argon2id:

creds := credential.NewService(client)
err := creds.CreatePassword(ctx, credential.CreatePasswordInput{
    PrincipalID: principalID,
    Password:    plaintext,
})

docs.title: Organizations
docs.text:
INSERT INTO sf_organizations
    (id, created_at, updated_at, name, slug, org_type, active)
SELECT t.id, t.created_at, now(), t.name, t.slug, 'team', true
FROM tenants t
WHERE t.deleted_at IS NULL
ON CONFLICT (id) DO UPDATE SET
    name = EXCLUDED.name,
    updated_at = now();

org_type is one of personal, team, or enterprise. Organizations have no plan; map a tenant's paid tier to a marketplace subscription or license instead.

docs.title: Memberships
docs.text:
role is an application-defined string.

INSERT INTO sf_principal_memberships
    (id, created_at, updated_at, principal_id, organization_id, role, active)
SELECT gen_random_uuid(), m.created_at, now(), m.user_id, m.tenant_id, m.role, true
FROM tenant_members m
JOIN sf_principals p ON p.id = m.user_id
JOIN sf_organizations o ON o.id = m.tenant_id
ON CONFLICT (principal_id, organization_id) DO UPDATE SET
    role = EXCLUDED.role,
    active = true,
    updated_at = now();

docs.title: Compare Counts
docs.text:
-- People
SELECT
    (SELECT count(*) FROM users WHERE deleted_at IS NULL) AS old_count,
    (SELECT count(*) FROM sf_principals WHERE type = 'human') AS new_count;

-- Organizations
SELECT
    (SELECT count(*) FROM tenants WHERE deleted_at IS NULL) AS old_count,
    (SELECT count(*) FROM sf_organizations) AS new_count;

-- Memberships
SELECT
    (SELECT count(*) FROM tenant_members) AS old_count,
    (SELECT count(*) FROM sf_principal_memberships) AS new_count;

docs.title: Find Missing Records
docs.text:
-- Users in the old table with no SystemForge principal
SELECT u.id, u.email
FROM users u
LEFT JOIN sf_principals p ON p.id = u.id
WHERE u.deleted_at IS NULL AND p.id IS NULL;

-- Principals missing their human row
SELECT p.id, p.identifier
FROM sf_principals p
LEFT JOIN sf_humans h ON h.principal_id = p.id
WHERE p.type = 'human' AND h.id IS NULL;

docs.title: Compare Data
docs.text:
SELECT u.id, u.email AS old_email, h.email AS new_email
FROM users u
JOIN sf_humans h ON h.principal_id = u.id
WHERE u.email <> h.email;

docs.title: Keep the Old Tables in Sync
docs.text:
During the dual-write phase, mirror SystemForge changes back to the old tables so reads can move back if needed:

func mirrorToOldTable(ctx context.Context, oldDB *sql.DB, p *ent.Principal) error {
    if p.Edges.Human == nil {
        return fmt.Errorf("principal %s loaded without its human edge", p.ID)
    }
    _, err := oldDB.ExecContext(ctx, `
        UPDATE users SET email = $2, name = $3, updated_at = now()
        WHERE id = $1
    `, p.ID, p.Edges.Human.Email, p.DisplayName)
    return err
}

Load the principal with its human edge, for example client.Principal.Query().Where(principal.IDEQ(id)).WithHuman().Only(ctx).

docs.title: Switch Reads Back
docs.text:
Gate reads behind a flag so they can move back to the old tables without a deploy:

var useOldTables = os.Getenv("USE_OLD_TABLES") == "true"

docs.title: Archive Old Tables
docs.text:
CREATE SCHEMA archive;

ALTER TABLE users SET SCHEMA archive;
ALTER TABLE tenants SET SCHEMA archive;
ALTER TABLE tenant_members SET SCHEMA archive;

docs.title: Drop After Validation
docs.text: DROP SCHEMA archive CASCADE;

docs.title: Integer User IDs
docs.text:
Principal IDs are UUIDs. If your old tables use integers, generate a mapping first and use new_id everywhere a principal ID is needed:

CREATE TABLE user_id_mapping (
    old_id BIGINT PRIMARY KEY,
    new_id UUID NOT NULL UNIQUE
);

INSERT INTO user_id_mapping (old_id, new_id)
SELECT id, gen_random_uuid()
FROM users;

docs.title: Password Hashes in Another Format
docs.text: Only Argon2id hashes in the encoded form above can be imported. Users whose hashes use another algorithm must reset their password after the migration.

docs.title: Marketplace
docs.text: SystemForge provides a SaaS marketplace infrastructure with Stripe integration for subscription billing, license management, and seat-based access control.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Listings - Product catalog with multiple tiers and pricing
  • Subscriptions - Stripe-powered recurring billing
  • Licenses - Flexible licensing models (unlimited, per-seat, time-limited)
  • Seat Management - Assign and revoke user access to subscriptions

docs.title: 1. Create Services
docs.text:
import (
    "github.com/plexusone/systemforge/marketplace"
    "github.com/plexusone/systemforge/marketplace/stripe"
)

// Create services with Ent client
listingSvc := marketplace.NewEntListingService(entClient, nil)
licenseSvc := marketplace.NewEntLicenseService(entClient, nil)
seatSvc := marketplace.NewEntSeatAssignmentService(entClient, nil)
subSvc := marketplace.NewEntSubscriptionService(entClient, nil)

// Create Stripe checkout service
checkoutSvc := stripe.NewCheckoutService(stripe.Config{
    SecretKey:     os.Getenv("STRIPE_SECRET_KEY"),
    WebhookSecret: os.Getenv("STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET"),
    SuccessURL:    "https://app.example.com/checkout/success",
    CancelURL:     "https://app.example.com/checkout/cancel",
}, licenseSvc, subSvc)

docs.title: 2. Create a Listing
docs.text:
listing, err := listingSvc.Create(ctx, &marketplace.Listing{
    ID:          uuid.New(),
    Name:        "Pro Plan",
    Description: "Full access to all features",
    Tier:        marketplace.TierPro,
    PriceCents:  4999, // $49.99/month
    Currency:    "usd",
    IsActive:    true,
})

docs.title: 3. Handle Checkout
docs.text:
// Create Stripe checkout session
session, err := checkoutSvc.CreateCheckoutSession(ctx, stripe.CheckoutRequest{
    ListingID:      listing.ID,
    OrganizationID: orgID,
    PrincipalID:    userID,
    Quantity:       1,
})

// Redirect user to session.URL
http.Redirect(w, r, session.URL, http.StatusSeeOther)

docs.title: 4. Handle Webhooks
docs.text:
// In your webhook handler
func handleStripeWebhook(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    payload, _ := io.ReadAll(r.Body)
    signature := r.Header.Get("Stripe-Signature")

    err := checkoutSvc.HandleWebhook(r.Context(), payload, signature)
    if err != nil {
        http.Error(w, err.Error(), http.StatusBadRequest)
        return
    }
    w.WriteHeader(http.StatusOK)
}

docs.text:
// 1. User selects a plan
listing, _ := listingSvc.Get(ctx, listingID)

// 2. Create checkout session
session, _ := checkoutSvc.CreateCheckoutSession(ctx, stripe.CheckoutRequest{
    ListingID:      listing.ID,
    OrganizationID: orgID,

// 6. For per-seat licenses, assign seats
