docs.title: Multi-App Framework
docs.text:
The multiapp package enables multiple apps to share backend infrastructure while maintaining complete data isolation. Apps can be deployed in two modes:

  • Multi-app mode: Multiple apps share a server, routed by X-App-ID header
  • Single-app mode: One app runs on dedicated infrastructure

docs.title: Multi-App Server
docs.text:
package main

import (
    "os"

    "github.com/plexusone/systemforge/multiapp"
    app1 "github.com/grokify/app1/multiapp"
    app2 "github.com/plexusone/app2/multiapp"
)

func main() {
    server, err := multiapp.NewServer(multiapp.Config{
        Mode:        multiapp.MultiAppMode,
        DatabaseURL: os.Getenv("DATABASE_URL"),
        RedisURL:    os.Getenv("REDIS_URL"),  // optional
    })
    if err != nil {
        panic(err)
    }

    // Register apps - each gets schema isolation
    server.RegisterApp(app1.NewBackend(nil))
    server.RegisterApp(app2.NewBackend(nil))

    server.Run(":8080")
}

docs.title: Making Requests
docs.text:
# Request to App1
curl -H "X-App-ID: app1" http://localhost:8080/api/courses

# Request to App2
curl -H "X-App-ID: app2" http://localhost:8080/api/dashboards

# Requests without X-App-ID return 404 (security)
curl http://localhost:8080/api/health
# 404 Not Found

docs.title: Schema-Per-App Isolation
docs.text:
Each app gets its own PostgreSQL schema (e.g., app_app1). This provides:

  • Complete data isolation between apps
  • Independent migrations per app
  • Shared database infrastructure
PostgreSQL Database
├── app_app1/          # App1 schema
│   ├── users
│   ├── organizations
│   ├── courses
│   └── ...
├── app_app2/          # App2 schema
│   ├── users
│   ├── organizations
│   ├── dashboards
│   └── ...
└── app_app3/         # App3 schema
    ├── users
    ├── organizations
    ├── proofs
    └── ...

docs.title: AppBackend Interface
docs.text:
Apps integrate by implementing the AppBackend interface:

type AppBackend interface {
    // Slug returns unique app identifier (used in X-App-ID header)
    Slug() string

    // Name returns human-readable app name
    Name() string

    // Routes returns the app's HTTP routes with injected dependencies
    Routes(deps Dependencies) chi.Router

    // Migrations returns database migrations (optional)
    Migrations() []Migration

    // OnRegister is called after app registration
    OnRegister(ctx context.Context, cfg *AppConfig) error

    // OnShutdown is called during graceful shutdown
    OnShutdown(ctx context.Context) error
}

docs.title: Dependencies
docs.text:
The Routes method receives injected dependencies:

type Dependencies struct {
    DB     *SchemaDB      // Schema-isolated database
    Cache  Cache          // App-prefixed cache
    Logger *slog.Logger   // App-tagged logger
    Config *AppConfig     // App configuration
}

docs.title: Step 1: Refactor Existing Server
docs.text:
Extract shared initialization to support external database:

// internal/server/server.go

// New - standalone mode, creates own database
func New(cfg Config) (*Server, error) {
    db, err := sql.Open("postgres", cfg.DatabaseURL)
    if err != nil {
        return nil, err
    }
    return newServerInternal(cfg, db)
}

// NewServerWithDatabase - multi-app mode, uses provided database
func NewServerWithDatabase(cfg Config, db *sql.DB) (*Server, error) {
    return newServerInternal(cfg, db)
}

// newServerInternal - shared initialization logic
func newServerInternal(cfg Config, db *sql.DB) (*Server, error) {
    // JWT service, router, middleware, storage, routes...
}

// Router returns the HTTP handler
func (s *Server) Router() http.Handler {
    return s.mux
}

docs.title: Step 2: Create AppBackend Adapter
docs.text:
Create a public multiapp/ package (not internal/multiapp/):

// multiapp/backend.go
package multiapp

import (
    "context"

    "github.com/go-chi/chi/v5"
    cfmultiapp "github.com/plexusone/systemforge/multiapp"
    "github.com/yourapp/internal/server"
)

type Backend struct {
    cfg    *server.Config
    server *server.Server
}

func NewBackend(cfg *server.Config) *Backend {
    if cfg == nil {
        cfg = server.DefaultConfig()
    }
    return &Backend{cfg: cfg}
}

func (b *Backend) Slug() string { return "yourapp" }
func (b *Backend) Name() string { return "Your App" }

func (b *Backend) Routes(deps cfmultiapp.Dependencies) chi.Router {
    // Create server with schema-isolated database
    var err error
    b.server, err = server.NewServerWithDatabase(b.cfg, deps.DB.Pool())
    if err != nil {
        deps.Logger.Error("failed to create server", "error", err)
        return chi.NewRouter()  // Return empty router
    }

    // Wrap http.Handler as chi.Router if needed
    r := chi.NewRouter()
    r.Mount("/", b.server.Router())
    return r
}

func (b *Backend) Migrations() []cfmultiapp.Migration {
    return nil  // Let Ent handle migrations
}

func (b *Backend) OnRegister(ctx context.Context, cfg *cfmultiapp.AppConfig) error {
    return nil
}

func (b *Backend) OnShutdown(ctx context.Context) error {
    if b.server != nil {
        return b.server.Close()
    }
    return nil
}

docs.title: Step 3: Schema-Isolated Ent Client
docs.text:
For apps using Ent ORM:

func createEntClient(schemaDB *cfmultiapp.SchemaDB) *ent.Client {
    pool := schemaDB.Pool()
    config := pool.Config().ConnConfig.Copy()

    // Set search_path to app's schema
    if config.RuntimeParams == nil {
        config.RuntimeParams = make(map[string]string)
    }
    config.RuntimeParams["search_path"] = schemaDB.Schema() + ", public"

    // Create standard DB connection
    connStr := stdlib.RegisterConnConfig(config)
    db, _ := sql.Open("pgx", connStr)

    // Create Ent client
    drv := entsql.OpenDB(dialect.Postgres, db)
    return ent.NewClient(ent.Driver(drv))
}

docs.title: Context Helpers
docs.text:
Access app and auth context in handlers:

func (h *Handler) HandleRequest(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    ctx := r.Context()

    // App context (from X-App-ID routing)
    appCtx := multiapp.AppContextFromContext(ctx)
    appCtx.AppID          // "app1"
    appCtx.AppSlug        // "app1"
    appCtx.AppName        // "App1"
    appCtx.DatabaseSchema // "app_app1"
    appCtx.Features       // ["feature1", "feature2"]
    appCtx.Settings       // map[string]any

    // JWT claims (from auth middleware)
    claims := middleware.ClaimsFromContext(ctx)
    claims.PrincipalID    // user UUID
    claims.OrganizationID // org UUID
    claims.Email          // user email

    // Full context (combines all)
    fc := multiapp.FullContextFromContext(ctx)
    fc.HasApp()           // true in multi-app mode
    fc.IsAuthenticated()  // true if JWT valid
}

docs.title: Multi-App Mode
docs.text:
Multiple apps share infrastructure, routed by header:

server, _ := multiapp.NewServer(multiapp.Config{
    Mode:        multiapp.MultiAppMode,
    DatabaseURL: "postgres://localhost:5432/platform",
})

server.RegisterApp(app1.NewBackend(nil))
server.RegisterApp(app2.NewBackend(nil))
server.RegisterApp(app3.NewBackend(nil))

server.Run(":8080")

docs.title: Single-App Mode
docs.text:
One app on dedicated infrastructure (no header routing):

server, _ := multiapp.NewServer(multiapp.Config{
    Mode:        multiapp.SingleAppMode,
    DatabaseURL: "postgres://localhost:5432/myapp",
})

server.RegisterApp(myapp.NewBackend(nil))

server.Run(":8080")

docs.title: Caching
docs.text:
The multiapp framework provides app-scoped caching:

// In Routes(), deps.Cache is pre-configured with app prefix
func (b *Backend) Routes(deps multiapp.Dependencies) chi.Router {
    // Cache keys are automatically prefixed: "app1:user:123"
    deps.Cache.Set(ctx, "user:123", userData, 5*time.Minute)

    userData, err := deps.Cache.Get(ctx, "user:123")
}

docs.title: Cache Implementations
docs.text:
• Redis: Production-ready with connection pooling
  • Memory: In-memory for development/testing
// Redis cache (from RedisURL config)
server, _ := multiapp.NewServer(multiapp.Config{
    RedisURL: "redis://localhost:6379",
})

// Memory cache (default when RedisURL empty)
server, _ := multiapp.NewServer(multiapp.Config{
    // No RedisURL = memory cache
})

docs.title: Generic 404 Responses
docs.text:
Missing or invalid X-App-ID returns generic 404 to prevent:

  • Routing mechanism disclosure
  • App ID enumeration attacks
  • Information leakage about valid apps

docs.title: Self-Contained Apps
docs.text:
Each app manages its own:

  • Users and authentication
  • Organizations and memberships
  • Business data and logic
  • API routes and middleware

No external dependencies required. SystemAuth integration is optional for SSO.

docs.title: Optional: SystemAuth Integration
docs.text:
Apps can optionally integrate with SystemAuth for:

  • Single Sign-On (SSO) across apps
  • Centralized user management
  • Cross-app analytics

This works by linking each person's SystemAuth identity to their principal: relying parties store the SystemAuth sub as sf_principal_id, and federation sync records the hub identity as an external identity on the principal.

docs.title: OAuth Apps
docs.text: OAuth apps represent client applications that can request access to your API.

docs.title: Schema
docs.text:
The sf_oauth_apps table contains:

Field Type Description id UUID Internal ID client_id string Public identifier name string Display name description string App description logo_url string App logo app_type enum web, spa, native, service, machine owner_id UUID Creating user organization_id UUID Owning organization redirect_uris []string Allowed redirects allowed_scopes []string Requestable scopes allowed_grants []string Allowed grant types access_token_ttl int Token lifetime (seconds) refresh_token_ttl int Refresh lifetime (seconds) first_party bool Skip consent screen public bool No client secret active bool App status

docs.title: App Types
docs.text: Type Description Secret PKCE web Traditional server-rendered apps Required Optional spa Single-page JavaScript apps None Required native Mobile or desktop apps None Required service Backend services Required No machine Automated systems/CI Required No

docs.title: First-Party SPA
docs.text:
app, err := client.OAuthApp.Create().
    SetClientID(generateClientID()).
    SetName("My Frontend App").
    SetAppType("spa").
    SetPublic(true).
    SetFirstParty(true).
    SetRedirectUris([]string{
        "http://localhost:3000/callback",
        "https://app.example.com/callback",
    }).

docs.title: Client ID Generation
docs.text:
Generate unique, URL-safe client IDs:

import (
    "crypto/rand"
    "encoding/base64"
)

func generateClientID() string {
    b := make([]byte, 16)
    rand.Read(b)
    return base64.RawURLEncoding.EncodeToString(b)

docs.title: Generate Secret
docs.text:
func generateSecret() string {
    b := make([]byte, 32)
    rand.Read(b)
    return base64.RawURLEncoding.EncodeToString(b)
}

docs.title: Hash Secret
docs.text:
import "golang.org/x/crypto/argon2"

func hashSecret(secret string) string {
    salt := make([]byte, 16)
    rand.Read(salt)

    hash := argon2.IDKey([]byte(secret), salt, 3, 64*1024, 4, 32)

    // Return encoded hash with parameters
    return fmt.Sprintf("$argon2id$v=19$m=65536,t=3,p=4$%s$%s",
        base64.RawStdEncoding.EncodeToString(salt),
        base64.RawStdEncoding.EncodeToString(hash),
    )
}

newHash := hashSecret(newSecret)

// Add new secret (old one still works)

    SetAppID(appID).
    SetSecretHash(newHash).
    SetSecretPrefix(newSecret[:8]).
    Save(ctx)

// Later: revoke old secret

    Where(oauthappsecret.IDEQ(oldSecretID)).
    SetRevoked(true).
    SetRevokedAt(time.Now()).
    Save(ctx)

docs.title: Authorization Code Grant
docs.text: The Authorization Code grant is the recommended flow for user-facing applications.

docs.title: PKCE (Proof Key for Code Exchange)
docs.text: PKCE is required for public clients and recommended for all clients.

docs.title: Generate Code Verifier
docs.text:
// Client-side (JavaScript)
function generateCodeVerifier() {
    const array = new Uint8Array(32);
    crypto.getRandomValues(array);
    return base64URLEncode(array);
}

function base64URLEncode(buffer) {
    return btoa(String.fromCharCode(...buffer))
        .replace(/\+/g, '-')
        .replace(/\//g, '_')
        .replace(/=/g, '');
}

docs.title: Generate Code Challenge
docs.text:
async function generateCodeChallenge(verifier) {
    const encoder = new TextEncoder();
    const data = encoder.encode(verifier);
    const hash = await crypto.subtle.digest('SHA-256', data);
    return base64URLEncode(new Uint8Array(hash));
}

docs.title: Step 1: Authorization Request
docs.text:
Redirect user to authorization endpoint:

GET /oauth/authorize?
  response_type=code&
  client_id=my-app&
  redirect_uri=https://app.example.com/callback&
  scope=openid+profile+email&
  state=xyz123&
  code_challenge=E9Melhoa2OwvFrEMTJguCHaoeK1t8URWbuGJSstw-cM&
  code_challenge_method=S256

docs.text: Parameter Required Description response_type Yes Must be code client_id Yes Your app's client ID redirect_uri Yes Must match registered URI scope Yes Space-separated scopes state Recommended CSRF protection code_challenge Public clients PKCE challenge code_challenge_method With challenge Must be S256

docs.title: Complete Example (JavaScript)
docs.text:
class OAuthClient {
    constructor(config) {
        this.clientId = config.clientId;
        this.redirectUri = config.redirectUri;
        this.authEndpoint = config.authEndpoint;
        this.tokenEndpoint = config.tokenEndpoint;
    }

    async startAuth(scopes) {
        const verifier = this.generateVerifier();
        const challenge = await this.generateChallenge(verifier);
        const state = this.generateState();

        // Store for later
        sessionStorage.setItem('pkce_verifier', verifier);
        sessionStorage.setItem('oauth_state', state);

        const params = new URLSearchParams({
            response_type: 'code',
            client_id: this.clientId,
            redirect_uri: this.redirectUri,
            scope: scopes.join(' '),
            state: state,
            code_challenge: challenge,
            code_challenge_method: 'S256'
        });

        window.location.href = `${this.authEndpoint}?${params}`;
    }

    async handleCallback() {
        const params = new URLSearchParams(window.location.search);
        const code = params.get('code');
        const state = params.get('state');

        // Verify state
        if (state !== sessionStorage.getItem('oauth_state')) {
            throw new Error('State mismatch');
        }

        const verifier = sessionStorage.getItem('pkce_verifier');

        // Exchange code for tokens
        const response = await fetch(this.tokenEndpoint, {
            method: 'POST',
            headers: {
                'Content-Type': 'application/x-www-form-urlencoded'
            },
            body: new URLSearchParams({
                grant_type: 'authorization_code',
                code: code,
                client_id: this.clientId,
                redirect_uri: this.redirectUri,
                code_verifier: verifier
            })
        });

        return response.json();
    }
}

docs.title: Server-Side Implementation
docs.text:
// Login handler - after successful authentication
func handleLogin(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    // Validate credentials
    user, err := validateCredentials(r)
    if err != nil {
        // Show login error
        return
    }

    // Create session
    session := createSession(user.ID)
    setSessionCookie(w, session)

    // Redirect back to OAuth flow
    if redirect := r.URL.Query().Get("redirect"); redirect != "" {
        http.Redirect(w, r, redirect, http.StatusFound)
        return
    }

    // Default redirect
    http.Redirect(w, r, "/", http.StatusFound)
}

docs.title: Client Credentials Grant
docs.text: The Client Credentials grant is used for server-to-server authentication where no user is involved.

docs.title: Use Cases

• Backend services accessing APIs
  • Scheduled jobs and cron tasks
  • CI/CD pipelines
  • Microservice communication

docs.title: Token Caching
docs.text:
Cache tokens to avoid unnecessary token requests:

type TokenCache struct {
    token     string
    expiresAt time.Time
    mu        sync.RWMutex
}

func (c *TokenCache) GetToken(ctx context.Context, config *clientcredentials.Config) (string, error) {
    c.mu.RLock()
    if c.token != "" && time.Now().Before(c.expiresAt.Add(-30*time.Second)) {
        defer c.mu.RUnlock()
        return c.token, nil
    }
    c.mu.RUnlock()

    // Fetch new token
    c.mu.Lock()
    defer c.mu.Unlock()

    token, err := config.Token(ctx)
    if err != nil {
        return "", err
    }

    c.token = token.AccessToken
    c.expiresAt = token.Expiry
    return c.token, nil
}

docs.title: IP Allowlisting
docs.text:
Consider restricting by IP for sensitive services:

func validateClientIP(r *http.Request, allowedIPs []string) bool {
    clientIP := r.RemoteAddr
    for _, allowed := range allowedIPs {
        if clientIP == allowed {
            return true
        }
    }
    return false
}

docs.title: Service Accounts
docs.text:
Non-human identities in SystemForge are service principals: a Principal of type service with a ServicePrincipal extension. A service principal can hold credentials such as API keys and public keys, scoped to the work it does.

JWT Bearer grant (RFC 7523) is not implemented

SystemAuth does not currently accept the urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:jwt-bearer grant: it is not registered with the OAuth server. Machine-to-machine clients should use the client credentials grant with an OAuth client today. The building blocks described below (service principals and keypair credentials) are what a future JWT Bearer grant will verify assertions against.

docs.title: Service Principals
docs.text:
A service principal is created through the identity/principal service:

import (
    "github.com/plexusone/systemforge/identity/principal"
)

svc := principal.NewService(client)

desc := "Deploys builds to staging and production"
sp, err := svc.CreateService(ctx, principal.CreateServiceInput{
    Identifier:     "cicd@myorg",
    DisplayName:    "CI/CD Pipeline",
    ServiceType:    "worker",
    Description:    &desc,
    OrganizationID: &orgID,
    CreatedBy:      &adminPrincipalID,
    AllowedScopes:  []string{"deploy:staging", "deploy:production"},
    AllowedIPs:     []string{"10.0.0.0/8"},
})
if err != nil {
    return err
}

CreateService writes the sf_principals row (type service) and its sf_service_principals extension in one transaction. Identifier is the principal's unique lookup key.

Service principals are updated with UpdateService and can be suspended and restored with Deactivate and Reactivate.

docs.title: Keypair Credentials
docs.text:
Public keys are stored as credentials of type keypair in sf_credentials, owned by the principal. The private key never reaches SystemForge: generate the key pair where the service runs and register only the public key.

import (
    "crypto/rand"
    "crypto/rsa"
    "crypto/x509"
    "encoding/pem"

    "github.com/plexusone/systemforge/identity/credential"
)

privateKey, err := rsa.GenerateKey(rand.Reader, 2048)
if err != nil {
    return err
}
pubBytes, err := x509.MarshalPKIXPublicKey(&privateKey.PublicKey)
if err != nil {
    return err
}
pubPEM := pem.EncodeToMemory(&pem.Block{Type: "PUBLIC KEY", Bytes: pubBytes})

creds := credential.NewService(client)
expires := time.Now().Add(365 * 24 * time.Hour)
kp, err := creds.CreateKeypair(ctx, credential.CreateKeypairInput{
    PrincipalID:  sp.ID,
    Name:         "deploy key",
    KeyAlgorithm: "RS256",
    PublicKeyPEM: string(pubPEM),
    Scopes:       []string{"deploy:staging"},
    ExpiresAt:    &expires,
})
if err != nil {
    return err
}

// kp.KeyID is generated by SystemForge; use it as the JWT "kid" header.

Keys are looked up and managed through the same service:

Method Purpose CreateKeypair Register a public key for a principal; returns the generated key ID GetKeypairByKeyID Resolve a key by its ID (the kid a verifier receives) ListKeypairs List a principal's keys, for rotation and audit Revoke Revoke a credential by ID with a reason

docs.text:
Revoke a token (access or refresh):

POST /oauth/revoke
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded
Authorization: Basic base64(client_id:client_secret)

token=8xLOxBtZp8&
token_type_hint=refresh_token

Note: Revocation always returns 200 OK, even if the token doesn't exist.

docs.title: Refresh Token Rotation
docs.text:
When enabled, each refresh creates a new refresh token:

// Enable rotation on the app
app, _ := client.OAuthApp.Create().
    SetRefreshTokenRotation(true).
    // ...
    Save(ctx)

docs.title: Rotation Benefits
docs.text:
1. Breach Detection: Reusing an old refresh token indicates theft
  2. Limited Window: Stolen tokens expire faster
  3. Audit Trail: Each token has a family ID for tracking

docs.title: Family-Based Revocation
docs.text:
If a rotated token is reused, revoke the entire family:

func revokeTokenFamily(ctx context.Context, familyID uuid.UUID) error {
    _, err := client.OAuthToken.Update().
        Where(oauthtoken.FamilyIDEQ(familyID)).
        SetRevoked(true).
        SetRevokedAt(time.Now()).
        SetRevokedReason("rotation_violation").
        Save(ctx)
    return err
}

docs.title: Token Validation Middleware
docs.text:
import "github.com/plexusone/systemforge/identity/oauth"

func main() {
    provider, _ := oauth.NewProvider(entClient, cfg)
    api, _ := oauth.NewAPI(provider)

    // Protected routes
    mux := http.NewServeMux()
    mux.Handle("/api/",
        api.Middleware(
            http.HandlerFunc(apiHandler),
        ),
    )
}

func apiHandler(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    // Get user from context
    userID := oauth.UserIDFromContext(r.Context())

    // Check scopes
    if !oauth.HasScope(r.Context(), "api:write") {
        http.Error(w, "insufficient scope", http.StatusForbidden)
        return
    }

    // Handle request...
}

docs.title: Token Cleanup
docs.text:
Periodically clean expired tokens:

func cleanupExpiredTokens(ctx context.Context, client *ent.Client) error {
    // Delete expired access tokens
    _, err := client.OAuthToken.Delete().
        Where(
            oauthtoken.AccessExpiresAtLT(time.Now()),
            oauthtoken.Or(
                oauthtoken.RefreshExpiresAtIsNil(),
                oauthtoken.RefreshExpiresAtLT(time.Now()),
            ),
        ).
        Exec(ctx)
    if err != nil {
        return err
    }

    // Delete expired auth codes
    _, err = client.OAuthAuthCode.Delete().
        Where(oauthauthcode.ExpiresAtLT(time.Now())).
        Exec(ctx)

    return err
}

// Run as cron job
func startCleanupJob() {
    ticker := time.NewTicker(1 * time.Hour)
    go func() {
        for range ticker.C {
            cleanupExpiredTokens(context.Background(), entClient)
        }
    }()
}

docs.title: List User's Tokens
docs.text:
tokens, err := client.OAuthToken.Query().
    Where(
        oauthtoken.UserIDEQ(userID),
        oauthtoken.RevokedEQ(false),
    ).
    WithApp().
    All(ctx)

_, err := client.OAuthToken.Update().
    Where(oauthtoken.UserIDEQ(userID)).
    SetRevoked(true).
    SetRevokedAt(time.Now()).
    SetRevokedReason("user_logout").
    Save(ctx)

    Where(oauthtoken.AppIDEQ(appID)).
    SetRevoked(true).
    SetRevokedAt(time.Now()).
    SetRevokedReason("app_revoked").
    Save(ctx)

docs.title: Observability
docs.text: SystemForge integrates with omniobserve to provide vendor-agnostic observability including metrics, traces, and logs with support for multiple backends.

docs.title: Supported Backends
docs.text:
• OTLP - OpenTelemetry Protocol (vendor-agnostic)
  • Datadog
  • New Relic
  • Dynatrace

docs.title: 1. Import the Provider
docs.text:
Import the observability package and the provider you want to use:

import (
    "github.com/plexusone/systemforge/observability"
    _ "github.com/plexusone/omniobserve/observops/otlp"     // OTLP
    // or
    _ "github.com/plexusone/omniobserve/observops/datadog"  // Datadog
    // or
    _ "github.com/plexusone/omniobserve/observops/newrelic" // New Relic
)

docs.title: 2. Create Observability Instance
docs.text:
obs, err := observability.New(observability.Config{
    Provider:       "otlp",
    ServiceName:    "my-app",
    ServiceVersion: "1.0.0",
    Endpoint:       "localhost:4317",
})
if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}
defer obs.Shutdown(context.Background())

docs.title: SystemAuth (OAuth Server)
docs.text:
server, err := systemauth.NewEmbedded(cfg,
    systemauth.WithObservability(obs),
)

docs.title: Rate Limiting
docs.text:
limiter := ratelimit.New(storage,
    ratelimit.WithObservability(obs),
)
router.Use(limiter.Middleware())

docs.title: JWT Middleware
docs.text: router.Use(middleware.HTTPAuthWithObservability(jwtService, obs))

docs.title: API Key Middleware
docs.text:
config := middleware.DefaultAPIKeyMiddlewareConfig()
config.Service = apikeyService
config.Observability = obs
router.Use(middleware.APIKeyMiddleware(config))

docs.title: HTTP Request Tracing
docs.text: router.Use(obs.Middleware())

docs.title: slog Integration
docs.text:
// Use observability-integrated logging
handler := obs.SlogHandler(
    observops.WithSlogLocalHandler(slog.NewJSONHandler(os.Stdout, nil)),
)
slog.SetDefault(slog.New(handler))

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text: Variable Description Example OBSERVABILITY_PROVIDER Backend provider otlp, datadog, newrelic, dynatrace OBSERVABILITY_ENDPOINT Backend endpoint localhost:4317 OBSERVABILITY_API_KEY API key (if required) OBSERVABILITY_SERVICE_NAME Service name my-app OBSERVABILITY_SERVICE_VERSION Service version 1.0.0 OBSERVABILITY_DISABLED Disable observability true, false OBSERVABILITY_INSECURE Disable TLS true, false OBSERVABILITY_DEBUG Enable debug logging true, false

docs.title: Testing with Jaeger
docs.text:
Run Jaeger locally to test OTLP integration:

docker run -d --name jaeger \
  -p 16686:16686 -p 4317:4317 \
  jaegertracing/all-in-one:latest

Configure your app:

OBSERVABILITY_PROVIDER=otlp \
OBSERVABILITY_ENDPOINT=localhost:4317 \
OBSERVABILITY_INSECURE=true \
go run ./cmd/server

View traces at http://localhost:16686

docs.title: Recording Custom Metrics
docs.text:
Use the underlying observops.Provider for custom metrics:

meter := obs.Meter()

counter, _ := meter.Counter("my_custom_counter",
    observops.WithDescription("My custom counter"),
)

counter.Add(ctx, 1, observops.WithAttributes(
    observops.Attribute("key", "value"),
))

docs.title: Creating Custom Spans
docs.text:
ctx, span := obs.StartSpan(ctx, "my.custom.operation",
    observops.WithSpanKind(observops.SpanKindInternal),
    observops.WithSpanAttributes(
        observops.Attribute("user.id", userID),
    ),
)
defer span.End()

// ... your code here ...

if err != nil {
    span.RecordError(err)
    span.SetStatus(observops.StatusCodeError, err.Error())
}

docs.title: Disabling Observability
docs.text:
To disable observability entirely:

obs, _ := observability.New(observability.Config{
    Disabled: true,
})

Or via environment:

OBSERVABILITY_DISABLED=true

When disabled, all operations are no-ops with minimal overhead.

docs.title: ProductGraph Integration
docs.text: SystemForge integrates with ProductGraph for product analytics, enabling frontend-backend correlation and user journey tracking.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
import (
    "github.com/plexusone/systemforge/observability"
    "github.com/plexusone/systemforge/productgraph"
)

// Create observability instance
obs, err := observability.New(observability.ConfigFromEnv())
if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}

// Configure ProductGraph
err = obs.SetProductGraph(productgraph.Config{
    ProjectID: "my-project",
    Endpoint:  "https://api.productgraph.io/v1/events",
    APIKey:    os.Getenv("PRODUCTGRAPH_API_KEY"),
})
// Or from environment:
// err = obs.SetProductGraphFromEnv()

defer obs.Shutdown(context.Background())

docs.title: Middleware
docs.text:
Use the combined middleware for automatic request tracking with frontend correlation:

router := chi.NewRouter()

// Combined middleware (recommended)
router.Use(obs.ProductGraphMiddleware())

// Or use components separately:
// router.Use(productgraph.CorrelationMiddleware)           // Extract headers
// router.Use(obs.ProductGraphRequestTrackerMiddleware())   // Track requests

docs.title: Frontend Correlation Headers
docs.text:
ProductGraph correlates backend requests with frontend sessions using these headers:

Header Description X-Session-ID Frontend session identifier X-Request-ID Per-request identifier (auto-generated if missing) X-User-ID Authenticated user identifier

Access correlation IDs in handlers:

func handler(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    ctx := r.Context()
    sessionID := productgraph.SessionIDFromContext(ctx)
    requestID := productgraph.RequestIDFromContext(ctx)
    userID := productgraph.UserIDFromContext(ctx)
}

docs.title: Manual Event Tracking
docs.text:
// Track API calls
obs.TrackAPICall(ctx, "POST", "/api/checkout", 200, 150*time.Millisecond)

// Track errors
obs.TrackError(ctx, "ValidationError", "invalid card number")

// Track user journey steps
obs.TrackJourneyStep(ctx, "checkout_flow", "payment", "Enter Payment")

// Track custom events
obs.TrackProductGraphEvent(ctx, productgraph.Event{
    EventType: productgraph.EventTypeUIClick,
    UIElement: "checkout_button",
})

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text: Variable Description Default PRODUCTGRAPH_PROJECT_ID Project identifier PRODUCTGRAPH_ENDPOINT API endpoint PRODUCTGRAPH_API_KEY Authentication key PRODUCTGRAPH_BATCH_SIZE Events per batch 50 PRODUCTGRAPH_BATCH_INTERVAL Flush interval (seconds) 5 PRODUCTGRAPH_DEBUG Enable debug logging false

docs.title: Event Types
docs.text:
ProductGraph follows OTel semantic conventions for event types:

Event Type Description page.view Page navigation ui.click, ui.input, ui.scroll, ui.submit User interactions api.request, api.response API calls journey.step User journey progression error Application errors performance Performance metrics

See ProductGraph Design Docs for detailed architecture.

docs.title: SystemForge Authority Model
docs.text: Version: 1.0 (Draft) Status: In Development

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The SystemForge Authority Model defines a four-tier hierarchical system for governing access and administration across SaaS applications. This model supports both standalone deployments and federated multi-product platforms.

docs.title: 1. Hierarchical Delegation
docs.text: Authority flows downward through the hierarchy. Each tier can delegate to lower tiers but cannot exceed its own authority bounds.

docs.title: 2. Least Privilege
docs.text: Each tier receives only the permissions necessary for its operational scope. Higher tiers have broader scope but not unlimited power.

docs.title: 3. Scope Isolation
docs.text: Authority is scoped to specific domains. A Tenant Owner in App A has no authority in App B unless explicitly granted.

docs.title: 4. Audit Trail
docs.text: All authority delegations and actions are auditable. The complete chain of authority can be traced for any operation.

docs.title: Tier 1: Federation Admin
docs.text:
Scope: Platform-wide governance across all federated applications

Available In: Federated mode only (via SystemAuth)

docs.title: Capabilities
docs.text: Capability Description Register applications Add new SystemForge apps to the federation Detach applications Remove apps from federation (with data preservation) Define global policies Create policies that apply across all apps Manage identity providers Configure federation-wide SSO/SAML/OIDC Configure global roles Define cross-product role templates Access audit streams View aggregated audit logs from all apps Manage MSP partnerships Create and configure MSP relationships Policy conflict resolution Override when app policies conflict

docs.title: Constraints
docs.text:
• Cannot directly access application business data
  • Cannot manipulate application databases
  • Operates only through Product Contract interfaces
  • Cannot bypass tenant isolation within apps

docs.title: Example Actions
docs.text:
{
    "action": "federation:app:attach",
    "actor": {
        "type": "human",
        "authority_tier": "federation_admin"
    },
    "resource": {
        "type": "application",
        "app_id": "academy-os"
    },
    "context": {
        "federation_id": "uuid"
    }
}

docs.title: Tier 2: Managed Service Provider (MSP)
docs.text:
Scope: Multi-customer operations across assigned tenants

Available In: Both standalone and federated modes

docs.title: Capabilities
docs.text: Capability Description Operate multiple tenants Access assigned customer tenants Manage tenant configs Configure tenant-level settings Apply delegated policies Implement policies within delegation bounds View aggregated metrics Cross-customer dashboards Provision new tenants Create tenants for managed customers Delegated user management Manage users within assigned tenants Support operations Handle support requests across customers

docs.title: Constraints
docs.text:
• Cannot override federation-level policies
  • Cannot access non-assigned customer tenants
  • Cannot modify app-level configurations
  • Authority limited to assigned scope (tenants, apps)
  • Actions audited with delegation chain

docs.title: Permission Model
docs.text:
type MSPAssignment struct {
    MSPID       uuid.UUID
    AppID       string
    TenantID    uuid.UUID
    Permissions []MSPPermission
    AssignedAt  time.Time
    AssignedBy  uuid.UUID
    ExpiresAt   *time.Time
}

type MSPPermission string
const (
    MSPPermissionRead      MSPPermission = "read"
    MSPPermissionManage    MSPPermission = "manage"
    MSPPermissionProvision MSPPermission = "provision"
    MSPPermissionSupport   MSPPermission = "support"
)

docs.title: Tier 3: App Owner
docs.text:
Scope: Application-level configuration and management

Available In: Both standalone and federated modes

docs.title: Capabilities
docs.text: Capability Description Configure app settings Application-wide configuration Define app roles Create application-scoped roles Manage integrations Configure webhooks, APIs, OAuth clients Define policy extensions App-specific policy rules Feature management Enable/disable app features App-level analytics View application-wide metrics Manage app principals Create service accounts, API keys

docs.title: Constraints
docs.text:
• Cannot override federation identity core (in federated mode)
  • Cannot break tenant isolation
  • Cannot modify federation-wide policies
  • Cannot access tenant data without explicit permission

docs.title: Standalone vs Federated
docs.text: Aspect Standalone Federated Identity source Local Federation (synced) Policy scope Full control Within federation bounds Audit destination Local Local + streamed SSO configuration Local IdP Federation IdP Contract operations (identity, policy, audit) Refused unless AllowUnauthenticatedStandalone is set (Product Contract) SystemAuth tokens and their permissions

docs.title: Tier 4: Tenant Owner
docs.text:
Scope: Standard SaaS tenant administration

Available In: Both standalone and federated modes

docs.title: Capabilities
docs.text: Capability Description Manage users Add, remove, update tenant users Assign roles Grant roles within allowed set Configure features Tenant-specific feature settings Access tenant data Full access to tenant's data Billing management Manage subscription (if applicable) Audit viewing View tenant's audit log Integration config Configure tenant-specific integrations

docs.title: Constraints
docs.text:
• Cannot access other tenants
  • Cannot modify app-level configurations
  • Cannot override delegated policies (from MSP or Federation)
  • Role assignment limited to allowed role set
  • Cannot create custom roles (only assign predefined)

docs.title: Authority Context
docs.text: Every authenticated request carries an authority context that determines what actions are permitted.

docs.title: Context Structure
docs.text:
type AuthorityContext struct {
    // Identity
    PrincipalID   uuid.UUID
    PrincipalType PrincipalType  // human, application, agent, service

    // Authority Domain
    Tier          AuthorityTier
    DomainType    DomainType
    DomainID      uuid.UUID

    // Effective permissions
    Permissions   []Permission

    // Delegation chain (for agents and MSP)
    Delegation    []DelegationLink

    // Constraints
    Constraints   AuthorityConstraints
}

type AuthorityTier int
const (
    TierFederation AuthorityTier = 1
    TierMSP        AuthorityTier = 2
    TierApp        AuthorityTier = 3
    TierTenant     AuthorityTier = 4
)

type DomainType string
const (
    DomainFederation DomainType = "federation"
    DomainMSP        DomainType = "msp"
    DomainApp        DomainType = "app"
    DomainTenant     DomainType = "tenant"
)

docs.title: Delegation Chains
docs.text:
When authority is delegated (MSP operations, agent actions), the full chain is tracked:

type DelegationLink struct {
    PrincipalID   uuid.UUID
    PrincipalType PrincipalType
    Tier          AuthorityTier
    DomainType    DomainType
    DomainID      uuid.UUID
    Constraints   DelegationConstraints
    GrantedAt     time.Time
}

type DelegationConstraints struct {
    AllowedActions    []string
    AllowedResources  []string
    AllowedTenants    []uuid.UUID
    MaxTokenLifetime  time.Duration
    RequiresApproval  bool
    ExpiresAt         *time.Time
}

docs.title: Evaluation Result
docs.text:
type EvaluationResult struct {
    Allowed     bool
    Reason      string
    Policies    []string     // Contributing policy IDs
    Delegations []string     // Delegation chain if applicable
    Tier        AuthorityTier
    EvaluatedAt time.Time
}

docs.title: Federation → App
docs.text:
{
    "scenario": "Federation admin attaches new app",
    "actor_tier": "federation",
    "target_tier": "app",
    "flow": [
        "1. Federation admin initiates attach",
        "2. SystemAuth validates app contract compliance",
        "3. Identity sync begins (federation → app)",
        "4. Policy sync configured",
        "5. Audit streaming enabled",
        "6. App status updated to 'active'"
    ]
}

docs.title: MSP → Tenant
docs.text:
{
    "scenario": "MSP provisions new tenant",
    "actor_tier": "msp",
    "target_tier": "tenant",
    "flow": [
        "1. MSP requests tenant creation",
        "2. Verify MSP has 'provision' permission",
        "3. Create tenant with MSP assignment",
        "4. Initial admin user created",
        "5. Audit event with delegation chain",
        "6. MSP can now manage tenant"
    ]
}

docs.title: Agent Delegation
docs.text:
{
    "scenario": "Human delegates to AI agent",
    "actor_tier": "tenant",
    "delegation_target": "agent",
    "flow": [
        "1. Human creates delegation to agent",
        "2. Constraints defined (allowed actions, resources)",
        "3. Agent token issued with constrained capabilities",
        "4. Agent actions carry delegation chain",
        "5. All actions audited with human attribution",
        "6. Human can revoke at any time"
    ]
}

docs.title: Standalone Mode
docs.text: In standalone mode (no SystemAuth federation):

docs.title: Available Tiers
docs.text: Tier Available Notes Federation No Requires SystemAuth MSP Yes Local MSP configuration App Yes Full control Tenant Yes Standard operation

docs.title: Authority Source
docs.text:
• All authority defined locally
  • App Owner has maximum authority
  • No federation policy overlay
  • Local identity management

docs.title: Upgrade Path
docs.text:
When joining a federation:

  1. Export current identity mappings
  2. Map local users to global identities
  3. Apply federation policies (additive)
  4. Enable audit streaming
  5. MSP relationships preserved or remapped

docs.title: Privilege Escalation Prevention
docs.text:
• Tier boundaries enforced at API level
  • Delegation cannot exceed delegator's authority
  • Cross-tenant access requires explicit MSP assignment
  • Agent capabilities always subset of delegator

docs.title: Audit Requirements
docs.text:
All authority-related actions must emit audit events:

{
    "event_type": "authority.delegation.created",
    "actor": {
        "id": "uuid",
        "type": "human",
        "tier": "tenant"
    },
    "target": {
        "id": "uuid",
        "type": "agent"
    },
    "constraints": {
        "allowed_actions": ["documents:read", "documents:create"],
        "expires_at": "2024-12-31T23:59:59Z"
    },
    "context": {
        "tenant_id": "uuid",
        "app_id": "academy-os"
    }
}

docs.title: Revocation
docs.text: Revocation Type Scope Effect Token revocation Single token Immediate Delegation revocation Delegation chain All child tokens invalid MSP assignment removal Tenant access Immediate loss of access App detachment Federation membership Graceful transition to standalone

docs.title: For SystemForge Apps
docs.text:
1. Implement authority context extraction from tokens
  2. Use Casbin or Cedar for policy evaluation
  3. Support delegation chain in JWT claims
  4. Emit audit events for all authority changes

docs.title: For SystemAuth Integration
docs.text:
1. Expose /systemforge/policy/evaluate endpoint
  2. Accept and apply synced policies
  3. Stream authority-related audit events
  4. Support federation token validation

docs.title: References
docs.text:
• Platform Vision
  • Product Contract
  • SystemAuth PRD
  • OAuth 2.0 (RFC 6749)
  • RBAC (NIST INCITS 359)

docs.title: SystemForge Product Contract Specification
docs.text: Version: 1.0 (Draft) Status: In Development

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The SystemForge Product Contract defines the standardized interfaces that SystemForge applications must implement to participate in federated deployments via SystemAuth.

Applications implementing this contract can:

  • Operate in standalone mode (default)
  • Join a SystemAuth federation
  • Leave a federation cleanly
  • Transfer between federations

docs.title: 1. Federation is Optional
docs.text: Applications must function fully without joining a federation. The contract endpoints themselves are not a standalone feature: their identity, policy and audit operations authenticate callers with SystemAuth tokens, so they are refused until the application is federated (see Standalone Mode).

docs.title: 2. Additive Integration
docs.text: Federation adds capabilities; it never restricts standalone functionality.

docs.title: 3. Graceful Degradation
docs.text: If federation becomes unavailable, applications should continue operating using local state.

docs.title: Metadata Endpoint
docs.text:
Purpose: Expose application capabilities and configuration to SystemAuth.

GET /systemforge/meta

Response:

    "app_id": "my-saas-app",
    "display_name": "My SaaS Application",
    "version": "1.2.0",
    "contract_version": "1.0",
    "capabilities": [
        "identity",
        "rbac",
        "audit",
        "tenancy"
    ],
    "endpoints": {
        "identity": "/systemforge/identity",
        "policy": "/systemforge/policy",
        "audit": "/systemforge/audit",
        "health": "/systemforge/health"

docs.title: Service-to-Service Authentication
docs.text:
SystemAuth authenticates to applications using signed JWTs:

type SystemAuthServiceToken struct {
    // Standard JWT claims
    Issuer    string `json:"iss"` // "systemauth.example.com"
    Subject   string `json:"sub"` // "federation:{federation_id}"
    Audience  string `json:"aud"` // "{app_id}"
    IssuedAt  int64  `json:"iat"`
    ExpiresAt int64  `json:"exp"`

    // SystemAuth claims
    FederationID string   `json:"federation_id"`
    Permissions  []string `json:"permissions"`
}

Applications MUST validate:

  1. Token signature against SystemAuth's public key
  2. Issuer matches expected SystemAuth instance
  3. Audience matches application's app_id
  4. Token is not expired
  5. Required permissions are present

docs.title: Permission Scopes
docs.text: Permission Description identity:read Read principals and tenants identity:sync Synchronize identity data policy:read Read roles and permissions policy:sync Synchronize policies audit:config Configure audit streaming health:read Read health status

docs.text:
Applications must emit audit events in this standardized format:

{
    "id": "uuid",
    "timestamp": "2024-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "event_type": "user.created",
    "action": "create",

    "actor": {
        "id": "uuid",
        "type": "human",
        "identifier": "admin@example.com"
    },

    "resource": {
        "type": "user",
        "id": "uuid",
        "identifier": "newuser@example.com"
    },

    "context": {
        "tenant_id": "uuid",
        "session_id": "string",
        "client_ip": "192.168.1.1",
        "user_agent": "Mozilla/5.0..."
    },

    "outcome": "success",
    "details": {
        "changes": {
            "email": "newuser@example.com",
            "role": "member"
        }
    }
}

docs.text: Event Type When to Emit principal.created New principal created principal.updated Principal modified principal.deleted Principal deleted principal.login Successful authentication principal.logout Session terminated role.assigned Role assigned to principal role.revoked Role removed from principal permission.evaluated Access decision made tenant.created New tenant created tenant.updated Tenant modified

docs.title: Standalone Mode
docs.text:
When not federated, there is no SystemAuth issuer to authenticate callers against:

  1. The identity, policy and audit operations return 403 Forbidden
  2. /systemforge/meta, /systemforge/health and /systemforge/health/federation stay open; the last returns federation_status: "standalone"
  3. Sync endpoints return 503 Service Unavailable

This holds whenever the application has no federation ID: before it first joins, and after it leaves or is detached.

To serve the operations without credentials while standalone, set Config.AllowUnauthenticatedStandalone. It is off by default. Enable it only where untrusted callers cannot reach the endpoints, such as local development and tests.

provider, err := contract.NewProvider(&contract.Config{
    AppID:                          "my-app",
    DisplayName:                    "My App",
    Version:                        "1.0.0",
    AllowUnauthenticatedStandalone: true, // local development only
}, nil)

docs.title: Federation Attachment
docs.text:
When joining a federation:

  1. SystemAuth calls /systemforge/meta to validate compatibility
  2. SystemAuth calls identity sync endpoints to map users
  3. SystemAuth configures audit streaming
  4. Application updates federation status in metadata

docs.title: Federation Detachment
docs.text:
When leaving a federation:

  1. SystemAuth notifies application of pending detachment
  2. Application exports identity mappings
  3. Audit streaming is disabled
  4. Application reverts to standalone mode
  5. Local data is preserved

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
Standard error response format:

{
    "error": {
        "code": "IDENTITY_SYNC_CONFLICT",
        "message": "Principal with identifier already exists",
        "details": {
            "identifier": "user@example.com",
            "existing_id": "uuid"
        }
    }
}

docs.title: Error Codes
docs.text: Code HTTP Status Description NOT_FEDERATED 503 App not in federation mode SYNC_IN_PROGRESS 409 Another sync operation running IDENTITY_CONFLICT 409 Identity mapping conflict POLICY_INVALID 400 Invalid policy definition UNAUTHORIZED 401 Invalid or missing auth FORBIDDEN 403 Insufficient permissions

docs.title: Versioning
docs.text:
Contract versions follow semantic versioning:

  • Major: Breaking changes to required endpoints
  • Minor: New optional endpoints or fields
  • Patch: Bug fixes, clarifications

Applications declare supported contract version in metadata. SystemAuth validates compatibility before attachment.

docs.title: Data Protection
docs.text:
• All endpoints must use TLS
  • Sensitive data encrypted at rest
  • PII handled per compliance requirements

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
• All federation endpoints require authentication
  • Tokens must be validated on every request
  • Short token lifetimes (< 1 hour recommended)

docs.title: Authorization
docs.text:
• Validate permissions on every request
  • Log all access attempts
  • Rate limit sync operations

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: SystemForge is an open-source Go framework for building SaaS applications with built-in identity, authorization, tenancy, and audit capabilities. It is designed to support both standalone applications and integration into multi-product platform ecosystems.

docs.title: Strategic Positioning
docs.text:
SystemForge represents the open-source foundation of a larger platform strategy:

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    SystemAuth (Commercial)                  │
│           Federation / Governance / Multi-Product            │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                    SystemForge (Open Source)                   │
│              Runtime / Identity / RBAC / Audit               │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                    Your SaaS Application                     │
│                   Domain Logic & Features                    │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

docs.title: SystemForge (Open Source)
docs.text:
• Complete SaaS runtime framework
  • Local identity management
  • Tenant-aware architecture
  • Authorization abstraction
  • Audit framework
  • Fully self-hostable
  • No external dependencies required

docs.title: SystemAuth (Commercial - Separate Repository)
docs.text:
• Federation layer for multiple SystemForge apps
  • Global identity overlay
  • Cross-product policy governance
  • MSP (Managed Service Provider) support
  • Enterprise compliance features

docs.title: 1. Complete Without Federation
docs.text:
Every SystemForge application must be fully functional in standalone mode:

  • ✅ Local user management
  • ✅ Local authentication (password, OAuth)
  • ✅ Local RBAC
  • ✅ Local audit logging
  • ✅ Local tenant management

Federation via SystemAuth is additive, never required.

docs.title: 2. Contract-Based Integration
docs.text:
SystemForge defines standard interfaces that enable federation:

  • Identity contract
  • Authorization contract
  • Audit contract
  • Metadata contract

Applications implementing these contracts can optionally integrate with SystemAuth.

docs.title: 3. Portable Applications
docs.text:
SystemForge applications can:

  • Run independently
  • Join a federation
  • Leave a federation
  • Transfer between organizations
  • Merge into unified platforms

This supports real-world scenarios like:

  • Acquisitions
  • Divestitures
  • Partnership integrations
  • White-label deployments

docs.title: Authority Model
docs.text: SystemForge implements a four-tier authority model designed for multi-product ecosystems:

docs.title: Tier 1: Federation (SystemAuth Only)
docs.text:
• Platform-wide governance
  • Cross-app identity
  • Global policies
  • Managed via SystemAuth

docs.title: Tier 2: MSP (Managed Service Provider)
docs.text:
• Multi-customer operations
  • Delegated administration
  • Partner-level access

docs.title: Tier 3: Application
docs.text:
• App-level configuration
  • App-scoped roles
  • Feature management

docs.title: Tier 4: Tenant
docs.text:
• Standard SaaS administration
  • User management
  • Tenant-level features

docs.title: Principal-Centric Identity
docs.text:
SystemForge uses a principal-centric identity model that supports:

Principal Type Description Auth Method Human Interactive users Password, OAuth, SSO Application OAuth clients client_credentials Agent AI assistants Delegated auth Service Backend systems JWT bearer, API key

This unified model enables:

  • Consistent authorization across principal types
  • Delegation chains for AI agent actions
  • Cross-app identity mapping in federated mode

docs.title: Dual-Mode Architecture
docs.text: Every SystemForge application supports two operational modes:

docs.title: Phase 1: Single-Product Excellence (Current)
docs.text:
• Build production-ready SaaS applications
  • Harden identity, RBAC, audit
  • Validate abstractions across multiple apps

docs.title: Phase 2: Standardized Contracts
docs.text:
• Formalize Product Contract specification
  • Implement federation-ready endpoints
  • Design authority model

docs.title: Phase 3: Federation (SystemAuth)
docs.text:
• Enable optional federation mode
  • Shared identity overlay
  • Cross-app policy governance

docs.title: Phase 4: Platform Ecosystem
docs.text:
• Multi-product orchestration
  • App lifecycle management
  • Enterprise governance

Initiates the authorization code flow.

POST /oauth/authorize

docs.title: OAuth Provider
docs.text:
import "github.com/plexusone/systemforge/identity/oauth"

// Create provider
cfg := oauth.DefaultConfig("https://api.example.com", []byte("secret"))
provider, err := oauth.NewProvider(entClient, cfg)

// Get Fosite provider
fosite := provider.OAuth2Provider()

// Get storage
storage := provider.Storage()

// Create session
session := provider.Session("user-id")

docs.title: OAuth API
docs.text:
// Create API with Huma/Chi router
api, err := oauth.NewAPI(provider)

// Mount the router - all endpoints are automatically registered:
// - /oauth/authorize (GET/POST)
// - /oauth/token (POST)
// - /oauth/introspect (POST)
// - /oauth/revoke (POST)
// - /.well-known/openid-configuration (GET)
// - /.well-known/jwks.json (GET)
http.Handle("/", api.Router())

// Middleware for protected routes
protected := api.Middleware(myHandler)

docs.title: Context Helpers
docs.text:
import "github.com/plexusone/systemforge/identity/oauth"

// In handler after middleware
func myHandler(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    ctx := r.Context()

    // Get user ID
    userID := oauth.UserIDFromContext(ctx)

    // Get scopes
    scopes := oauth.ScopesFromContext(ctx)

    // Check scope
    if oauth.HasScope(ctx, "admin") {
        // Has admin scope
    }

    // Get full access request
    ar := oauth.AccessRequestFromContext(ctx)
}

docs.title: Ent Schema Reference
docs.text: Reference for the SystemForge Ent schemas in identity/ent/schema. Table names come from each schema's entsql annotation; every table uses the sf_ prefix. Columns marked "FK" are foreign keys created from the schema's edges.

docs.title: Identity Schemas
docs.text: Every actor is a Principal. Its type selects a one-to-one extension: Human for people, ServicePrincipal for backend services, Application for OAuth client applications, and Agent for AI agents. Credentials, upstream login identities, and organization memberships all belong to the principal.

docs.title: Principal
docs.text:
Table: sf_principals

Principal is the unified identity root representing any type of actor: human, application, agent, or service.

Field Type Constraints Description id UUID PK, immutable Primary key created_at time immutable Creation time updated_at time — Last modification time type enum immutable Type of principal: human, application, agent, service identifier string unique, not empty Unique identifier (email, client_id, service@org) display_name string not empty Human-readable display name active bool default: true Whether the principal is active capabilities JSON — Principal capabilities (can_access_ui, can_delegate, etc.) allowed_scopes JSON — Scopes this principal can request metadata JSON nullable Custom metadata organization_id UUID FK → Organization, nullable Organization this principal belongs to

type values: human, application, agent, service

Edges:

  • organization → Organization (M2O)
  • human → Human (O2O)
  • application → Application (O2O)
  • agent → Agent (O2O)
  • service_principal → ServicePrincipal (O2O)
  • credentials → Credential (O2M)
  • external_identities → ExternalIdentity (O2M)
  • principal_tokens → PrincipalToken (O2M)
  • principal_memberships → PrincipalMembership (O2M)
  • owned_organizations → Organization (O2M)
  • owned_oauth_apps → OAuthApp (O2M)
  • oauth_consents → OAuthConsent (O2M)
  • sent_invites → Invite (O2M)
  • owned_listings → Listing (O2M)
  • purchased_licenses → License (O2M)
  • seat_assignments → SeatAssignment (O2M)
  • assigned_seats → SeatAssignment (O2M)

Unified credentials. Credentials can be passwords, API keys, keypairs, WebAuthn credentials, or TOTP secrets.

Field Type Constraints Description id UUID PK, immutable Primary key type enum — Type of credential identifier string nullable Unique identifier for this credential (e.g., key prefix) secret_hash string nullable, sensitive Hashed secret (Argon2id for passwords/secrets, SHA256 for tokens) public_key string nullable Public key (PEM format) for keypair credentials key_algorithm string nullable Key algorithm (RS256, ES256, etc.) key_id string unique, nullable Key ID for keypair credentials (used in JWT kid header) webauthn_credential_id bytes nullable WebAuthn credential ID webauthn_public_key bytes nullable WebAuthn public key (COSE format) webauthn_aaguid string nullable WebAuthn authenticator AAGUID webauthn_sign_count uint32 nullable, default: 0 WebAuthn signature counter scopes JSON — Scopes this credential grants active bool default: true Whether this credential is active expires_at time nullable When this credential expires (nil = never) revoked bool default: false Whether this credential has been revoked revoked_at time nullable When this credential was revoked revoked_reason string nullable Reason for revocation last_used_at time nullable Last time this credential was used last_used_ip string nullable IP address of last use name string nullable Human-readable name for this credential metadata JSON nullable Custom metadata created_at time immutable Creation time updated_at time — Last modification time principal_id UUID FK → Principal Principal that owns this credential

Table: sf_external_identities

Links a Principal to an upstream login identity (e.g. a GitHub or Google account). The (provider, subject) pair is the stable key used to find the principal on every social login; email is recorded for information and verified-email linking only.

docs.title: Releases
docs.text:
Release notes, one file per version, newest first. The changelog is generated from CHANGELOG.json and lists every change with its commit.

The latest release, v0.17.0, lets relying-party applications manage managed principals through an API on SystemAuth and a Go client, requires consent before anyone becomes a manager, and refuses contract operations until an application is federated. The last two are breaking; read its upgrade notes first.

The previous release, v0.16.0, added reconnecting, bindings and per-connection grants to the connections API and renamed the connection library from connectionforge to connectforge. The rename is breaking for deployments that enabled connections in v0.15.0.

The release before it, v0.15.0, added key management through keyforge, connections to external services, invite-only sign-up with a waitlist, an app catalog for product switchers, and the orgs claim with per-application roles in embedded SystemAuth.

Earlier, v0.14.0, made Principal the sole identity root, added managed principals and a security pass over the APIs, and completed the organization model. It is a breaking release with migrations 0002 to 0009; read its upgrade notes first.

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text:
All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.

The format is based on Keep a Changelog, this project adheres to Semantic Versioning, commits follow Conventional Commits, and this changelog is generated by Structured Changelog.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• Relying-party applications manage managed principals through SystemAuth: a /managed-principals API served by systemauthsvc, called with the manager's access token, and the mpclient Go client
  • Nobody becomes a manager without agreeing: managers other than the creator join by invitation or claim
  • The contract's identity, policy and audit operations refuse requests until the application is federated

docs.title: Upgrade Guide
docs.text:
• Standalone applications that serve the contract API: set Config.AllowUnauthenticatedStandalone in development and tests, or federate the application; identity, policy and audit operations otherwise answer 403
  • Code calling managedprincipal.Service.Create with managers other than the actor, or AddManager: invite those managers or issue a claim, or build the service with WithDirectManagerAdds for administrator tooling
  • Managers in roles registered with WithRoles can no longer issue login tokens; issue them as a guardian or educator
  • To let a relying party manage managed principals, enable managed_principals for the deployment and its client and add systemforge:managed_principals to the client's scopes

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• SystemAuth built by systemauthsvc serves the managed-principal API at /managed-principals when managed principals are enabled, for relying parties calling with a manager's access token granted systemforge:managed_principals; Options.AuditEmitter, ManagedPrincipalRates and ManagedPrincipalOptions, and Service.ManagedPrincipals() (a76d041)
  • managedprincipal.NewHandler relying-party mode (WithRequestClient): the client is the access token's, creation names only the caller, unknown and unmanaged principals answer 403; WithCodeRateLimit for code routes; GET / (Service.ListManagedBy) and POST /{id}/login-tokens (af30b5b)
  • managedprincipal/mpclient, a typed client for the managed-principal API with errors wrapped in *APIError (eaca813)
  • systemauth.Server.BearerAccess and BearerAuthenticator: bearer access that carries the token's client, scopes and grant, adapted to requestprincipal (c0c4e8d)

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• BREAKING: The contract's identity, policy and audit operations answer 403 until the application is federated; Config.AllowUnauthenticatedStandalone restores the open behavior for development and tests (9883be5)
  • BREAKING: managedprincipal.Service.Create accepts only the actor as manager and AddManager is refused with ErrConsentRequired, so managers join by invitation or claim; WithDirectManagerAdds keeps direct adds for administrator tooling (53a2655)
  • Issuing a login token requires manage_credentials (bf1c347)
  • The managed-principal handler answers 403 for an unknown or unmanaged principal, as for one the caller does not manage (0124078)

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
• Managed principals guide covers the API on SystemAuth, its configuration and scope, and the client
  • INIT-SYSTEMFORGE-012 specification for managed principals in relying-party applications (a18e9f1)
  • v0.17.0 release notes; relying-party, embedding and README updates for the managed-principal API

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• Connections can be reconnected in place, track what depends on them with bindings, and be shared with a principal through per-connection role grants
  • The connection library is renamed from connectionforge to connectforge; imports, tables (connectforge_*) and the key purpose (connectforge.credential) change, which is breaking for deployments that enabled connections in v0.15.0

  • Run systemauth migrate to create the connectforge_* tables

docs.text:
• POST .../connections/{id}/reconnect, GET, PUT and DELETE .../connections/{id}/bindings, and GET, PUT and DELETE .../connections/{id}/grants/{principal} (5a4bf33)
  • systemauthsvc registers the systemforge_connection resource type so connection grants are role grants read by the role-based provider (8f501c3)

docs.title: Changed
docs.text: • BREAKING: Depend on connectforge instead of connectionforge; tables are now connectforge_* and credentials are sealed under the connectforge.credential purpose (7eb410b)

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• Key management: keys wires keyforge as the platform's one key library, with envelope encryption, rotation without re-encrypting, the root key read through omnivault, and key events sent to the audit trail (ADR-013)
  • Connections to external services: connections composes connectionforge so organizations connect accounts at services such as a CDN or analytics product, with credentials sealed under managed keys and applications receiving an authenticated HTTP client, never the secret (ADR-017)
  • A connections API at /api/v1/organizations/{org}/connections, enabled by the new connections configuration section and protected by systemforge:connections:read and :write scopes
  • Invite-only sign-up: a gate on social login that admits only verified emails holding an invite, a consent-recording waitlist for everyone else, and systemauth invite and systemauth waitlist commands
  • App catalog: a host publishes the applications it runs, and the browser session lists it so each shell can show the products a person holds a role in, for a product switcher
  • Embedded SystemAuth emits the orgs claim with per-application roles, limited to the deployment's default entitlements
  • Fixed rls.Helper.SetTenant and SetUser, which failed on every PostgreSQL connection because SET LOCAL does not accept bind parameters
  • No breaking changes; run systemauth migrate for the new tables

docs.title: Upgrade Guide
docs.text:
• Run systemauth migrate (or systemauthsvc.Service.Migrate) to create sf_signup_invites and sf_signup_waitlist. Existing tables are unchanged and no SQL migration file is needed
  • To enable connections, add the connections section, create the root key (openssl rand -base64 32) and store it in the vault, and back up keys_dir with the database. systemauth migrate then creates the connectionforge_* tables and enables row-level security on PostgreSQL

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• keys package: Open, Seal and Open over keyforge's single-host setup, with VaultSource reading the root key from an omnivault vault, and an audit sink that records lifecycle events without key material (1f3095e)
  • connections package: connectionforge's SQL store on the platform database with row-level security keyed on owner_id, credentials sealed by keys, deployment secrets read from omnivault, authorization through authz, and audit events to the platform trail (5975b1e)
  • connections.RolePermissions grants organization owners and admins view, use and manage on connections, and members view (dfcd4ed)
  • connections.Handler: the organization-scoped connections HTTP API (providers, list, connect, get, rename, test, disconnect) that never returns a credential and reports a refused view as not found (dfcd4ed)
  • connections.MigrateSchema creates the connection tables and enables row-level security without opening the keys, so systemauth migrate needs no root key (dfcd4ed)
  • systemauth.Server.BearerPrincipal and WriteBearerError authenticate API requests by bearer access token and scope with RFC 6750 responses (ccc1d03)
  • connections section of the SystemAuth configuration (keys_dir, vault, root_key, allow_private_egress), the systemauthsvc.Options.Providers registry, Service.Connections and Service.RunJobs (7b51e06)
  • systemauth serve runs the key lifecycle jobs while serving (dfb3597)
  • systemauth invite add|list|revoke and the --invite-only and --signup-denied-url flags, with SignupInvite (sf_signup_invites), the signupgate store and gate, and systemauth.SignupGate on social login (3471a81)
  • For host binaries: systemauthsvc.Options.InviteOnly, SignupDeniedURL and WaitlistPage, Service.SignupInvites and Service.SignupWaitlist, and the signupgate/signupcmd package with the invite and waitlist command groups to mount in a host's own CLI (dc2af08)
  • Sign-up waitlist: /signup/waitlist records an address with the consent text shown and its version, with SignupWaitlistEntry (sf_signup_waitlist), signupgate.Waitlist and systemauth waitlist list [--csv] and remove (72ac85b)
  • appcatalog package: App and an ordered, validated Catalog, with Static and Remote sources, the last cached and kept through an outage (538133c)
  • systemauth.WithAppCatalog serves the catalog at /.well-known/sf-apps; relyingparty.BFFConfig.Apps adds the catalog to /bff/session as apps, which a shell filters by the membership's applications; systemauthsvc.Options.Apps publishes a host's catalog and warns about entries with no registered vocabulary (31cc7a9)
  • systemauthsvc.Options.Vocabularies and DefaultEntitlements install an Ent-backed orgs claim source with application roles from approle (cffe439)

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text: • rls.Helper.SetTenant and SetUser use set_config(name, value, true), which has the transaction scope of SET LOCAL and takes the value as a parameter; the previous SET LOCAL ... = $1 was a PostgreSQL syntax error (6149cc1)
