docs.title: v0.11.0
docs.text:
Release Date: 2026-10-02

Finishes the CoreForge→SystemForge rename that v0.10.0's module-path move began: the Core-era names are retired. Hard cutover, no dual-name compatibility — no consumer app has shipped yet, so this is the cheapest it will ever be to do (see ADR-001).

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• coreauth → systemauth — the identity/auth server package, binary, bootstrap user, JWKS key id, env var, and observability metric namespace all rename; the parallel CoreControl naming (contract/, multiapp/, identity/oauthclient) is retired in favor of the same name.
  • cf_ table prefix → sf_ — all 26 identity tables, via the Ent schema annotations; rls.SystemForgeTables updated to match.
  • API-key visible prefix cf_ → sf_ — newly issued keys read sf_live_…/sf_test_….
  • Unified cross-app principal-link field: sf_principal_id — PrincipalMixin's field (consumed by every downstream app that embeds it) replaces the divergent core_control_principal_id / core_auth_principal_id spelling.

docs.title: Service renamed coreauth → systemauth
docs.text:
// Old
import "github.com/plexusone/systemforge/identity/coreauth"

// New
import "github.com/plexusone/systemforge/identity/systemauth"

The binary is now systemauth (was coreauth); the bootstrap user is system@systemauth.local; the JWKS key id is systemauth-1; the config env var is SYSTEMAUTH_SECRET; observability metrics/spans are under the systemauth.* namespace. CoreControlConfig and related types in identity/oauthclient are now SystemAuthConfig, etc.

docs.title: Table prefix cf_ → sf_
docs.text: Every identity table is renamed, e.g. cf_principals → sf_principals, cf_oauth_tokens → sf_oauth_tokens. No production data exists at the old prefix. An existing Postgres dev database with cf_* data can be migrated in place with migrations/0001_rename_cf_to_sf.sql; a fresh database needs no migration — just run systemauth migrate.

docs.title: API-key prefix cf_ → sf_
docs.text: identity/apikey.DefaultPrefix and the legacy identity/credential.APIKeyPrefix both move from cf_/cf_ to sf_/sf_. Newly issued keys carry the new prefix; any dev-issued cf_-prefixed key must be reissued.

docs.title: Principal-link field renamed to sf_principal_id
docs.text: PrincipalMixin's SSO-federation link field — embedded by every app that uses the Principal model — is now sf_principal_id. Consumers previously on core_control_principal_id or core_auth_principal_id rename their column and regenerate Ent.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
• README.md's Database Tables and Migration Strategy sections updated to sf_*.
  • A CI grep gate blocks any new cf_/coreauth/corecontrol/core_control/core_auth occurrence from landing again.

docs.title: What's Next
docs.text: Consumer convergence: systemforge-web, dashforge, academyos, and proofminds-web each adopt sf_/systemauth/sf_principal_id and bump to this release before any of them ships.

docs.title: v0.12.0
docs.text:
Release Date: 2026-10-06

SystemAuth becomes a deployable, central login service for every SystemForge application: GitHub/Google social login, a hardened session and token lifecycle, OpenID Connect ID tokens and UserInfo, and a reusable relying-party package so applications federate to SystemAuth instead of each implementing social login. Sessions and login state are durable in PostgreSQL, so restarts and multi-instance deployments keep users signed in. Design of record: ADR-002 and INIT-SYSTEMFORGE-005.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• Social login on SystemAuth — /login, /login/{provider} and callback routes for GitHub and Google, principal upsert keyed by provider subject (verified-email linking only), a hardened __Host-sf_login session, state CSRF + PKCE, and an allowlisted post-login redirect.
  • Session and token lifecycle — refresh-token rotation with reuse detection and absolute expiry, real logout with token revocation, and a minimal consent page.
  • OpenID Connect — SystemAuth now issues ID tokens, optional RS256 JWT access tokens (features.enable_jwt_access_tokens), and serves /oauth/userinfo.
  • identity/relyingparty — OIDC client, sub → sf_principal_id principal linking, a /bff/* cookie-session surface for browser apps, and bearer middleware for JWT access tokens and API keys.
  • Durable stores — Ent-backed SystemAuth login sessions, login state and consent grants; identity/relyingparty/pgstore PostgreSQL session and login-state stores with AES-256-GCM encryption at rest and key rotation (pgstore.NewStores, pgstore.KeysFromEnv).
  • Production-deployable systemauth binary — PostgreSQL via pgx, signing key from a secret with a stable key ID, /healthz and /readyz, and a production mode that refuses unsafe configuration.

docs.title: session/oauth removed
docs.text:
The unused duplicate social-login package is gone; identity/oauthclient is the single sanctioned package and gains everything worth keeping from it.

// Old
import "github.com/plexusone/systemforge/session/oauth"

// New
import "github.com/plexusone/systemforge/identity/oauthclient"
// oauthclient.NewGitHubConnector / NewGoogleConnector, StateStore, User.EmailVerified

docs.title: systemauth production mode
docs.text: Without --dev, cmd/systemauth now refuses to start unless it has a signing key (keys.private_key_file, keys.private_key_pem, --signing-key-file, or SYSTEMAUTH_SIGNING_KEY), an https issuer, and a persistent database, and it rejects social_login.insecure_cookies. Local setups pass --dev. --listen is kept as a deprecated alias of --addr.

docs.title: Refresh-token reuse revokes the token family
docs.text: Every refresh issues a new refresh token and retires the old one. Presenting a rotated refresh token returns invalid_grant and revokes the whole family; clients must store the newest refresh token after each refresh. Absolute lifetime is tokens.refresh_token_absolute_lifetime (default 720h).

docs.title: Header-trusting session provider bypassed when social login is enabled
docs.text: With social_login configured, the X-User-ID-trusting DefaultSessionProvider can no longer bypass login; the __Host-sf_login cookie session is consulted first. Custom providers set with WithSessionProvider still apply after the cookie.

docs.title: Schema additions
docs.text: New tables sf_external_identities, sf_login_sessions, sf_login_states, sf_consent_grants; OAuth codes and tokens gain a subject column and the auth-code user_id becomes nullable (social-login principals have no legacy user row). Run systemauth migrate (or --migrate). Relying-party applications create sf_rp_sessions / sf_rp_login_states in their own database with pgstore.EnsureSchema.

docs.title: New Features
docs.text:
• identity/oauthclient: provider Connector with overridable endpoints, User.EmailVerified (Google email_verified; GitHub /user/emails), pluggable single-use StateStore with a race-free MemoryStateStore.
  • identity/systemauth: PrincipalDirectory (Ent and memory) with external-login account linking; social_login configuration with ${ENV} expansion; CurrentLoginSession; options WithPrincipalDirectory, WithLoginSessionStore, WithLoginStateStore, WithSocialConnector, WithConsentStore, WithReadinessCheck; idp_hint authorization parameter.
  • identity/relyingparty: Client (Discover, AuthCodeURL, Exchange, Refresh, Revoke, VerifyIDToken, VerifyAccessToken, UserInfo), ResolvePrincipal, MembershipSource (claims-based memberships), SessionStore with DeleteBySubject / DeleteBySID for future back-channel logout, NewBFF, BearerMiddleware, PrincipalFromContext.
  • identity/relyingparty/pgstore: NewSessionStore, NewLoginStateStore, NewStores, Keys, KeysFromEnv, EnsureSchema, DecodeKey, DeleteExpired.
  • Shared store conformance suites (identity/systemauth/storetest, identity/relyingparty/storetest) run against memory and PostgreSQL implementations.

docs.title: Bug Fixes
docs.text:
• SystemAuth did not issue ID tokens: the Fosite OpenID Connect handlers were not registered, and discovery did not serve the advertised UserInfo endpoint.
  • Ent storage could not complete a real login: the login session was not persisted, access tokens were inserted twice, PKCE marked the code used before the exchange finished, and auth codes required a legacy user row.
  • A reused refresh token could crash the server (nil request after the inactive-token error).
  • cmd/systemauth registered no PostgreSQL driver for ent.Open("postgres").
  • Configured clients that already existed in a persistent database failed startup with a unique-constraint error; they are now updated.
  • DefaultSessionProvider concatenated returnURL into redirects without query escaping.
  • The relying-party seal nonce is generated in a dedicated buffer (sealed format unchanged).

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
• New guides: Social Login, Relying Parties, Deployment, Production Stores; updated SystemAuth overview and OAuth client.
  • README: social login and relying-party features, package layout, and the new tables.

docs.title: Upgrade Notes
docs.text:
1. Replace any session/oauth import with identity/oauthclient.
  2. Run systemauth migrate against existing SystemAuth databases.
  3. For production, provide a signing key and key ID, an https issuer, and PostgreSQL; use --dev only locally.
  4. Applications federating to SystemAuth: register an OIDC client (PKCE, redirect https://<app>/bff/auth/callback), mount relyingparty.NewBFF, and use pgstore.NewStores with a 32-byte session key for durable sessions.

docs.title: What's Next
docs.text: INIT-SYSTEMFORGE-005 Phase 3: consumer convergence onto the relying-party contract and a CI gate against direct GitHub/Google OAuth wiring outside identity/oauthclient. Suite single sign-on follow-ups: memberships and entitlements in token claims and UserInfo, silent first-party SSO with back-channel logout, and token exchange for on-behalf-of calls between applications.

docs.title: v0.13.0
docs.text:
Release Date: 2026-10-06

SystemAuth can now be embedded in a host binary. The new identity/systemauthsvc package exposes everything the standalone systemauth command does — configuration loading, production safety checks, database setup, migrations, client bootstrap, health — so an application that composes several services in one process can mount SystemAuth next to its own handlers without copying code. Relying parties in the same process can be built from SystemAuth's provider metadata directly, without fetching discovery over the network. No breaking changes.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• identity/systemauthsvc — LoadConfig / LoadConfigBytes with overrides, CheckProduction, and New(ctx, cfg, Options) returning a Service with Handler(), Migrate, Ready, Close, Issuer(), and Metadata().
  • Production checks in the library — a signing key, an https issuer, a persistent database and secure cookies are enforced by New itself, not only by the command.
  • Discovery-free relying parties — Service.Metadata() feeds relyingparty.NewClientWithMetadata, so an in-process application can build its OIDC client before the listener is up.
  • Override-first configuration — overrides now apply before defaults and validation, so a host can supply values the file omits (for example the issuer), and SystemAuth configuration can be loaded from bytes embedded in a host's own config file.

docs.title: New Features
docs.text:
• identity/systemauthsvc:
    • LoadConfig(path, ...Override), LoadConfigBytes(data, format, ...Override) (yaml, yml, json, or auto-detect).
    • Overrides: WithIssuer, WithDefaultIssuer, WithDatabase, WithSigningKeyFile, WithDefaultSigningKeyPEM, WithKeyID.
    • CheckProduction(cfg, opts) reports every problem at once, wrapping ErrNotProductionReady.
    • Options: Dev, Logger, SigningKey, an injected DB + DBDialect or EntClient, Migrate, ServerOptions. A database or Ent client supplied by the caller is left open on Close.
    • Service: Handler(), ServeHTTP, Migrate(ctx) (idempotent), Ready(ctx), Close(), Issuer(), KeyID(), Metadata(), Discovery(), Server(), Config(), StorageName(), EntClient().
    • Helpers: OpenDatabase, Migrate(ctx, cfg), NewLogger.
  • identity/systemauth: Server.OpenIDConfiguration() and Server.Ready(ctx); DecodeConfig(data, format) and DecodeConfigFile(path) decode (with ${ENV} expansion) without applying defaults or validating.

docs.title: Changes
docs.text:
• cmd/systemauth is now a thin caller of systemauthsvc. Flags, environment variables and defaults are unchanged. The production-refusal message now begins systemauthsvc: refusing to start in production mode: and still lists every problem with a hint; the MySQL driver error reads "not supported".
  • ParseConfig and LoadConfig in identity/systemauth behave as before (decode, defaults, validate).

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
• New guide: Embedding SystemAuth in a host binary, including the security trade-off (the token-signing key shares the process with application code, and restarts affect sign-in for every application).
  • Design of record for the next feature set: ADR-003 and INIT-SYSTEMFORGE-006 — verified email in SystemAuth, delivered through omnimail.

docs.title: Upgrade Notes
docs.text: No code changes are required. Applications that embed SystemAuth should switch from copied setup code to systemauthsvc. Note that importing systemauthsvc links the SQLite driver, which needs cgo; builds with CGO_ENABLED=0 work and use PostgreSQL.

docs.title: What's Next
docs.text: Verified email for SystemAuth via omnimail (INIT-SYSTEMFORGE-006), and consumer convergence onto the relying-party contract (INIT-SYSTEMFORGE-005 Phase 3).

docs.title: v0.14.0
docs.text:
Release Date: 2026-10-11

A breaking release with five themes. Principal is the sole identity root: the legacy User model and its tables are gone, so password login, social login, federation sync, and SCIM all resolve a person to the same principal (ADR-004). Managed principals let an application create humans without an email, such as young learners, whom guardian and educator managers control and sign in with QR-friendly login tokens (ADR-005), and management is now derived from manager relationships (ADR-009). A security pass makes the marketplace, organization, and invite APIs act for the authenticated caller and check organization permissions, instead of trusting the IDs a request names. The organization model is completed: organizations without a plan, signup on first login, slugs, application roles and entitlements carried in an orgs claim, collaborators and resource grants (ADR-006 to ADR-008), and real-time invalidation of access changes (ADR-010). Finally, the authorization modes are named rbac and rebac and chosen by configuration.

This release covers everything since v0.13.0. Read the upgrade notes before deploying; they are in two parts, one for the identity and security changes and one for the organization model.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• One identity model — Principal(type=human) + Human everywhere; systemauth.Storage works on HumanPrincipal.
  • Managed principals — opt-in per deployment and per client; guardian and educator managers; login tokens, a rate-limited exchange endpoint, manager visibility and revocation, guardian claims, and attaching an email later. See Managed Principals.
  • Caller-bound, authorized APIs — the marketplace, organization, and invite APIs identify the caller through requestprincipal and check organization permissions; without an authorizer they refuse rather than trust the request.
  • Provider parity — the simple and SpiceDB providers grant identical organization and manager permissions, enforced by a parity test against the base schema and a shared conformance suite.
  • AI agents at resource servers — identity/requestprincipal with an AAuth authenticator (aauthrs) next to bearer, API-key, and BFF-session authentication.
  • No organization plan — sf_organizations.plan and organization.Plan* are gone; organization responses carry entitlements derived from the marketplace. See Application roles and entitlements.
  • Slugs — reserved names, rename with a 7-day cooling-off period, aliases for old links, and personal-to-team conversion. See Organization slugs and Converting a personal organization to a team.
  • Application roles — assigned per principal, organization and application, limited to entitled applications and seat limits, and granted by invites. See Invites.
  • orgs claim and membership sources — ClaimsMemberships is the default relying-party source; RemoteMemberships reads GET /oauth/userinfo/memberships.
  • Real-time invalidation — access tokens default to 10 minutes (at most 15), every access-reducing change is recorded in sf_access_changes, and relying parties refuse earlier tokens; polling, replay and back-channel delivery cover replicas and separate deployments. See Access-change invalidation.
  • Collaborators and resource grants — viewer, contributor and maintainer on one resource, in rbac and rebac, and invites that target a resource. See Collaborators and resource grants.
  • Authorization mode as configuration — the authz key and authz/mode.New. See Configuring the authorization mode.
  • Management is a relationship — release, manager invitations (accept or decline), authorized managing operations and deletion.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
These fix vulnerabilities present in v0.13.0. Upgrade promptly.

  • Marketplace checkout took the purchaser from the request body, so anyone could start a purchase in another principal's name for any organization.
  • Marketplace listing, license, and seat endpoints acted on any IDs a request named.
  • The organization API listed every organization and let any caller read, change, or delete organizations, change members, and transfer ownership.
  • Invite management needed no permission, and anyone holding an invite link could accept it as any principal.
  • Invite tokens were stored in plain text; they are now SHA-256 hashes.
  • SpiceDB principal and organization cleanup ignored failures and missed editor and manager relations, leaving access behind while reporting success.
  • Refresh tokens could be used more than once, and refreshing near expiry extended a session indefinitely; rotation is now atomic, a session keeps its original expiry, and reusing a rotated refresh token revokes the whole token family.
  • Stripe checkout granted a license before a delayed payment cleared, an invalid seat count produced an unlimited seat-based license, and cancelling a subscription left its license in place.
  • Deactivating a principal did not stop its tokens: access tokens stayed valid and refresh tokens kept issuing new ones for up to 30 days. Tokens of an inactive principal are now refused wherever they are used or refreshed.
  • Agent delegation failed open: revoking a delegation gave the agent unrestricted access, constraints that did not overlap allowed everything, and expiry and action limits were never stored.
  • Revoking platform administration through principal.UpdateHuman was not synced to SpiceDB.
  • Signing up with an invite accepted any email, and SignupOrGetExisting returned existing accounts for unverified emails.
  • Anyone who could reach SystemAuth's authorization endpoint, or identity/oauth's, could obtain tokens for any user by sending an X-User-ID header. Header identity is now an explicit, gated opt-in, and identity/oauth also requires consent for third-party clients.
  • Rate limits, BFF sessions, and API key usage records believed client-supplied X-Forwarded-For, X-Real-IP, and Cloudflare headers, so a client could evade a limit or forge its address. They now key on the direct peer and believe forwarding headers only from proxies you configure.
  • SCIM listings skipped authorization, and a SCIM API mounted without a hook was open; the federation identity sync endpoint trusted its request body from anyone; token introspection accepted any token or public client as the caller; and the default storage accepted replayed client assertions.
  • API keys could be managed by ID alone and granted any scope when no allow-list was set; the BFF proxy could forward the browser's session cookie upstream; concurrent logins could exceed the lockout limit; and multiapp trusted the X-App-ID header.
  • BFF cookies could lose Secure and HttpOnly; cookie-authenticated writes skipped the same-origin check; JWTs without exp were accepted; client secret checks revealed which client IDs exist; and multiapp could leave one application's schema on a pooled connection.

docs.title: 1. Database
docs.text:
Run these against an existing PostgreSQL database; a fresh database needs only systemauth migrate.

Script When What migrations/0002_drop_legacy_user_tables.sql Before starting this release Creates the system service principal, reassigns OAuth apps owned by legacy users, drops the legacy tables migrations/0003_hash_invite_tokens.sql When deploying Hashes stored invite tokens so outstanding invite links keep working migrations/0004_drop_organization_plan.sql When deploying Drops sf_organizations.plan migrations/0005_subscriptions_per_listing.sql When deploying Adds listing_id to subscriptions and allows one subscription per listing beside the platform subscription migrations/0006_invite_app_roles.sql When deploying Adds sf_invites.app_roles migrations/0007_oauth_app_backchannel_logout_uri.sql When deploying Adds sf_oauth_apps.backchannel_logout_uri migrations/0008_drop_editor_viewer_roles.sql When deploying Maps editor to member and viewer to collaborator in memberships and pending invites, recording an access change for each active membership it changes migrations/0009_invite_resource_target.sql When deploying Adds the resource target columns to sf_invites

Run them in order; each is safe to run more than once. Then run systemauth migrate (or systemauthsvc.Service.Migrate) for the new tables and columns: sf_manager_relationships, sf_manager_claims, sf_client_assertion_jtis, the login_token credential type, and OAuthApp.managed_principals_enabled and login_token_ttl.

The organization model adds further tables, created by the same command: sf_app_roles, sf_slug_reservations, sf_access_changes, sf_resource_grants and sf_manager_invites.

docs.title: 2. Configure authorization for the HTTP APIs
docs.text:
The marketplace, organization, and invite APIs now require an authenticated caller, set by requestprincipal.Middleware, and an authorizer. Until the authorizer is configured, organization-scoped endpoints answer 501.

orgs := organization.NewService(db)
authorizer := rbac.New(
    rbac.WithRoleGetter(organization.MembershipRoleGetter(orgs)),
    rbac.WithPlatformAdminChecker(isPlatformAdmin), // optional
)

orgCfg := organization.DefaultAPIConfig()
orgCfg.Authorizer = authorizer
orgAPI := organization.NewAPI(orgs, orgCfg)

inviteCfg := invite.DefaultAPIConfig()
inviteCfg.Authorizer = authorizer
inviteAPI := invite.NewAPI(invite.NewService(db, baseURL), orgs, inviteCfg)

marketplace.NewAPI(humaAPI, marketplace.APIConfig{}, svc,
    marketplace.WithAuthorizer(authorizer))

// Mount each behind requestprincipal.Middleware so requests carry the caller.

With SpiceDB, pass the SpiceDB provider instead. MembershipRoleGetter counts only active memberships; a role getter built on GetMembership directly would also count deactivated ones.

docs.title: 3. Client changes
docs.text:
• Request fields that named the acting principal are optional and deprecated, and when sent must equal the caller: marketplace purchaser_id, owner_id, assigned_by; invite inviter_principal_id and principal_id; the email query on pending invites.
  • Accepting or declining an invite requires the caller's email to match the invite.
  • Listing organizations returns the caller's organizations (all of them for platform administrators).
  • Creating an organization makes the caller its owner.
  • Unpublished marketplace listings are visible only to the creator organization.

docs.title: 4. Go API changes
docs.text:
• Removed Ent schemas and packages: user, membership, oauthaccount, refreshtoken, apikey, serviceaccount, serviceaccountkeypair, and mixin.UserBase / mixin.MembershipBase.
  • systemauth.Storage user methods became CreateHuman, GetHuman, GetHumanByEmail, GetHumanByExternalIdentity, LinkExternalIdentity, UpdateHuman, DeleteHuman on HumanPrincipal; systemauth.User and ErrUserNotFound / ErrUserExists are replaced by HumanPrincipal, ErrPrincipalNotFound, ErrPrincipalExists.
  • OAuth tokens and authorization codes use the subject column; OAuthConsent.user_id is principal_id; OAuthApp.owner references Principal.
  • Human.email is optional; HumanPrincipal.Email, principal.Human.Email, and contract identity types may be empty for a managed principal. Existing creation paths still require an email.
  • invite.Invite has no Token field; the token is only in InviteResult.InviteURL.
  • The authz providers are named for the mode they evaluate: authz/simple is now authz/rbac (role-based: roles plus direct grants), and authz/spicedb is now authz/rebac/spicedb (relationship-based, with SpiceDB as the engine). The old paths remain as deprecated forwarding packages for this release; change imports to the new paths, and staticcheck reports any you miss.
  • spicedb.BaseSchema equals authz.BaseSpiceDBSchema and is deprecated: members hold contribute, not edit, on an organization, and editors are recognized.
  • Interfaces gained methods: authz.RelationshipSyncer (AddPrincipalManager, RemovePrincipalManager) and credential.Service (IssueLoginToken, VerifyLoginToken).
  • organization.Service ListMembers and ListMemberships exclude inactive memberships unless IncludeInactive is passed.
  • identity/token returns typed errors: ErrInvalidAccessToken, ErrInvalidRefreshToken, ErrRefreshTokenReused, ErrDPoPMismatch, ErrScopeNotGranted.
  • marketplace.LicenseService gains GetByStripeSubscriptionID.
  • identity/delegation returns typed errors, Link gains Active, and an agent without a delegation is denied.
  • signup.SignupOrGetExisting returns an existing account only when SignupInput.EmailVerified is set; SignupWithInvite requires the invited email.
  • apikey.Service Get, Revoke, and Delete take the owning principal first; use RevokeInOrganization for an administrator of an organization-scoped key. A service with no AllowedScopes refuses keys that request scopes unless AllowAnyScope is set, and MaxKeysPerUser is enforced.
  • rls.Helper.SetTenant and SetUser return ErrNotInTransaction for *sql.DB and *sql.Conn, because SET LOCAL outside a transaction scopes nothing. rls.Middleware.SetRLSContext only puts the caller on the request context; run queries through Middleware.WithTx or rls.WithTenant.
  • principal lookups return principal.ErrNotFound; type-specific updates return ErrWrongType; CreateAgent returns ErrInvalidDelegator.

docs.title: 5. Behavior changes
docs.text:
• The default BFF session cookie is sf_session (was cf_session); browsers holding the old cookie sign in again.
  • SCIM users are human principals; users provisioned before this release are not visible through SCIM. Managed principals are never SCIM users.

docs.title: 6. Stripe webhooks
docs.text: Subscribe your Stripe webhook endpoint to checkout.session.async_payment_succeeded in addition to checkout.session.completed: licenses for delayed payment methods are now granted when the payment clears, not when checkout completes. Subscribing to customer.subscription.deleted makes cancellation revoke the license.

docs.title: 7. User authentication for the authorization endpoint
docs.text:
systemauth.WithUserIDHeader is removed, and DefaultSessionProvider no longer believes any header on its own: it sends every authorization request to the login URL. A deployment that relied on a gateway setting X-User-ID must say so, and say which requests may be believed:

gate, err := systemauth.TrustedProxyNetworks("10.0.0.0/8") // the gateway's addresses
if err != nil { return err }
provider := systemauth.NewDefaultSessionProvider(
    systemauth.WithTrustedUserIDHeader("X-User-ID", gate),
)

Use systemauth.TrustAllRequests only when the server is reachable solely through a gateway that overwrites the header; the gate judges the direct peer address, never X-Forwarded-For. Social login and custom SessionProviders need no change. identity/oauth takes oauth.WithUserAuthenticator (or WithTrustedUserIDHeader) and WithConsent; without them its authorization endpoint answers server_error or access_denied.

docs.title: 8. Proxies, SCIM, federation, and introspection
docs.text:
• Behind a reverse proxy, tell SystemForge which proxies to believe, or every client will share the proxy's address: ratelimit.ForwardedIPKey("10.0.0.0/8") for limits, bff.ClientIPConfig{TrustProxy: true, TrustedProxies: ...} for sessions (and CloudflareIPRanges for Cloudflare), systemauth.WithLoginTokenClientIP(...), and an IPExtractor for the API key middleware.
  • SCIM now answers 403 until you pass scim.WithAuthorizationHook (for example scim.NewScopedAuthorizationHook(true)).
  • Federation: pass systemauth.WithFederationAuthenticator(systemauth.SharedSecretAuthenticator(secret)) to NewFederationEndpoints, or the sync and lookup routes are not registered.
  • Introspection: resource servers must authenticate as a confidential client or present a token carrying the introspect scope.
  • Rate limiting fails closed: a storage outage answers 503. Pass ratelimit.WithFailOpen() to keep the old behavior.
  • Tokens: session/jwt and the contract middleware require exp; use jwt.ValidateAccessTokenForAudience or middleware.HTTPAuthForAudience on routes that serve one kind of client.
  • Lockout: call Lockout.Begin before verifying a password and Attempt.Success or Failure after; CheckAndRecord is deprecated.
  • multiapp apps that share a signing key should set MiddlewareConfig.AppAudiences and mint tokens with jwt.TokenOptions{Audience: ...}; apps with their own keys need nothing.
  • multiapp: AppAwareDB.ForSchema returns an error; SchemaDB.AcquireConn is deprecated in favor of Begin.

docs.title: 9. Managed principals (optional)
docs.text: Nothing changes unless you opt in. To enable, set managed_principals.enabled in the SystemAuth configuration and managed_principals: true on each client that may use them, then wire identity/managedprincipal. If you use the marketplace, add stripe.WithPurchaserChecker(managedPrincipalService) so managed principals cannot purchase.

docs.title: Organization model
docs.text: The next sections cover the organization model; they apply to every deployment.

docs.title: 10. Organization roles and the plan
docs.text:
• editor and viewer are no longer organization roles. The roles are owner, admin, member and collaborator; any other value is refused with ErrInvalidRole. Replace them in your own tables, vocabularies and invites; use resource roles for access to one resource.
  • Remove Plan from organization inputs and filters, and from API requests. Supply APIConfig.Entitlements with marketplace.EntitlementSource to return entitlements.

docs.title: 11. Entitlements fail closed
docs.text: An approle.Service with no entitlement source entitles no organization to any application. Build it with marketplace.ApproleOptions(src), and declare applications free to everyone with marketplace.WithDefaultEntitlements. approle.EntitleAll is for development and tests. marketplace.WarnIfNoEntitlements logs a startup warning when nothing entitles anyone.

docs.title: 12. Relying parties read claims
docs.text: The default membership source is ClaimsMemberships, which decodes the orgs claim. LocalMemberships is no longer picked up implicitly; pass it explicitly for development and tests. Use ClaimsOrRemoteMemberships when the claim may be truncated or absent.

docs.title: 13. Token lifetime and revocation
docs.text: The default access token lifetime is 10 minutes (it was 15), a configured value above 15 minutes is refused at load, and per-client values are capped. Pass a relyingparty.RevocationCache to BearerMiddleware and NewBFF, and feed it as described in Access-change invalidation.

docs.title: 14. Authorization schema and packages
docs.text:
• The marketplace SpiceDB fragment attaches to the base organization through a marketplace_org facet and no longer redefines principal or organization. Compose schemas with MergeSchema, or let authz/mode.New compose and write them.
  • Build the provider from configuration with authz/mode.New. The authz/simple and authz/spicedb forwarding packages (renamed in this release) remain deprecated and will be removed in the next major release; import authz/rbac and authz/rebac/spicedb.
  • Switching to rebac starts with an empty graph; write existing memberships, application roles and grants through the syncer before serving requests.

docs.title: New Features
docs.text:
• identity/managedprincipal: Create, AddManager, RemoveManager, ListManagers, ManagerRoles, IsManaged, IssueLoginToken, ListLoginTokens, RevokeLoginToken, ListSessions, RevokeSession, RevokeAll, IssueClaim, RedeemClaim, AttachVerifiedEmail, and NewHandler.
  • SystemAuth: POST /login-token, the managed claim, Server.ManagedPrincipalsAllowed, Server.LoginTokenPolicy, WithCredentialService, WithLoginTokenRateLimit.
  • identity/credential: login tokens and LoginTokenPolicy.
  • authz: OrgRolePermissions, PermOrg*, ManagerRolePermissions, PermManage*, NewPrincipalResource; rbac.WithManagerRoleGetter; providertest.RunOrgPermissionTests and RunManagerRelationTests; spicedb.Client.DeleteRelationships (now under authz/rebac/spicedb).
  • identity/requestprincipal: RequestPrincipal, authenticator chain and middleware, PrincipalUUID; aauthrs for AAuth agents; relyingparty.NewRequestAuthenticator.
  • marketplace: WithAuthorizer, WithPurchaseAuthorizer, OrgRolePurchaseAuthorizer, WithCallerResolver, PurchaserChecker; stripe.WithPurchaserChecker.
  • organization: MembershipRoleGetter, ErrMembershipNotFound, ListOrganizationsInput.MemberPrincipalID.
  • identity/pgschema (PostgreSQL lower(email) unique index), identity/clientassertion JWT ID replay protection, and store.Config.TrustProvisionedEmail for SCIM.
  • Signup on first social login (signup.SlugForLogin, CreatePersonalOrgInTx, EnsurePersonalOrgInTx); reserved slugs (organization.ReservedSlugs, WithReservedSlugs); Rename, ResolveSlug, WithSlugCoolingOff; ConvertToTeam; personal organization rules (ErrPersonalOrganization).
  • identity/approle: Assign, Change, Remove, RemoveForMember, EffectiveRoles, endpoints under /organizations/{slug}/members/{principal_id}/app-roles, and authz.AppRoleSyncer.
  • marketplace: EntitlementSource, ApproleOptions, WithDefaultEntitlements, WarnIfNoEntitlements; listings may name an application and subscriptions may be per listing.
  • systemauth: the orgs claim, GET /oauth/userinfo/memberships, GET /access-changes, NewBackchannel, and the backchannel_logout_uri client setting.
  • identity/accesschange, relyingparty.RevocationCache, NewAccessChangePoller, Replay, BackchannelHandler; relying-party membership sources ClaimsMemberships, RemoteMemberships, ClaimsOrRemoteMemberships, ProvisioningMemberships.
  • identity/resourcegrant, the resource-role ladder and authz.ResourceGranter; rbac.WithResourceGrants; resource-targeted invites.
  • authz.ModeConfig, authz/mode.New and systemauth.Config.Authz.
  • identity/managedprincipal: Release, manager invitations with accept and decline, Delete, and the managing operations over HTTP.

docs.title: Fixes
docs.text:
• The marketplace, organization, and invite APIs panicked at registration.
  • The simple provider denied every organization permission check.
  • SCIM listing panicked on every ascending sort.
  • identity/oauth.NewProvider panicked on construction, and token revocation had no effect.
  • private_key_jwt client authentication failed under foreign-key enforcement.
  • A managed principal's first relying-party sign-in failed; empty emails could be matched or adopted; invite emails were compared case-sensitively; organizations created without a plan failed.
  • Accepting an invite, and social login signup, register memberships, principals and organizations with the authorization graph.
  • Signup creates the principal and personal organization in one transaction.
  • The application-role seat limit cannot be exceeded by concurrent assignments, and assigning with no seat left answers 409.
  • Manager authority checks for AddManager, RemoveManager and Release run inside the row-locked transaction, a managed principal is never a valid manager, and access-change reasons are accurate.

The complete list is in the changelog.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
• Managed Principals, and updates to Users, Account Security, and authorization conventions.
  • ADRs live in docs/design/adrs/, with an index of statuses and a Design section in the docs nav.
  • Architecture pages describe the implemented behavior: Organizations and Membership, Managed Principals and Authorization.
  • New guides: Invites, Application roles and entitlements, Collaborators and resource grants, Organization slugs, Personal to team conversion, Access-change invalidation and Authorization mode.
  • Design of record: ADR-004, ADR-005, ADR-006, ADR-007, ADR-008 (with guidance on choosing rbac or rebac), ADR-009 and ADR-010.
  • Feature specifications moved from docs/design/ to docs/specs/.

docs.title: What's Next
docs.text: Verified email for SystemAuth through omnimail (INIT-SYSTEMFORGE-006), which also drives the managed-principal attach-email flow.

docs.title: v0.15.0
docs.text:
Release Date: 2026-10-13

This release covers everything since v0.14.0. It has five themes: key management through keyforge, connections to external services through connectionforge, invite-only sign-up with a waitlist, an app catalog for product switchers, and the orgs claim with per-application roles in embedded SystemAuth. It has no breaking changes. Run systemauth migrate for the new tables.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• Key management. The keys package wires keyforge as the platform's one key library: envelope encryption, rotation without re-encrypting stored data, the root key read through omnivault, and key events sent to the audit trail. See Key management and ADR-013.
  • Connections to external services. The connections package composes connectionforge: an organization connects accounts at services such as a CDN or analytics product, credentials are sealed under managed keys, and an application receives an authenticated HTTP client, never the secret. See Connections and ADR-017.
  • A connections API. /api/v1/organizations/{org}/connections is served by SystemAuth when the new connections configuration section is set, behind the systemforge:connections:read and :write scopes.
  • Invite-only sign-up. Social login can admit only verified emails that hold an invite. Everyone else reaches a waitlist that records the consent text they were shown. systemauth invite and systemauth waitlist manage both. See Deploying SystemAuth.
  • App catalog. A host publishes the applications it runs at /.well-known/sf-apps, and /bff/session lists the catalog so each shell shows the products a person holds a role in for the current organization.
  • Per-application roles in tokens. Embedded SystemAuth emits the orgs claim with each organization's application roles, so relying parties keep no membership tables.
  • A PostgreSQL fix. rls.Helper.SetTenant and SetUser failed on every real PostgreSQL connection; they now work.

docs.title: Upgrade notes
docs.text:
There are no breaking changes, but there are new tables and one new optional configuration section.

  1. Migrate. Run systemauth migrate (or systemauthsvc.Service.Migrate). It creates sf_signup_invites and sf_signup_waitlist. Existing tables are unchanged and there is no SQL migration file to apply by hand.
  2. Enabling connections is optional. Without the connections section nothing changes: no routes are mounted and no keys are opened.
  3. To enable them, add the section, create a root key, and back up the keys directory with the database:
connections:
  keys_dir: /var/lib/systemauth/keys
  vault: env://
  root_key: SYSTEMAUTH_KEYS_ROOT

export SYSTEMAUTH_KEYS_ROOT="$(openssl rand -base64 32)"   # keep a second copy offline

Connections need a database and the role-based authorization mode. systemauth migrate then creates the connectionforge_* tables and, on PostgreSQL, enables row-level security on them keyed on owner_id. Run the migration with a role allowed to change the schema. 4. Register providers. An embedding application passes the providers it supports through systemauthsvc.Options.Providers. Without any, the API serves an empty provider list. 5. Request the new scopes. Clients of the connections API ask for systemforge:connections:read and systemforge:connections:write.

docs.title: Key management
docs.text:
Piece Where it lives Root key Your secret store, read through omnivault at startup Key ring A file in the keys directory, sealed under the root key Registry A SQLite database in the same directory Data Your database, as ciphertext that names the key version 
k, err := keys.Open(ctx, keys.Options{
    Dir:      "/var/lib/myapp/keys",
    Root:     keys.VaultSource(vault, "MYAPP_KEYS_ROOT"),
    Purposes: []keyforge.Purpose{"myapp.sessions"},
})
sealed, err := k.Seal(ctx, "myapp.sessions", []byte("value"), []byte("user:42"))

This release uses keyforge's single-host setup. Moving its registry to the platform database needs keyforge to accept an external registry and is recorded in ADR-013. keyforge is not externally audited.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
• Each connection is validated with its provider before it is stored, and a rejected credential stores nothing.
  • A connection holds no secret. Its credential is sealed under the connectionforge.credential purpose with additional data binding the organization, the connection and the credential version.
  • Organization owners and admins can view, use and manage connections; members can view them. A connection's creator manages it.
  • Requests made through a connection reach only its provider's hosts, over HTTPS, never a private address.
  • Tenant isolation holds twice: queries filter on the organization, and on PostgreSQL row-level security refuses another organization's rows.
Method and path Action GET /api/v1/providers Provider manifests GET /api/v1/organizations/{org}/connections Connections the caller may view POST /api/v1/organizations/{org}/connections Connect and validate GET, PATCH, DELETE .../connections/{id} Read, rename, disconnect POST .../connections/{id}/test Validate again; the result is in health

docs.title: Sign-up gating
docs.text:
• SignupGate decides whether an upstream login may create a new account. It never affects people who already have one.
  • A refusal never says why, and goes to WithSignupDeniedURL (validated at startup) or to the waitlist page.
  • The waitlist records the consent text shown and its version, answers the same whether or not an address was already listed, and is rate-limited per client and per address.
  • serve --invite-only, systemauth invite add|list|revoke, and systemauth waitlist list [--csv] and remove.
  • A host binary embedding SystemAuth sets systemauthsvc.Options.InviteOnly, SignupDeniedURL and WaitlistPage, and mounts the same commands from signupgate/signupcmd in its own CLI.

docs.title: App catalog and the orgs claim
docs.text:
• appcatalog describes the applications a deployment hosts: identifier, name, launch URL, icon and order. Static serves one in the same process; Remote fetches what SystemAuth publishes, cached and kept through an outage.
  • systemauthsvc.Options.Apps publishes a catalog and warns about entries with no registered vocabulary, since nobody can hold a role in them.
  • systemauthsvc.Options.Vocabularies and DefaultEntitlements install the orgs claim source: application roles come from approle, limited to the default entitlements. An owner holds the top role of each entitled application, and a registered application outside the defaults stays closed.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text: • rls.Helper.SetTenant and SetUser on PostgreSQL. They issued SET LOCAL ... = $1, which PostgreSQL rejects because SET takes no bind parameters. They use set_config(name, value, true), which has the same transaction scope and takes the value as a parameter, so a value with a quote is safe. A test now runs it against a real server.

docs.title: Dependencies
docs.text:
Module Version github.com/plexusone/keyforge v0.1.0 (new) github.com/plexusone/connectionforge v0.1.0 (new) github.com/plexusone/omnivault v0.5.0 (new) github.com/plexusone/omnistorage-core v0.5.2 github.com/go-chi/chi/v5 v5.4.0 github.com/grokify/guardsql v0.3.0 golang.org/x/crypto v0.58.0

github.com/yaronf/httpsign stays at v0.5.2: v0.6 removed NewJWSSignerV3, which aauth-go v0.2.0 still calls, and pulls in jwx/v4. Requires Go 1.26.

docs.title: Known limitations
docs.text:
• Connections support static API tokens only. GitHub App and OAuth connections follow in connectionforge.
  • Role-based authorization only for connections. Startup refuses connections with the relationship-based mode.
  • No grants API for connections yet. Only owners, admins and a connection's creator can use one; the resource-grant ladder is mapped but not exposed.
  • SystemAuth passes no audit store to keys, so key lifecycle events are not recorded there, and connection events go to the server log.
  • keyforge's control plane is not mounted, so there is no status or manual rotation endpoint yet.
  • keyforge and connectionforge are not externally audited.

docs.title: v0.16.0
docs.text:
Release Date: 2026-10-14

This release has two themes: connection sharing and dependency tracking (reconnect, bindings and grants over the connections API) and the rename of the connection library from connectionforge to connectforge. The rename is breaking for anyone who deployed v0.15.0 with connections enabled; see the upgrade notes.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• Reconnect. POST .../connections/{id}/reconnect replaces a connection's credential in place when a token expires or is revoked, keeping its bindings and grants.
  • Bindings. GET, PUT and DELETE .../connections/{id}/bindings record which features depend on a connection, so disconnecting shows what would stop working.
  • Grants. GET, PUT and DELETE .../connections/{id}/grants/{principal} give a principal a viewer, contributor or maintainer role on one connection. They are the platform's resource grants (ADR-008) on the new systemforge_connection resource type, not a second authority.
  • Renamed library. connections now depends on github.com/plexusone/connectforge v0.3.0. See Connections and ADR-017.

docs.title: Upgrade notes
docs.text:
1. Update imports. Code that imports github.com/plexusone/connectionforge must import github.com/plexusone/connectforge. The API is otherwise unchanged.
  2. Deployments that enabled connections in v0.15.0 need a data step. The tables are now named connectforge_* and credentials are sealed under the connectforge.credential key purpose. systemauth migrate creates the new tables; it does not copy rows from connectionforge_*, and existing credentials, sealed under the old purpose, are not readable under the new one. Before upgrading, either re-create the connections after migrating or rename the tables and re-seal credentials under the new purpose. Deployments that never enabled connections are unaffected.
  3. Run systemauth migrate. On PostgreSQL it also enables row-level security on the new tables.
  4. New roles, no new scopes. Grants reuse systemforge:connections:read and :write. Members still hold only view on a connection until it is granted to them.

docs.title: Known limits
docs.text:
• Disconnecting does not yet require acknowledging the bindings it would stop; list them with GET .../bindings first.
  • OAuth authorization, its callback and credential replacement through a provider flow are not yet supported.

docs.title: v0.17.0
docs.text:
Release Date: 2026-10-18

This release lets relying-party applications manage managed principals (people without an email, such as a child, whose accounts managers control) through SystemAuth, instead of holding SystemAuth's database. It also tightens two defaults: nobody becomes a manager without agreeing, and an application that is not federated refuses contract operations. Both are breaking; see the upgrade notes.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• Managed-principal API on SystemAuth. When managed principals are enabled, SystemAuth built by systemauthsvc serves /managed-principals. A relying party calls it with the signed-in manager's access token, granted systemforge:managed_principals, to create and list managed principals, issue and revoke login tokens, end sessions, list and remove managers, issue and redeem claims, and invite managers. The client is taken from the token and every write is audited when Options.AuditEmitter is set. See Managed Principals.
  • A client for relying parties. identity/managedprincipal/mpclient is a typed Go client over that API, with errors wrapped in *APIError. See Relying Parties.
  • Bearer access with the client. systemauth.Server.BearerAccess and BearerAuthenticator authenticate SystemAuth access tokens and carry the token's client, scopes and token ID, adapted to requestprincipal.
  • Managers join with consent. managedprincipal.Service.Create names only the acting manager, and AddManager is refused; other managers join by accepting an invitation or redeeming a claim. WithDirectManagerAdds keeps direct adds for administrator tooling.
  • Issuing a login token needs manage_credentials, which guardians and educators hold, so an application-defined role cannot issue one.
  • One answer for principals that are not the caller's. The managed-principal handler answers 403 for an unknown or unmanaged principal, as for one the caller does not manage.
  • Contract operations need federation. The contract's identity, policy and audit operations answer 403 until the application is federated, including after it leaves a federation. Meta and health stay open. See Product Contract.

docs.title: Upgrade notes
docs.text:
1. Standalone applications that serve the contract API. Identity, policy and audit operations now answer 403 while the application is not federated. Federate the application, or set Config.AllowUnauthenticatedStandalone in development and tests where untrusted callers cannot reach the endpoints.
  2. Code that adds managers directly. Create with managers other than the actor, and AddManager, return ErrConsentRequired. Invite those managers or issue a claim. Administrator tooling and migrations can build the service with managedprincipal.WithDirectManagerAdds().
  3. Custom manager roles. A manager in a role registered with WithRoles can no longer issue login tokens. Issue them as a guardian or educator.
  4. Enabling the API for a relying party. Set managed_principals.enabled for the deployment, managed_principals: true on the application's client, and add systemforge:managed_principals to the client's scopes. The application requests the scope when the manager signs in.
  5. No migration. This release adds no schema changes.

docs.title: Known limits
docs.text:
• The API does not attach a verified email to a managed principal: a relying party cannot prove that an address belongs to the principal. It waits for verified email through SystemAuth.
  • Rate-limit storage for the API's code routes is in memory by default; deployments with several instances pass shared storage through Options.ManagedPrincipalRates.
  • Organization management is not served to relying parties; organizations are managed in SystemAuth and reach applications through the orgs claim.

docs.title: v0.2.0 Release Notes
docs.text:
Release Date: 2026-03-08

SystemForge v0.2.0 introduces SpiceDB for Zanzibar-style relationship-based access control (ReBAC), a principal-based identity model, and SCIM 2.0 user provisioning. This release also removes the Casbin authorization provider in favor of SpiceDB.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• SpiceDB authorization provider for Zanzibar-style relationship-based access control (ReBAC)
  • Principal-based identity model supporting humans, agents, applications, and service principals
  • SCIM 2.0 user provisioning with filter, patch, and bulk operations
  • Identity-authorization sync automatically maintains SpiceDB relationships on identity changes

docs.title: SpiceDB Authorization
docs.text:
A complete SpiceDB integration for fine-grained, relationship-based access control:

  • Embedded mode for development with in-memory or PostgreSQL datastores
  • Remote mode for production SpiceDB clusters
  • BaseSchema providing organization and platform permission models
  • ResourceSchema() helper for defining custom resource types
  • RelationshipSyncer interface for identity lifecycle integration
  • Integration tests with embedded SpiceDB server

docs.title: Principal-Based Identity
docs.text:
A unified identity model supporting multiple principal types:

  • Human principals with email, password hash, locale, timezone, and avatar
  • Agent principals for AI/bot identities
  • Application principals for OAuth client applications
  • ServicePrincipal for service-to-service authentication
  • PrincipalMembership for organization role assignments
  • PrincipalToken for token lifecycle management

docs.title: SCIM 2.0 Provisioning
docs.text:
Standards-compliant user provisioning for enterprise identity management:

  • User CRUD endpoints following SCIM 2.0 specification
  • Filter support for querying users by attributes
  • Patch operations with SystemForge-compliant handling
  • Bulk operations for batch user management
  • Enterprise extension support for department, manager, etc.

docs.title: Coreauth Authentication Server
docs.text:
A standalone authentication server built on Fosite:

  • OAuth 2.0 endpoints for authorization, token, and introspection
  • OIDC discovery and JWKS endpoints
  • Principal integration with the new identity model
  • CLI tool for server and key management operations

docs.title: Identity-Authorization Sync
docs.text:
Automatic synchronization between identity and authorization layers:

  • RelationshipSyncer interface for abstracting sync operations
  • SpiceDB syncer implementation with batch support
  • No-op syncer for deployments without SpiceDB
  • Strict and eventual sync modes for consistency trade-offs
  • Organization service wiring for membership sync
  • Principal service wiring for lifecycle sync

docs.title: Casbin Removal
docs.text:
The Casbin authorization provider has been removed. Applications using Casbin should migrate to either:

  • SpiceDB provider for relationship-based access control
  • Simple provider for basic role hierarchy checks

Migration steps:

  1. Replace authz/casbin imports with authz/spicedb
  2. Update provider initialization to use SpiceDB
  3. Define SpiceDB schema for your resource types
  4. Migrate existing policies to SpiceDB relationships

docs.title: Identity Model Changes
docs.text:
The identity model has been refactored to use principals:

  • User entity renamed to Human (principal subtype)
  • Membership replaced by PrincipalMembership
  • New Principal entity as unified identity root

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: go get github.com/grokify/systemforge@v0.2.0

docs.title: Quick Start: SpiceDB
docs.text:
package main

import (
    "context"
    "github.com/grokify/systemforge/authz/spicedb"
)

func main() {
    // Create embedded SpiceDB client (development)
    client, err := spicedb.NewClient(spicedb.Config{
        Mode: spicedb.ModeEmbedded,
        EmbeddedConfig: &spicedb.EmbeddedConfig{
            Datastore: "memory",
        },
    })
    if err != nil {
        panic(err)
    }
    defer client.Close()

    // Write schema
    schema := spicedb.BaseSchema + spicedb.ResourceSchema("document")
    if err := client.WriteSchema(context.Background(), schema); err != nil {
        panic(err)
    }

    // Create provider
    provider := spicedb.NewProvider(client)

    // Check permission
    allowed, err := provider.Can(ctx, principal, "view", resource)
}

docs.title: Quick Start: Principal Identity
docs.text:
package main

import (
    "context"
    "github.com/grokify/systemforge/identity/principal"
)

func main() {
    svc := principal.NewService(entClient)

    // Create human principal
    human, err := svc.CreateHuman(ctx, principal.CreateHumanInput{
        Email:           "user@example.com",
        DisplayName:     "Example User",
        IsPlatformAdmin: false,
    })
}

docs.title: From v0.1.0
docs.text:
1. Update imports: Replace authz/casbin with authz/spicedb or authz/simple
  2. Update identity code: Use Human instead of User, PrincipalMembership instead of Membership
  3. Add SpiceDB schema: Define your resource types using BaseSchema and ResourceSchema()
  4. Wire syncer: Inject RelationshipSyncer into identity services

docs.title: SpiceDB Setup
docs.text:
For production, deploy SpiceDB separately:

# docker-compose.yml
services:
  spicedb:
    image: authzed/spicedb:latest
    command: serve
    environment:
      SPICEDB_GRPC_PRESHARED_KEY: your-secret-key
      SPICEDB_DATASTORE_ENGINE: postgres
      SPICEDB_DATASTORE_CONN_URI: postgres://...
    ports:

docs.title: v0.3.0 Release Notes
docs.text:
Release Date: 2026-03-14

SystemForge v0.3.0 introduces vendor-agnostic observability through OmniObserve integration, a SaaS marketplace with Stripe billing, and Redis-backed rate limiting. This release also adds OAuth client management and CoreAuth provider abstraction.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• Vendor-agnostic observability with OmniObserve supporting Datadog, New Relic, Dynatrace, and OTLP backends
  • SaaS marketplace infrastructure with Stripe subscription management and seat-based licensing
  • Redis-backed rate limiting with sliding window and token bucket algorithms
  • OAuth client management and provider abstraction for CoreAuth

docs.title: Observability Integration
docs.text:
A complete observability package wrapping OmniObserve for vendor-agnostic telemetry:

  • Provider-agnostic API supporting OTLP, Datadog, New Relic, and Dynatrace
  • HTTP middleware for automatic request tracing and metrics
  • slog integration with trace context injection
  • Pre-defined metrics for CoreAuth and rate limiting
  • Zero-config defaults with environment variable configuration

docs.title: Marketplace
docs.text:
A SaaS marketplace implementation with Stripe integration:

  • Listing entity for marketplace products with tiers and pricing
  • Subscription management with Stripe webhook handling
  • License model supporting per-seat and usage-based billing
  • SeatAssignment for managing user access to subscriptions
  • Stripe SDK v82 integration for payment processing

docs.title: Rate Limiting
docs.text:
Production-ready rate limiting infrastructure:

  • CoreAPI package with policy-based rate limit controls
  • Redis backend for distributed rate limiting
  • Sliding window algorithm for accurate request counting
  • Token bucket algorithm for burst handling
  • Middleware integration with session context

docs.title: OAuth Client Management
docs.text:
Enhanced OAuth client capabilities:

  • OAuth client service in identity/oauthclient package
  • Provider abstraction for pluggable CoreAuth backends
  • Federation handlers with improved context handling
  • JWT enhancements with audience and issuer validation

docs.title: Session Improvements
docs.text:
Session and middleware enhancements:

  • Context utilities for session data access
  • Improved middleware composition patterns
  • Enhanced JWT claims with standard claim validation

package main

}

docs.title: v0.5.0 Release Notes
docs.text: Release Date: 2026-04-05

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• Audience-Aware JWT Tokens: Separate BFF (web browser) and API (programmatic) clients with distinct audience claims for strict path separation
  • Ent-Backed Stores: Production-ready database storage for API keys and BFF sessions using Ent ORM
  • Token Encryption: AES-256-GCM encryption for tokens at rest in BFF session storage
  • Reusable Ent Mixins: Drop-in schema mixins for API keys and BFF sessions

docs.title: Audience-Aware JWT Tokens (session/jwt)
docs.text:
New methods for generating audience-scoped tokens:

  • GenerateBFFTokenPair(): Create token pairs for web clients with aud: "bff"
  • GenerateAPIToken(): Create scoped tokens for API clients with aud: "api"
  • GenerateAccessTokenWithAudience(): Create tokens with custom audiences
  • ValidateAccessTokenWithAudience(): Validate tokens with audience checking

New Claims helpers:

  • Audience(): Get first audience value
  • HasAudience(aud): Check for specific audience
  • WithAudience(...): Set audience (builder pattern)
import "github.com/grokify/systemforge/session/jwt"

// Generate BFF token pair for web clients
pair, err := svc.GenerateBFFTokenPair(userID, email, name)

// Generate API token for programmatic access
token, err := svc.GenerateAPIToken(userID, email, name, []string{"read:users"})

// Validate with audience checking
claims, err := svc.ValidateAccessTokenWithAudience(token, "api")

decrypted, err := encryptor.DecryptString(encrypted)

docs.title: Ent Schema Mixins (identity/ent/mixin)
docs.text:
Reusable mixins for your Ent schemas:

APIKey Mixin fields:

  • id, name, prefix, key_hash (sensitive)
  • owner_id, organization_id, scopes, description
  • environment (live/test), expires_at, last_used_at, last_used_ip
  • revoked, revoked_at, revoked_reason, metadata, timestamps
  • Indexes: owner_id, organization_id, prefix, key_hash (unique), environment

BFFSession Mixin fields:

  • id, user_id, organization_id
  • access_token_encrypted, refresh_token_encrypted (sensitive)
  • dpop_key_pair_encrypted, dpop_thumbprint
  • ip_address, user_agent, metadata
  • last_accessed_at, expires_at, timestamps
  • Indexes: user_id, expires_at, organization_id
// your-app/ent/schema/api_key.go
package schema

import (
    "entgo.io/ent"
    cfmixin "github.com/grokify/systemforge/identity/ent/mixin"
)

type APIKey struct {
    ent.Schema
}

func (APIKey) Mixin() []ent.Mixin {
    return []ent.Mixin{
        cfmixin.APIKeyMixin{},
    }
}

docs.title: v0.6.0 Release Notes
docs.text: Release Date: 2026-04-12

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• Multi-App Platform: Run multiple SaaS apps on shared backend infrastructure with complete data isolation
  • Schema-Per-App Isolation: Each app gets its own PostgreSQL schema for database isolation
  • X-App-ID Routing: Header-based request routing to registered app backends

docs.title: Multi-App Server (multiapp/)
docs.text:
New package for running multiple apps on shared infrastructure:

  • MultiAppMode: Multiple apps share a server, routed by X-App-ID header
  • SingleAppMode: One app runs on dedicated infrastructure
  • Schema-per-app database isolation using PostgreSQL schemas (app_ prefix)
  • Redis and in-memory cache implementations with app-scoped prefixes
import "github.com/grokify/systemforge/multiapp"

// Create multi-app server
server, err := multiapp.NewServer(multiapp.Config{
    Mode:        multiapp.MultiAppMode,
    DatabaseURL: os.Getenv("DATABASE_URL"),
    RedisURL:    os.Getenv("REDIS_URL"),  // optional
})

// Register apps
server.RegisterApp(app1.NewBackend(nil))
server.RegisterApp(app2.NewBackend(nil))
server.RegisterApp(app3.NewBackend(nil))

// Run server
server.Run(":8080")

docs.title: AppBackend Interface
docs.text:
Composable interface for app registration with lifecycle hooks:

type AppBackend interface {
    // Slug returns unique app identifier (used in X-App-ID header)
    Slug() string

    // Name returns human-readable app name
    Name() string

    // Routes returns the app's HTTP routes
    Routes(deps Dependencies) chi.Router

    // Migrations returns database migrations (optional)
    Migrations() []Migration

    // OnRegister is called after app registration
    OnRegister(ctx context.Context, cfg *AppConfig) error

    // OnShutdown is called during graceful shutdown
    OnShutdown(ctx context.Context) error
}

docs.title: SystemForge Integration (multiapp/)
docs.text:
Integration helpers connecting multiapp with SystemForge modules:

  • Claims Helpers: JWT claims extraction and validation for multi-tenant context
  • Session Management: Multi-tenant session helpers with app-scoped storage
  • Ent Factory: Create schema-isolated Ent clients from multiapp database
  • HTTP Middleware: Authentication and tenant context propagation
// In your handlers:
func (h *Handler) HandleRequest(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    ctx := r.Context()

    // App context (from X-App-ID routing)
    appCtx := multiapp.AppContextFromContext(ctx)
    appCtx.AppID          // "app1"
    appCtx.DatabaseSchema // "app_app1"

    // JWT claims (from auth middleware)
    claims := middleware.ClaimsFromContext(ctx)
    claims.PrincipalID    // user UUID
    claims.OrganizationID // org UUID
}

docs.text:
Complete example demonstrating the AppBackend interface:

type ExampleBackend struct{}

func (b *ExampleBackend) Slug() string { return "example" }
func (b *ExampleBackend) Name() string { return "Example App" }

func (b *ExampleBackend) Routes(deps multiapp.Dependencies) chi.Router {

        w.Write([]byte("OK"))
    })
    return r
}

docs.title: Generic 404 Responses
docs.text:
The multiapp middleware now returns generic 404 responses for missing or invalid X-App-ID headers. This prevents:

  • Information leakage about the routing mechanism
  • App ID enumeration attacks
  • Revealing which app IDs are valid
// Before: Detailed error messages
// "X-App-ID header required" (400)
// "app \"xyz\" not found" (404)

// After: Generic 404 for all cases
// 404 Not Found

docs.title: Implementing AppBackend for Existing Apps
docs.text:
1. Refactor server to accept external database:
// Before: Server creates its own database
func NewServer(cfg Config) (*Server, error) {
    db, _ := sql.Open("postgres", cfg.DatabaseURL)
    return newServerInternal(cfg, db)
}

// After: Add factory for external database
func NewServerWithDatabase(cfg Config, db *sql.DB) (*Server, error) {
    return newServerInternal(cfg, db)
}

func newServerInternal(cfg Config, db *sql.DB) (*Server, error) {
    // Shared initialization logic
}
  1. Create multiapp adapter package (multiapp/backend.go):
package multiapp

import (
    cfmultiapp "github.com/grokify/systemforge/multiapp"
    "github.com/yourapp/internal/server"
)

type Backend struct {
    server *server.Server
}

func NewBackend(cfg *Config) *Backend {
    return &Backend{}
}

func (b *Backend) Slug() string { return "yourapp" }
func (b *Backend) Name() string { return "Your App" }

func (b *Backend) Routes(deps cfmultiapp.Dependencies) chi.Router {
    // Create server with schema-isolated database
    b.server, _ = server.NewServerWithDatabase(cfg, deps.DB.Pool())
    return b.server.Router()
}

func (b *Backend) OnShutdown(ctx context.Context) error {
    return b.server.Close()
}
  1. Move from internal/multiapp to multiapp (public package):
# multiapp package must be importable by other modules
mv internal/multiapp multiapp

docs.text:
New integration with ProductGraph for product analytics:

import (
    "github.com/grokify/systemforge/observability"

obs, _ := observability.New(observability.ConfigFromEnv())
obs.SetProductGraphFromEnv()

docs.title: Session Invalidation
docs.text:
New session/invalidation package for multi-device session management:

import "github.com/grokify/systemforge/session/invalidation"

store := invalidation.NewMemoryStore()  // Or NewRedisStore for production
manager := invalidation.NewManager(store,
    invalidation.WithSessionTTL(24*time.Hour),
    invalidation.WithMaxSessionsPerUser(5),
)

// Create session with device info
session, _ := manager.CreateSession(ctx, userID,
    invalidation.WithDeviceInfo("Chrome on macOS"),
    invalidation.WithIPAddress("192.168.1.100"),
)

// Logout all devices
manager.InvalidateAllSessions(ctx, userID)

// Logout other devices (keep current)
manager.InvalidateOtherSessions(ctx, userID, currentSessionID)

See Session Invalidation for details.

docs.title: Account Lockout Protection
docs.text:
New identity/security package for brute-force protection:

import "github.com/grokify/systemforge/identity/security"

store := security.NewMemoryLockoutStore()  // Or NewRedisLockoutStore
lockout := security.NewLockout(store,
    security.WithMaxAttempts(5),
    security.WithLockoutDuration(15*time.Minute),
)

// In login handler
err := lockout.CheckAndRecord(ctx, email, loginSuccess)
if errors.Is(err, security.ErrAccountLocked) {
    return fmt.Errorf("account locked, try again later")
}

See Account Security for details.

docs.title: DPoP moved to goauth/dpop
docs.text:
The session/dpop package has been removed. DPoP now lives in the standalone github.com/grokify/goauth/dpop package (released as goauth v0.24.0), so it can be consumed independently of the SystemForge session layer.

Update your imports:

// Old
import "github.com/grokify/systemforge/session/dpop"

// New
import "github.com/grokify/goauth/dpop"

The package API is unchanged — only the import path moved. The session/bff layer that binds DPoP to sessions (proof injection on the proxy, per-session key pairs) remains in SystemForge and now depends on goauth/dpop.

docs.title: GuardSQL Authorization Adapter (authzguardsql)
docs.text:
A new adapter maps GuardSQL schemas and policies to SystemForge authorization:

import "github.com/grokify/systemforge/authzguardsql"

It builds SystemForge PolicyBuilder, ResourceBuilder, and DefaultResourceBuilder values from GuardSQL definitions. The dependency direction is systemforge → guardsql (GuardSQL stays dependency-light and never imports SystemForge). This was previously the nested guardsql/authzsystemforge module; consolidating it into SystemForge removes the fragile cross-module tagging burden.

docs.title: OpenAPI 3.1 + Interactive API Reference
docs.text: The docs site now includes an OpenAPI 3.1 specification and a Scalar interactive API reference, integrated into the site navigation.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text: • The bff reverse proxy migrated from the deprecated httputil.ReverseProxy.Director to Rewrite (Go 1.26 SA1019); the session value propagates via the cloned outbound request's context.

docs.title: Session Management
docs.text: SystemForge provides a comprehensive session management system for BFF (Backend for Frontend) architectures. It supports server-side sessions with HTTP-only cookies, OAuth token storage, and distributed storage backends.

docs.title: Session Store (session/bff)
docs.text:
The BFF session package provides:

  • Session interface - Create, Get, Update, Delete, Touch
  • Cookie manager - HTTP-only, Secure, SameSite cookies
  • Session middleware - Automatic session loading per request
  • Multiple backends - Memory, Ent (SQL), OmniStorage (Redis)

BFF Sessions →

docs.title: Session Invalidation (session/invalidation)
docs.text:
For managing active sessions across devices:

  • Track sessions with device info and metadata
  • "Logout all devices" functionality
  • Maximum sessions per user enforcement
  • Memory and Redis backends

Session Invalidation →

docs.title: Basic BFF Session Setup
docs.text:
import (
    "github.com/plexusone/systemforge/session/bff"
)

// Create session store (using omnistorage for Redis support)
store, err := bff.NewOmniStorageStore(bff.OmniStorageConfig{
    Backend:        "redis",
    RedisURL:       "redis://localhost:6379",
    MaxSessionSize: 1024 * 1024, // 1MB
    DefaultTTL:     24 * time.Hour,
})

// Create cookie manager
cookies := bff.NewCookieManager(bff.CookieConfig{
    Name:     "session",
    Domain:   "example.com",
    Path:     "/",
    Secure:   true,
    HTTPOnly: true,
    SameSite: http.SameSiteLaxMode,
    MaxAge:   86400,
})

// Apply middleware
router.Use(bff.SessionMiddleware(store, cookies))

docs.title: Accessing Session in Handlers
docs.text:
func handleRequest(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    // Get session from context
    session := bff.SessionFromContext(r.Context())
    if session == nil {
        // No session (not logged in)
    }

    // Access session data
    userID := session.UserID
    orgID := session.OrganizationID
    accessToken := session.AccessToken
}

docs.title: Storage Backends
docs.text: Backend Use Case Distributed Memory Development, testing No Ent (SQL) Single-server production No OmniStorage (Memory) Development, testing No OmniStorage (Redis) Multi-server production Yes

docs.title: OmniStorage Backend (Recommended)
docs.text:
The OmniStorage backend provides:

  • Size limits - Prevent session bloat attacks
  • JSON validation - Block non-serializable data
  • Violation callbacks - Hook into metrics/alerting
  • Structured errors - Machine-readable error codes
store, err := bff.NewOmniStorageStore(bff.OmniStorageConfig{
    Backend:        "redis",
    RedisURL:       os.Getenv("REDIS_URL"),
    MaxSessionSize: 1024 * 1024,
    ControlOptions: []omnisession.ControlOption{
        omnisession.WithLogger(logger),
        omnisession.WithViolationHandler(metricsHandler),
    },
})

See omnistorage-core docs for details.

docs.title: Session Structure
docs.text:
type Session struct {
    ID                    string
    UserID                uuid.UUID
    OrganizationID        *uuid.UUID

    // OAuth tokens (stored server-side)
    AccessToken           string
    RefreshToken          string
    AccessTokenExpiresAt  time.Time
    RefreshTokenExpiresAt time.Time

    // DPoP (if using OAuth 2.1)
    DPoPKeyPairJSON       []byte
    DPoPThumbprint        string

    // Metadata
    Metadata              map[string]string
    IPAddress             string
    UserAgent             string

    // Timestamps
    CreatedAt             time.Time
    UpdatedAt             time.Time
    LastAccessedAt        time.Time
    ExpiresAt             time.Time
}

docs.title: Security Considerations
docs.text:
1. HTTP-only cookies - Session ID not accessible to JavaScript
  2. Server-side tokens - OAuth tokens never sent to browser
  3. Size limits - Prevent session bloat attacks
  4. JSON-only data - Prevent serialization vulnerabilities
  5. CSRF protection - Origin/Referer checking for mutations
  6. Secure cookies - HTTPS-only in production

docs.title: BFF Sessions
docs.text: The BFF (Backend for Frontend) session package provides server-side session management with HTTP-only cookies for secure web applications.

docs.title: Why BFF Sessions?
docs.text:
Traditional SPA architectures store tokens in browser storage (localStorage/sessionStorage), which exposes them to XSS attacks. BFF sessions keep tokens server-side:

Approach Token Location XSS Risk CSRF Risk localStorage Browser High None sessionStorage Browser High None HTTP-only Cookie Server None Mitigated

docs.title: Store Interface
docs.text:
type Store interface {
    // Create stores a new session.
    Create(ctx context.Context, session *Session) error

    // Get retrieves a session by ID.
    Get(ctx context.Context, id string) (*Session, error)

    // Update updates an existing session.
    Update(ctx context.Context, session *Session) error

    // Delete removes a session by ID.
    Delete(ctx context.Context, id string) error

    // DeleteByUserID removes all sessions for a user.
    DeleteByUserID(ctx context.Context, userID string) (int, error)

    // Touch updates the LastAccessedAt timestamp.
    Touch(ctx context.Context, id string) error

    // Cleanup removes expired sessions.
    Cleanup(ctx context.Context) (int, error)

    // Close closes the store.
    Close() error
}

docs.title: Memory Store
docs.text:
For development and single-server deployments:

store := bff.NewMemoryStore()

docs.text:
For SQL databases via Ent ORM:

store := bff.NewEntStore(entClient)

docs.text:
For production with Redis and security controls:

    Backend:         "redis",
    RedisURL:        "redis://localhost:6379",
    MaxSessionSize:  1024 * 1024, // 1MB
    DefaultTTL:      24 * time.Hour,
    CleanupInterval: 5 * time.Minute,
    KeyPrefix:       "myapp:session:",
})

docs.text: Field Description Default Backend "memory" or "redis" "memory" RedisURL Redis connection URL Required for redis MaxSessionSize Max session size in bytes 1MB DefaultTTL Session lifetime 24 hours CleanupInterval Cleanup frequency 5 minutes KeyPrefix Redis key prefix "session:" ControlOptions Logger, violation handler None

docs.title: With Observability
docs.text:
import omnisession "github.com/plexusone/omnistorage-core/session"

store, err := bff.NewOmniStorageStore(bff.OmniStorageConfig{
    Backend:        "redis",
    RedisURL:       os.Getenv("REDIS_URL"),
    MaxSessionSize: 1024 * 1024,
    ControlOptions: []omnisession.ControlOption{
        omnisession.WithLogger(slog.Default()),
        omnisession.WithViolationHandler(func(ctx context.Context, event omnisession.ViolationEvent) {
            // Record metric
            metrics.SessionViolations.Inc(event.Type)

            // Alert on abuse
            if event.Type == omnisession.ViolationSizeExceeded {
                alerting.Warn("Session size exceeded", event)
            }
        }),
    },
})

docs.title: Cookie Manager
docs.text:
cookies := bff.NewCookieManager(bff.CookieConfig{
    Name:     "session",      // Cookie name
    Domain:   "example.com",  // Cookie domain
    Path:     "/",            // Cookie path
    Secure:   true,           // HTTPS only (set false for local dev)
    HTTPOnly: true,           // Not accessible to JavaScript
    SameSite: http.SameSiteLaxMode,
    MaxAge:   86400,          // 24 hours in seconds
