docs.title: TRD — Retire Legacy User — Principal as the Sole Identity Root
docs.text: Initiative: INIT-SYSTEMFORGE-008 Design of record: ADR-004

docs.title: Two human models
docs.text: Concern Legacy (User) Target (Principal + Human) Table sf_users sf_principals, sf_humans Email User.email (required, unique) Human.email (required, unique) Name name Principal.display_name, Human.given_name/family_name Password User.password_hash sf_credentials type password Platform admin is_platform_admin Human.is_platform_admin Active active Principal.active Upstream identities sf_oauth_accounts sf_external_identities Federation link User.federation_id none (maps to an ExternalIdentity) Memberships sf_memberships sf_principal_memberships Refresh tokens sf_refresh_tokens sf_principal_tokens API keys sf_api_keys (owner → User) sf_credentials type api_key Org ownership — Organization.owner_principal_id (already)

docs.title: Live dependencies on the legacy model
docs.text:
Non-test, non-generated code only:

Location What it does identity/systemauth/storage.go, storage_ent.go, storage_memory.go CreateUser, GetUser, GetUserByEmail, GetUserByFederationID, UpdateUser, DeleteUser; legacyUserID() sets the optional user edge on OAuth tokens when a User row exists identity/systemauth/provider_identity.go, provider_auth.go Password login: GetIdentityByEmail → storage.GetUserByEmail identity/systemauth/federation_handlers.go Identity sync create/update/delete keyed by federation_id identity/systemauthsvc/database.go, service.go ensureSystemUser creates system@systemauth.local in sf_users as owner of static OAuth clients; health check queries User identity/scim/store/ent.go Full SCIM store on User + Membership rls/testing.go Test helper inserts into cf_memberships (stale pre-rename name)

Legacy schemas with no live callers: OAuthAccount, RefreshToken, APIKey, ServiceAccount, ServiceAccountKeyPair. Membership is used only by the SCIM store.

Edges from other schemas into User: OAuthApp.owner, OAuthToken.user, OAuthAuthCode.user, OAuthConsent.user (all optional), ServiceAccount.creator.

Social login (social_directory_ent.go) already creates Principal + Human + ExternalIdentity and is the reference implementation for the target model.

docs.title: 1. SystemAuth storage on Principal
docs.text:
Replace the User-backed methods in systemauth.Storage with Principal/Human-backed ones, and collapse the package's two human DTOs into one:

  • systemauth.User (federation_handlers.go; used by storage, password login, federation sync) and systemauth.LoginPrincipal (social_directory.go; used by social login) become a single HumanPrincipal value type: ID, Email, EmailVerified, DisplayName, GivenName, FamilyName, AvatarURL, Locale, Active, Metadata. The Federated / FederationID fields are dropped; federation is an ExternalIdentity like any other provider.
  • Storage methods are renamed with the type: CreateHuman, GetHuman(id), GetHumanByEmail, GetHumanByExternalIdentity(provider, subject), UpdateHuman, DeleteHuman.

Implementations:

  • GetHumanByEmail → query Human by EmailEqualFold, join Principal.
  • GetHuman(id) → Principal.Get with human edge; non-human principals return not-found.
  • CreateHuman → create Principal(type=human, identifier=email, display_name) + Human(email, ...) in one transaction, mirroring what social_directory_ent.go does today; social login then calls the same helper instead of its own.
  • UpdateHuman / DeleteHuman → update Principal.active and Human fields; delete cascades through the principal.
  • GetHumanByExternalIdentity → query ExternalIdentity by (provider, subject) and return its principal.
  • Remove legacyUserID; Fosite request subjects are principal IDs and the OAuth token/auth-code/consent builders no longer set a user edge.

The memory storage mirrors the same semantics.

Password verification is already injected (WithProviderPasswordVerifier); the default verifier provided by systemauthsvc uses identity/credential.Service against sf_credentials type password.

docs.title: 2. Federation sync as external identities
docs.text:
federation_handlers.go keeps its wire contract (contract/ types are unchanged). Internally:

  • create: find by email via GetUserByEmail; if absent, CreateUser and record ExternalIdentity{provider: <federation provider name>, subject: req.Identity.ID}.
  • update / delete: resolve via the external identity, then update Human/Principal.active.

The provider name is a constant exported from systemauth so the identity can be distinguished from social providers.

docs.title: 3. Bootstrap owner is a service principal
docs.text: ensureSystemUser becomes ensureSystemPrincipal: a Principal(type=service) with a fixed well-known UUID and identifier system@systemauth.local, plus a ServicePrincipal extension row. OAuthApp.owner is repointed to Principal; the health check in service.go queries Principal.

docs.title: 4. SCIM store on principals
docs.text:
Rewrite identity/scim/store/ent.go. The group side is already on the target model and does not change:

  • Groups ↔ Organization (by ID, slug, display name, external ID), exactly as today.
  • Members ↔ PrincipalMembership replacing Membership: AddMemberToGroup creates PrincipalMembership(principal_id, organization_id, role = config.DefaultRole) with the same idempotent no-op when it exists; RemoveMemberFromGroup deletes by (principal_id, organization_id); group member listing reads PrincipalMembership instead of Membership.
  • Users ↔ Principal(type=human) + Human. SCIM userName/emails map to Human.email; active to Principal.active; name to given_name/family_name/display_name. User create goes through the shared CreateHuman helper from §1.
  • Filtering and pagination run on the Human/Principal query with the same SCIM filter semantics the existing tests encode.

So the rewrite is a Membership → PrincipalMembership substitution plus re-targeting the user CRUD; no SCIM resource changes meaning.

The SCIM mapper (identity/scim/mapper) and schema packages are unchanged except for type references.

docs.title: 5. Service accounts
docs.text: Confirm whether the RFC 7523 JWT-bearer path (identity/token, identity/oauthclient) authenticates against ServicePrincipal + keypair credentials or against sf_service_accounts. If the former, remove ServiceAccount and ServiceAccountKeyPair with the other legacy schemas. If the latter, repoint ServiceAccount.creator to Principal in this initiative and open a follow-on to migrate the flow.

docs.title: 6. Schema removal and migration
docs.text: Delete identity/ent/schema/{user,membership,oauth_account,refresh_token, api_key}.go (plus service account schemas per §5), remove the corresponding edge.From(... User.Type) declarations, regenerate Ent, and add migrations/0002_drop_legacy_user_tables.sql dropping sf_users, sf_memberships, sf_oauth_accounts, sf_refresh_tokens, sf_api_keys (and service-account tables per §5), including their FK constraints.

docs.title: 7. Documentation and guard
docs.text:
• Rewrite docs/identity/users.md, memberships.md, api-keys.md around Principal, Human, PrincipalMembership, and Credential; remove the stale cf_users schema table.
  • Update the README feature list (Users/Memberships/OAuth Accounts/API Keys bullets) to describe the principal model.
  • Fix rls/testing.go to use sf_principal_memberships.
  • Extend the existing CI grep gate (from INIT-SYSTEMFORGE-004) to fail on sf_users, ent\.User\b, identity/ent/user", and identity/ent/membership".
  • Rewrite docs/identity/api-keys.md to state that the identity/apikey interface is backed by sf_credentials type api_key, with the identity/credential service as the reference implementation; note the removal of sf_api_keys in the v0.14.0 release notes as a consumer-facing change.

docs.title: Sequencing Constraints
docs.text:
• §1 and §3 share storage_ent.go and the bootstrap; land §3 first so the OAuth-client owner is valid before legacyUserID is removed.
  • §4 (SCIM) depends on §1 so it can reuse the same creation helper.
  • §6 can only land after §1–§5; it is the point of no return and is followed immediately by §7 and the tag.

docs.title: Risks
docs.text:
• SCIM behavior drift. Mitigate by expanding SCIM tests (filters, pagination, membership add/remove) before the rewrite and treating them as the contract.
  • Hidden User dependency in generated or reflective code (e.g. RLS policies naming sf_users). Mitigate with the CI gate and a repo-wide grep for table names in SQL and Go string literals, not just Ent identifiers.
  • Service-account scope ambiguity (§5). Resolve in the first RMI of Phase 2 so the schema-removal RMI has a fixed list.

docs.title: Testing Strategy
docs.text:
• Keep identity/systemauth/storetest and identity/relyingparty/storetest as conformance suites; extend them with "same email via two sign-in methods yields one principal" cases.
  • Rewrite the two legacy User test files in identity/systemauth against the principal-backed storage.
  • SCIM: add filter/pagination/membership cases first, then rewrite the store and keep them green.
  • Bootstrap: test idempotent creation of the system service principal across two concurrent calls.
  • Migration: apply 0001 then 0002 on a fresh dev database and run the full suite.

docs.title: ROADMAP — Post-Cutover Identity Follow-Ups
docs.text:
Initiative: INIT-SYSTEMFORGE-009 Repository: github.com/plexusone/systemforge

Fixes and hygiene found while retiring the legacy User model (INIT-SYSTEMFORGE-008, ADR-004). The RFC 7523 JWT-bearer grant is tracked as its own feature initiative. Commits implementing an item carry Refs: RMI-SYSTEMFORGE-<NNN>.

docs.title: Phase 1 — Correctness
docs.text:
Theme: Behavior that is wrong or inconsistent today

  • [x] RMI-SYSTEMFORGE-112 Fix identity/oauth.NewProvider, which panics on construction because its storage does not implement fosite.Storage (ClientAssertionJWTValid is missing); add a construction test
  • Delivered: storage now satisfies every Fosite interface the provider composes, enforced by compile-time assertions. Also fixed: SystemAuth recorded client-assertion JTIs as auth-code rows with a nil app ID, so private_key_jwt authentication failed and replay was never detected (now a dedicated sf_client_assertion_jtis store shared by both); and identity/oauth never recorded a token family, so revocation matched nothing.
  • [x] RMI-SYSTEMFORGE-113 Rename the Core-era default BFF session cookie cf_session to sf_session, with a release note that existing sessions sign in again
  • Delivered: a single DefaultCookieName constant now feeds both the cookie manager and the OpenAPI security scheme. No application hardcoded the old name. The last cf_ table names in current docs were also corrected.
  • [x] RMI-SYSTEMFORGE-114 Membership listing excludes inactive memberships by default, with an option to include them, matching the SCIM store
  • Delivered: IncludeInactive() option and an includeInactive query parameter on the members endpoint; signup keeps reporting the stored owner membership.
  • [x] RMI-SYSTEMFORGE-115 Opt-in configuration to treat SCIM-provisioned emails as verified, default off, so a later social login can link automatically when a deployment trusts its identity provider
  • Delivered: store.Config.TrustProvisionedEmail. Also fixed: changing an email through SCIM kept the previous address's verification.

docs.title: Phase 2 — Integrity and Model Hygiene
docs.text:
Theme: Close the remaining gaps the cutover left

  • [x] RMI-SYSTEMFORGE-116 PostgreSQL case-insensitive unique index on sf_humans email, created by the migrate step with the dialect passed in, so concurrent creates cannot race past the transactional check
  • Delivered: identity/pgschema holds PostgreSQL-only DDL, applied by the migrate step; the dialect is recorded for configured, injected-pool, and injected-client storage. Ent's exec-query feature is enabled so an injected client can apply it.
  • [x] RMI-SYSTEMFORGE-117 Retire or realign the legacy-shaped mixins in identity/ent/mixin (UserBase, MembershipBase, OAuthAccountMixin, RefreshTokenMixin, and HumanMixin fields absent from sf_humans) after inventorying their consumers
  • Depends on: RMI-SYSTEMFORGE-114
  • Delivered: UserBase and MembershipBase had no consumers and are removed. HumanMixin, OAuthAccountMixin, and RefreshTokenMixin are deprecated rather than removed, because an application still builds a local identity schema from them; removal follows its move to SystemAuth.

docs.title: PLAN — JWT Bearer Authorization Grant — Service Principals with Keypair Credentials
docs.text: Initiative: INIT-SYSTEMFORGE-010

docs.title: Entry Gate
docs.text:
• PRD open questions resolved (client authentication default; agent principals).
  • INIT-SYSTEMFORGE-009 released, since the grant reuses its client-assertion JTI store.

docs.title: Phase 1 — Storage and Composition
docs.text: Build the key-storage adapter with its rejection rules and scope intersection, then register the Fosite factory behind configuration and advertise the grant in discovery. Exit: an embedded SystemAuth issues a token for a correctly signed assertion and rejects every PRD failure case.

docs.title: Phase 2 — Client, Documentation, Release
docs.text: Add the reference client helper, rewrite the service principals page with an end-to-end walkthrough, add release notes, and tag after CI passes. Exit: PRD success criteria hold.

docs.title: Risks and Mitigations
docs.text: Risk Mitigation Accepting a key for the wrong subject Adapter enforces key ownership and self-issuance; direct tests Enabling the grant by accident Disabled by default; discovery only advertises it when enabled

docs.title: Follow-On
docs.text:
• Trusted third-party issuers (workload identity federation).
  • Admin endpoints for keypair registration and rotation.
  • Agent principals using the grant, if the PRD question resolves that way.

docs.title: PRD — JWT Bearer Authorization Grant — Service Principals with Keypair Credentials
docs.text: Initiative: INIT-SYSTEMFORGE-010 Status: Draft Home repo: github.com/plexusone/systemforge

docs.title: Problem
docs.text:
Machine-to-machine access to SystemAuth today uses the client-credentials grant: a backend holds a client secret and exchanges it for a token. Shared secrets have to be distributed, stored, and rotated on both sides, and a leaked secret is immediately usable by anyone.

The RFC 7523 JWT-bearer grant lets a workload prove its identity with a private key it never shares: it signs a short-lived assertion, and the authorization server verifies it with the registered public key. SystemForge documented this capability as "service accounts" but never implemented it, and the tables it described have been removed (ADR-004). The building blocks now exist on the principal model: service principals, keypair credentials, and a store for used assertion IDs.

docs.title: Goals
docs.text:
1. SystemAuth accepts the JWT-bearer grant (grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:jwt-bearer) at the token endpoint and issues an access token for a service principal.
  2. Keys are keypair credentials owned by the service principal, with their own scopes, expiry, and revocation.
  3. Assertions cannot be replayed: every assertion carries a jti, and a used jti is rejected until the assertion would have expired.
  4. Least privilege: a token's scopes are limited to what the key allows, the principal allows, and the request asks for.
  5. Documentation and a reference client so a workload can be set up end to end.

docs.title: Non-Goals
docs.text:
• Assertions issued by third-party identity providers (iss different from the principal). This release accepts self-issued assertions only; a trusted-issuer registry is a follow-on.
  • JWT client authentication (private_key_jwt, RFC 7523 section 2.2), which Fosite already supports through client keys and the existing assertion-ID store.
  • Refresh tokens for this grant. Workloads sign a new assertion instead.
  • Human principals using this grant.

docs.title: Users and Stakeholders
docs.text: Who Needs Platform operators Register a service principal and its public keys, rotate and revoke keys, see when a key was last used Workload developers A documented assertion format and a small client to exchange an assertion for a token Security reviewers Replay protection, short assertion lifetimes, scoped tokens, and an audit trail

docs.title: Functional
docs.text:
• F1. The token endpoint accepts the JWT-bearer grant and verifies the assertion signature with the keypair credential named by the assertion's kid.
  • F2. The assertion's iss and sub must both equal the service principal's identifier, and the key must belong to that principal.
  • F3. aud must name SystemAuth's token endpoint (or issuer); exp is required, iat and jti are required, and the assertion's lifetime may not exceed a configured maximum (default one hour).
  • F4. A used jti is rejected until the assertion's exp.
  • F5. The key and the principal must be active and unexpired, and the key unrevoked; the principal must be of type service.
  • F6. Granted scopes are the requested scopes intersected with the key's scopes and the principal's allowed scopes; requesting no scopes grants the intersection of the key's and principal's scopes.
  • F7. The issued access token's subject is the service principal's ID, and no refresh token is issued.
  • F8. Successful exchanges update the key's last-used time.
  • F9. Discovery advertises the grant type when it is enabled; it is disabled unless configured.

docs.title: Non-Functional
docs.text:
• N1. The grant uses Fosite's RFC 7523 handler; SystemForge supplies storage, not protocol code.
  • N2. Failures return RFC 6749 errors without revealing whether a key or principal exists.
  • N3. Unit tests cover every rejection rule; an end-to-end test signs real assertions with RSA and ECDSA keys.

docs.title: Success Criteria
docs.text:
• A service principal with a registered public key obtains a scoped access token by signing an assertion, and the token validates at a resource server.
  • Replaying the same assertion fails; an expired, revoked, or wrong-subject key fails; scopes never exceed the key's or principal's.

docs.title: Risks
docs.text: Risk Mitigation Long-lived assertions widen the replay window Required jti, bounded maximum lifetime, JTI store Over-broad tokens Scope intersection across request, key, and principal Key sprawl Keys carry expiry; last-used time makes unused keys visible

docs.title: Open Questions
docs.text:
• Should the grant require client authentication in addition to the assertion? Proposed: no by default, since the signed assertion is the credential, with a configuration switch to require it.
  • Should agents (principals of type agent) also be allowed to use the grant? Proposed: not in this release.

docs.title: ROADMAP — JWT Bearer Authorization Grant — Service Principals with Keypair Credentials
docs.text:
Initiative: INIT-SYSTEMFORGE-010 Repository: github.com/plexusone/systemforge

Implements the RFC 7523 JWT-bearer authorization grant on Fosite's handler, with service principals and keypair credentials. Commits implementing an item carry Refs: RMI-SYSTEMFORGE-<NNN>.

docs.title: Phase 1 — Storage and Composition
docs.text:
Theme: SystemAuth verifies signed assertions and issues scoped tokens

  • [ ] RMI-SYSTEMFORGE-118 Key-storage adapter implementing rfc7523.RFC7523KeyStorage: key lookup by kid with ownership, self-issuance, status, and expiry checks; JWK conversion; scope intersection; JTI delegation to the client-assertion store
  • [ ] RMI-SYSTEMFORGE-119 Register the JWT-bearer grant behind configuration (enabled, maximum assertion lifetime, client authentication, token lifetime) and advertise it in discovery when enabled
  • Depends on: RMI-SYSTEMFORGE-118
  • [ ] RMI-SYSTEMFORGE-120 Record key usage on successful exchanges and issue tokens with the service principal as subject and no refresh token
  • Depends on: RMI-SYSTEMFORGE-119
  • [ ] RMI-SYSTEMFORGE-121 End-to-end tests with RSA and ECDSA keys covering issuance, introspection, replay, expiry, overlong lifetime, missing jti, wrong audience, and revoked keys
  • Depends on: RMI-SYSTEMFORGE-120

docs.title: Phase 2 — Client, Documentation, Release
docs.text:
Theme: Workloads can adopt it end to end

  • [ ] RMI-SYSTEMFORGE-122 Reference client helper in identity/oauthclient that signs an assertion and exchanges it for a token
  • Depends on: RMI-SYSTEMFORGE-119
  • [ ] RMI-SYSTEMFORGE-123 Rewrite the service principals page with an end-to-end walkthrough, add release notes, tag after CI passes, and record the release
  • Depends on: RMI-SYSTEMFORGE-121
  • Depends on: RMI-SYSTEMFORGE-122

docs.title: TRD — JWT Bearer Authorization Grant — Service Principals with Keypair Credentials
docs.text: Initiative: INIT-SYSTEMFORGE-010

docs.title: Current State
docs.text:
• SystemAuth composes Fosite (v0.49) with the authorization-code, client credentials, refresh, introspection, revocation, PKCE, and OpenID Connect factories. The RFC 7523 factory is not registered.
  • Fosite provides compose.RFC7523AssertionGrantFactory and the handler in handler/rfc7523, which needs storage implementing rfc7523.RFC7523KeyStorage: GetPublicKey, GetPublicKeys, GetPublicKeyScopes (each keyed by issuer, subject, and key ID), IsJWTUsed, and MarkJWTUsedForTime.
  • Service principals are Principal(type=service) with a ServicePrincipal extension (identity/principal).
  • Keypair credentials are sf_credentials rows of type keypair with a globally unique key_id, key_algorithm, PEM public key, scopes, expiry, active, and revoked flags (identity/credential CreateKeypair, GetKeypairByKeyID, ListKeypairs).
  • identity/clientassertion.JTIStore records used assertion IDs in sf_client_assertion_jtis with Fosite's replay semantics.

docs.title: 1. Key storage adapter
docs.text:
A new type in identity/systemauth implementing RFC7523KeyStorage over Ent:

  • GetPublicKey(ctx, issuer, subject, keyID): look up the keypair credential by key_id; require it active, unrevoked, and unexpired; load its principal and require type service, active, and identifier == subject; require issuer == subject (self-issued only). Parse the PEM public key into a jose.JSONWebKey with the stored algorithm and key ID. Any failure returns fosite.ErrNotFound so callers cannot distinguish missing from rejected keys.
  • GetPublicKeys(ctx, issuer, subject): the same checks for the principal, returning all of its usable keypair credentials as a JWK set (used when an assertion has no kid).
  • GetPublicKeyScopes: the key's scopes intersected with the principal's allowed_scopes.
  • IsJWTUsed and MarkJWTUsedForTime: delegate to clientassertion.JTIStore (Valid reports used as ErrJTIKnown).
  • On a successful exchange, update the credential's last_used_at and last_used_ip through the existing credential service.

docs.title: 2. Server composition and configuration
docs.text:
• Register compose.RFC7523AssertionGrantFactory when oauth.jwt_bearer.enabled is true (default false).
  • Configuration: max_assertion_lifetime (default 1h, mapped to Fosite's JWT max duration), require_client_auth (default false, mapped to the inverse of GrantTypeJWTBearerCanSkipClientAuth), token_lifetime (default 1h). jti and iat are required (Fosite's ID-optional and issued-date-optional settings off).
  • The audience accepted is SystemAuth's token endpoint URL and issuer.
  • Discovery adds the grant type to grant_types_supported when enabled.

docs.title: 3. Issued tokens
docs.text:
• Subject: the service principal's ID. No refresh token.
  • Granted scopes: Fosite intersects requested scopes with GetPublicKeyScopes; when none are requested, grant all of them.
  • Tokens are stored with the existing token storage, so introspection and revocation work unchanged.

docs.title: 4. Management
docs.text: Keys are managed with the existing identity/credential API (CreateKeypair, ListKeypairs, Revoke). This initiative documents the flow rather than adding endpoints; admin endpoints are a follow-on if needed.

docs.title: 5. Reference client
docs.text: identity/oauthclient gains a helper that builds and signs an assertion (RS256, ES256, EdDSA) from a private key and principal identifier and exchanges it for a token, so workloads written in Go need no JWT code of their own.

docs.title: Testing Strategy
docs.text:
• Adapter unit tests: unknown key, revoked, expired, inactive key; wrong principal type, inactive principal, subject or issuer mismatch; scope intersection; JTI delegation.
  • End-to-end tests against an embedded SystemAuth: RSA and ECDSA keys exchange signed assertions for tokens that introspect as active with the expected subject and scopes; replay, expired assertion, overlong lifetime, missing jti, and wrong audience are rejected.
  • Discovery reflects the enabled flag.

docs.title: Risks
docs.text:
• Fosite's key lookup is keyed by issuer and subject; enforcing that the key belongs to the subject must happen in the adapter, and is tested directly.
  • PEM parsing of stored keys must accept the formats CreateKeypair writes; tests round-trip keys created through the credential service.

docs.title: PLAN — Suite Organizations: Lifecycle, Claims, Collaborators, Real-Time Invalidation
docs.text: Initiative: INIT-SYSTEMFORGE-011

docs.title: Entry Gate
docs.text:
• ADR-006, ADR-007, ADR-008, ADR-009 and ADR-010 accepted.
  • INIT-SYSTEMFORGE-008 complete: one Principal root, one Human model, legacy tables gone.
  • INIT-SYSTEMFORGE-007 complete: ManagerRelationship, identity/managedprincipal, login_token, the managed claim and the manager authorization relations exist, so Phase 5 amends them rather than creating them.
  • The authz/rbac and authz/rebac/spicedb packages exist under their mode names with authz/simple and authz/spicedb forwarding to them.
  • No release was cut between INIT-007/INIT-008 and this initiative, and the local aauth-go replace directive left no earlier commit that could be tagged, so all of it ships together as v0.14.0.

docs.title: Build Order
docs.text: Phases 1, 2 and 3 are sequential on the tables and claims they share. Phase 4 depends only on the collaborator membership role from Phase 1 and can proceed alongside Phases 2 and 3. Phase 5 depends on the invite work in Phase 2. Phase 6 closes.

docs.title: Phase 1 — Organization lifecycle (ADR-006)
docs.text: Wire SystemAuth's social login to signup.SignupOrGetExisting; centralize slug derivation and reserved names in signup; add sf_slug_reservations with Rename, ResolveSlug and the seven-day rule; enforce the personal organization invariants; add ConvertToTeam; drop the plan column and replace it with the entitlements summary. The plan removal is first in the phase because Phase 2's entitlement derivation builds on its absence. Exit: a first GitHub login yields a personal organization with the GitHub username as slug and a second login creates nothing; a rename followed by a reclaim within seven days succeeds and a stranger's attempt is refused; ConvertToTeam keeps the ID and memberships and gives the owner a fresh personal organization; no Plan symbol remains in the organization API.

docs.title: Phase 2 — Memberships and entitlements as claims (ADR-007)
docs.text: Add sf_app_roles and its service; derive entitled applications from the marketplace with default entitlements and seat accounting; emit the orgs claim in the ID token, userinfo and access token with truncation and the memberships endpoint; add ClaimsMemberships and RemoteMemberships to relyingparty with the provisioning hook; make invites and member management carry application roles. Exit: an application configured with ClaimsMemberships and no membership table shows a member only the applications they were assigned, shows an owner admin everywhere, and provisions itself for an organization on the organization's first use.

docs.title: Phase 3 — Real-time invalidation of access (ADR-010)
docs.text: Add sf_access_changes and record a row in every change transaction; stop revoking refresh tokens on role and membership change; set the access-token lifetime default and ceiling; implement the in-process revocation cache with the skew margin and expiry; add the replica poller, the replay endpoint and suspect mode; add back-channel delivery with retry and its receiver. The recording and the cache land together because a recorded change nobody reads is a false promise. Exit: in one process, a removal at request N is refused at request N+1 with a token-expired error; on a second replica it is refused within the polling interval; after a restart the cache is rebuilt from /access-changes before serving.

docs.title: Phase 4 — Resource-scoped collaborators (ADR-008)
docs.text: Extend the base schema with collaborator and list, reserve the resource-role ladder in the conventions, and update the parity test; add sf_resource_grants and the grant operations to rbac; add relationship grants and LookupResources to rebac/spicedb; extend providertest to cover grants and lookups on both; add resource-targeted invites; add the authz.mode configuration and the removal schedule for the forwarders. Exit: providertest passes for both modes on every grant and lookup case; a collaborator sees exactly the resources granted and the organization only through list; a resource-targeted invite creates membership and grant in one transaction.

docs.title: Phase 5 — Management is a relationship (ADR-009)
docs.text: Derive IsManaged and the managed claim from active relationships; accept an optional email at creation; add Release and the manager invitation kind; keep managed slugs free of email. Exit: a managed principal with a verified email keeps its managers until Release; removing the last manager of a principal without a verified email is still refused; a self-managed human becomes managed only by accepting an invitation.

docs.title: Phase 6 — Documentation and release
docs.text: Rewrite the organizations, managed-principals and authorization architecture pages to describe what shipped and empty their planned sections; add guides for invites, application roles, collaborators and slugs; update the changelog and release notes; tag v0.14.0 after CI passes and record the release. Exit: the PRD success criteria hold and the mkdocs strict build is clean.

docs.title: Risks and Mitigations
docs.text: Risk Mitigation The plan drop lands before entitlements can replace it RMI-129 ships the entitlements summary in the same change; Phase 2 derives the full set from it Access-change recording misses a site The TRD enumerates every change site; each has a test asserting a row in sf_access_changes inside the same transaction Phase 3 ships the table without the cache Phase 3 is tagged only whole; no partial release Mode parity drifts between rbac and rebac Every grant and lookup case is added to providertest before the second implementation, so the suite is the specification Claims grow past token limits The 50-organization cap and orgs_truncated are in RMI-132; RemoteMemberships handles the rest Cooling-off and aliases interact badly with conversion ConvertToTeam is specified in terms of Rename and the reservation table and tested for every direction of handle hand-over Phase 5 changes behavior for the original managed-principal consumer A child created without an email behaves exactly as before; the regression suite from INIT-007 runs unchanged

docs.title: Release
docs.text: v0.14.0, after all phases are complete and CI passes on the pushed commits; tag only after CI is green. The release notes call out the plan removal, the changed refresh-token semantics, the new token lifetime default and ceiling, the collaborator role, and the forwarder removal schedule as behavior changes.

docs.title: Follow-On
docs.text:
• Teams as carriers of application roles, if assigning roles one person at a time becomes the problem (ADR-007 defers them).
  • A second rebac engine beside SpiceDB under the same mode name.
  • Moving a resource between organizations, with its grants and implied collaborator memberships, for applications that need it.

docs.title: PRD — Suite Organizations: Lifecycle, Claims, Collaborators, Real-Time Invalidation
docs.text: Initiative: INIT-SYSTEMFORGE-011 Status: Draft Home repo: github.com/plexusone/systemforge Design of record: ADR-006, ADR-007, ADR-008, ADR-009, ADR-010 Depends on: INIT-SYSTEMFORGE-007 (managed principals and manager relationships), INIT-SYSTEMFORGE-008 (single Principal root)

docs.title: Problem
docs.text:
SystemForge models organizations, memberships, invites, managed principals, a marketplace and two authorization providers, but the lifecycle that ties them into something an application can build on is missing. Five accepted ADRs describe the gaps; this initiative implements them together because they share tables, claims and transactions.

Organizations have no lifecycle (ADR-006). SystemAuth's social login creates a bare principal and never calls signup, so a person's first sign-in leaves them in no organization and every application needs an operator step before the person can do anything. Slugs can be changed freely: nothing remembers a freed slug, so a rename can be followed at once by someone else taking the old name, and links to the old slug break. A personal organization cannot become a team without creating a new organization and moving everything, and nothing enforces what makes a personal organization personal. The plan column on organizations is a placeholder from before the marketplace: set at creation, never consulted, and unable to describe an organization that holds several subscriptions.

Applications keep their own membership tables (ADR-007). SystemAuth is meant to be the source of truth for memberships, roles and entitlements, but it emits none of them, so every application keeps its own table fed by operators or its own invite flow. In a deployment of several applications behind one SystemAuth, the same organization has to be created in each, a person has to be added to each separately, and removal from one does not remove from another. The marketplace records what an organization is entitled to, but applications cannot learn that from a login either.

Access changes wait for token expiry (ADR-010). Claims make requests cheap because a relying party asks SystemAuth nothing per request; the cost is that removing someone from an organization is not seen until their token expires. For routine offboarding that is tolerable; for a contractor cut off during a dispute, a compromised account or an agent whose mission was revoked, it is not. Introspection on every request would reintroduce the network hop the claims model removed; shorter lifetimes shrink the window but never close it.

Every grant is organization-wide (ADR-008). There is no way to give someone access to one resource — a project, a document, a site — without making them a member of the organization. Solo users need that for contractors, teams need it for outside reviewers, and personal organizations have no members at all. The substrate already has the pieces (relationships, vocabularies, lookups); the pattern should be defined once rather than rebuilt per application.

Management is inferred from a missing email (ADR-009). A managed principal is currently a human whose email is null. That excludes children with a school-issued address, who still need a guardian in control, and adults managed by arrangement, whose manager's authority comes from a relationship they both accept. The email answers whether a person can be contacted and verified; the relationship answers who may act for them.

docs.title: Goals
docs.text:
1. A working organization after one login. A first social login creates the principal and its personal organization in one transaction, with a slug derived from how the person arrived.
  2. Safe, reversible renames. A freed slug is held for seven days for its previous holder, resolves to its previous organization as an alias for that time, and the same rule applies to every kind of rename.
  3. Solo to team without moving data. A personal organization converts to a team keeping its ID, data and memberships; the person keeps their handle on a fresh personal organization.
  4. Entitlement per listing, not per organization. The plan column is removed and an entitlements summary derived from marketplace subscriptions and licenses takes its place.
  5. Memberships, application roles and entitlements as claims. The ID token, userinfo and access token carry an orgs claim; applications read it through relyingparty and keep no membership tables of their own.
  6. Access changes take effect within one request in the same process, within the polling interval on replicas, within back-channel delivery time across deployments, and within one token lifetime if every signal is lost.
  7. Collaborators on both authorization modes. Resource grants, ListResources and resource-targeted invites behave the same under rbac and rebac, verified by a shared conformance suite.
  8. Management is a relationship. IsManaged and the managed claim derive from active manager relationships; email decides only whether management may end.

docs.title: Non-Goals
docs.text:
• Pricing and packaging policy: which tiers exist, whether there is a free tier, trial lengths. The marketplace expresses them; applications choose them.
  • Custom or organization-defined application roles, and teams as carriers of roles. The roles are the ones an application's vocabulary declares; teams are the first addition if per-person assignment becomes the problem.
  • Resource grants as claims. The orgs claim lists a collaborator's organizations; the resources they may access are the application's to look up.
  • Revocation of agent tokens. AAuth tokens carry their own cascading revocation keyed by jti; this initiative covers SystemAuth-issued tokens.
  • Moving a resource between organizations. An application that supports it must move the grants and the collaborator memberships they imply.
  • Deciding what a managed principal may do for itself. The platform supplies the relationship, the roles and the managed claim; the split is the application's vocabulary.
  • Any product-specific signup page, organization switcher or invite screen. SystemAuth's own pages and API are in scope; an application's user interface is not.

docs.title: Users and Stakeholders
docs.text: Who Needs A person signing in for the first time An organization that works at once, with a handle they recognize, no operator involved A solo user Contractors with access to one resource, not the organization; a path to a team that keeps their data and ID An organization administrator Invites and member screens that choose application roles per application; role changes that take effect now; a rename that does not break links An application on SystemForge Organizations, roles and entitlements from the login, keyed by a stable organization ID; a first-use provisioning hook; a one-line revocation cache; ListResources to filter queries for collaborators A suite of applications behind one SystemAuth One membership, one invite, one removal across every application; no per-application organization tables A manager of a managed principal Management that survives the principal gaining an email; an explicit, audited release A deployment operator A configured access-token lifetime, clock-skew margin, default entitlements and authz.mode, each documented with its default

docs.title: Organization lifecycle (ADR-006)
docs.text:
• F1. SystemAuth's GitHub and Google login call signup.SignupOrGetExisting for a principal they have not seen; the principal and its personal organization are created in one transaction with the principal as owner. A later login resolves by provider identity first, then by verified email, and creates nothing.
  • F2. The personal slug is derived in one place, signup.SlugForLogin: the GitHub username; the local part of a Google email; for a managed principal, a manager-entered name or a generated slug that reveals nothing about the person; a numeric suffix on collision.
  • F3. A reserved-slug list (admin, api, o, login, oauth, well-known names and deployment-configured product names) is refused by SlugAvailable.
  • F4. Every slug change frees the old slug into a seven-day cooling-off period during which only the releasing principal, or an organization that principal owns, may take it. The freed slug resolves to its previous organization as an alias until reassigned or expired; lookups consult aliases after exact matches. The rule applies to personal and team organizations and in every direction.
  • F5. A personal organization has exactly one member, its owner. AddMember and invites are refused for personal organizations except for role collaborator; TransferOwnership is refused.
  • F6. ConvertToTeam keeps the organization's ID, data and memberships, sets its type to team, takes a free team slug chosen at conversion, and creates a new personal organization with the person's handle for the owner, in one transaction.
  • F7. The plan column is removed from sf_organizations, the organization service inputs and list filter, API responses, the SCIM default and the Plan* constants. The organization API gains an entitlements summary derived from the marketplace.

docs.title: Memberships and entitlements as claims (ADR-007)
docs.text:
• F8. Application roles are stored per (principal, organization, application) in sf_app_roles, validated against the application's AppVocabulary ladder. Owners hold admin in every entitled application implicitly; admins and members hold only what is assigned, none by default; collaborators hold none. Removal from the organization removes every application role.
  • F9. The applications an organization may assign roles in derive from its active subscriptions and licenses per listing, mapped to registered application identifiers, plus deployment-configured default entitlements. A deployment with no entitlements at all logs a warning at startup. A seat-licensed application counts its sf_app_roles rows against the license.
  • F10. The ID token and userinfo carry orgs: a list of {id, slug, name, type, role, apps} with apps a map of application identifier to application role. JWT access tokens carry the compact {id, role, apps}. A token carries at most 50 organizations, personal first then by most recent membership, with orgs_truncated: true when any were omitted; GET /userinfo/memberships returns the full paginated list.
  • F11. relyingparty reads memberships from claims by default (ClaimsMemberships), from the memberships endpoint when truncated or when only the compact form is present (RemoteMemberships), and keeps LocalMemberships for development only. Applications get a first-use provisioning hook keyed by organization ID.
  • F12. Invite creation and acceptance, and member management, carry per-application role selection with none preselected; roles change per application without touching the membership. SystemAuth's pages and API expose both.

docs.title: Real-time invalidation of access (ADR-010)
docs.text:
• F13. Every access change — membership removal, organization or application role change, a grant reduction, deactivation, session revocation — is recorded in sf_access_changes as (principal_id, organization_id or null, changed_at, reason) inside the transaction that makes the change.
  • F14. A role or membership change no longer revokes refresh tokens; the next refresh carries the reduced claims. Deactivation and explicit session revocation still revoke.
  • F15. The access-token lifetime defaults to 10 minutes, is configurable, and may not exceed 15 minutes.
  • F16. relyingparty keeps a revocation cache keyed by principal (and organization when scoped) and accepts a token only if `iat >= changed_at
  • margin, with a configurable clock-skew margin defaulting to 30 seconds and floored at 15. A rejected token is answered as expired so the client refreshes. Entries expire atchanged_at + maximum lifetime + margin`.
  • F17. In one process the cache is shared memory, written in the recording transaction. Replicas poll sf_access_changes every one to two seconds. Separate deployments receive an OIDC Back-Channel Logout token carrying an access_change event, with retry and logging.
  • F18. After a restart a relying party replays GET /access-changes?since= before serving and treats every token as suspect until replay succeeds.

docs.title: Resource-scoped collaborators (ADR-008)
docs.text:
• F19. The base schema gains a collaborator relation and a list permission on organization; collaborators have no view, edit or manage. collaborator is a membership role. The viewer/contributor/maintainer resource-role ladder is reserved in docs/authz-conventions.md.
  • F20. authz gains GrantResourceRole, RevokeResourceRole, ListResourceGrants and ListResources, implemented by rbac through sf_resource_grants and by rebac/spicedb through relationships and LookupResources. The first grant to a non-member creates a collaborator membership; revoking the last grant removes it.
  • F21. Invites may target a resource (type, ID, role); acceptance creates the collaborator membership and the grant in one transaction.
  • F22. Applications configure authz.mode: rbac | rebac and, for rebac, an engine. The deprecated authz/simple and authz/spicedb forwarders are scheduled for removal in the next major release.

docs.title: Management is a relationship (ADR-009)
docs.text:
• F23. IsManaged and the managed claim derive from active manager relationships. ErrNotManaged means "has no active manager"; ErrLastManager keeps its meaning and is reworded to say the last manager of a principal without a verified email cannot be removed.
  • F24. Creating a managed principal accepts an optional email, verified like any other before it counts for release.
  • F25. Release removes the last manager of a principal with a verified email and clears the managed state in one transaction.
  • F26. A self-managed human enters management only by accepting a manager invitation, a new invite kind carrying the manager role.
  • F27. Slugs for managed principals keep the manager-entered or generated form whether or not an email exists; an email's local part is never used.

docs.title: Non-Functional
docs.text:
• N1. Every operation that spans tables — signup, rename, conversion, invite acceptance, grant plus membership, release, access-change recording — is one database transaction.
  • N2. The per-request cost of the revocation check is a map lookup; the cache holds only changes within one token lifetime plus the margin.
  • N3. Both authorization modes pass the same providertest suite for organization roles, application roles, resource grants and lookups.
  • N4. Existing conformance suites pass; tests that added members to personal organizations use team organizations.
  • N5. golangci-lint reports no findings; the mkdocs strict build passes.
  • N6. Every manager action, role assignment, grant and release is audited with the acting principal.

docs.title: Success Criteria
docs.text:
• A new person signs in with GitHub and lands in a personal organization whose slug is their GitHub username; signing in again creates nothing.
  • Renaming a personal organization, giving the old slug to a team, and reclaiming it within seven days each succeed; a stranger taking it within seven days is refused; links to the old slug resolve throughout.
  • An application that keeps no membership table provisions itself for an organization on first use from the orgs claim, shows the person only the applications they hold a role in, and sees an owner as admin everywhere.
  • Removing a person from an organization is rejected by the application's next request in the same process, with a token-expired error that leads to a refresh carrying the reduced claims, and the person stays signed in to their other organizations.
  • A collaborator granted viewer on one resource sees that resource and no other, under rbac and under rebac, and the organization appears in their switcher with role collaborator.
  • A managed principal with a school-issued email keeps its guardian; releasing it is an explicit, audited call that succeeds only when the email is verified.

docs.title: Risks
docs.text: Risk Mitigation Dropping plan breaks consumers that read it The column is unconsulted today; the entitlements summary ships in the same item, and the change is called out in the release notes A missed access-change site leaves a stale claim honored The recording call is in the service transaction, not the handler; the list of change sites is enumerated in the TRD and tested one by one; the token lifetime remains the bound Clock skew between SystemAuth and a separate relying party The margin, its floor and the expiry rule are specified in the TRD; in-process both timestamps come from one clock The two authorization modes drift providertest grows cases for every grant and lookup operation and runs against both Slug cooling-off is gamed or locks a handle forever Reservations expire; only the releasing principal or their organizations may reclaim; reserved names are refused up front Deployment with no entitlements refuses every organization Startup warning; default entitlements are a documented configuration

docs.title: ROADMAP — Suite Organizations: Lifecycle, Claims, Collaborators, Real-Time Invalidation
docs.text:
Initiative: INIT-SYSTEMFORGE-011 Repository: github.com/plexusone/systemforge

Design of record: ADR-006, ADR-007, ADR-008, ADR-009, ADR-010. A first login yields a personal organization; memberships, application roles and entitlements reach applications as claims; an access change takes effect within one request; access to one resource needs no membership; management is a relationship, not a missing email. Builds on INIT-SYSTEMFORGE-007 and INIT-SYSTEMFORGE-008.

  • Depends on: RMI-SYSTEMFORGE-129
  • [ ] RMI-SYSTEMFORGE-132 The orgs claim: ID token and userinfo carry id, slug, name, type, role, apps (app → role); JWT access tokens carry the compact {id, role, apps}; at most 50 organizations with orgs_truncated; GET /userinfo/memberships paginated
  • Depends on: RMI-SYSTEMFORGE-130

  • [ ] RMI-SYSTEMFORGE-133 Relying-party membership sources: relyingparty.ClaimsMemberships (default) and RemoteMemberships; LocalMemberships documented as development-only; a first-use provisioning hook keyed by organization ID for applications
  • Depends on: RMI-SYSTEMFORGE-132
  • [ ] RMI-SYSTEMFORGE-134 Invites and member management carry application roles: invite create/accept with per-application role selection (none preselected); role changes per application without touching membership; SystemAuth pages and API
  • Depends on: RMI-SYSTEMFORGE-130
  • [ ] RMI-SYSTEMFORGE-150 Authz graph sync for application roles: AddAppRole/RemoveAppRole on the relationship syncer, as an optional interface so existing implementers keep working
  • [ ] RMI-SYSTEMFORGE-151 Fix: invite.Accept never syncs the new membership to the authorization graph
  • [ ] RMI-SYSTEMFORGE-153 Fix: race-free seat-limit check in approle.Assign: count the seats and insert the role under a PostgreSQL advisory lock inside the assigning transaction so concurrent assignments cannot exceed the limit; concurrency test on PostgreSQL

docs.title: Phase 3 — Real-time invalidation of access (ADR-010)
docs.text:
Theme: An access change takes effect within one request in the monolith and within one token lifetime at worst.

  • [ ] RMI-SYSTEMFORGE-135 Access-change records and refresh semantics: sf_access_changes written in the transactions for membership removal, organization or application role change, grant reduction, deactivation and session revocation; role or membership changes no longer revoke refresh tokens (deactivation and explicit revocation still do); access-token lifetime default 10 minutes, configurable, maximum 15
  • [ ] RMI-SYSTEMFORGE-136 Relying-party revocation cache: in-process shared cache (AccessChangeSink) written in the recording transaction; acceptance rule iat >= changed_at + margin with a configurable clock-skew margin (default 30 s, floor 15 s); entries expire at changed_at + max lifetime + margin; rejection answered as token-expired so clients refresh
  • Depends on: RMI-SYSTEMFORGE-135
  • [ ] RMI-SYSTEMFORGE-137 Replica poller and replay: instances poll sf_access_changes newer than their last read every 1–2 s; GET /access-changes?since= for rebuilding the cache after a restart; suspect mode until replay succeeds
  • Depends on: RMI-SYSTEMFORGE-136
  • [ ] RMI-SYSTEMFORGE-138 Back-channel delivery: OIDC Back-Channel Logout token carrying an access_change event to registered relying-party endpoints, with retry and logging; receiver in relyingparty

docs.text:

  • [ ] RMI-SYSTEMFORGE-140 Resource grants in rbac: sf_resource_grants; GrantResourceRole, RevokeResourceRole, ListResourceGrants, ListResources; first grant creates the collaborator membership, last revoke removes it

  • [ ] RMI-SYSTEMFORGE-141 Resource grants in rebac/spicedb: grants as relationships, ListResources via LookupResources, vocabulary-fragment validation for collaborator-able resources; providertest parity suite for grants and lookups across both modes
  • Depends on: RMI-SYSTEMFORGE-139
  • [ ] RMI-SYSTEMFORGE-142 Resource-targeted invites: invite fields for resource type, ID and role; acceptance creates collaborator membership and grant in one transaction
  • Depends on: RMI-SYSTEMFORGE-140
  • Depends on: RMI-SYSTEMFORGE-141
  • [ ] RMI-SYSTEMFORGE-143 authz.mode configuration: rbac | rebac with engine selection for rebac; the deprecated authz/simple and authz/spicedb forwarders scheduled for removal next major release; guidance in the authorization architecture page

docs.text:
Theme: A managed principal is one with a manager, whether or not it has an email.

  • [ ] RMI-SYSTEMFORGE-145 Release and manager invitations: Release removes the last manager of a principal with a verified email; a manager-invitation kind accepted by the signed-in principal for self-managed humans entering management; slugs for managed principals never derived from an email

docs.text: Initiative: INIT-SYSTEMFORGE-011 Design of record: ADR-006, ADR-007, ADR-008, ADR-009, ADR-010

docs.title: Current State
docs.text:
Organizations. identity/organization models Organization{ID, Name, Slug, OrgType, OwnerPrincipalID, ..., Plan, Active} with OrgType in personal | team | enterprise and Plan in free | starter | pro | enterprise (Plan* constants, Ent enum defaulting to free). The Service has Create, CreatePersonalOrg, GetByID, GetBySlug, GetPersonalOrg, Update, Delete, List, AddMember, UpdateMember, RemoveMember (a hard delete), GetMembership, ListMembers, ListMemberships, SlugAvailable, GenerateSlug and TransferOwnership, built with WithAuthzSyncer, WithSyncMode and WithLogger. Slugs match ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*[a-z0-9]$ at 3 to 63 characters, are unique by the Ent constraint plus an exact-match SlugAvailable pre-check, and are not updatable through UpdateOrganizationInput. There are no reserved slugs, no slug history, and no Rename, ConvertToTeam or ResolveSlug. Membership roles are owner, admin and member (constants; the column is a free string); nothing checks OrgType in AddMember, the members API or invite acceptance, so personal organizations accept members, and the API lets clients create personal organizations and set plan on create and update. SCIM group provisioning sets plan to free in both the mapper and the Ent store.

Signup and social login. identity/signup.Service has Signup, SignupWithInvite and SignupOrGetExisting; SignupInput requires PersonalOrgSlug from the caller and no slug derivation exists. SignupOrGetExisting looks up by email and returns the existing account only when EmailVerified is set. No non-test code calls signup. SystemAuth's social login (identity/systemauth/social_login.go) resolves an account through ResolveExternalLogin: the (provider, subject) link, then a verified-email match which it links, then PrincipalDirectory.CreateFromExternal, which writes the human, principal and ExternalIdentity rows and no organization or membership.

Claims and tokens. socialSessionProvider.GetUserClaims returns sub, managed (when the login has no email), and the scope-gated email, email_verified, name and picture. UserInfoClaims filters standard claims by scope and passes others through; prepareAccessClaims adds only sub and client_id to JWT access tokens. There is no orgs claim, no /userinfo/memberships (userinfo is /oauth/userinfo), and no back-channel logout: no code, and no logout URI on OAuthApp. Token lifetimes live under tokens in systemauth.Config (access_token_lifetime 15m, refresh_token_lifetime 168h, refresh_token_absolute_lifetime 720h, id_token_lifetime 1h) with per-client overrides in ClientConfig and the OAuthApp columns access_token_ttl, refresh_token_ttl, login_token_ttl. RevokeSubjectTokens is called only from /logout; RemoveMember, UpdateMember and TransferOwnership call the authz syncer and nothing else, so membership changes have never revoked refresh tokens. ADR-007 decision 9 described an intended behavior, not an implemented one; ADR-010 decision 5 therefore removes nothing and only fixes the rule.

Invites. identity/invite.Invite carries OrganizationID, InviterPrincipalID, Email, Role, Status, Message, ExpiresAt, ... with a hashed token; Accept checks status and expiry, refuses an existing member, creates the membership with inv.Role in a transaction and marks the invite accepted. It does not call RelationshipSyncer.AddOrgMembership (DefaultService holds only the client and base URL), so a relationship engine never learns of members who joined by invite. There are no resource fields, no invite kind and no application-role selection.

Relying parties. identity/relyingparty has MembershipSource, MembershipQuery{Principal, Subject, Claims}, MembershipLister, LocalMemberships and NoMemberships; defaultMembershipSource picks the explicit source, else LocalMemberships when the PrincipalStore implements MembershipLister, else NoMemberships. Membership{ID, OrganizationID, OrganizationName, OrganizationSlug, Role, JoinedAt}. ResolvePrincipal(ctx, store, VerifiedIdentity, now) is the existing first-sign-in hook and VerifiedIdentity.Managed comes from the managed claim. pgstore creates sf_rp_sessions and sf_rp_login_states only. There is no revocation cache and no access-change handling; SessionStore.DeleteBySubject and DeleteBySID exist with comments written for back-channel logout.

Managed principals. identity/managedprincipal.Service.IsManaged answers human.EmailIsNil(), and the managed claim is lp.Email == "". CreateInput{ClientID, DisplayName, Managers, ActorID} has no email; RemoveManager refuses the last manager only when Email == nil; AttachVerifiedEmail sets the email and default capabilities and keeps the relationships. There is no Release. The only manager-invitation path is the claim code (IssueClaim/RedeemClaim, sf_manager_claims). The deployment switch is managed_principals.enabled with login_token_ttl, login_token_max_ttl and single_use_token_ttl beside it.

Authorization. The real packages are authz/rbac and authz/rebac/spicedb; authz/simple and authz/spicedb are deprecated type-alias forwarders (the package doc in authz/authorizer.go and the opening comment of authz/rbac/provider.go still say "simple" and "spicedb"). Authorizer{Can, CanAll, CanAny, Filter}, OrgAuthorizer{CanForOrg, GetRole, IsMember}, PlatformAuthorizer, DecisionAuthorizer and FeatureAuthorizer{CanWithFeature} are defined; FeatureAuthorizer has no implementation. RelationshipSyncer has organization membership, principal, organization, platform-admin and manager operations. BaseSpiceDBSchema defines organization with relations owner, admin, editor, member, viewer and permissions manage = owner + admin, edit = manage + editor, contribute = edit + member, view = contribute + viewer, the four management permissions equal to manage, and delete = owner; principal with guardian/educator; platform. There is no collaborator relation and no list permission, no GrantResourceRole, RevokeResourceRole, ListResourceGrants or ListResources on the contract (only rebac/spicedb.Client.LookupResources and the provider's raw relationship writes), and no authz.mode configuration (the only Mode is SpiceDB's embedded | remote). docs/authz-conventions.md documents the owner/admin/editor/member/viewer ladder. authz/schema_parity_test.go holds OrgRolePermissions and ManagerRolePermissions equal to the schema; authz/providertest runs interface, behavior, organization-permission and manager-relation suites against rbac. marketplace/schema/marketplace.zed carries its own organization definition (owner/admin/member/viewer, edit = manage + member, use/billing/purchase) that conflicts with the base schema.

Marketplace. Listing{CreatorOrgID, ProductType, ProductID, ...}, License{ListingID, OrganizationID, LicenseType, Seats, UsedSeats, ValidFrom, ValidUntil, ...}, SeatAssignment{LicenseID, PrincipalID, ...}, Subscription{OrganizationID, PlanTier, Status, ...} with PricingModel in free | one_time | subscription | per_seat, LicenseType in seat_based | team | unlimited and SubscriptionStatus in active | trialing | past_due | canceled | unpaid. Nothing maps a listing to a registered application identifier, and Subscription.PlanTier is never written to Organization.plan. PurchaserChecker{IsManaged} is implemented by managedprincipal.Service.

Schema. Tables are sf_* under identity/ent/schema; relevant ones are sf_organizations, sf_principal_memberships (unique on (principal_id, organization_id)), sf_invites, sf_manager_relationships, sf_manager_claims, sf_oauth_apps, sf_oauth_tokens, sf_principal_tokens, sf_login_sessions, sf_listings, sf_licenses, sf_seat_assignments, sf_subscriptions. sf_slug_reservations, sf_app_roles, sf_access_changes and sf_resource_grants do not exist. Migrations so far: 0001_rename_cf_to_sf.sql, 0002_drop_legacy_user_tables.sql, 0003_hash_invite_tokens.sql.

docs.title: 1.1 Signup on first social login (RMI-124)
docs.text: ResolveExternalLogin keeps its order: provider identity, then verified email, then create. The create step changes: EntPrincipalDirectory. CreateFromExternal calls signup.SignupOrGetExisting with PersonalOrgSlug from SlugForLogin (§1.2) and links the external identity in the same transaction, so a first login produces the human, principal, external identity, personal organization (type personal, owner set) and owner membership together, or nothing. SignupOrGetExisting gains a ProviderIdentity lookup before the email lookup so the two paths agree, and keeps refusing an unverified email. The directory is built with the signup.Service (NewEntPrincipalDirectory(client, signupSvc)); MemoryPrincipalDirectory creates an in-memory personal organization so handler tests observe the same shape.

docs.title: 1.2 Slug derivation and reserved slugs (RMI-125)
docs.text:
// signup
func SlugForLogin(provider, providerLogin, email string) string
func SlugForManaged(entered string) string   // entered or generated

SlugForLogin returns the GitHub username for github, the local part of the email for google, and otherwise the local part; the result passes through slugify (lowercase, invalid runes to -, -org padding under three characters) and the collision rule in organization.GenerateSlug (-1 … -100, then an 8-character random suffix). SlugForManaged returns the manager-entered value when present, else two words and a number from a fixed word list (quiet-otter-42), never anything derived from an email (ADR-009). organization.ReservedSlugs is the built-in list (admin, api, o, login, logout, oauth, scim, invites, organizations, well-known, www, support, help, about, settings, new) plus WithReservedSlugs(...) for deployment-configured product names; SlugAvailable refuses them with ErrSlugReserved, and Create, CreatePersonalOrg, Rename and SCIM group creation go through SlugAvailable.

docs.title: 1.3 Slug changes with cooling-off and aliases (RMI-126)
docs.text:
New Ent schema SlugReservation → sf_slug_reservations:

Field Notes slug unique released_by_principal_id → Principal; the acting principal released_from_organization_id → Organization, nullable (the organization may be deleted) released_at expires_at released_at + 7 * 24h (organization.SlugCoolingOff, configurable)

Indexed on expires_at. Rows are deleted when the slug is reassigned or on first read after expiry.

Rename(ctx, orgID uuid.UUID, slug string, actor uuid.UUID) error
ResolveSlug(ctx, slug string) (*Organization, bool /*alias*/, error)

Rename in one transaction: validates the new slug; SlugAvailable (exact match, reserved list, and a live reservation held by someone other than actor or an organization actor owns → ErrSlugCoolingOff); writes the organization; deletes any reservation for the new slug; inserts a reservation for the old slug with actor. ResolveSlug tries the exact match, then a live reservation's released_from_organization_id. GetBySlug keeps exact-match semantics; HTTP handlers that resolve {slug} use ResolveSlug and answer with the current slug in the body. The rule is symmetric: it does not care whether either organization is personal or team, so person → organization, organization → person, organization → organization and reclaiming one's own handle are the same code path.

docs.title: 1.4 Personal organization rules (RMI-127)
docs.text: AddMember, UpdateMember, invite.Create, the members API and SCIM group membership refuse a personal organization with ErrPersonalOrganization unless the role is collaborator (§4). TransferOwnership refuses with the same error. The organization API stops accepting org_type: personal on create (enum:"team,enterprise"); personal organizations are created only by signup and by ConvertToTeam. Existing tests that add members to a personal organization move to team organizations.

docs.title: 1.5 ConvertToTeam (RMI-128)
docs.text:
ConvertToTeam(ctx, orgID uuid.UUID, teamSlug string, actor uuid.UUID) (*ConvertResult, error)
// ConvertResult{Team *Organization, Personal *Organization}

One transaction, in order: assert orgID is personal and actor is its owner; handle := org.Slug; Rename(orgID, teamSlug) (which reserves handle for actor); set org_type = team; CreatePersonalOrg{Owner: actor, Slug: handle} (allowed by the reservation, which it consumes). Memberships, settings and the ID are untouched; the owner membership becomes the team's first owner. Audit records both organization IDs.

docs.title: 1.6 Remove the plan column (RMI-129)
docs.text:
Drop plan from the Organization Ent schema (migration 0004_drop_organization_plan.sql), Organization, UpdateOrganizationInput, ListOrganizationsInput, the create/update/list API, the SCIM mapper and store, and the Plan type with its constants. The organization API gains:

"entitlements": {
  "apps": {"<application>": {"source": "subscription|license|default", "listing_id": "...", "seats": 10, "seats_used": 3}}
}

derived by marketplace.Entitlements(ctx, orgID) (§2.2); until Phase 2 lands, the summary contains only default entitlements. marketplace. PlanTier* stays: it describes a subscription, not an organization.

docs.title: 2. Memberships and entitlements as claims (Phase 2, ADR-007)
2.1 Application roles (RMI-130)
docs.text:
New Ent schema AppRole → sf_app_roles:

Field Notes principal_id → Principal organization_id → Organization application application identifier as registered in authz.VocabularyRegistry role validated against AppVocabulary.Roles() assigned_by → Principal timestamps BaseMixin

Unique on (principal_id, organization_id, application); indexed on (organization_id, application) for seat counting. A new package identity/approle owns Assign, Change, Remove, ListForPrincipal, ListForOrganization and EffectiveRoles(ctx, principalID, orgID) map[string]string, which overlays the implicit admin for the organization owner on every entitled application. Rules: the application must be entitled for the organization (§2.2); the principal must hold an active membership with role owner, admin or member (collaborators hold none); organization.RemoveMember deletes the principal's rows in its transaction and records an access change (§3.1). Assigning to oneself is allowed and audited. The authz syncer gains AddAppRole / RemoveAppRole so rebac writes {app}_org#<role> relationships.

docs.title: 2.2 Entitlements from the marketplace (RMI-131)
docs.text: Listing gains an optional application field mapping the listing to a registered application identifier. marketplace.Entitlements(ctx, orgID) returns the set of applications with an active subscription (active or trialing) or a license valid now on such a listing, merged with marketplace.WithDefaultEntitlements(apps ...string) (deployment configuration, marketplace.default_entitlements). A deployment whose registry has applications but no default entitlements and no listings with application set logs a warning at startup. For seat-licensed listings (LicenseType seat_based), approle.Assign counts sf_app_roles rows for (organization, application) against Seats and refuses with ErrNoSeats; SeatAssignment becomes derived from sf_app_roles and its API is kept as a view for one release, then removed.

docs.title: 2.3 The orgs claim (RMI-132)
docs.text:
ID token and userinfo (/oauth/userinfo):

"orgs": [
  {"id": "…", "slug": "jane", "name": "Jane", "type": "personal", "role": "owner",
   "apps": {"notes": "admin", "boards": "admin"}},
  {"id": "…", "slug": "acme", "name": "Acme", "type": "team", "role": "member",
   "apps": {"notes": "contributor"}}
],
"orgs_truncated": false

JWT access tokens: "orgs": [{"id": "…", "role": "owner", "apps": {...}}] and orgs_truncated. Both are built by one function, systemauth.OrgsClaim(ctx, principalID, compact bool), ordered personal first, then by membership created_at descending, capped at MaxOrgsInToken = 50; apps comes from approle.EffectiveRoles filtered to entitled applications, so an application absent from apps is one the principal may not open. Collaborators appear with role collaborator and empty apps. The claim is emitted regardless of scope (it is authorization data, like managed). GET /oauth/userinfo/memberships? limit=&cursor= returns the full list for the presenting token's principal, in the ID-token shape, paginated by membership ID.

docs.title: 2.4 Relying-party membership sources (RMI-133)
docs.text:
func ClaimsMemberships() MembershipSource      // orgs claim from ID token or userinfo
func RemoteMemberships(c *Client) MembershipSource // GET /oauth/userinfo/memberships

Membership gains OrganizationType, Apps map[string]string and Truncated on the result. defaultMembershipSource becomes ClaimsMemberships chained to RemoteMemberships when orgs_truncated is set or the claims hold only the compact form (no slug); LocalMemberships must be chosen explicitly and its doc comment says development and tests only. BFFConfig gains OnFirstUse func(ctx, OrganizationRef) error, called once per organization ID per process (memoized with single-flight) when a principal holding a role in it first makes a request, so an application provisions its own rows keyed by the SystemAuth organization ID. The stale role comment on Membership.Role is corrected to the ADR-007 roles.

docs.title: 2.5 Invites and member management carry application roles (RMI-134)
docs.text: Invite gains AppRoles map[string]string (JSON column app_roles), validated at Create against the organization's entitlements and each application's ladder, with no application preselected on the SystemAuth invite page. Accept creates the membership, the sf_app_roles rows and (fixing the existing gap) calls the authz syncer, in one transaction. PATCH /organizations/{slug}/members/{principal_id}/apps/{application} assigns or changes one application role; DELETE removes it; neither touches the membership row. The SystemAuth member page lists entitled applications with a role picker per application.

docs.title: 3.1 Access-change records and refresh semantics (RMI-135)
docs.text:
New Ent schema AccessChange → sf_access_changes:

Field Notes principal_id → Principal organization_id → Organization, nullable (null = every organization) changed_at server clock at commit reason enum: membership_removed, org_role_changed, app_role_changed, grant_reduced, deactivated, sessions_revoked

Indexed on changed_at. accesschange.Record(ctx, tx, Change) is called inside the transactions of: organization.RemoveMember, UpdateMember (role change), TransferOwnership (both principals); approle.Change and Remove; authz RevokeResourceRole and a grant change to a lower role (§4.2); principal.Deactivate; RevokeSubjectTokens, managedprincipal.RevokeSession and RevokeAll. Every record is also pushed to the configured AccessChangeSink (§3.2) after commit. Refresh tokens are revoked by deactivation and explicit revocation only; a role or membership change leaves the refresh token valid and the next refresh re-evaluates OrgsClaim. tokens.access_token_lifetime defaults to 10m and is validated at load to be at most MaxAccessTokenLifetime = 15m; per-client and OAuthApp overrides are clamped to the same ceiling. Rows older than MaxAccessTokenLifetime + margin + 1h are pruned by the existing maintenance job.

docs.title: 3.2 Relying-party revocation cache (RMI-136)
docs.text:
// relyingparty
type AccessChange struct {
    PrincipalID    string
    OrganizationID string // "" for every organization
    ChangedAt      time.Time
    Reason         string
}

type AccessChangeSink interface { Record(AccessChange) }

type RevocationCache struct { /* mutex, map[string]time.Time keyed by principal and principal+"/"+org */ }
func NewRevocationCache(opts ...CacheOption) *RevocationCache // WithSkewMargin, WithMaxTokenLifetime, WithClock
func (c *RevocationCache) Record(ch AccessChange)
func (c *RevocationCache) Accept(principalID, orgID string, iat time.Time) bool

Algorithm. On Record, store max(existing, changed_at) under the principal key when OrganizationID is empty, else under the principal/organization key. On every request, after signature verification, Accept is evaluated for the token's sub and for the organization the request addresses (when the middleware knows it):

margin   = max(configured, 15s); default 30s
changed  = latest of cache[principal], cache[principal/org]
accept   = no entry || iat >= changed + margin

A token stamped inside the margin is treated as issued before the change and refused. A refusal is answered as 401 with error=invalid_token, error_description="token expired" so the OIDC client refreshes; the refresh yields the reduced claims. Entries are dropped when now > changed_at + maxTokenLifetime + margin, sweeping on Record and on a ticker; after that moment no token issued before the change can still be valid at any verifier, however its clock drifted within the margin. Cache size is therefore bounded by the number of changes within one lifetime plus margin. In one process, SystemAuth's accesschange.Record writes to the same RevocationCache instance passed as the sink, in the recording transaction's post-commit hook; both timestamps come from one clock so the margin is moot there, but it is applied uniformly.

docs.title: 3.3 Replica poller and replay (RMI-137)
docs.text: relyingparty.NewAccessChangePoller(db, cache, interval) runs an indexed query WHERE changed_at > $last ORDER BY changed_at every interval (default 1s, allowed 1–2s), records each row and advances last to the newest changed_at seen minus the margin (so a late-committing row with an earlier timestamp is re-read, deduplicated by max). SystemAuth adds GET /access-changes?since=<RFC 3339> (bearer-authenticated with a client credential holding scope access_changes:read) returning rows newer than since in the sink shape. relyingparty.Replay(ctx, client, cache) is called before the server starts serving with since = now − maxTokenLifetime − margin; until it returns, the middleware is in suspect mode: every token is accepted only after a RemoteMemberships call for its principal (memoized per jti), which is slower but never wider than the pre-change state. Replay failure is retried with backoff and logged; the server stays in suspect mode.

docs.title: 3.4 Back-channel delivery (RMI-138)
docs.text: OAuthApp gains backchannel_logout_uri (and ClientConfig the same). systemauth.Backchannel sends, for each registered client, an OpenID Connect Back-Channel Logout 1.0 logout token (typ: logout+jwt) with sub, sid when known, and events: {"http://schemas.openid.net/event/backchannel-logout": {}, "urn:systemforge:event:access_change": {organization_id, changed_at, reason}}, signed with the issuer key, POSTed as logout_token=<jwt>. Delivery is queued after commit, retried with exponential backoff for up to the token lifetime, and failures are logged against the client ID. relyingparty.BackchannelHandler(cache, verifier) verifies the token against the issuer's JWKS, records the access_change event into the cache, and on a plain logout event deletes sessions by sid or subject through the existing SessionStore methods. An application configures one of WithSharedCache(cache), WithPoller(db) or WithBackchannel(path) depending on the boundary it sits on.

docs.title: 4.1 Base schema and conventions (RMI-139)
docs.text: BaseSpiceDBSchema.organization gains relation collaborator: principal and permission list = view + collaborator. The owner decided that editor and viewer are dropped as organization roles, leaving owner, admin, member and collaborator: edit = manage, contribute = edit + member, view = contribute, and list = view + collaborator, so every remaining role keeps list and collaborators gain only it; view, edit, manage and the management permissions exclude collaborators. Migration 0008_drop_editor_viewer_roles.sql maps stored editor to member and viewer to collaborator (recording an access change for each active membership it changes), and every path that writes a membership refuses any other role with ErrInvalidRole. organization.RoleCollaborator = "collaborator" joins the role constants and the API enums; OrgRolePermissions[collaborator] = {PermOrgList} with the new PermOrgList = "list", and schema_parity_test.go checks both. docs/authz-conventions.md reserves the resource-role ladder viewer < contributor < maintainer with the fragment shape from ADR-008 and states that admin on a resource is not a resource role (it is an application role). marketplace/schema/marketplace.zed drops its own organization definition and attaches use, billing and purchase through a marketplace_org facet on the base organization, as the vocabulary rules require. Personal organizations accept memberships of role collaborator only (§1.4).

docs.title: 4.2 Resource grants in rbac (RMI-140)
docs.text:
New Ent schema ResourceGrant → sf_resource_grants:

Field Notes principal_id → Principal organization_id → Organization (the resource's organization) resource_type {app}_{type} as declared in the vocabulary resource_id string role viewer | contributor | maintainer granted_by → Principal

Unique on (principal_id, resource_type, resource_id); indexed on (organization_id, principal_id) and (resource_type, principal_id). The authz contract gains:

type ResourceGranter interface {
    GrantResourceRole(ctx, principal, resource Resource, role string, granter uuid.UUID) error
    RevokeResourceRole(ctx, principal, resource Resource) error
    ListResourceGrants(ctx, resource Resource) ([]Grant, error)
